dataset_metadata.title: Fictional Weapons System OSCAL-Inspired Platform Seed
dataset_metadata.disclaimer: The WS-X90 system, program and assurance records are entirely fictional. The framework reference layer is not: the control catalog, the SP 800-53B baselines, the SP 800-53A Rev 5 assessment objectives and the DISA CCI identifiers are the real published content, and the CNSSI 1253 allocation is a third-party extraction of the real publication flagged authoritative:false. Control and requirement narratives remain synthetic and do not reproduce authoritative NIST control text.

profiles.name: WS-X90 Tailored Security Baseline

overlays.name: CNSSI 1253 National Security System Allocation
overlays.reason: CNSSI 1253 (2022) allocates controls against confidentiality, integrity and availability independently. At C=high, I=high, A=moderate it selects 554 controls, adding 201 the SP 800-53B High baseline does not carry and withdrawing 17 it does.
overlays.provenance_note: Selections come from a third-party text extraction of CNSSI 1253 (2022), not an official CNSS machine-readable release. Treat every selection as derived.

overlays.name: Mission Assurance Overlay
overlays.reason: Demo overlay emphasizing isolation, integrity, and supply-chain assurance; removes wireless-specific requirement from this configuration.
overlays.resolution_note: Adds and removes are re-expressed against the resolved CNSSI 1253 set. Removing a base control withdraws its enhancements; an add already carried by the resolved set is recorded as a reaffirmation.

overlays.name: Deployed Platform Overlay
overlays.reason: Adds protections for deployed/fielded operation and controlled maintenance.
overlays.resolution_note: Adds and removes are re-expressed against the resolved CNSSI 1253 set. Removing a base control withdraws its enhancements; an add already carried by the resolved set is recorded as a reaffirmation.

overlays.name: Customer A Tailoring
overlays.reason: Adds penetration testing and vulnerability monitoring while excluding external-system use for this isolated configuration.
overlays.resolution_note: Adds and removes are re-expressed against the resolved CNSSI 1253 set. Removing a base control withdraws its enhancements; an add already carried by the resolved set is recorded as a reaffirmation.

profiles.tailoring_rationale: Resolved through the documented pipeline: SP 800-53 Rev 5 catalog -> SP 800-53B High baseline (370) -> CNSSI 1253 C/I/A allocation at C=high, I=high, A=moderate (554) -> three named overlays (546) -> program tailoring (none authored) -> parameter values. Each selection, addition and withdrawal is preserved as an ordered provenance event rather than flattened away.

systems.name: WS-X90 Sentinel Mission System
systems.description: Synthetic mission platform used only to exercise security engineering, compliance, assessment, SSP, and POA&M workflows.

subsystems.name: Mission Computing Subsystem
subsystems.description: Hosts mission applications, security services, and platform orchestration.

subsystems.name: Navigation & Timing Subsystem
subsystems.description: Provides trusted position, navigation, timing, and integrity monitoring.

subsystems.name: Communications Subsystem
subsystems.description: Provides external and internal protected communications interfaces.

subsystems.name: Payload Interface Subsystem
subsystems.description: Provides controlled command/data interfaces to mission payload LRUs.

subsystems.name: Platform Management Subsystem
subsystems.description: Provides health monitoring, maintenance access, update, and configuration services.

subsystems.name: Ground Support Subsystem
subsystems.description: Provides maintenance, provisioning, logging export, and support tooling.

components.name: Mission Computer
components.description: Runs mission software and hosts security enforcement services.

components.name: Secure Boot Controller
components.description: Enforces authenticated boot and platform integrity state.

components.name: Cryptographic Services Module
components.description: Provides protected cryptographic operations and key use.

components.name: Navigation Processor
components.description: Processes navigation data and integrity checks.

components.name: Timing Receiver
components.description: Provides trusted timing input and holdover monitoring.

components.name: Navigation Sensor Interface
components.description: Aggregates navigation sensor inputs.

components.name: Protected Network Gateway
components.description: Mediates external communications and network policy enforcement.

components.name: Tactical Data Radio
components.description: Provides mission data communications.

components.name: Internal Ethernet Switch
components.description: Provides internal segmented data transport.

components.name: Payload Interface Controller
components.description: Mediates commands and telemetry between mission compute and payload.

components.name: Payload Safety Interlock
components.description: Provides independent authorization and state interlocks.

components.name: Payload Telemetry Unit
components.description: Collects and forwards payload health and status telemetry.

components.name: Platform Management Controller
components.description: Hosts platform health, inventory, and administrative services.

components.name: Maintenance Access Gateway
components.description: Controls technician maintenance sessions and service access.

components.name: Secure Storage Module
components.description: Stores protected configuration, audit, and recovery material.

components.name: Update & Recovery Controller
components.description: Stages authenticated updates and controlled recovery.

components.name: Provisioning Workstation
components.description: Performs controlled provisioning and configuration workflows.

components.name: Security Log Collector
components.description: Collects and correlates exported platform security logs.

components.name: Maintenance Laptop
components.description: Authorized support endpoint used for bounded maintenance activity.

components.name: Configuration Repository
components.description: Stores approved configuration baselines and signed release metadata.

requirements.title: Annual reissue of the WS-X90 acquisition procedure set
requirements.description: The WS-X90 system and services acquisition policy and its supporting procedures, held as controlled items in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), shall be reviewed and reissued at least annually, and each issue published from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall record the designated acquisition security official and a dissemination acknowledgement from every role that performs acquisition actions on the program. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A signed issue of both the acquisition policy and the acquisition procedures, dated within the preceding 12 months, is present in LRU-020.
The release metadata for that issue names the designated acquisition security official.
Dissemination acknowledgements are recorded for every acquisition role listed in the WS-X90 role register.

requirements.title: Discrete security resourcing line for WS-X90 subsystems and ground support tooling
requirements.description: The Platform Lead shall be able to walk an assessor through the WS-X90 security resourcing record for the current program year and show, per subsystem, the allocated security engineering effort and the funded refresh of the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), identifying the budget line each is drawn from. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead can name the budget line that carries WS-X90 security engineering effort.
The resourcing record shows an allocation against each of SUB-01 through SUB-06.
Ground support tooling refresh for LRU-017 and LRU-019 appears as a funded item with a target year.

requirements.title: Life-cycle phase tagging enforced at build intake
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 build admitted to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall carry a life-cycle phase tag and the named security role accountable for that phase, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to provision any LRU from a build record missing either field. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every build in the LRU-020 current release set carries a non-empty phase tag and accountable role.
A provisioning attempt from an untagged build record is rejected by LRU-017 and the rejection is logged.
Waivers admitting an untagged build are individually recorded with an expiry date.

requirements.title: Preproduction bench provisioned from the flight baseline and segregated from operational segments
requirements.description: The WS-X90 preproduction integration bench shall be provisioned from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) using the same signed baseline issued to flight units, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be barred by configuration from holding a bench connection and an operational network connection at the same time. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The bench build record cites the same signed baseline identifier as the current flight release.
LRU-019 network configuration shows no route between the bench segment and any operational segment.
Bench provisioning runs are logged with the operator identity and baseline identifier.

requirements.title: Expiring recorded approval for operational data on the preproduction bench
requirements.description: Use of operational WS-X90 mission data on the preproduction bench shall require an approval record held with the bench provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) that names the data set, the approving authority and an expiry no more than 90 days after issue, and the bench shall refuse a live-data load once the approval has expired. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every live-data load on the bench resolves to an approval record with a named data set and approving authority.
No approval record carries an expiry more than 90 days after its issue date.
An expired approval produces a refused load with a logged reason.

requirements.title: Bench and maintenance endpoint handled at flight protection level while live data is present
requirements.description: While an approved operational data set is present on the WS-X90 preproduction bench, the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the bench storage shall be handled at the protection level applied to the flight Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), and the laptop shall be sanitised to a recorded procedure before it is returned to general support use. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The bench handling instruction cites the same protection level as the LRU-015 storage handling rule.
A sanitisation record exists for every LRU-019 return following a live-data approval.
No live-data approval is open against an endpoint that has already been returned to general support use.

requirements.title: Dated refresh decision points for navigation and timing hardware
requirements.description: The WS-X90 technology refresh schedule shall carry a dated replacement decision point for the Timing Receiver (LRU-005), Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) falling no later than the vendor end-of-production date recorded for each item, and the schedule shall be reviewed whenever a supplier revises that date. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of LRU-004, LRU-005 and LRU-006 has a decision date in the refresh schedule.
No decision date falls after the recorded vendor end-of-production date for that item.
A supplier end-of-production change produces a dated schedule revision.

requirements.title: Allocated control requirements carried into each LRU procurement package
requirements.description: Each WS-X90 LRU procurement package shall reference, by control id from the tailored profile, the security functional and assurance requirements allocated to that LRU, and the resulting first-article acceptance record shall be filed against the LRU entry in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) before the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) marks the inventory entry accepted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every LRU entry in the LRU-013 inventory marked accepted resolves to a first-article acceptance record in LRU-020.
Each package names allocated control ids in the fixed format used by the tailored profile.
LRUs whose package predates the current tailoring are listed with the engineering change retrofitting the shortfall.

requirements.title: Supplier functional properties description for boot and cryptographic enforcement functions
requirements.description: The suppliers of the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall deliver, for each security function exposed at the LRU boundary, a functional properties description stating the accepted inputs, the returned outputs and error states, and the externally observable behaviour of each enforcement decision including denial. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A current functional properties description exists for every security function listed in the LRU-002 and LRU-003 interface registers.
Each description states an observable behaviour for the denial case, not only the success case.
The assessment procedures for boot and key-use controls cite the description by revision.

requirements.title: Design and implementation detail sufficient to trace enforcement decisions to named interfaces
requirements.description: Security-relevant external interface specifications and design information for the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall be held at a depth that lets an assessor trace every enforcement decision to a named interface and its stated preconditions, without relying on supplier assertion. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each enforcement decision named in the LRU-003, LRU-007 and LRU-011 control narratives resolves to a documented interface.
The design set states preconditions and denial behaviour for each traced interface.
Any interface whose design detail is not yet delivered is listed with the contractual action opened against it.

requirements.title: Supplier demonstration of the life cycle used for the shipped mission software release
requirements.description: The supplier of the mission software hosted on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall be able to demonstrate the systems engineering, security engineering and verification methods used for the release that shipped, tracing each claimed gate to an artefact in the build record held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The supplier can name the security engineering method applied to the shipped release.
Each claimed development gate resolves to a dated artefact in the LRU-020 build record.
Divergence between the proposed and the practised process is recorded with a rationale.

requirements.title: LRUs delivered with the approved hardened configuration already applied
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 LRU shall arrive with the approved hardened configuration already applied, and the configuration hash read at first power-on shall match the approved baseline recorded in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with no post-delivery hardening step required to reach the approved state. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: First power-on configuration hash equals the approved baseline hash for the LRU under test.
No acceptance procedure contains a hardening step performed after delivery.
A mismatch at first power-on stops acceptance and is recorded against the LRU entry.

requirements.title: Approved configuration reapplied as the default on reinstallation and recovery
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall reapply the approved delivery configuration as the default on every reinstallation and controlled recovery, so that a recovered LRU reaches the approved hardened state without technician intervention. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A recovery run on a mission computing LRU produces a configuration hash equal to the approved baseline.
No technician step is required between recovery completion and the approved state being reached.
LRUs that recover to a supplier default profile are listed with the change action opened against them.

requirements.title: Evaluation status recorded for commercial assurance products in the comms and crypto path
requirements.description: Commercial information assurance products used in the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall each carry a register entry naming the applicable NIAP Protection Profile and evaluation identifier, or, where no profile applies to the technology type and the product enforces its policy with cryptography, the module validation or approval certificate number. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three LRUs has a register entry naming either an evaluation identifier or a module certificate number.
Entries recording 'no applicable profile' state the technology type that was searched.
Any product with neither an evaluation nor a certificate is listed as an accepted deviation with an approver.

requirements.title: Permitted network services generated from supplier function, port and protocol declarations
requirements.description: Each supplier shall declare the functions, ports, protocols and services its LRU uses in operational configuration, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) rule set and Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) segment policy — including the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) sensor bus allow-list — shall be generated from those declarations so that any undeclared service is denied by default. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The deployed LRU-007 and LRU-009 policies are byte-identical to the policy generated from the current declaration set.
An undeclared service attempt is denied and appears in the platform log with the service identifier.
A declaration change produces a reviewed policy delta before the release ships.

requirements.title: Approved-products selection for ground support credential readers
requirements.description: Credential readers fitted to the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be drawn from the approved products list for the credential type in use, and the selected product and its list entry shall be recorded against the workstation baseline. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each fitted credential reader resolves to an entry on the approved products list.
The workstation baseline records the reader product and list entry.
Where no reader is fitted, the absence is recorded as an accepted configuration with an approver.

requirements.title: Administrator documentation reissued with each maintenance baseline change
requirements.description: Administrator documentation for the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall describe the secure configuration and operation of every privileged maintenance function and the known configuration weaknesses a technician must avoid, and shall be reissued with each configuration baseline change so that the issued set matches the baseline on the unit. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current administrator set revision cites the configuration baseline identifier deployed on LRU-013 and LRU-014.
Every privileged maintenance function in the LRU-014 function register appears in the administrator set.
Known configuration weaknesses are listed with the avoidance action rather than only named.

requirements.title: Operator documentation states observable behaviour when a security function denies
requirements.description: Operator documentation for the mission software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the payload health indications fed by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall describe each security function an operator can invoke and the behaviour the system exhibits when that function denies an action, including the indication shown when telemetry integrity cannot be confirmed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every operator-invocable security function in the LRU-001 interface register appears in the operator set.
Each entry states the denial behaviour an operator will observe.
The payload health section names the indication shown when LRU-012 telemetry integrity is unconfirmed.

requirements.title: Architecture description traces each engineering principle to a named design decision
requirements.description: The WS-X90 security architecture description shall name, for each of the six subsystems, the engineering principles applied and the specific design decision that carries each one, so that a reviewer can trace a principle to a mechanism on the Mission Computer (LRU-001), Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) or Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) rather than to a statement of intent. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every principle claimed for a subsystem resolves to a named mechanism in the architecture description.
No subsystem section claims a principle without a design decision reference.
Sections not yet written to that depth are listed with the owner and the target review.

requirements.title: Single named abstraction for payload command authority
requirements.description: Mission applications on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall obtain payload command authority through one named abstraction exposed by the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), and the controller shall reject register-level writes that do not arrive through that entry point. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-010 interface register lists exactly one entry point for payload command authority.
No mission application build links against a register-level payload symbol.
A register-level write attempted outside the abstraction is rejected and logged.

requirements.title: Per-trust-level message queues with enforced switch quotas
requirements.description: Mission applications of differing trust levels hosted on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall not share a message-passing mechanism; each trust level shall use its own queue carried on a dedicated Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) VLAN with an enforced quota, so that saturation by one trust level does not delay another. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each declared trust level maps to a distinct queue and VLAN in the deployed configuration.
Saturating the lowest trust level's quota leaves higher-level message latency inside its budget.
No message path exists that carries two trust levels through one queue.

requirements.title: Navigation integrity checking separated into its own signed module
requirements.description: Navigation integrity checking on the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall be a separately loadable module with a declared interface, so that a change to sensor fusion cannot alter the integrity check without a separate signed module release, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) layer map shall continue to show no upward calls from enforcement services into mission applications. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-004 release manifest lists the integrity-check module with its own signature.
A sensor fusion release that does not change the integrity module leaves the integrity module signature unchanged.
The LRU-001 layer map shows no call from an enforcement service into an application layer.

requirements.title: Acyclic initialisation order rooted at the boot controller
requirements.description: The WS-X90 initialisation order shall be a declared directed acyclic graph in which the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) completes before any service it protects, and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall start from a boot-time default that does not depend on navigation data. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The declared initialisation graph contains no cycle.
No service protected by LRU-002 appears in the graph before LRU-002 completion.
LRU-006 cold start completes with navigation data unavailable.

requirements.title: Payload command mediation performed once inside a 5 ms budget
requirements.description: Payload command mediation shall occur once, at the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), and shall add no more than 5 ms to the command path measured at the interface, with no alternative unmediated route available to mission applications on the Mission Computer (LRU-001). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Measured mediation latency at the LRU-010 interface is at or below 5 ms at the specified command rate.
A command reaching the payload without passing the mediation point is not observed under test.
The interface specification records the measured figure, not only the budget.

requirements.title: No buffer reuse across security domains without zeroisation
requirements.description: The Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall partition working buffers by security domain, and any buffer released by one domain shall be zeroised before it is made available to another, with residue absent when the buffer is re-read. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Buffer pools in the deployed builds are declared per domain.
A buffer read immediately after cross-domain release contains no prior-domain content.
The zeroisation path is exercised by a build-time test rather than only by inspection.

requirements.title: Payload authorization path bounded and fully reviewable
requirements.description: The Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) authorization path and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) integrity path shall each be implemented as a bounded state machine with no dynamic memory allocation after initialisation and no externally reachable entry point absent from the interface specification, so that each path can be reviewed in full at every release. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The authorization and integrity paths contain no allocation call after initialisation.
Every externally reachable entry point in the built image appears in the interface specification.
A full review of each path is recorded against the release it covers.

requirements.title: Versioned, capability-declaring update format
requirements.description: The WS-X90 update format handled by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall carry explicit version and capability fields recorded against the release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), so that a future security function can be introduced without weakening verification of the current one, and an image declaring a capability the controller cannot verify shall be refused. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The fielded update format specification defines version and capability fields as mandatory.
An image declaring an unsupported capability is refused at staging with a logged reason.
The LRU-020 release record carries the capability set for every current release.

requirements.title: Declared trustworthiness basis for components carrying security decisions
requirements.description: Each WS-X90 component another component depends on for a security decision shall carry a declared trustworthiness basis, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall not accept an authorization from a component whose declared basis is weaker than its own, measured against the bases recorded for the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every security-decision dependency in the architecture resolves to a component with a recorded basis.
No component with an unrecorded basis appears upstream of an LRU-011 authorization.
Components whose assurance case is undelivered are listed with the contractual action against them.

requirements.title: Key release conditioned on a present boot measurement
requirements.description: Platform trust on WS-X90 shall be rooted in the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) measurement chain, and the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall refuse to release key material to any caller for which a current boot measurement is absent, rather than accepting the caller on identity alone. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A key release request from a caller with no recorded measurement is refused.
The refusal is recorded with the caller identity and the missing measurement slot.
No key release path exists that bypasses the measurement precondition.

requirements.title: Modification authority graded by component trust
requirements.description: Modification of the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall require a stronger authorization than modification of a mission application, so that the components carrying the most platform trust are the hardest to change. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The signing policy defines at least two authority levels with LRU-002 and LRU-015 at the higher one.
An image for LRU-002 signed at the lower authority is refused.
Authority level is recorded in the release metadata for every signed image.

requirements.title: Protected services obtained only from equal or higher trust components
requirements.description: A WS-X90 component shall obtain a protected service only from a component at or above its own trust level; mission applications on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall not depend on peer-provided protection, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall hold no dependency on a lower-trust component for its authorization decision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The service dependency map shows no edge from a higher trust level to a lower one.
Each protected service names the trust level it is provided at.
Exceptions are individually recorded with an approver and a removal date.

requirements.title: Payload authorization trusted set limited to two named elements
requirements.description: The set of WS-X90 elements that must be trusted for payload command authorization shall be limited to the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) and the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), and any addition to that set shall require a recorded architecture change decision rather than a code review. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The authorization trusted set recorded in the architecture contains exactly the two named elements.
No third element performs an authorization check in the delivered payload path.
Any proposed addition carries an architecture change decision record.

requirements.title: Service privilege sets fixed by approved manifest and enforced at start
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 platform service and mission application shall declare its required privileges in a manifest, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall refuse to start any service on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) or grant any Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session a privilege the approved baseline does not declare, logging each refusal with the requested privilege. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A service whose manifest requests an undeclared privilege fails to start and the refusal is logged with that privilege.
No running service holds a privilege absent from its approved manifest.
A maintenance session cannot acquire a privilege beyond the declared task scope.

requirements.title: Two independent authorities required before the payload interlock opens
requirements.description: A WS-X90 payload release action shall require the concurrence of two independent authorities, presented over separate paths, before the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) opens and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) forwards the command. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A release attempt carrying one authority does not open the interlock.
The two authorities are presented over paths that do not share a single point of compromise.
Each concurrence is recorded with both authority identities.

requirements.title: Timing receiver holds over rather than passing unvalidated external time
requirements.description: On loss of the external timing reference, or on disagreement between that reference and internal holdover beyond the declared tolerance, the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall enter holdover and mark its output degraded, and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall record the degraded state rather than treating the value as validated time. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Removing the external reference produces a holdover state and a degraded output marking within the declared detection window.
An injected reference offset beyond tolerance produces the same degraded marking rather than an accepted step.
Records written while the marking is degraded carry the degraded indication.

requirements.title: Composed security policy analysed across the external boundary
requirements.description: The security policy that results from composing WS-X90 with each external mission system it connects to shall be stated and analysed at the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) boundary, identifying any protection that neither side provides once composed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A composed-policy statement exists for each external mission system connection.
Each statement names protections assumed from the other side.
Gaps identified by the composition are recorded as risks rather than left in the analysis.

requirements.title: External channels mutually authenticated and fail closed
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 connection that crosses the platform boundary — the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) wired path and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) mission link — shall complete mutual authentication using key material held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) before carrying traffic, and shall fail closed with no unauthenticated fallback if authentication does not complete. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A peer presenting no valid credential is refused and no traffic is carried.
No configuration option enables an unauthenticated external channel.
Key use for channel authentication is performed inside LRU-003 with no key export.

requirements.title: Internal payload channel bound to LRU identity
requirements.description: Traffic between the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall run on an authenticated channel bound to the LRU identity established at boot, so that a substituted or spoofed unit cannot present itself as the payload interface, and the switch shall refuse to forward payload traffic from an unbound port. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Payload traffic offered from an unbound switch port is not forwarded.
A substituted LRU-010 without the bound identity cannot establish the internal channel.
Channel binding failures are logged with the port and the presented identity.

requirements.title: Stored security material stays sealed until platform integrity is established
requirements.description: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall expose no plaintext security material at any point in the WS-X90 boot sequence before the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) has established the platform integrity state, and a boot whose verification fails shall leave the material sealed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No plaintext material is observable on the storage interface before the integrity state is set.
A boot with an injected verification failure ends with the material still sealed.
Power domains that come up before the integrity state is set are listed with the material they can reach.

requirements.title: Telemetry metadata protected to the same level as telemetry content
requirements.description: Labels, timestamps and source identifiers produced by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall be protected to the same level as the telemetry content when exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), and the collector shall reject a record whose metadata binding does not verify. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No telemetry metadata field is carried outside the protected envelope on the export path.
A record with an altered source identifier is rejected at LRU-018.
The rejection is recorded with the claimed and the verified identifier.

requirements.title: Navigation and timing self-check of the checking function itself
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall each run a self-check of their own integrity and holdover monitoring functions at least once per mission phase and report the outcome to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), which shall raise a fault when a report is absent rather than treating absence as normal. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A self-check report is present for each mission phase for both LRUs.
Suppressing the self-check produces a fault at LRU-013 within one mission phase.
An injected fault in the checking function is reported rather than masked.

requirements.title: Security-relevant records attributable to actor and originating unit
requirements.description: Every security-relevant record exported from the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall carry an actor identity and an originating unit identity that the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) resolves from the record itself rather than inferring from the transport, and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall retain records at full fidelity while resolution is incomplete. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Sampled LRU-012 records carry both an actor identity and an originating unit identity.
LRU-018 resolves the unit without reference to the source address.
Records that resolve only to subsystem level are counted and reported.

requirements.title: Restrictive defaults enforced at baseline intake and restored on recovery
requirements.description: Every configurable WS-X90 security option shall be set to its restrictive state in the delivered baseline; the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall reject at intake any baseline carrying a permissive default, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall restore the restrictive state on recovery, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall report any runtime deviation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A baseline submitted with a permissive default is rejected at LRU-020 intake with the option named.
A recovery run leaves every configurable option in its restrictive state.
A runtime deviation appears on the LRU-013 health view within one reporting interval.

requirements.title: Failure states grant no capability at the boot controller and payload interlock
requirements.description: On a failed integrity check the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall halt in a state that grants no capability and pass control to nothing, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall remain closed through any failure of its inputs rather than defaulting open. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An injected integrity failure at LRU-002 ends in a halt with no service started.
Loss of every interlock input leaves LRU-011 closed.
Neither failure path exposes a maintenance or debug capability.

requirements.title: Recovery verifies its source or stops
requirements.description: Recovery performed by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall restore only from a signed image held in the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), shall stop rather than proceed when the source cannot be verified, and shall not reduce the platform protection state in order to complete faster. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A recovery attempt from an unverifiable image stops without writing to the target LRU.
The protection state after recovery equals the state recorded in the approved baseline.
Recovery runs on the payload interface path are covered by the same test case.

requirements.title: Protection strength related to adversary cost and protected value
requirements.description: WS-X90 protections on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall be selected and sized against a recorded analysis of the adversary cost of defeating them relative to the value of what they protect. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An adversary-cost analysis exists for each protection claimed on LRU-001 and LRU-013.
Each analysis states the protected value it was compared against.
Protections whose cost does not exceed the protected value are recorded as accepted risks.

requirements.title: Performance budget allocated to security functions
requirements.description: WS-X90 security functions on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) command path shall hold an allocated performance budget, and their measured cost shall be recorded against that budget at each release. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each security function on the two LRUs has an allocated performance budget.
Measured cost is recorded against the budget for the current release.
Functions exceeding their budget are listed with the disposition taken.

requirements.title: Maintenance interfaces reviewed for likely technician error
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session flow and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) support tooling shall be reviewed for the errors a technician is likely to make under field conditions, and each identified error shall have a design response recorded rather than a procedural warning alone. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A human factors review record exists for the maintenance session flow.
Each identified likely error carries a design response, not only a procedural note.
Technicians can describe the recovery path for the two most common errors.

requirements.title: Acceptability of security controls to technicians assessed
requirements.description: The WS-X90 program shall record whether the security constraints imposed by the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) workflows are acceptable to the technicians who use them, and shall identify controls being worked around in the field rather than inferring compliance from the absence of complaints. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An acceptability record exists covering both workflows.
Identified workarounds are listed with the control they avoid.
Each workaround has a disposition — control change, procedure change or accepted.

requirements.title: Provisioning executed from a repeatable numbered procedure
requirements.description: Provisioning of a WS-X90 LRU from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall be executed from a numbered procedure whose steps produce the same recorded outcome on repetition, and each run shall write a provisioning record to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) naming the procedure revision followed and the resulting configuration hash. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Two runs of the procedure on identical units produce identical configuration hashes.
Every provisioning record in LRU-020 names a procedure revision.
No procedure step is described as being at the technician's discretion.

requirements.title: Procedural rigour graded by the trust of the component touched
requirements.description: WS-X90 ground support procedures shall apply rigour proportionate to the trust of the component they touch: a procedure that writes to a high-trust component shall require two-person execution recorded from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), while a read-only diagnostic run from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall require single-person execution. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every ground support procedure states an execution rigour and the component trust level it derives from.
Two-person execution is recorded for each write to a high-trust component.
No read-only diagnostic is graded above single-person execution.

requirements.title: Measurement chain re-established before a modified image runs operationally
requirements.description: After applying a modification, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall re-establish and confirm the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) measurement chain before the modified image is permitted to run operationally, so that no window exists in which the platform runs a changed image in an unconfirmed protection state. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A modified image does not enter operational service before its measurement is recorded.
A modification whose measurement does not confirm is rolled back rather than left running.
The confirmation is recorded with the image identifier and the measurement value.

requirements.title: Design documentation sufficient to locate enforcement without source access
requirements.description: The WS-X90 design documentation held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall let an independent engineer determine, without access to source, which component enforces each security decision and the behaviour that component exhibits on denial, beginning with the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session controls. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each security decision in the control narratives resolves to a named enforcing component in the documentation.
Each documented decision states the denial behaviour.
An independent reviewer completes the LRU-014 session control trace without source access.

requirements.title: Documented control set and ongoing monitoring for external services
requirements.description: Each external service WS-X90 depends on — the archive receiving exports from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and the release signing service populating the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) — shall operate under a documented control set with named oversight roles on both sides, and its compliance shall be re-checked at least quarterly by a defined method rather than asserted at onboarding. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each external service has a documented control set and a named Aurora oversight role.
A compliance re-check dated within the last quarter exists for each service.
Services with no defined monitoring method are listed with the action opened against them.

requirements.title: Risk assessment and recorded approval before a security service is connected
requirements.description: Before any external security service is connected to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) export path or the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) intake, a risk assessment shall be recorded and the acquisition approved by a named program security authority, and the connection shall not be enabled without both. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each connected external security service resolves to a dated risk assessment.
Each acquisition carries an approval naming the approving authority.
The Platform Lead can describe the gate that prevents connection without both.

requirements.title: External provider service declarations enforced on the wired boundary
requirements.description: Providers of all external information systems and services used by WS-X90 shall declare the functions, ports, protocols and services their service requires, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) rule set — including the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) export destination — shall be generated from those declarations so that no external flow absent from a declaration is permitted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every external flow permitted by the deployed LRU-007 rule set appears in a current provider declaration.
The generated rule set and the deployed rule set reconcile with no difference.
A declaration withdrawn by a provider removes the corresponding permission at the next release.

requirements.title: Tactical link service declaration reconciled before deployment
requirements.description: The provider of the tactical data service reached through the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall declare, for all external information systems and services in the mission network, the waveform services and message sets in use, and the declaration shall be reconciled against the radio's configured service list before each deployment with the reconciliation recorded. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A dated reconciliation record exists for each deployment of the current radio configuration.
Every configured waveform service appears in the provider declaration.
Services configured but not declared are removed or recorded as an approved deviation.

requirements.title: Documented trust conditions for external service providers
requirements.description: The trust relationship with each WS-X90 external service provider shall be documented with the specific security properties the program relies on — key custody for the service signing metadata into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), retention and access constraints for the archive receiving Security Log Collector (LRU-018) exports — and reviewed whenever either side changes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each provider relationship carries a signed trust statement naming the relied-upon properties.
Each statement names the event that triggers a review.
Properties relied on but not stated are listed as open contractual items.

requirements.title: Jurisdictional constraint on external processing and storage locations
requirements.description: The external archive receiving Security Log Collector (LRU-018) exports and the signing service populating the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall each state the facilities at which WS-X90 information is processed and stored, and the service agreement shall constrain those facilities to the permitted jurisdiction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each provider has stated its processing and storage facility locations.
Each service agreement carries a jurisdictional constraint clause.
A provider change of facility triggers a recorded re-approval.

requirements.title: Signed manifest verified before an image is staged
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 software and firmware component shall carry a detached signature and a manifest entry in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall refuse to stage any image whose signature does not verify against the current release key, recording the refusal with the image identifier. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every component in the current release has a manifest entry and a verifiable detached signature.
An image with an altered byte is refused at staging and the refusal is logged.
No staging path exists that skips signature verification.

requirements.title: Firmware integrity measured at every boot
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall verify and record a measurement of each firmware image at every boot, so that a modification made after staging and before execution is detected before the image is given control, and shall halt rather than pass control when a measurement does not verify. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A measurement record exists for every firmware image in the boot chain after a cold start.
An image altered after staging fails verification and control is not passed.
Measurement records are retained across the boot for later comparison.

requirements.title: Hardware identity read and compared against the accepted inventory at power-on
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall read a supplier-provisioned hardware identity from each WS-X90 LRU at power-on, anchored to the platform measurement produced by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002), and shall raise a fault within one power-on cycle for any LRU whose identity is absent, unreadable or not matched to the accepted inventory. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A substituted LRU fitted with the identity part raises a fault within one power-on cycle.
LRUs whose suppliers do not fit an identity part are listed by id with the fallback in use.
An identity match on an unmeasured platform is not accepted as valid.

requirements.title: Security disposition required before a change is approved for build
requirements.description: Every change request raised against a WS-X90 configuration item in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall carry a recorded security disposition from a named System Security Engineer before it is approved for build, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) inventory shall reflect only changes carrying one. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No change request reaches approved-for-build without a named security disposition.
Each disposition names the engineer and the date it was given.
Inventory entries diverging from the approved change set are reported.

requirements.title: Static analysis on the exact built revision with dispositioned high-severity findings
requirements.description: Mission and platform software entering the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), including the Mission Computer (LRU-001) mission software, shall have passed a static analysis run citing the same source revision hash as the built image, with every high-severity finding either fixed or carrying a recorded engineering disposition naming the reviewer, before the build is released. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis run recorded for the current release cites the same revision hash as the built image.
No high-severity finding is open and undispositioned at release.
A submission citing a mismatched revision hash is rejected by the pipeline.

requirements.title: Reviewed threat model per external and payload interface
requirements.description: A reviewed threat model shall exist for each WS-X90 external and payload interface — Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) — stating the assumed adversary access, the mediating component and a disposition for each identified attack path, and shall be re-run when the interface changes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A threat model exists for each of the three interfaces and names the assumed adversary access.
Every identified attack path carries a disposition agreed outside the design team.
A change to an interface produces a dated model revision.

requirements.title: Build toolchain pinned and builds reproducible from the recorded tool set
requirements.description: The WS-X90 build toolchain shall be pinned by version and configuration in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) so that a release is reproducible from the recorded tool set, a toolchain change shall be processed as a controlled change with its own impact statement, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to run a build whose record cites no pinned toolchain. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A rebuild from the recorded tool set reproduces the released image for mission software.
Every toolchain change in the last release cycle carries a controlled change record.
Builds produced on an unpinned toolchain are listed by LRU with the contractual action against them.

requirements.title: Criticality analysis recorded at each design review decision point
requirements.description: A criticality analysis shall be recorded at each WS-X90 design review decision point ranking components by the consequence of their failure or subversion, and shall place the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011), Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) in the highest tier with the protection measures attaching to that tier named explicitly. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A criticality analysis exists for the most recent design review decision point.
The three named LRUs appear in the highest tier with named protection measures.
Each tier states the consequence basis for placement rather than only a rank.

requirements.title: Release candidates scanned against their declared component inventory
requirements.description: Each WS-X90 release candidate shall be scanned for known vulnerabilities against the component inventory declared with the release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the scan output, an exploitation assessment made in the WS-X90 configuration and the proposed mitigations shall be delivered to the Product Security Engineer and exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) before the release is approved. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A scan result exists for the current release candidate covering every declared inventory item.
Each finding carries an exploitation assessment made against the WS-X90 configuration.
The release approval record cites the scan output by identifier.

requirements.title: Supplier-delivered training as a precondition for maintenance credentials
requirements.description: Suppliers of the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the WS-X90 ground support tooling shall deliver hands-on training covering the security functions their products expose and the behaviour on failure, and recorded completion shall be a precondition for issuing a maintenance credential usable from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) or Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Supplier training material exists covering the security functions and their failure behaviour.
No active maintenance credential is held by a technician without a recorded completion.
A technician can describe the failure behaviour of the session controls they use.

requirements.title: Design specification shows control allocation and how mediation points compose
requirements.description: The WS-X90 design specification shall show the allocation of every tailored control to a physical or logical component and shall describe how the mediation points on the Mission Computer (LRU-001), Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) combine into one protection story, including the behaviour at the seam between mission computing and the payload interface. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every tailored control resolves to at least one allocated component in the specification.
The specification describes the interaction between the three named mediation points, not only each in isolation.
Sections not yet written to that depth are listed with an owner and a target review.

requirements.title: Access authorization verified before signing authority is issued and on role change
requirements.description: Personnel holding commit or signing authority over WS-X90 mission software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) or Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) firmware shall hold the access authorization the program requires for that role, verified before the authority is issued and re-verified whenever the role changes, with the authority withdrawn if verification lapses. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every active signing identity resolves to a current verified authorization.
A role change produces a re-verification record before the authority continues.
A lapsed verification results in a withdrawn authority within the stated interval.

requirements.title: Vendor support end dates held for every inventory item with a 12-month replacement trigger
requirements.description: The WS-X90 component inventory held by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall carry a vendor support end date for every hardware and software item including the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and Timing Receiver (LRU-005), and any item within 12 months of that date shall appear on the replacement or alternative-support list before support lapses. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every inventory item carries a vendor support end date or is listed as an outstanding supplier request.
Items within 12 months of their end date appear on the replacement or alternative-support list.
No component is in operational use past its support end date without a recorded alternative-support arrangement.

requirements.title: Annual review of the SC policy and procedure baseline
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the current WS-X90 system and communications protection policy and its implementing procedures as a signed baseline object with a named owner, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to build a provisioning package that references a policy baseline issued more than 12 months earlier. Aurora Defense Systems reissues both documents at least annually, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value carried for SC-1. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The signed policy baseline object in LRU-020 carries an issue date within the last 12 months and a named owner.
LRU-017 blocks a provisioning build that references a stale policy baseline, and the block is recorded against the release request.
The superseded revision immediately before the current one is still retrievable from LRU-020.

requirements.title: Mission partitions cannot reach platform management endpoints
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall run mission application partitions and the platform management agent in separate memory-protected partitions with no shared writable region, and no management service endpoint offered by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall be reachable from a mission application partition; a call attempted from a mission partition shall be rejected within 50 ms and shall increment a partition-violation counter. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A harness call from a mission partition to any LRU-013 management endpoint is rejected and produces no management-plane response.
The partition-violation counter on LRU-001 increments exactly once per rejected call.
The LRU-001 partition table in the approved build shows no writable region shared between a mission partition and the management partition.

requirements.title: Security enforcement services isolated from mission workloads
requirements.description: Security enforcement services on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall execute in a dedicated partition with its own scheduling budget and no shared writable memory with non-security functions, the partition configuration shall be measured and locked by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) before mission code starts, and all key use shall be delegated to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) across a single mediated interface. Shared last-level cache between the security partition and mission workloads is not yet partitioned. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-001 build manifest shows the security partition with a distinct budget and no writable region shared with any mission partition.
Every key operation observed on the mediated interface resolves to LRU-003 and none is performed inside a mission partition.
The unpartitioned last-level cache is recorded as an open gap in the isolation analysis with a remediation owner.

requirements.title: Shared buffers and storage blocks are cleared before reuse
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall overwrite every shared memory buffer and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall overwrite every released storage block with the approved fill pattern on the release path, before the resource can be reallocated to another partition or another mission, so that a read of a freshly allocated resource returns zero bytes of prior content. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A read of a newly allocated LRU-001 shared buffer returns only the fill pattern across its full extent.
A block released and re-issued by LRU-015 shows no residue of the previous object in a byte-level comparison.
Sanitisation is observed on the release path, so a consumer that reads immediately after allocation cannot race it.

requirements.title: Ingress rate limiting and storm control at the platform boundary
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall rate-limit ingress on each external interface to the value in the approved traffic profile and shed the excess without dropping an established mission session, and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall apply per-port broadcast and multicast storm control at the same profile values. Consistent with the moderate availability categorization WS-X90 limits rather than eliminates flooding effects; no redundant ingress path is fielded and none is claimed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress offered at twice the profiled rate is shed at LRU-007 while an established mission session stays up at its committed rate.
LRU-009 storm control engages at the profiled threshold on the port under test and the drop counter increments.
The rate and threshold values in the running configuration match the approved traffic profile.

requirements.title: Egress capping so the platform cannot flood an external system
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall cap egress toward any single external destination at the profiled rate and shall drop egress that does not match an approved flow, so a compromised on-platform process cannot use the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) to generate a flood against an external system. The cap is enforced per destination but is not aggregated across destinations, so a low-rate pattern spread across many destinations is not currently constrained. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Egress generated above the profiled per-destination rate is dropped at LRU-007 and the drop counter attributes it to the originating partition.
Egress that does not match an approved flow is dropped regardless of its rate.
The absence of an aggregate cross-destination egress cap is recorded as an open gap with a remediation owner.

requirements.title: Documented capacity headroom for internal transport and the radio
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall be provisioned with documented capacity and bandwidth headroom against the worst-case mission traffic profile, with the reserve figure recorded in the approved configuration baseline. WS-X90 is categorized moderate for availability and will manage headroom by provisioning rather than by adding redundant links. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A capacity analysis exists for LRU-009 and LRU-008 against the worst-case mission traffic profile.
The provisioned headroom figure for each appears in the approved configuration baseline.
The analysis states explicitly that no redundant transport is provided and that loss of a link degrades rather than fails over.

requirements.title: Boundary counters exported and alerted on connection-rate excursions
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall export interface utilisation, connection-rate and drop counters at least once every 60 seconds, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall raise exactly one alert when the connection-rate counter exceeds the profiled threshold for three consecutive intervals. Occupancy of the LRU-007 session table is not yet exported, so detection covers link-level indicators only. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Counters arrive at LRU-018 at the 60-second cadence with no sequence gap across a one-hour capture.
A synthetic connection-rate excursion held for three intervals raises exactly one alert, and a two-interval excursion raises none.
The missing session-table occupancy counter is recorded as an open gap against the LRU-007 telemetry set.

requirements.title: Exactly two external network connections, both on the gateway
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall present exactly two external network connections, both terminating on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007): the ground data link and the maintenance service port. No other LRU shall carry an interface reachable from outside the platform boundary in the fielded configuration, and enabling a third external connection shall require an approved configuration change. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-007 running configuration shows exactly two enabled external interfaces and no others.
An interface inventory across all 20 LRUs shows no second externally reachable termination.
Enabling an additional external interface is refused without an approved configuration change record.

requirements.title: Managed interface and traffic-flow policy per external service
requirements.description: Each external telecommunication service shall terminate on a managed interface of the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) with a named traffic-flow policy, and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall carry mission traffic only through that policy. Control-plane traffic arriving from external networks is filtered at LRU-007, but the outbound publication that would let a remote network detect unauthorized control-plane traffic originating from WS-X90 is not built. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every external service in the interface inventory maps to exactly one named traffic-flow policy on LRU-007.
LRU-008 has no path to an external network that bypasses the LRU-007 managed interface.
Inbound control-plane traffic is filtered and counted, and the missing outbound publication is recorded as an open gap.

requirements.title: Traffic-flow policy exceptions reviewed at least every 180 days
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold every approved exception to a WS-X90 traffic-flow policy with its mission justification, owner and expiry, each exception shall be reviewed at least every 180 days, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value carried for SC-7(4), and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to build a gateway configuration containing an exception past its review date. The 180-day review is run by hand today and is not enforced by LRU-017. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every exception object in LRU-020 carries a justification, a duration of need, an owner and a last-review date.
No exception in the current gateway baseline is past its 180-day review date.
The manual nature of the review and the not-yet-enforcing LRU-017 check are recorded together as one open gap.

requirements.title: Deny by default on every gateway and switch interface
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall carry a terminating deny rule on every interface so that traffic not matching an explicitly approved flow is dropped and counted, and the fielded rule sets shall contain no permit-any rule on any interface in either direction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each interface rule set on LRU-007 and LRU-009 ends in a deny that increments a per-interface counter.
A packet outside every approved flow is dropped and exactly one deny counter increments.
A rule-set review across both devices finds no permit-any rule on any interface in either direction.

requirements.title: No split tunnelling while a maintenance session is open
requirements.description: While a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) session is open to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), the gateway shall be the laptop's only active route and LRU-014 shall drop the session within 5 seconds of detecting a second active interface on the endpoint. Detection relies on the endpoint's own posture report; LRU-014 does not independently verify the endpoint routing table, so a tampered posture report would not be caught. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Bringing up a second interface on LRU-019 during an open session causes LRU-014 to drop the session within 5 seconds.
The drop is logged with the endpoint identity, the session identifier and the reason.
The dependence on a self-reported posture rather than independent verification is recorded as an open gap.

requirements.title: External-bound traffic routed through the authenticated proxy
requirements.description: All on-platform traffic destined for a network outside Aurora Defense Systems' control shall be routed through the authenticated proxy function of the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), and only flows explicitly exempted by the authorizing official may bypass it, each named in the running configuration with a reference to its decision record. Proxy authentication is enforced on the ground data link; the maintenance service port still permits an unproxied path used for firmware retrieval. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A direct connection attempt to an external address from any on-platform LRU is refused unless it matches a named exemption.
Each named exemption in the LRU-007 configuration carries a reference to an authorizing-official decision record.
The unproxied maintenance-port firmware retrieval path is recorded as an open gap with a remediation owner.

requirements.title: Threatening outbound traffic dropped and attributed to its origin
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall drop outbound traffic matching a threat signature in the approved egress rule set and shall emit a record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 seconds naming the originating LRU and partition. The record does not yet name the operator identity behind a maintenance session, so denied traffic originating from maintenance activity cannot always be attributed to an individual. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Outbound traffic matching an egress threat rule is dropped at LRU-007 and counted.
A denial record reaches LRU-018 within 60 seconds naming the originating LRU and partition.
The absent operator identity for maintenance-originated denials is recorded as an open gap.

requirements.title: Export restricted to approved data types and cryptographically wrapped
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall block egress of any object that is not one of the approved mission data types and shall require every permitted export to be wrapped by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) under the mission key in force. Exfiltration testing has been run once against the ground data link; a repeating test cadence and coverage of the maintenance service port are not in place. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An object of an unapproved type offered for export is blocked at LRU-007 and counted.
Every permitted export carries an LRU-003 wrap naming the in-force mission key identifier.
The completed single exfiltration test is recorded and the missing test cadence and maintenance-port coverage are an open gap.

requirements.title: Inbound traffic restricted to approved source and destination pairs
