requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall accept inbound traffic only from the ground control addresses named in the approved source list and shall forward it only to the destination LRUs named for that source, and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall enforce the same source-to-destination pairing on the internal segment so a permitted source cannot reach an LRU outside its set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Inbound traffic from an address outside the approved source list is dropped at LRU-007 and counted.
Traffic from an approved source addressed to an LRU outside its permitted destination set is dropped at LRU-009.
The source and destination pair lists in both running configurations match the approved baseline exactly.

requirements.title: Host-based boundary filters on every component able to run one
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 component able to host it shall run a host-based boundary filter in the approved baseline - the Mission Computer (LRU-001), the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) - and every LRU without one shall be listed with the reason. The filter is enforcing on LRU-001 and LRU-017; on LRU-019 the ruleset is present but left in log-only mode, so it observes rather than blocks. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved baselines for LRU-001 and LRU-017 show the host filter present and in enforcing mode.
The LRU-019 baseline shows the ruleset present with its mode recorded as log-only and a date for the enforcing switch.
Every LRU that carries no host filter appears in the exemption list with the reason it cannot host one.

requirements.title: Security tooling reachable only through a managed management interface
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall sit on a management segment separated from mission traffic by the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and shall be reachable only through a managed interface carrying an explicit rule set. The separation is a VLAN on shared switch hardware rather than a physically separate subnetwork, so the fielded implementation is short of the isolation the enhancement describes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-009 configuration shows the management VLAN and the explicit rule set on its managed interface.
No mission-segment host can reach an LRU-018 service except through the managed interface.
The physical-separation shortfall is recorded with either an accepted-risk decision or a remediation owner.

requirements.title: Physical port protection on boundary-crossing interfaces
requirements.description: Every managed interface that crosses the WS-X90 boundary or reaches an external network - the two Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) external terminations and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) service connector - shall be fitted with a keyed physical port lock recorded in the platform inventory, and unused Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) ports shall be physically blanked. The LRU-014 connector carries a lock but no tamper-evident seal, so an unauthorized connection there leaves no physical trace. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each LRU-007 external termination and the LRU-014 connector carries a keyed lock recorded against a key holder in the platform inventory.
Unused LRU-009 ports are blanked and the blanking is recorded per port.
The missing LRU-014 tamper-evident seal appears on the open action list with an owner and a target.

requirements.title: All privileged network access through the maintenance gateway
requirements.description: All networked privileged access to WS-X90 shall traverse the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014); the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall accept a privileged session only when it arrives on the LRU-014 interface, and each accepted session shall carry the operator identity, the LRU-014 session identifier and a record of every command issued in that session. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A privileged session offered to LRU-013 on any interface other than the LRU-014 path is refused and counted.
Each accepted privileged session carries an operator identity and an LRU-014 session identifier in the LRU-013 record.
The command record for a completed session lists every command issued, in order, with its result.

requirements.title: Boundary device fails closed within two seconds
requirements.description: On failure of any packet-forwarding or policy-evaluation function, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall stop forwarding within 2 seconds and shall hold the boundary closed until an operator explicitly restores it, including across a power cycle; no detected failure path shall reach a permissive forwarding mode. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An induced policy-engine failure stops forwarding within 2 seconds, measured at the external interface.
The boundary remains closed after a power cycle and reopens only on an explicit operator restore.
The LRU-007 failure-mode analysis shows no detected failure path that reaches a permissive forwarding mode.

requirements.title: Payload command function isolated on its own segment
requirements.description: The payload command function shall be isolated from all other WS-X90 functions: the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall carry payload command traffic on a dedicated segment reaching only the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011), and no mission or management host shall hold a route onto that segment. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A route trace from every non-payload LRU shows no path onto the payload command segment.
LRU-010 and LRU-011 accept payload command frames only on the dedicated segment interface and count discards elsewhere.
The payload segment definition in the LRU-009 running configuration matches the approved baseline exactly.

requirements.title: No external connection without an approved boundary protection device
requirements.description: No WS-X90 connection to a network outside the platform boundary shall be made without an approved boundary protection device in the path, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall remain the only permitted termination. The device required for the planned unclassified ground segment connection has not been selected, and that interface stays disabled in the baseline until it is fielded and accredited. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-007 baseline shows the unclassified ground segment interface disabled and its state measured at boot.
A device selection decision with a named approval owner is recorded before the interface can be enabled.
No alternative direct path to an external network exists on any other LRU.

requirements.title: No direct connection from any component to a public network
requirements.description: No WS-X90 system component shall have a direct connection to a public network. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall terminate only the approved government network paths and hold no default route toward a public network, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall operate disconnected from any routable public network, taking updates only from removable media checked into the Configuration Repository. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-007 route table contains no default route and no destination outside the approved external address set.
LRU-017 has no enabled interface to a routable public network in the approved baseline.
The provisioning transfer procedure names enrolled removable media as the only ingress path to LRU-017.

requirements.title: Critical functions on logically separate subnets
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall place mission compute, platform management, payload command and log export on four logically separate subnets, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall reject any arming frame that did not arrive on the payload command subnet. Log export and platform management currently share one subnet, so three of the four intended separations are in place. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An arming frame injected on any subnet other than payload command is rejected by LRU-011 and counted.
The LRU-009 subnet map matches the approved segmentation design for mission, payload command and the combined management segment.
The unsplit management and log-export subnet is recorded as an open gap with a target configuration change.

requirements.title: Transmitted mission data encrypted and integrity-protected end to end
requirements.description: All WS-X90 traffic leaving the platform shall be encrypted and integrity-protected by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) before it reaches the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) or the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), which is what CNSSI 1253 asks of this enhancement for national security systems: prevent unauthorized disclosure and detect changes. A capture on either external path shall yield no plaintext mission field, and a modified frame shall be rejected at the receiver rather than processed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A capture on the ground data link and on the radio path contains no plaintext mission field.
A frame with a single flipped bit is rejected at the receiver and counted as an integrity failure rather than parsed.
LRU-007 and LRU-008 both refuse to transmit a frame that has not been wrapped by LRU-003.

requirements.title: Protected staging of mission data before and after transmission
requirements.description: The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall preserve both the confidentiality and the integrity of mission data while it is staged for sending and while it is being received - the property pair CNSSI 1253 carries for SC-8(2) - by holding it in a staging region readable only through the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) interface and overwriting that region with the approved fill pattern before reuse. Overwrite is implemented on the transmit path; on the receive path the buffer is reused without an explicit overwrite, leaving a residue window. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A transmit staging buffer read after release contains only the approved fill pattern.
No process other than the LRU-003 crypto interface can map or read the staging region.
The receive-path residue window is recorded as an open gap with a fix identified in the LRU-008 firmware plan.

requirements.title: Maintenance sessions disconnected after 15 minutes of inactivity
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall tear down a maintenance network session when the operator ends it and after no more than 15 minutes of inactivity, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value carried for SC-10, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall tear down the associated transport state so the session cannot be resumed without a new authentication. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A maintenance session idle for 15 minutes is terminated by LRU-014 and the termination is logged with the reason.
The LRU-007 transport state for that session is absent after the termination.
Resuming from the client side requires a fresh authentication rather than a transport reconnect.

requirements.title: Collaborative computing peripherals not controlled on support endpoints
requirements.description: No collaborative computing device or application is fielded on any WS-X90 LRU, but no mechanism prevents one being enabled on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) or the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and neither endpoint gives a physically present user an indication that an attached camera or microphone is in use. WS-X90 makes no claim of coverage for this control until a peripheral decision is recorded. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A peripheral inventory for LRU-017 and LRU-019 records whether a camera or microphone is present and enabled.
A decision is recorded on whether to disable the peripherals in the baseline or tailor the control out of the profile.
No use-indication mechanism is claimed in any WS-X90 baseline until one is built.

requirements.title: Source and integrity attributes on navigation messages
requirements.description: Every navigation message the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) forwards to the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall carry a source and integrity attribute in its header, and LRU-004 shall refuse to use a message whose attribute set is absent or carries an unrecognised value rather than defaulting it. The attribute is carried on the internal navigation bus but is not preserved when navigation state is exported to the mission computer, so it does not survive the whole path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A navigation message presented with no attribute set is refused by LRU-004 and counted.
A message carrying an unrecognised attribute value is refused rather than treated as a default.
The loss of the attribute on export to the mission computer is recorded as an open gap.

requirements.title: Authorization-state attributes on payload command and telemetry frames
requirements.description: Payload command frames issued by the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and health frames returned by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall each carry an authorization-state attribute identifying the command authority in force, and LRU-010 shall discard a telemetry frame whose attribute does not match the authority it issued under. Attribute carriage works in both directions, but the attribute is not included in the record LRU-012 writes to platform telemetry storage. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A telemetry frame carrying a mismatched authority attribute is discarded by LRU-010 and counted.
Every command frame captured on the payload segment carries a populated authorization-state attribute.
The missing attribute in stored telemetry records is recorded as an open gap against the LRU-012 record format.

requirements.title: Keyed integrity check over transmitted attribute blocks
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall verify a keyed integrity check over the attribute block of every received message before the attribute is used in an authorization or admission decision, and shall treat a failed check as an absent attribute. Attribute carriage exists today but no keyed check is computed over it, so a modified attribute block is currently accepted at face value. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design record names the keyed check algorithm, the covered extent and the interface that computes it.
A message with a corrupted attribute block is treated as unattributed rather than trusted once the check is fielded.
The firmware drop carrying the check is identified in the plan with a target date.

requirements.title: Anti-spoofing binding for claimed navigation integrity results
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall detect and reject navigation inputs whose attributes claim an integrity check that the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) did not perform, by binding the claim to a per-boot value that only LRU-006 can produce. No such binding is implemented today, so a forged attribute claiming a passed check would be accepted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design names the per-boot value, where it is held on LRU-006 and how LRU-004 learns it.
An attribute replayed from a previous boot is rejected once the binding is fielded.
The current acceptance of forged integrity claims is recorded as an open risk with an owner.

requirements.title: Cryptographic binding of attributes to the message body
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall bind the attribute block of a navigation or payload message to the message body with a signature computed over both, and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall reject a message whose binding does not verify, so an attribute cannot be lifted from one message and attached to another. The binding is designed but not fielded; attributes currently travel alongside the body with no cryptographic tie. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The binding design names the signed extent and the key held in LRU-003 for it.
A message assembled from one body and another message's attribute block fails verification once fielded.
A key-use rate analysis confirms LRU-003 can meet the per-message rate in the worst-case mission profile.

requirements.title: Platform certificates from the approved PKI with a closed trust store
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall obtain every platform certificate from the approved government public key infrastructure under the certificate policy named in the program agreement, and the trust store held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall contain only the approved root anchors, with the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holding the authoritative anchor list and its signed change history. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-003 trust store contents match the approved anchor list in LRU-020 exactly, with no additional anchor.
Every fielded platform certificate chains to an approved anchor and names the program certificate policy.
Each anchor change in the LRU-020 history carries a signed approval record with an owner.

requirements.title: Acceptable interpreted-code technologies named and enforced at build
requirements.description: The WS-X90 software baseline shall name which interpreted and dynamically loaded code technologies are acceptable on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and the build process shall reject a load module containing a technology outside that list. The list exists with a named owner and the build check is enforced for both endpoints, the LRU-017 tooling pipeline having been brought under it on 2026-11-03. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline contains a dated acceptable and unacceptable technology list with a named owner.
An LRU-001 load module containing a listed unacceptable technology fails the build and the failure names the technology.
Tooling built for LRU-017 fails its build on a listed unacceptable technology in the same way an LRU-001 load module does.

requirements.title: Unacceptable code identified in release packages and escalated
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall flag any release package whose manifest names a technology on the unacceptable list, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to provision a flagged package and shall raise it to the software configuration control board with an owner. Flagging works on manifests only; a package whose content differs from its manifest is not detected. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A package whose manifest names an unacceptable technology is flagged in LRU-020 and refused by LRU-017.
Each refusal produces a software configuration control board item with a named owner.
The manifest-only scope of the check is recorded as an open gap with content inspection identified as the fix.

requirements.title: Mobile code category recorded and handling rules met before release
requirements.description: Every load module accepted into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall record which mobile code category its embedded interpreted content falls into, using the category scheme CNSSI 1253 carries for this enhancement, and shall show that the category's handling rules were met before the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) may release it. The category field is not part of the acceptance record today; acquisition and development artifacts are reviewed for it by hand. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-020 acceptance record schema gains a category field with a defined allowed value set.
A package with no category recorded cannot be released by LRU-017 once the field is enforced.
The interim manual review is documented with the reviewer role and the artifacts it covers.

requirements.title: No run-time code fetch on the mission computer, signed packages only
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall execute only signed load modules from the approved baseline and shall refuse to fetch or execute code delivered over any interface at run time, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall block download of a package that fails signature verification, since unsigned code and code obtained from an untrusted source are the categories CNSSI 1253 marks unacceptable for SC-18(3). Run-time fetch is blocked on LRU-001; LRU-017 blocks unsigned packages by default but retains an operator override that is only recorded after the fact. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An attempt to load code over any LRU-001 interface at run time is refused and counted.
An unsigned package offered to LRU-017 is blocked by default without operator action.
Each LRU-017 operator override is recorded with the operator and package identity, and removal of the override path appears in the plan.

requirements.title: Automatic execution of embedded document code blocked on support endpoints
requirements.description: The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall block automatic execution of code embedded in documents, spreadsheets and mail attachments, which is the application scope CNSSI 1253 carries for this enhancement; such a file shall open with the embedded construct disabled and shall require an explicit operator action, logged with the file and operator identity, before any embedded code runs. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A test document containing an auto-execute construct opens on both endpoints with the construct disabled.
Enabling the construct requires an explicit operator action and produces a log record naming the file, the construct and the operator.
The blocking policy is present in the approved baseline for both endpoints and cannot be changed by a local operator.

requirements.title: Signed responses from the internal authoritative name service
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall serve the internal WS-X90 name space as its authoritative source and shall return origin-authentication and integrity artifacts with every response, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall discard an internal name response that carries no artifact. The authoritative service exists but signs nothing today; the artifact format and the key holder are still to be selected. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A design record names the artifact format and the key holder for internal name response signing.
The internal name zone content is under configuration control before signing is enabled.
LRU-007 is configured to discard unsigned internal responses at the point signing goes live.

requirements.title: Resolution confined to the internal authoritative service
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall resolve names only through the resolver on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), and that resolver shall accept a resolution response only from the internal authoritative service and shall never recurse to an external resolver. Origin authentication of responses is not verified today, so the resolver relies on path restriction rather than on a checked signature. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: LRU-001 has no configured resolver other than the LRU-007 address and no fallback resolver entry.
A resolution response arriving from any source other than the internal authoritative service is discarded and counted.
The absence of response signature verification is recorded as an open gap tied to the authoritative-signing work.

requirements.title: Role separation between authoritative and resolver name instances
requirements.description: WS-X90 name resolution shall run as two instances on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) reachable through separate Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) segments, with the authoritative role and the resolver role held by different instances. One instance runs today and holds both roles; consistent with the moderate availability categorization the second instance is for role separation, not for continuous failover, and loss of an instance degrades resolution rather than failing over transparently. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A design record shows the two instances and which role each holds, with their segment placement.
The resolver instance holds no authoritative zone and has no write path to the zone content.
The design states that loss of one instance degrades resolution rather than failing over transparently.

requirements.title: Session identifiers invalidated on every termination path
requirements.description: On operator logout, session timeout or link loss, the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall invalidate the session identifier immediately and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall reject any later message bearing it, so a captured identifier cannot be replayed after the session ends on any of the three termination paths. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A message replayed with a logged-out session identifier is rejected by LRU-013 and counted.
The identifier is invalidated on all three termination paths: operator logout, inactivity timeout and link loss.
No terminated session's identifier remains in the LRU-014 active table after termination.

requirements.title: System-generated session identifiers of at least 128 bits
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall accept only session identifiers it generated itself, each at least 128 bits drawn from the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) random source, and shall reject any identifier supplied by a client rather than adopting it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A client-supplied session identifier is rejected by LRU-014 rather than adopted or echoed.
Sampled identifiers are 128 bits or longer with no repeat across a 10,000-session sample.
The LRU-014 identifier generator draws from the LRU-003 random source and from no other source.

requirements.title: Protected sessions only against the allowed certificate authorities
requirements.description: A protected session shall be established only when the peer certificate chains to a certificate authority on the WS-X90 allowed-CA list held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), with the authoritative list under configuration control in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). Chain validation is enforced against the allowed roots, but intermediate authorities are accepted by chaining rather than by explicit listing, so the accepted set is wider than intended. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A session offered with a certificate that does not chain to an allowed root is refused by LRU-003 and counted.
The allowed-CA list in the fielded LRU-003 store matches the LRU-020 baseline exactly.
The acceptance of unlisted intermediate authorities is recorded as an open gap with pinning identified as the fix.

requirements.title: Mission computer halts to a defined secure state on integrity failure
requirements.description: On a detected integrity or execution failure the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall halt the Mission Computer (LRU-001) in the defined secure state within 5 seconds - external interfaces down, keys evicted, no partial mission function running - rather than continuing in a degraded mode, which is the known secure state CNSSI 1253 carries for this control. Coverage is complete for boot-time and watchdog failures; a failure detected inside a running mission partition still relies on that partition's own handler. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An induced boot integrity failure brings LRU-001 to the defined secure state within 5 seconds.
In the secure state no external interface is up and no key material remains loaded in LRU-001 memory.
The gap covering failures detected inside a running mission partition is recorded with a named owner.

requirements.title: Failure cause and last known good configuration preserved in failure
requirements.description: On entry to the secure failure state the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall write the failure cause, the last known good configuration identifier and the platform integrity state to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) before power-down, so the cause can be determined and the platform returned to service from a known configuration with least disruption. The record is written for boot and update failures; a failure during a recovery operation is not captured because LRU-016 is itself the failing element. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A record naming cause, last known good configuration identifier and integrity state is present in LRU-015 after an induced failure.
The record survives a power cycle and is readable through the maintenance procedure without a normal boot.
The uncovered recovery-time failure case is recorded as an open gap with a remediation owner.

requirements.title: All stored information encrypted and integrity-protected at rest
requirements.description: All WS-X90 information at rest - configuration baselines, audit records, key material and recovery images - shall be stored on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) encrypted and integrity-protected under keys held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), covering all components, media and information as CNSSI 1253 directs for this enhancement. A raw read of LRU-015 media outside the platform shall yield no plaintext and no usable object, and a modified stored block shall fail its integrity check on read. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A raw media image taken from LRU-015 contains no plaintext configuration, audit or key object.
A modified stored block fails its integrity check on read and is refused rather than returned.
The LRU-015 object inventory shows no stored object type exempt from encryption, including recovery images.

requirements.title: Cryptographic keys held only in the hardware key store
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 cryptographic key shall be held in the hardware-protected key store of the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and shall be usable only through the module's operation interface; no key shall be exportable in plaintext by any command available in the fielded configuration, including under maintenance authority. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every key in the platform key inventory resolves to an LRU-003 hardware key store slot.
No fielded LRU-003 command returns plaintext key material, including commands available under maintenance authority.
Other LRUs are observed using keys by handle through the operation interface with no key bytes crossing the interface.

requirements.title: Operations security review of released configuration and provisioning artifacts
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall apply an operations security review to WS-X90 configuration, release and provisioning artifacts before they leave program control, covering what the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) exposes in release metadata and what the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) prints or exports. The review exists as an intent in the program plan; no criteria, reviewer role or record have been defined. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A named role can describe the review trigger, the criteria applied and where the decision is recorded.
The set of artifact types in scope for the review is written down and agreed.
A first review is scheduled against a named release with a reviewer assigned.

requirements.title: Unused ports disabled in firmware on airborne components
requirements.description: Unused physical ports on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) - external storage, debug and console - shall be disabled in firmware in the fielded configuration, so connecting a device produces no enumeration and no log-in prompt. The LRU-013 debug port is disabled by a jumper rather than in firmware, so a physical action can re-enable it without a configuration change. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Connecting a storage device to a disabled LRU-001 port produces no enumeration event and no prompt.
The LRU-001 and LRU-013 firmware port settings match the approved port-state baseline and are covered by the boot measurement.
The jumper-controlled LRU-013 debug port is recorded as an open gap with a remediation owner and target.

requirements.title: Removable media and wireless interfaces closed on support endpoints
requirements.description: Removable-media and wireless interfaces on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall be disabled except for the single provisioning media port, which shall accept only media enrolled in the platform inventory. Wireless is physically removed on both endpoints; the media whitelist is enforced on LRU-017 but not yet on LRU-019, which accepts any media presented to it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No wireless interface is present or enabled on either endpoint, verified against the hardware inventory.
Unenrolled media inserted into LRU-017 is refused and the attempt is recorded with the media identity.
The missing LRU-019 media whitelist is on the open action list with an owner and a target date.

requirements.title: Single platform time reference held within 50 milliseconds
requirements.description: The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall distribute a single platform time reference, and every WS-X90 LRU that timestamps a record - starting with the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) - shall hold its clock within 50 milliseconds of that reference, so records produced by different LRUs can be ordered against one another. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Sampled clock offsets on LRU-001 and LRU-012 against the LRU-005 reference stay within 50 ms across a four-hour run.
Every LRU in the timestamping inventory is a client of the LRU-005 distribution with no local free-running clock in use.
Records collected from two different LRUs during the run order correctly against one another.

requirements.title: Clock compared to the authoritative source every 60 seconds
requirements.description: The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall compare its internal clock against the authoritative external time source at least once every 60 seconds and shall step or slew the platform reference when the difference exceeds 1 second, and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall mark navigation solutions produced while the receiver is in holdover. Comparison and correction work in the fielded build; the holdover marking is applied to the solution but is not propagated into the navigation output message. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Comparison records appear at no more than 60-second spacing across a one-hour capture with no gaps.
An injected 1.5-second offset is corrected and the correction is logged with before and after values.
The unpropagated holdover marking on the navigation output message is recorded as an open gap.

requirements.title: Audit timestamps carry the platform reference and its synchronisation state
requirements.description: Audit records written to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and forwarded to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall carry a timestamp taken from the platform reference and a flag showing whether the reference was synchronised or in holdover when the record was written. The timestamp is carried; the synchronisation flag is not in the record format, so a record written during holdover cannot be distinguished from one written while synchronised. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every sampled record in LRU-015 and LRU-018 carries a platform-reference timestamp rather than a local counter value.
Timestamps from two LRUs for one correlated event differ by no more than the 50 ms distribution tolerance.
The missing synchronisation flag is recorded as an open gap against the audit record format.

requirements.title: No alternate communications path for command and control
requirements.description: WS-X90 command and control runs over a single path today: the ground data link terminating on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and carried by the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008). No alternate communications path is established, and loss of that path suspends command and control until it is restored. Consistent with the moderate availability categorization no alternate path has been funded or designed, and none is claimed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The communications architecture record states that a single command and control path exists.
A decision is recorded on whether an alternate path is required for the mission profile at the moderate availability categorization.
No WS-X90 configuration or plan claims an alternate path until one is built.

requirements.title: SI policy and procedure set held under configuration control
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall hold the WS-X90 system and information integrity policy and its implementing procedures as a signed, version-controlled document set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), shall review and reissue both at least annually and after any change to the SI control allocation, and shall carry the approved policy version identifier in the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) release manifest before that image is issued to the field. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Configuration Repository holds a signed SI policy document whose approval date is within the last 12 months.
The procedure set names one accountable official and enumerates the SI controls it implements.
The Provisioning Workstation release manifest cites the same policy version identifier as the repository copy.

requirements.title: Quarterly automated software and firmware update status sweep
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall query every WS-X90 line replaceable unit for its installed software and firmware version at least quarterly, compare each reported version against the approved release manifest held by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), and record any component behind the manifest on a security-relevant update as a deviation in the platform inventory record without technician action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A quarterly sweep record exists carrying a version string and a comparison verdict for all 20 mapped LRUs.
A deliberately down-level component is reported as a deviation within one sweep cycle.
The deviation list is retrievable from the platform inventory export without connecting the Maintenance Laptop.

requirements.title: Flaw remediation interval measured against program benchmarks
requirements.description: For every security-relevant flaw raised against WS-X90, the program shall record the date the flaw was identified and the date the corrective build was accepted into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and shall publish the elapsed interval per severity band against the program remediation benchmark in the monthly Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) status export. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each flaw record carries both an identification date and a corrective-build acceptance date.
The monthly status export shows elapsed interval per severity band alongside the benchmark value.
Flaws exceeding their benchmark are listed separately with an owner.

requirements.title: Single signed patch bundle staged per maintenance visit
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall accept security patches only as a single signed bundle produced by the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) patch pipeline, so that a technician applies one authenticated bundle per maintenance visit rather than installing per-LRU packages by hand, and shall refuse any bundle whose component list is not fully covered by the pipeline build record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A bundle whose manifest omits one included component is refused with a recorded reason.
A complete signed bundle installs across all targeted LRUs from one technician action.
The applied bundle identifier appears in the platform inventory record after the visit.

requirements.title: Superseded firmware images erased after successful cutover
requirements.description: Once an update has been accepted and the platform has completed one successful mission-ready cycle on the new version, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall erase from the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) all upgraded or replaced software and firmware components that are no longer required for operation, retaining exactly one prior recovery image per LRU and leaving no other superseded image readable. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: After a cutover cycle, exactly one prior image per LRU remains in the Secure Storage Module inventory.
A read attempt against a superseded image slot returns no recoverable content.
The erase action is recorded with the component id and the retired version string.

requirements.title: Quarantined objects analysed and fed back into response and remediation
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall forward any file or firmware object quarantined by the platform malicious-code checks to the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) offline analysis enclave, and the resulting behaviour report shall be attached to the corresponding incident record and to the flaw-remediation item before that item is closed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead can walk through the transfer path from quarantine to the offline enclave for a named object class.
A closed flaw-remediation item that began as a quarantine event carries an attached analysis report.
The procedure states who may operate the enclave and how results re-enter the incident record.

requirements.title: Single merged intrusion detection view across platform sensors
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall be the single correlation point for intrusion detection output from the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and from the platform host sensors, presenting one merged detection view rather than per-sensor consoles, and shall mark any registered sensor that has not reported within 15 minutes as unavailable in that view. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every registered detection sensor appears in the merged view with a last-report timestamp.
A sensor silenced for 20 minutes is shown as unavailable without an operator query.
A detection raised at the gateway is visible in the merged view without opening a gateway console.

requirements.title: Near real-time analysis of received security events
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall apply its detection rule set to newly received platform security events within 60 seconds of receipt and shall raise a queue-depth alarm when unanalysed events exceed 5,000, so that analysis is continuous rather than dependent on a scheduled operator review. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Injected events are matched against the rule set within 60 seconds under nominal event rate.
A synthetic event burst that drives the backlog above 5,000 raises the queue-depth alarm.
The active rule-set version is displayed with the analysis view.

requirements.title: Continuous inbound and outbound traffic monitoring against flow policy
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall continuously monitor traffic entering and leaving the platform against the approved WS-X90 flow policy, and shall emit a security event for any flow whose source, destination, protocol or direction falls outside that policy, including flows that are correctly encrypted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Monitoring remains active with no configurable sampling interval or duty cycle on any of the three interfaces.
An injected out-of-policy flow produces a security event naming source, destination and direction.
An encrypted but out-of-policy flow is reported on the same basis as a cleartext one.

requirements.title: Operator alert on approved compromise indicators
requirements.description: When the platform detects an indicator on the approved WS-X90 compromise-indicator list — repeated authentication failure on a maintenance port, an unexpected boot measurement, or a flow policy violation — the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall raise an alert on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) operator panel within 60 seconds of detection and shall keep that alert visible until it is explicitly acknowledged. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each indicator on the approved list produces a panel alert within 60 seconds when injected.
An unacknowledged alert survives an operator panel refresh and a controller restart.
Acknowledgement is recorded with the acknowledging account and time.

requirements.title: Encrypted external sessions made visible to platform monitoring
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall terminate approved external sessions so that their decrypted content is presented to the platform monitoring path inside the gateway boundary, with session keys held only in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and no plaintext session content written to persistent storage on the gateway. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Content of an approved terminated session is matched by the monitoring rule set.
Session keys are not readable from gateway storage or a gateway memory capture.
No plaintext session content is present on gateway persistent storage after the session closes.

requirements.title: Outbound traffic profiled per mission phase for anomalies
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall profile outbound traffic volume, destination set and periodicity per declared mission phase, and shall raise an anomaly event when observed outbound volume exceeds the profiled envelope for the active phase by more than 25 percent over a rolling 5-minute window. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A stored profile exists for each declared mission phase on both external interfaces.
A synthetic 30 percent volume excursion raises an anomaly event within one rolling window.
A new destination not in the phase profile is reported even at nominal volume.

requirements.title: Automated alerts on privileged and configuration activity
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall raise an automated alert to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), with no operator query, for privileged account creation, security configuration change outside an approved maintenance window, and interruption of audit forwarding exceeding 5 minutes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three trigger classes produces an alert without an operator initiating a search.
An audit-forwarding stall of 6 minutes raises the interruption alert.
Alerts carry the triggering account or component identifier.

requirements.title: Emitter observation reporting from the tactical radio
requirements.description: The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall report emitter observations in its assigned bands to the platform monitoring path so that rogue or unexpected emitters operating inside the WS-X90 physical envelope can be identified, recording each detection with time, band and observed signal strength. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design record defines which bands are observed and the detection reporting interface.
The observation record format includes time, band and signal strength fields.
The monitoring path has an allocated ingest route for emitter observations.

requirements.title: Radio-to-wireline traffic inspected at the crossing point
requirements.description: Traffic crossing from the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) onto the wireline segment served by the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall pass an inspection point applying the same detection rule set used on the wireline side, so that no radio-originated flow reaches internal hosts uninspected. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An inspection point is defined on the radio-to-wireline path in the approved network design.
The rule set applied at that point is the same version as the wireline rule set.
No bypass route from the radio to an internal host exists in the approved topology.

requirements.title: Correlated monitoring timeline on a trusted time base
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall correlate platform host events, network detections and maintenance-session records into a single timeline stamped from the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) trusted time source, and shall flag any contributing source whose clock offset from that source exceeds 1 second. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Events from three different source classes appear on one ordered timeline.
A source skewed by 2 seconds is flagged in the correlation view.
The timeline records which time source stamped each correlated entry.

requirements.title: Enhanced session recording for elevated-risk maintainers
requirements.description: Where the program has designated a maintainer as posing elevated risk, the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall place that individual's sessions into an enhanced-recording mode capturing full command transcripts from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), and the Platform Lead shall be able to describe how the designation is applied, reviewed and withdrawn. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead can state who authorises a designation and on what evidence.
The procedure defines a review interval and a withdrawal path for the designation.
Enhanced-recording mode is described as a gateway setting, not a laptop setting.

requirements.title: Privileged maintenance sessions transcribed and separately retained
requirements.description: Every privileged session established through the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be recorded as a command-level transcript and forwarded to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which shall retain privileged-session transcripts separately from routine platform audit and alert on any privileged session opened outside an approved maintenance window. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A privileged session produces a transcript containing every command issued.
Transcripts are stored in a separate retention class from routine platform audit.
A session opened outside the approved window raises an alert naming the account.

requirements.title: Detection of network services outside the approved service baseline
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall compare observed listening services and open ports against the approved WS-X90 service baseline at least daily and shall both write an audit record and raise an alert for any service not on that baseline, including a service offered by an otherwise authorised LRU. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A daily comparison record exists naming the baseline version used.
An unauthorised listening service introduced on an authorised LRU is both audited and alerted.
Removing an approved service produces no alert.

requirements.title: Host-level monitoring sensors fixed in the signed baseline
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall each run a host-level sensor reporting process start, privileged operation and configuration-file change events to the platform monitoring path, and that sensor shall be a signed element of the approved baseline so that it cannot be disabled or removed from a maintenance session. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The signed baseline manifest lists the host sensor for both LRUs.
The sensor service cannot be stopped from an authenticated maintenance session.
The three declared event classes are present in an exported sensor sample.

requirements.title: Indicators of compromise distributed as a versioned set
requirements.description: Indicators of compromise received from the program's approved threat sources shall be held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as a versioned, signed indicator set and distributed into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) detection rules, with the active indicator-set version shown in the monitoring view. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The repository holds indicator sets with a version identifier and a source attribution.
The monitoring view displays the indicator-set version currently loaded.
The distribution path from repository to collector is documented and signed end to end.

requirements.title: Traffic visibility at external and key internal interfaces
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall provide mirrored visibility of internal segment traffic to the platform monitoring path at the two segment boundaries carrying mission and maintenance traffic, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall do the same at the external interface, so that monitoring coverage does not depend on host cooperation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror configuration exists at both named internal boundaries and at the external interface.
The monitoring path receives traffic from a host with no local sensor installed.
Mirror destinations are restricted to the monitoring path in the switch configuration export.

requirements.title: Security advisories published as machine-readable records
requirements.description: Security alerts and advisories accepted by the program shall be published as machine-readable advisory records in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and pushed to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) advisory view, so that engineering and maintenance staff receive them without a manual mail distribution step. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Advisory records carry an identifier, an affected-component list and an action class.
The advisory view shows the newest advisory without an operator import.
Advisories affecting a fielded baseline are linked to the corresponding flaw-remediation item.

requirements.title: Security function self-test on the mission computing chain
requirements.description: At power-on, at transition into mission-ready state, and on privileged command, the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall self-test its security enforcement functions — access decision, audit record generation, and cryptographic service availability from the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) — taking the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) reported platform state as a precondition, and shall alert the system/security administrator at a minimum on any failed test. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: All three self-test triggers are demonstrable and produce a recorded result set.
A forced cryptographic service failure produces an alert to the system/security administrator.
A self-test failure prevents transition to mission-ready state.

requirements.title: Payload interlock verification before each arming sequence
requirements.description: The Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall verify its authorization and state-interlock logic before each payload arming sequence and report the verification result through the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012); a failed verification shall hold the interlock in the safe state and alert the system/security administrator at a minimum, rather than restarting the payload interface. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every arming sequence is preceded by a recorded interlock verification result.
An induced interlock logic fault holds the safe state and does not arm.
The failure alert reaches the system/security administrator through the telemetry path.

requirements.title: Verification results reported to responsible security personnel
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall compile platform security function verification results into a periodic report exported through the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) to responsible security personnel (e.g., AO, CISO/SAISO or equivalent, ISSO, ISSM), including every failed verification and the action taken on it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A named recipient in each listed role can describe when they last received the report.
The report includes failed verifications and the disposition of each.
The distribution list is held with the report definition, not in an individual's mailbox rules.

requirements.title: Boot-time integrity check of the mission software set
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall measure the Mission Computer (LRU-001) boot loader, kernel and signed application set at every startup, compare each measurement against the value recorded in the approved release manifest, and refuse to release the platform to mission-ready state on any mismatch. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every startup produces a complete measurement set covering loader, kernel and application set.
A modified application binary blocks transition to mission-ready state.
The mismatching measurement slot is named in the resulting record.

requirements.title: Periodic integrity re-verification of navigation and timing software
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall re-verify the integrity of their loaded navigation and timing software against stored reference digests at startup and at least once every 24 hours of continuous operation, and shall report any verification failure to the platform monitoring path within 60 seconds. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A re-verification record exists at startup and at no more than 24-hour intervals thereafter.
An altered reference image produces a monitoring-path report within 60 seconds.
Re-verification does not interrupt navigation output on a passing check.

requirements.title: Automated notification on integrity verification discrepancy
requirements.description: On any integrity verification discrepancy, the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall emit a discrete integrity-violation event naming the failing measurement slot, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall notify the on-call security engineer automatically within 5 minutes, with no operator poll. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An induced discrepancy produces an event naming the failing measurement slot.
Notification reaches the on-call route within 5 minutes with no operator action.
The notification is retained even when the platform is subsequently restarted.

requirements.title: Restricted state and controlled recovery after an integrity violation
requirements.description: When the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) detects an integrity violation in the mission software set, the platform shall automatically hold in a restricted state permitting only maintenance and recovery functions, and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall make the last known-good signed image available for controlled, technician-authorised recovery rather than reimaging automatically. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An induced integrity violation places the platform in the restricted state without operator action.
Mission functions are unavailable while the restricted state is held.
Recovery from the last known-good image requires an authenticated technician action.

requirements.title: Integrity detections routed into the incident response path
requirements.description: Unauthorized change detections — unexpected boot measurements, configuration drift from the signed baseline, and the appearance of an unapproved service — shall be raised by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) as incident-class events and opened as incident records by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) workflow, so that integrity detections enter the same response path as reported incidents. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The responder can name the three detection classes that open an incident automatically.
An example incident record traceable to a boot-measurement detection exists.
The response procedure states the handoff between monitoring and incident handling.

requirements.title: Audit record for every potential integrity violation
requirements.description: Every potential integrity violation shall produce an audit record written to the write-protected region of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), carrying the failing component, the expected and observed measurement identifiers, and the action taken. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An induced violation produces a record in the write-protected region carrying all four fields.
The record cannot be modified or deleted from a maintenance session.
The exported copy at the collector matches the on-platform record.

requirements.title: Measured boot chain from an immutable root of trust
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall verify the boot process of the Mission Computer (LRU-001) from an immutable root of trust through each stage of the boot chain, extending one measurement per stage and making the resulting platform state available for attestation; this applies to all devices capable of verification of the boot process within the mission computing subsystem. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each boot stage extends a distinct measurement that is readable after boot.
A substituted stage image changes the reported platform state.
The root of trust cannot be updated through the normal maintenance path.

requirements.title: Boot image verification on navigation and payload controllers
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004), the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) — as all devices capable of verification of the boot process outside mission computing — shall verify their own boot images against a stored signature before enabling their external interfaces, and shall report boot verification status to the platform monitoring path at each start. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three LRUs reports a boot verification status at every start.
A corrupted boot image leaves the LRU external interface disabled.
Verification completes before the first sensor or payload message is accepted.

requirements.title: Boot firmware held write-protected outside authenticated update
requirements.description: Boot firmware on all capable devices shall be held in a write-protected region that the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) re-opens only under an authenticated update sequence staged by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), and any write attempt outside that sequence shall be blocked and logged. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A write to boot firmware outside the authenticated sequence is refused and logged.
The write-protect state is readable as part of the platform state report.
The protection re-asserts automatically at the end of an authenticated update.

requirements.title: Vendor code signature verified before installation
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall verify the vendor signature of all software and firmware from vendors or sources that provide cryptographic mechanisms to enable the validation of code authenticity and integrity, using keys held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and release metadata drawn from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and shall refuse installation where the signature is absent or fails. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unsigned package is refused installation with a recorded reason.
A package signed by a key not in the approved set is refused.
Verification keys are used from the Cryptographic Services Module and are not exportable.

requirements.title: Runtime self-protection for mission applications
requirements.description: Mission applications hosted on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall run with runtime protections that detect control-flow and memory-corruption attempts within the application process, terminate the affected process, and raise a security event rather than continuing execution. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design record names the runtime protection mechanisms selected for each mission application.
The build configuration enabling those protections is under configuration control.
A security event class for runtime protection triggers is defined in the monitoring rule set.

requirements.title: Content screening at platform entry and exit points
requirements.description: Message and file content entering or leaving WS-X90 through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), or transferred through the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), shall be screened against the approved content policy at that entry or exit point, with unsolicited or non-conforming content rejected and logged rather than delivered. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead can name the entry and exit points that screening covers and those it does not.
The procedure states the disposition of rejected content and who reviews it.
Screening is described as a gateway function, not a mission application function.

requirements.title: Weekly refresh of the content screening rule set
requirements.description: The content-screening rule set used by the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall be refreshed at least weekly from the signed rule package built on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and the active rule-set version and refresh timestamp shall be reported to the platform monitoring path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A signed rule package build exists on the Provisioning Workstation with a weekly cadence.
The gateway reports an active rule-set version and refresh timestamp.
A refresh older than 7 days is visible as a stale condition.

requirements.title: Documented and repeatable behaviour on invalid inputs
requirements.description: When the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006), the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) or the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) receives an input that fails validation, it shall take the documented action for that input class — reject, clamp to the documented safe value, or hold current state — and shall not enter an undocumented state; behaviour across the defined invalid-input set shall be identical on three consecutive test runs. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every input class in the invalid-input set has a documented expected action.
Three consecutive runs of the invalid-input set produce identical outcomes on all three LRUs.
No invalid input results in a reset, hang or undocumented mode transition.

requirements.title: Navigation inputs restricted to approved sources and formats
requirements.description: The Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall accept navigation inputs only from the sensor identifiers listed in the approved sensor configuration and only in the approved message formats, discarding any message whose source identifier, format version or length is not on that list before it reaches the Navigation Processor (LRU-004). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A message from an unlisted sensor identifier is discarded at the interface and counted.
A malformed or over-length message of an approved type is discarded without partial parsing.
The Navigation Processor receives no message that failed source or format screening.

requirements.title: Payload commands restricted to the authorised source and format
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall accept payload commands only from the authorised mission-compute source over the designated command channel and only in the approved command format, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall independently reject any command that arrives without a matching authorisation token. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A command injected on a non-designated channel is rejected at the controller.
A correctly formatted command without a valid authorisation token is rejected by the interlock.
Rejections are counted and reported to the platform monitoring path.

requirements.title: External data never interpreted as command syntax
requirements.description: Mission software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and command handling on the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall treat all externally sourced data as untrusted, using fixed-length structured decoding and parameterised interfaces so that received data is never assembled into command, query or path syntax. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No externally sourced field is concatenated into a command, query or file path in the reviewed code paths.
Structured decoders are bounded by declared field lengths for every external message type.
The static analysis configuration includes an injection rule set and its findings are dispositioned.

requirements.title: Error messages disclose no exploitable detail
requirements.description: Error messages generated by the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and surfaced through the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall carry a stable error code and a corrective-action class only, with no memory addresses, key identifiers, file paths or account names, while full diagnostic detail remains available to privileged maintenance roles through the platform log path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Induced errors across the defined fault set expose only code and action class in telemetry.
No memory address, key identifier, file path or account name appears in any telemetry error string.
The corresponding full diagnostic entry is retrievable by a privileged maintenance role.

requirements.title: Cryptographic erase at end of retention
requirements.description: Protected configuration, audit and key material held in the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall be disposed of at end of retention by cryptographic erase of the wrapping key held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), followed by an overwrite pass of the affected region, and the disposal event shall be recorded with the object class and date. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The responsible engineer can describe the erase sequence and who authorises it.
Retention periods per object class are documented and drive the disposal trigger.
A disposal record exists carrying object class and date for the most recent disposal.

requirements.title: Telemetry output validated against the published schema
requirements.description: The Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall validate telemetry and status output produced by mission and payload software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) against the published output schema and range set before transmission, suppressing and logging any field outside the expected content rather than forwarding it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An out-of-range field injected upstream is suppressed and logged, not transmitted.
The schema and range set in use carries a version identifier reported with the telemetry stream.
Suppression counts are visible to the platform monitoring path.

requirements.title: Navigation and timing cache refreshed and cleared
requirements.description: The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall refresh cached almanac, ephemeris and timing correction data at least every 24 hours of operation, and shall delete cached navigation state at mission end so that stale position and timing information is neither retained nor reused on a subsequent sortie. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Cached navigation and timing data carries an age that never exceeds 24 hours in operation.
Cached navigation state is absent after a recorded mission-end transition.
A cold start after mission end does not reuse the previous sortie's position solution.

requirements.title: WS-X90 incident response policy and procedure set held under signed revision control
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall hold the WS-X90 system-level incident response policy and its supporting procedures as signed, version-controlled releases in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), review and update both at least annually and following any incident that changes the WS-X90 escalation chain, and republish each approved revision to the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) so that ground support technicians work only from the current copy. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds a signed incident response policy revision whose approval date is within the preceding twelve months.
The procedure set names an accountable official and carries a revision history entry for the most recent review event.
The copy staged on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) has the same digest as the current repository revision.

requirements.title: Incident response role training completed within 30 working days and refreshed annually
requirements.description: Every individual holding a WS-X90 incident response role shall complete role-specific incident response training within 30 working days of assuming the role or acquiring system access, and at least annually thereafter, with completion recorded against that individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) before a responder account is issued on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A named responder can walk through the WS-X90 escalation path and the containment actions available on each of the six subsystems without reference to a written aid.
Every current responder has a completion date on LRU-017 that is less than twelve months old.
No responder account exists on LRU-018 for an individual whose training record is absent or older than twelve months.

requirements.title: Scripted simulated incidents injected into each annual training cycle
