requirements.description: Each annual WS-X90 incident response training cycle shall include at least one injected simulated event in which the responder works a scripted navigation-spoofing or maintenance-session-abuse scenario end to end against a recorded event set staged from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and replayed on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), with elapsed time to first containment decision recorded and scored against the expected sequence. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The scenario library holds at least two scripted WS-X90 incident scenarios with an expected containment sequence for each.
Every responder in the current cycle has a scored run recorded, including elapsed time to first containment decision.
Replay on LRU-019 generates no command traffic toward any operational LRU.

requirements.title: Standalone incident response training environment isolated from operational buses
requirements.description: A standalone incident response training environment shall run on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and replay recorded WS-X90 event sets with no connection to any operational LRU, so that a responder exercise cannot place traffic on the mission bus or open a session against a fielded component. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The training environment configuration on LRU-017 shows no route to any operational subsystem interface.
The replay corpus is drawn from sanitised recorded events with mission payload content removed.

requirements.title: Annual incident response capability test with recorded acknowledgement times
requirements.description: The WS-X90 incident response capability shall be tested at least annually by injecting a controlled detection case into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and a controlled privileged-account-abuse case into the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and each test shall record the elapsed time from event generation to responder acknowledgement and to first containment action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A test report exists whose test date is within the preceding twelve months and which covers both injected cases.
Elapsed time from event generation to responder acknowledgement is recorded for each case.
Every deviation observed in the test is carried into the program corrective action list with an owner.

requirements.title: Incident response test scheduled jointly with the contingency and recovery rehearsal
requirements.description: Each annual WS-X90 incident response test shall be scheduled in the same window as the contingency and recovery rehearsal so that the controlled-recovery path on the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) is exercised against a declared incident, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) restart sequence is walked through jointly by the responder and the recovery operator. WS-X90 availability is categorised moderate, so the joint rehearsal targets an orderly bounded restart rather than uninterrupted operation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A single scheduled window covers both the incident response test and the recovery rehearsal.
The recovery operator can describe which incident classes trigger the LRU-016 controlled-recovery path and which do not.
The rehearsal record states the bounded restart duration achieved, not an availability claim the system does not hold.

requirements.title: Automatic triage and incident record creation within five minutes
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall triage incoming platform security events against the WS-X90 detection rule set without responder action and shall open an incident record in the protected incident store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) within 5 minutes of the triggering event, carrying the detection rule identifier, the originating LRU and the raw event reference. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An injected event matching a detection rule produces an incident record on LRU-015 in under 5 minutes with no operator input.
The opened record names the detection rule identifier and the originating LRU.
An event matching no rule produces no incident record and is retained in the raw event stream.

requirements.title: Containment directive executed on mission compute and external gateway within 30 seconds
requirements.description: On receipt of a containment directive against an open incident, the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall suspend the named non-essential mission service and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall drop the named external session, each within 30 seconds of the directive, and each action shall be written back to the incident record as a discrete containment entry with its own timestamp. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A containment directive suspends the named LRU-001 service in under 30 seconds and the suspension is observable in the service state table.
The named external session on LRU-007 is dropped in under 30 seconds and does not re-establish without a new authorisation.
Both actions appear as separate timestamped containment entries on the incident record.

requirements.title: Declared mission-continuation incident classes drive payload inhibit and navigation fallback
requirements.description: For the two declared WS-X90 incident classes that bear on mission continuation — payload command-path compromise and navigation integrity loss — the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall stop accepting payload commands, the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall latch to the inhibit state, and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) shall revert to its last validated navigation solution and raise a degraded-integrity flag, so that a bounded and safe mission capability is retained while the incident is worked. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Declaring the payload command-path compromise class latches LRU-011 to inhibit and LRU-010 rejects every subsequent payload command.
Declaring the navigation integrity loss class causes LRU-004 to publish the last validated solution with the degraded-integrity flag set.
Clearing either latch requires an explicit authorised action and is recorded against the incident.

requirements.title: Six-subsystem incident timeline with explicit source-silence marking
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall correlate events from all six WS-X90 subsystems, including the payload health and status records forwarded by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012), onto a single incident timeline keyed to platform time, and shall mark any contributing source silent for more than 15 minutes so that a gap in the correlated view is visible rather than implicit. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An incident timeline drawn for any open incident shows contributions from every subsystem that was reporting during the window.
Suppressing the LRU-012 telemetry feed for 20 minutes produces a visible silence marker on the timeline.
Timeline ordering is stable when two sources report the same platform timestamp.

requirements.title: Insider-threat branch triggered by privileged-session and account-change anomalies
requirements.description: The WS-X90 incident handling procedure shall define an insider-threat branch that is entered on privileged-session anomalies observed at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) or on out-of-policy account changes made on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and that routes the case to a restricted responder list rather than to the standard on-call rotation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The procedure names the specific LRU-014 and LRU-013 conditions that enter the insider-threat branch.
A case in the insider-threat branch is not visible to the standard on-call responder role.
The restricted responder list is held under change control with a named approver.

requirements.title: Insider-threat cases coordinated with the defined privacy and cybersecurity roster
requirements.description: Insider-threat incidents raised against WS-X90 shall be coordinated with, at a minimum, the Senior Agency Official for Privacy or designee and key cybersecurity personnel, and that coordination roster shall be held with the restricted case record so that access to Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session captures and Security Log Collector (LRU-018) extracts is granted only to individuals named on it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The restricted case record carries a coordination roster that includes the Senior Agency Official for Privacy or designee and key cybersecurity personnel.
An individual not on the roster cannot retrieve the LRU-014 session capture attached to the case.
A roster holder can describe the handover point at which the case leaves program engineering.

requirements.title: Compromise reporting to the National Manager through the designated cyber centre
requirements.description: For at a minimum a known or suspected compromise or unauthorized access, the WS-X90 program shall share a sanitised incident summary with the National Manager through the appropriate Federal Cyber Center or other designated central department point of contact, and that summary shall leave the platform only through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) as a release-reviewed package assembled by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The reporting procedure names the designated central department point of contact and the trigger condition of a known or suspected compromise or unauthorized access.
The package assembled on LRU-018 carries no mission payload content and no raw navigation data.
No egress path for incident summaries exists that bypasses LRU-007 release review.

requirements.title: Supply chain incident handling holds further staging of the implicated release
requirements.description: When a WS-X90 incident implicates a supplied component or a delivered software load, the program shall identify the affected release from the signed release metadata held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), notify the supplying organisation, and place a hold on further staging of that release by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) until the supplier response is recorded against the incident. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The incident record names the affected release identifier drawn from LRU-020 signed release metadata.
LRU-016 refuses to stage a held release and records the refusal against the incident.
The hold is released only by a recorded decision that cites the supplier response.

requirements.title: Integrated incident response team deployable within 72 hours with a current-image laptop
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall maintain a named integrated incident response team able to deploy to a WS-X90 operating location within 72 hours of a declared incident, carrying a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) built from the current approved image held on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and provisioned with the credentials needed for the declared incident class and no others. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A named team roster exists with a deployment call-out procedure and a stated 72-hour readiness commitment.
The deployment kit LRU-019 image digest matches the current approved image on LRU-017.
Credentials provisioned for a deployment are scoped to the declared incident class and expire on return.

requirements.title: Hashed forensic capture of mission compute and boot integrity state retained 180 days
requirements.description: After a WS-X90 incident is contained, the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall retain a read-only forensic capture of the affected Mission Computer (LRU-001) executable region and loaded module list together with the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) platform integrity state recorded at the time of the incident, for at least 180 days, and each capture shall be hashed at collection so later analysis can demonstrate the artifact was not altered. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A contained incident produces a capture on LRU-015 that includes the LRU-001 loaded module list and the LRU-002 integrity state word.
The capture digest recorded at collection matches the digest recomputed at retrieval.
A capture is still retrievable 180 days after collection and is not writable at any point after collection.

requirements.title: Navigation and timing anomaly records held as a distinct behaviour-analysis stream
requirements.description: The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall emit an anomaly record whenever holdover is entered without a commanded cause, and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall emit one whenever cross-sensor divergence exceeds the configured navigation integrity threshold; the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall retain those records as a behaviour-analysis stream separate from routine navigation telemetry so that adversarial patterns can be examined without sampling the whole telemetry volume. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Forcing uncommanded holdover on LRU-005 produces an anomaly record within one reporting interval.
Driving cross-sensor divergence past the configured threshold on LRU-006 produces an anomaly record naming the diverging sensors.
The behaviour-analysis stream on LRU-018 is queryable independently of the routine telemetry store.

requirements.title: Out-of-hours watch on the exported security event feed with authority to declare
requirements.description: A staffed security operations watch shall monitor the WS-X90 security event feed exported by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) outside program working hours and shall hold the delegated authority to declare a WS-X90 incident without first raising the program engineering chain. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A watch roster covers every hour outside program working hours with a named on-duty individual.
The delegated declaration authority is documented and the watch can name the incident classes it may declare.

requirements.title: Unique incident identifier carried through state transitions without re-keying
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall assign every opened WS-X90 incident a unique tracking identifier and carry that identifier through the open, contained, eradicated and closed states without manual re-keying, writing each state transition to the protected incident store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) with the acting identity and the transition timestamp attached. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every incident opened in the sample window has exactly one tracking identifier and no duplicate identifier exists in the store.
Each state transition on LRU-015 carries an acting identity and a timestamp.
A state transition cannot be recorded out of order or with an earlier timestamp than its predecessor.

requirements.title: Initial incident report generated from the record within 15 minutes of declaration
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall generate the initial WS-X90 incident report directly from the incident record with no manual transcription, populating the reportable-incident category, the affected LRU list, the detection time and the containment time, and shall present that report for release review within 15 minutes of the incident being declared. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Declaring an incident produces a populated draft report in under 15 minutes with no operator typing.
The draft carries the reportable-incident category, the affected LRU list, the detection time and the containment time.
A field that has no value in the incident record is rendered as absent rather than blank-filled.

requirements.title: Released incident reports leave over the gateway with a radio fallback and acknowledgement
requirements.description: A released WS-X90 incident report shall leave the platform through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) on the approved reporting path, and where that path is unavailable the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall carry the abbreviated report under the same release approval, with each path recording a delivery acknowledgement against the incident tracking identifier. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A released report transits LRU-007 and a delivery acknowledgement is written back against the tracking identifier.
With the LRU-007 path disabled, the abbreviated report transits LRU-008 under the same release approval and also acknowledges.
An unreleased draft cannot be transmitted on either path.

requirements.title: Incident-implicated weaknesses named against the baseline and reported in five working days
requirements.description: Where a WS-X90 incident is traced to an exploitable weakness in a fielded configuration, the incident record on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall name the affected baseline item in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the weakness shall be reported to the WS-X90 system security engineering lead and the responsible design authority within 5 working days of containment. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each incident closed as configuration-related names a baseline item identifier held in LRU-020.
The weakness report date is no more than 5 working days after the recorded containment time.
The report reaches both the system security engineering lead and the responsible design authority.

requirements.title: Sanitised supplier incident notice naming part number and release identifier
requirements.description: Incident information that implicates a supplied WS-X90 component or software load shall be provided to the supplying organisation in a sanitised form that names the affected part number and release identifier drawn from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and that carries no mission data, no navigation data and no operating location. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The supplier notice template draws part number and release identifier from LRU-020 rather than from free text.
A completed notice contains no mission, navigation or operating-location content.

requirements.title: Named incident response support contact reachable during program hours
requirements.description: A named WS-X90 incident response support point of contact shall be reachable by any operator or technician during program working hours and shall be able to advise on reporting and on the bounded containment actions available from the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014); the current contact details shall be carried in the approved ground support procedure staged on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A technician can name the current support contact and the route used to reach them.
The contact details in the LRU-017 staged procedure match the current roster.
The support contact can describe which containment actions a technician may take at LRU-014 without escalation.

requirements.title: Signed offline incident response bundle refreshed on the maintenance laptop
requirements.description: The current WS-X90 incident reporting procedure, contact roster and containment checklist shall be held offline on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) as a signed bundle refreshed from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) whenever the roster changes, so that a responder at a remote location can obtain them without a network path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The bundle signature on LRU-019 verifies against the LRU-017 signing key.
The bundle roster revision matches the current roster revision on LRU-017.
The bundle opens and renders with the laptop offline.

requirements.title: Named working relationship with external network protection providers
requirements.description: The WS-X90 incident response team shall maintain a named working relationship with the external providers of the protected transport and network protection services used by the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), and shall identify its own responders to those providers by role and by name so that a cross-boundary event can be worked without a cold introduction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A current contact record exists on both sides naming responders by role and name.
A responder can describe the agreed first action for a cross-boundary event affecting the LRU-007 transport.

requirements.title: Incident response plan approved annually with a protected on-platform working copy
requirements.description: The WS-X90 incident response plan shall be reviewed and approved by the CISO/SAISO or equivalent at least annually, incorporating lessons learned from past incidents, and distributed to all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the incident response plan; the approved revision shall be held as a signed release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with a protected working copy on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) so the plan remains available during an incident that affects program information technology. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current plan revision in LRU-020 carries an approval by the CISO/SAISO or equivalent dated within the preceding twelve months.
The revision record cites at least one lesson learned from a prior incident.
The distribution list covers all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the plan, and the LRU-015 working copy matches the approved revision digest.

requirements.title: Spill isolation of the external boundary and the contaminated port within ten minutes
requirements.description: On declaration of an information spill onto WS-X90, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall block every external session for the affected enclave and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall isolate the contaminated LRU port, both within 10 minutes of declaration, and the responder alert shall be issued over a communications path that does not traverse the contaminated segment. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A declared spill blocks all LRU-007 external sessions for the affected enclave in under 10 minutes.
The contaminated LRU port on LRU-009 is isolated in under 10 minutes and passes no frames afterwards.
The responder alert is delivered on a path with no dependency on the contaminated segment.

requirements.title: Spill eradication with a cleared-region record and a baseline contamination trace
requirements.description: Eradication of spilled information from WS-X90 shall overwrite the affected regions of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) using the approved sanitisation routine and shall produce a completion record naming every region cleared, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall be queried for every baseline that received a copy of the affected artifact so that subsequently contaminated components are identified rather than assumed absent. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The sanitisation completion record names every cleared LRU-015 region and the routine applied.
A read of any cleared region returns the overwrite pattern and not residual content.
The LRU-020 query result lists every baseline that carried the affected artifact, including superseded revisions.

requirements.title: Information spillage response training on a cycle consistent with IR-2
requirements.description: Information spillage response training shall be delivered on a cycle consistent with IR-2 to every individual authorised to handle WS-X90 mission data, shall cover the declaration route and the prohibition on discussing a spill over the contaminated path, and shall be recorded against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every individual authorised to handle WS-X90 mission data has a spillage training completion date on LRU-017 within the IR-2 cycle.
A trained individual can state the out-of-band declaration route without reference to a written aid.

requirements.title: Bounded degraded-operations partition while contaminated storage is under correction
requirements.description: A documented degraded-operations procedure shall allow WS-X90 mission staff to continue assigned tasks on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) from an uncontaminated partition while contaminated storage is under corrective action, with the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) enforcing the partition boundary. WS-X90 availability is categorised moderate, so the procedure shall define a bounded continuation window and the point at which operations stop, rather than claiming uninterrupted operation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The procedure names the uncontaminated LRU-001 partition and the tasks that may continue within it.
LRU-013 rejects a cross-partition access attempt during the continuation window and records it.
The procedure states an explicit bounded continuation window and a defined stop point.

requirements.title: Exposure handling suspends maintenance sessions and quarantines the endpoint
requirements.description: Where a WS-X90 spill exposes information to an individual outside their access authorisation, that individual's maintenance sessions on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall be suspended, the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) used in the exposure shall be quarantined and imaged before reuse, and the individual shall be debriefed and shall sign an exposure acknowledgement before any access is restored. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The exposure procedure names the LRU-014 session suspension step and the LRU-019 quarantine and imaging step.
A signed exposure acknowledgement is a recorded precondition of access restoration.

requirements.title: Personnel security policy reviewed annually and disseminated to provisioning roles
requirements.description: The personnel security policy and supporting procedures that govern access to WS-X90 shall be reviewed and updated at least annually and following any change to the program's screening or national eligibility gating, and the approved revision shall be held as a signed release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and disseminated to every role that provisions accounts from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The signed personnel security policy revision in LRU-020 carries an approval date within the preceding twelve months.
A named official is designated to manage the policy and appears on the current revision.
The dissemination record covers every individual holding a provisioning role on LRU-017.

requirements.title: Position risk designations reviewed annually or on description change or vacancy
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 engineering and support position that can obtain a privileged account shall carry a recorded risk designation with associated screening criteria, those designations shall be reviewed at least annually or when the position description is updated or when the position is vacated, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to issue a privileged account for a position whose designation record is absent or out of review. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every position on the WS-X90 privileged-role list has a recorded risk designation and screening criteria.
Each designation shows a review event within the preceding twelve months, or a later event tied to a description update or vacancy.
LRU-017 refuses a privileged account request for a position with no current designation record.

requirements.title: Screening completion gates account creation and is re-verified at recertification
requirements.description: No WS-X90 account shall be created on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) until the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) holds a completed screening record for the individual at the level required by the position risk designation, and that screening record shall be re-verified at each account recertification cycle before the account is renewed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every account on LRU-013 maps to an individual with a completed screening record on LRU-017 at the required level.
An account request for an individual with no screening record is refused and the refusal is recorded.
The most recent recertification cycle shows a screening re-verification entry for every renewed account.

requirements.title: Verified national eligibility as a hard gate on mission data and maintenance access
requirements.description: Access to WS-X90 mission data and to privileged maintenance sessions on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall be restricted to individuals whose citizenship status is recorded and verified on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) as meeting the program's national eligibility requirement, and that check shall be enforced as a hard gate on account issue rather than as an advisory flag. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every individual on the LRU-014 privileged maintenance roster has a verified national eligibility record on LRU-017.
An account request lacking a verified eligibility record is refused rather than issued with a warning.
The eligibility field cannot be set by the requesting individual or by the provisioning technician alone.

requirements.title: Termination access disable within the voluntary and involuntary time bounds
requirements.description: On termination of an individual's employment, WS-X90 system access shall be disabled — if voluntary, as soon as possible and not to exceed 5 working days; if involuntary, within the same day as termination — with the disable applied on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and reflected in that individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every involuntary termination in the sample window shows an LRU-013 disable timestamp on the same calendar day as the termination.
Every voluntary termination in the sample window shows an LRU-013 disable timestamp within 5 working days.
The LRU-017 provisioning record for each terminated individual shows the closed state and the disable reference.

requirements.title: Termination revokes issued credentials and recovers assigned support property
requirements.description: Termination processing shall revoke the individual's WS-X90 authenticators: the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall place the issued credential on the program revocation list and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall reject that credential on the next session attempt, while any assigned Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and issued token shall be recovered and recorded as returned before the termination record is closed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A revoked credential presented to LRU-014 is rejected on the first session attempt after revocation.
The LRU-003 revocation list contains an entry for every terminated individual in the sample window.
The property record shows the assigned LRU-019 and any issued token as returned before the termination record is closed.

requirements.title: Post-employment obligations acknowledged at exit before the provisioning record closes
requirements.description: Individuals who held WS-X90 access shall be notified at the exit interview of the applicable legally binding post-employment obligations for protecting program information and shall sign an acknowledgement of those obligations, and the signed acknowledgement shall be filed against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) before that record is closed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The exit interview script names the post-employment obligations that apply to WS-X90 information.
A closed provisioning record on LRU-017 carries a signed acknowledgement reference or a documented exception.

requirements.title: Personnel-feed termination disables accounts and notifies within sixty minutes
requirements.description: A termination action entered in the Aurora personnel feed shall automatically disable the individual's WS-X90 accounts on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and raise a notification to the security operations distribution held by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 minutes, without a technician performing the disable by hand. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A termination entered in the personnel feed disables the mapped LRU-013 accounts in under 60 minutes with no technician action.
The notification appears on the LRU-018 security operations distribution with the individual identifier and the action time.
A personnel-feed entry that maps to no WS-X90 account produces a recorded no-op rather than a silent drop.

requirements.title: Transfer reassignment actions initiated within ten working days
requirements.description: When an individual is reassigned or transferred within Aurora Defense Systems, reassignment actions to ensure all system accesses no longer required — for example on need-to-know grounds — are removed or disabled shall be initiated within 10 working days of the formal transfer action, applied on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and confirmed against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every transfer in the sample window shows an LRU-013 access change initiated within 10 working days of the formal transfer action.
The retained access set after the change matches the operational need recorded for the new position.
The LRU-017 provisioning record shows the confirmation entry and the confirming role.

requirements.title: Access agreement signed before issue and re-signed at least annually
requirements.description: Every individual granted access to WS-X90 shall sign the program access agreement before an account is issued and shall re-sign it at least annually or whenever the agreement is updated, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall hold the signed agreement date as a precondition of account issue and of each recertification. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every current WS-X90 account holder has a signed access agreement date on LRU-017 within the preceding twelve months.
An account issue attempt with no signed agreement date is refused.
An agreement revision triggers a re-sign requirement against every holder of the superseded revision.

requirements.title: Post-employment obligations acknowledged as part of initial access
requirements.description: The WS-X90 access agreement shall state the applicable legally binding post-employment obligations for protecting program information, and the individual shall sign an acknowledgement of those obligations as part of being granted initial access rather than only at exit, with the acknowledgement recorded on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) alongside the signed access agreement. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current access agreement text includes the post-employment obligations clause.
Each initial-access record on LRU-017 carries an acknowledgement reference dated on or before the account issue date.

requirements.title: External provider personnel changes notified within one working day and reconciled monthly
requirements.description: External providers whose personnel hold WS-X90 credentials or maintenance access shall be required to notify the organizational security manager of any transfer or termination of those personnel as soon as possible and not to exceed 1 working day, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session roster and the issued Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) inventory shall be reconciled against each provider's personnel list monthly. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each provider agreement states the notification route to the organizational security manager and the 1 working day bound.
The most recent monthly reconciliation shows no LRU-014 roster entry without a matching current provider personnel record.
Every issued LRU-019 unit is accounted for against a named current provider individual or recorded as returned.

requirements.title: Formal sanctions initiated and notified for defined WS-X90 policy breaches
requirements.description: A formal sanctions process shall apply to individuals who breach WS-X90 security policy — for example bypassing the maintenance session controls on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) or suppressing records on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) — and initiation of that process shall be notified to the program security manager and to the individual's line manager within 5 working days, identifying the individual and the reason for the sanction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The sanctions procedure names the WS-X90 breach conditions that initiate it, including the LRU-014 and LRU-018 cases.
A notification record exists for each initiation, dated within 5 working days and naming the individual and the reason.

requirements.title: Security responsibilities stated in position descriptions for provisioning and baseline roles
requirements.description: Position descriptions for every WS-X90 role that can provision accounts from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or sign a configuration baseline into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall state the security responsibilities carried by that role, and the applicable position description revision shall be referenced from the individual's provisioning record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every role on the LRU-017 provisioning-authority list and the LRU-020 baseline-signing list has a position description that states security responsibilities.
Each provisioning record references the position description revision in force when access was granted.

requirements.title: Audit policy and procedure set held under signed revision control
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall hold the WS-X90 audit and accountability policy and its implementing procedures as a signed, version-controlled record set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), disseminate the current revision to all personnel holding a WS-X90 platform role, and re-approve both the policy and the procedures at least annually and after any change to the audit pipeline hosted on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Configuration Repository holds exactly one revision of the audit policy and one of the audit procedures marked approved, each carrying a signature and an approval date.
The approval date on each is no more than 12 months before the assessment date.
The dissemination record lists every current WS-X90 platform role holder against the approved revision number.

requirements.title: Payload command audit records carry the extended field set
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall add the payload command opcode, the originating crew-station identifier, the commanded payload state and the Payload Safety Interlock state read at command time to every payload command audit record, and shall emit that record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) with each of the four additional fields either populated or carrying an explicit null marker. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every record in a 200-record sample of payload command audit records carries all four additional fields.
No sampled record omits a field silently; unavailable values appear as an explicit null marker.
The Security Log Collector parses the extended record without falling back to the base AU-3 schema.

requirements.title: Closed audit segments transfer off the recording component daily
requirements.description: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall close and transfer each audit log segment to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), a physically separate component, at least once every 24 hours and whenever a segment reaches its size limit, and shall retain the local copy until LRU-018 acknowledges the transfer. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No segment observed on LRU-015 during a 14-day run remains untransferred for more than 24 hours after closure.
A segment forced past its size limit transfers without waiting for the 24-hour timer.
A local copy suppressed before acknowledgement is retried and the retry is recorded.

requirements.title: Audit storage warning at 75 percent of allocated capacity
requirements.description: When the audit partition on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) reaches a maximum of 75% of its allocated capacity, the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall raise a storage-capacity warning to the operator display and to the on-platform maintenance log within 60 seconds of the threshold being crossed, and shall repeat the warning at each further 5% of consumption. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A partition filled to 75% produces an operator warning within 60 seconds of the crossing timestamp recorded on LRU-015.
Warnings repeat at 80, 85, 90 and 95 percent without an operator acknowledgement clearing the series.
The maintenance log entry names the partition, the percentage and the crossing time.

requirements.title: Automated correlation and weekly reviewer queue
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall run the approved correlation rule set against newly ingested audit records without operator action, and shall present a reviewer queue to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) at least weekly covering every record ingested in the preceding seven days. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The correlation job runs on ingest with no scheduled operator step in the job definition.
A weekly queue is produced for four consecutive weeks with no gap in the seven-day coverage window.
Every rule in the approved set is present in the running configuration and none is disabled.

requirements.title: Audit records correlated across the platform store and the configuration history
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall correlate records drawn from the on-platform audit store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) with the configuration-change history held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) into a single analysis view keyed on actor identity and time, so that a configuration change and the audit records it produced resolve to one correlated event. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded configuration change and its resulting platform audit records return as one correlated event in the analysis view.
The correlated event names both source repositories and the actor identity used to join them.
A change with no matching audit record is reported as an unmatched change rather than dropped.

requirements.title: Single central review surface for all reporting LRUs
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall present one central review interface listing audit records from every reporting WS-X90 LRU, including the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006), so that an analyst can review platform-wide activity without logging in to an individual component. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The central view returns records for every LRU listed in the reporting-component register.
No review workflow step requires a direct login to a source LRU.
An LRU that has not reported inside its expected interval is shown as silent rather than omitted.

requirements.title: Monitoring and scan data joined to the audit analysis view
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall ingest the vulnerability scan results and the host monitoring stream produced for the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and present them in the same analysis view as the audit records, so that a monitoring alert and the audit records covering the same interval are read together. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved design names the scan and monitoring feeds, their formats and their ingest cadence.
The analysis view schema carries a source-type column that distinguishes audit, scan and monitoring rows.
A time-window query returns audit and monitoring rows in one result set.

requirements.title: Provisioning sessions correlated with facility access events
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall ingest the facility physical-access event feed covering the bay that houses the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and shall correlate each provisioning session with the badge entry that preceded it, flagging any provisioning session for which no matching entry exists. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The physical-access feed is named in the approved data-source register with an owning facility contact.
The correlation rule defines the time window inside which a badge entry is treated as matching.
A provisioning session with no matching badge entry appears on the exception list.

requirements.title: On-demand audit reduction that does not alter the source records
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall produce filtered audit reports on demand from a stored query without writing to, reordering or re-timestamping the source records, and shall record the query text, the requesting operator and the record count in the report header. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A digest taken over the source segment set before and after a report run is unchanged.
Records in the report appear in the same relative order as in the source segment.
The report header names the query, the operator identity and the record count.

requirements.title: Audit search across the platform record set within 30 seconds
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall process, sort and search stored audit records by event type, actor identity, source LRU identifier, outcome and event timestamp, and shall return a result set for a seven-day window over the full platform record volume within 30 seconds. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the five search fields returns a correct result set against a seeded record population.
A seven-day query over the full retained volume completes within 30 seconds on three consecutive runs.
Sorting on event timestamp is stable for records sharing a timestamp.

requirements.title: Audit copy held on a physically separate component at least weekly
requirements.description: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall write a copy of every closed audit segment to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), a physically separate component from the LRUs being audited, no less often than weekly; the fielded cadence is daily, and a week that closes with no successful copy shall raise a maintenance alert. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every calendar week in a six-week sample contains at least one acknowledged copy to LRU-018.
The copy target resolves to a component with a different chassis identifier from the audited LRUs.
A suppressed weekly copy produces a maintenance alert within that week.

requirements.title: Audit segments and audit tools signed and verified before use
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall sign each closed audit segment written by the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and each audit tool binary before it is used, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall reject any segment or tool whose signature does not verify against the current platform trust anchor. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A segment with a flipped byte fails verification on LRU-018 and is quarantined rather than ingested.
An unsigned audit tool binary is refused execution.
The trust anchor used for verification matches the anchor recorded in the platform key inventory.

requirements.title: Audit configuration management restricted to a named administrator subset
requirements.description: Management of audit logging configuration on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall be restricted to an audit-management group of no more than three named individuals at a time, drawn from the System Security Engineer role and disjoint from the general platform administration group on either LRU. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The audit-management group membership export lists three or fewer named individuals.
No individual appears in both the audit-management and the platform administration group lists.
The audit configuration objects on both LRUs are writable only by the audit-management group.

requirements.title: Dual authorization for movement or deletion of any audit information
requirements.description: Movement or deletion of any audit information held on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) or the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall require two distinct authenticated approvals from the audit-management group recorded in the same transaction, and a single-approval attempt shall fail closed and be logged as a denied action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A move or delete submitted with one approval is refused and the refusal is logged.
A move or delete carrying two distinct authenticated approvals succeeds and both approver identities are recorded.
The same identity supplying both approvals is treated as a single approval and refused.

requirements.title: Read-only exposure of audit content to analyst roles
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall expose audit content to read-only analysis accounts through an interface that offers no write, edit or delete verb, and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall present the underlying segment store as read-only to every identity except the audit writer service. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A read-only analysis session on LRU-018 exposes no mutating operation in the interface surface.
A write attempted against the segment store on LRU-015 as any non-writer role is refused.
The audit writer service identity is the only principal with write authority on the segment store.

requirements.title: Payload arm and release commands are signed at origin
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall attach to every payload arm and release command it forwards a signature produced by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) covering the command, the operator identity and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) state at command time, so that the originator of a payload command cannot later be repudiated. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every arm and release command in a captured mission run carries a signature over command, operator identity and interlock state.
A command replayed with an altered operator identity fails signature verification.
The interlock state inside the signed structure matches the state LRU-011 recorded independently.

requirements.title: Signing key custody and signature verification on ingest
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall hold the non-repudiation signing keys in protected storage with no export path, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall verify every command signature on ingest and mark any record whose signature fails or whose key identifier is unknown as unverifiable, retaining rather than discarding it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No interface on LRU-003 returns private key material for the non-repudiation key set.
A record signed with an unknown key identifier is ingested and marked unverifiable.
The count of unverifiable records is reportable per day and per source LRU.

requirements.title: Retrieval capability retained for the full audit retention period
requirements.description: Retrieval of an audit segment written 24 months earlier shall stay demonstrable for the whole of the required retention period, with the Platform Lead able to name the reader tooling and record schema version held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and the verification key retained on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) that the retrieval depends on. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead names the reader tooling version and the schema version applicable to a segment of a stated age.
The Platform Lead identifies where the verification key for that segment is retained and who can retrieve it.
The walkthrough reaches readable record content without recourse to a tool that is out of configuration control.

requirements.title: Platform time reference distributed to navigation LRUs within the AU-8 tolerance
requirements.description: The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall distribute a single platform time reference to the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and shall hold their audit timestamps within the platform time tolerance defined for AU-8, declaring holdover and marking emitted records as degraded-time whenever that tolerance cannot be guaranteed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Timestamps sampled from LRU-004 and LRU-006 stay within the AU-8 tolerance of the LRU-005 reference across a four-hour run.
Removing the reference input drives LRU-005 into declared holdover within one reporting interval.
Records emitted during holdover carry the degraded-time marker.

requirements.title: System-wide audit trail compiled on the platform time reference
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall compile audit records from every reporting LRU, including those relayed through the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009), into one system-wide audit trail ordered on the platform time reference published by the Timing Receiver (LRU-005), and shall mark any record whose source declared degraded time rather than interleaving it silently. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The compiled trail contains records from every LRU in the reporting-component register for the sampled window.
Records ordered on the platform time reference reproduce the known event order of a seeded sequence.
Degraded-time records are visibly marked in the compiled trail.

requirements.title: Authorized change of logged event types within a bounded time threshold
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall allow only the audit-management group to change which event types are logged on the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) and on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), by selection from the approved event-criteria set, and the change shall take effect on the target LRU within 15 minutes and shall itself be audited. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A logging change requested from the audit-management group is observable on LRU-018 within 15 minutes.
A logging change requested by any other role is refused and the refusal is audited.
Each accepted change produces an audit record naming the requester, the target LRU and the event criteria selected.

requirements.title: Maintenance session content recorded and forwarded at session close
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall record the full command and response content of every nonlocal maintenance session, whichever maintenance account opens it and with no account exempt, and shall forward the complete session transcript to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) when the session closes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A transcript exists on LRU-018 for every session recorded in the gateway session register for the sampled period.
A sampled transcript reproduces the commands and responses captured at the gateway with no truncation marker.
A session terminated abnormally still produces a transcript covering the content up to the break.

requirements.title: Session auditing enabled by the boot sequence before maintenance ports open
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall enable session auditing on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) as a step of the authenticated boot sequence, completed before any maintenance port is brought up, so that no maintenance session can be opened while session auditing is off. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The boot log shows session auditing enabled before the maintenance port transitions to up on 10 consecutive cold boots.
A boot in which session auditing fails to enable leaves the maintenance port down.
No operator action is required between power-on and session auditing being active.

requirements.title: Supervisor real-time view of an in-progress maintenance session
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall allow an authorized supervisor to observe an in-progress maintenance session in real time through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), with the observed session visibly marked to the technician conducting it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An approved design exists naming the observation path, the supervisor authorization and the technician notification.
The observation path is carried on the maintenance policy on LRU-007 rather than a general-purpose path.
The technician notification is present in the session interface specification.

requirements.title: Coordinated release of audit information across an organizational boundary
requirements.description: Where WS-X90 audit information crosses an organizational boundary, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall release it only through the approved coordination method, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall record the receiving organization, the record set released and the releasing authority for each transfer. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved coordination method is named in the design and bound to a specific egress policy on LRU-007 and LRU-008.
The transfer register schema on LRU-018 carries receiving organization, record set and releasing authority.
No egress path for audit content exists outside the named coordination method.

requirements.title: Originating identity preserved in exported audit records
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall preserve the originating individual identity in any audit record exported to a partner organization, using the platform identity binding held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) rather than a locally reassigned identifier. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The export mapping carries the platform identity binding through unchanged for every identity field.
No export transform substitutes a local or per-session identifier for the originating identity.
The identity binding source is the key material inventory on LRU-003.

requirements.title: Cross-organizational audit release gated on a recorded sharing agreement
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall release cross-organizational audit information only to organizations named in a current sharing agreement recorded in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and shall refuse any release request that names no such agreement. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The System Security Engineer can name where a sharing agreement would be recorded and what it must contain.
The walkthrough shows no current release path that bypasses an agreement check.
The gap is carried on the plan of action with a named owner.

requirements.title: Maintenance policy and procedures reviewed at least annually
requirements.description: The Platform Lead, as the accountable owner of the WS-X90 maintenance policy and procedure set held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), shall be able to show an assessor the current issue of each, naming the approving official, the at-least-annual review date, and the procedure that governs the nonlocal maintenance path implemented by the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The Platform Lead names the approving official and the review date for both the policy and the procedures.
The review date on each is no more than 12 months before the assessment date.
The nonlocal maintenance procedure the lead names matches the path configured on LRU-014.

requirements.title: Maintenance actions scheduled and gated by the automated workflow
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall schedule, dispatch and close out maintenance, repair and replacement actions through the automated maintenance workflow, and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall refuse to apply a maintenance action that carries no open work order. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A maintenance action submitted to LRU-016 without an open work order is refused and the refusal is recorded.
Scheduling, dispatch and close-out each produce a workflow state change on LRU-013 with an actor identity.
No manual override path applies a maintenance action outside the workflow.

requirements.title: Complete maintenance records held for every LRU
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold, for every WS-X90 LRU including the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012), a maintenance record showing when the action was raised, when it was booked, whether work is under way, and when it closed out, together with the acting technician and the parts fitted, and shall flag any record left in process for more than 30 days. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every LRU in the asset register has at least one maintenance record or an explicit no-maintenance entry.
A sampled completed record carries acting technician and parts fitted.
A record left under way for more than 30 days appears on the stale-record exception list.

requirements.title: Maintenance tool images inspected against the approved baseline before issue
requirements.description: The tool-issue inspection, in which the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) compares the tool image on a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) against the approved tool baseline and blocks issue on any difference in file set, version or signature, shall be demonstrable to an assessor by the Platform Lead. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The lead demonstrates where the approved tool baseline is held and how a difference is surfaced.
The lead can produce the inspection record for a named laptop serial number and issue date.
The lead states what happens to a laptop returned from the field, and whether it is re-inspected.

requirements.title: Diagnostic media scanned for malicious code before platform use
requirements.description: The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall scan every item of diagnostic or test media for malicious code using a signature set no more than seven days old before that media is presented to any WS-X90 interface, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall record the scan result against the media serial number. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Media presented without a recorded scan is refused at the platform interface.
The signature set date on a sampled scan is within seven days of the scan date.
A seeded test file is detected and the media is blocked from issue.

requirements.title: Release control for maintenance equipment holding platform information
requirements.description: Maintenance equipment that has held WS-X90 information, including a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), shall not leave the facility until it is verified clear, sanitized, destroyed or granted a recorded exemption by a named authorizing official, and the release record shall be retained against the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session history; the Platform Lead shall be able to produce that record for a sampled unit. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The lead names the four permitted release dispositions and who may authorize an exemption.
The lead can show where a release record is retained and how it is joined to the maintenance session that used the equipment.
The lead states the check that prevents equipment leaving with no disposition recorded.

requirements.title: Maintenance tool invocation restricted to authorized technicians
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall accept a maintenance tool invocation only from an authenticated technician on the current authorized-maintainer list, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall refuse to launch a platform maintenance tool without a valid session token issued by LRU-014. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An invocation from an identity removed from the authorized-maintainer list is refused within one session.
A tool launched on LRU-019 with an expired or absent token does not reach the platform interface.
Every accepted invocation resolves to a named technician in the maintainer list.

requirements.title: Privileged maintenance tool use monitored and alerted
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall emit an audit record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) for every maintenance tool invocation that runs with elevated platform privilege, naming the tool, the technician and the privilege level, and LRU-018 shall raise an alert for any privileged invocation that falls outside an open work order. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every privileged invocation in a sampled period has a matching audit record on LRU-018.
The audit record names the tool, the technician identity and the privilege level.
A privileged invocation seeded outside a work order raises an alert.

requirements.title: Maintenance tools inspected against the approved patch level
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the current approved patch level for every WS-X90 maintenance tool, and each Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be inspected against that level before issue, with any tool below the approved level withheld from issue. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An approved patch level exists in LRU-020 for each tool in the maintenance tool register.
The issue workflow includes a patch-level check with a defined withhold action.
A tool below the approved level is recorded as withheld rather than issued with a note.

requirements.title: Nonlocal maintenance sessions logged and reviewed within one working day
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall log session start, authentication outcome, every privileged command, every file transfer and session end for each nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic session, using the event set defined in the WS-X90 audit policy for AU-1, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall present those sessions for review within one working day of session close. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: All five event classes appear in the log for a sampled nonlocal session.
Each sampled session appears in the review queue on LRU-018 within one working day of its close time.
The event set logged matches the event set named in the audit policy revision in force.

requirements.title: Nonlocal maintenance initiated only from a comparably protected endpoint
requirements.description: A nonlocal maintenance session shall be initiated only from a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) whose configuration baseline provides authentication, session encryption, endpoint integrity checking and audit forwarding at the level enforced on the platform, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall refuse a session from an endpoint that does not attest to that baseline. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The endpoint baseline for LRU-019 names all four protections and their platform equivalents.
The gateway session policy on LRU-014 requires a baseline attestation before session establishment.
Any endpoint accepted without attestation is recorded with a named waiver and an expiry date.

requirements.title: Remove, clear and re-verify path for LRUs serviced off-platform
requirements.description: Where an LRU is removed for service rather than serviced in place, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall clear mission information from it while the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) retains the recovery material, and LRU-016 shall re-verify the component image against the approved baseline before the LRU is reconnected. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A removed LRU returns a clear-complete confirmation from LRU-016 before it leaves the platform.
Recovery material for the removed LRU is present on LRU-015 and is usable to restore configuration.
Reconnection is refused for a component whose image does not verify against the approved baseline.

requirements.title: Replay-resistant authentication and separated maintenance path
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall authenticate every nonlocal maintenance session with a replay-resistant authenticator and shall carry that session on a dedicated VLAN on the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and a dedicated policy on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), logically separated from mission traffic. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A captured authentication exchange replayed against LRU-014 is refused.
Maintenance frames observed on LRU-009 carry the dedicated VLAN tag and no mission VLAN tag.
The LRU-007 policy applied to the maintenance session differs from the mission traffic policy in the configuration export.

requirements.title: Maintenance traffic protected with CNSSP 15 Annex B approved algorithms
requirements.description: Nonlocal maintenance traffic between the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall be protected for integrity and confidentiality using the approved algorithms listed in CNSSP 15 Annex B, with keys issued and held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), and the session shall fail closed if algorithm negotiation resolves outside that set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The negotiated suite for a sampled maintenance session is inside the approved set.
A client offering only algorithms outside the approved set is refused rather than downgraded.
Session keys resolve to a key identifier issued by LRU-003 and present in the key inventory.

requirements.title: Confirmed termination of maintenance sessions and network connections
requirements.description: At the end of a nonlocal maintenance session the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall confirm that the session context is destroyed and that the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) has torn down the network connection, and shall record a confirmed-terminated state; an unconfirmed teardown shall raise an alert. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every closed session in a sampled period carries a confirmed-terminated record.
A session context queried after close returns not found on LRU-014.
A connection left established on LRU-007 after session close raises an alert.

requirements.title: Escorted maintenance by personnel without required access approvals
requirements.description: Maintenance personnel who lack the required clearance or access approval shall work only under escort by a cleared, technically qualified escort, and the Platform Lead shall be able to walk an assessor through the procedure by which the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is placed in restricted maintenance mode, the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is replaced by an uncleared-session image, and volatile mission information on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is cleared before that work begins. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The lead names the escort qualification standard and who confirms it before work starts.
The lead identifies the restricted maintenance mode on LRU-014 and what it withholds.
The lead states the alternate control applied where a component can be neither cleared in place nor physically detached.

requirements.title: Maintenance support or spares obtained within 30 days of failure
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall obtain maintenance support or a serviceable spare for a failed Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) or Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) within 30 days of the failure being reported, a period set to match the moderate availability categorization of WS-X90, and shall record the elapsed time against each reported failure. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A support agreement or spares holding covering LRU-008, LRU-016 and LRU-013 names a response period of 30 days or less.
The failure register records report date and support or spare arrival date for each entry.
No entry in the register exceeds 30 days without a recorded exception.

requirements.title: Preventive maintenance performed at least every 12 months
requirements.description: Preventive maintenance shall be performed at least every 12 months and recorded against the LRU serial number for the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) — retention-battery and recovery-media checks on LRU-016, oscillator ageing and holdover calibration checks on LRU-005, connector and calibration checks on LRU-012. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The preventive maintenance schedule names all three LRUs, the specific checks and a 12-month interval.
Each installed LRU-016, LRU-005 and LRU-012 serial number has a recorded check date or a first-due date.
No serial number is past its 12-month due date without a recorded exception.

requirements.title: Physical and environmental protection procedure set for WS-X90 support areas
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall maintain a WS-X90 physical and environmental protection procedure set that names the Platform Lead as the accountable official and covers the integration bay holding the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017); the set shall be reviewed and reissued at least annually and after any facility move or change to the accreditation boundary. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The controlled copy in circulation carries an approval signature dated within the last 12 months.
The cover sheet names a specific Platform Lead as accountable official, not a generic function.
The revision log shows an out-of-cycle review entry for the most recent facility change.

requirements.title: Facility access roster for the WS-X90 integration, maintenance and provisioning areas
requirements.description: The WS-X90 facility access roster shall list every individual authorised to enter the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), the maintenance bay holding the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the controlled storage holding the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019); the roster shall be reviewed at least annually and a departing or reassigned individual shall be struck from it, and their badge credential revoked, within 5 working days of the need for access ending. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
