acceptance_criteria: Every name on the roster resolves to a current badge credential and a stated business need.
The most recent roster review is signed and dated within the last 12 months.
For a sampled leaver, the roster removal date is within 5 working days of the departure date.

requirements.title: System-level physical access enforcement for the protected equipment bay
requirements.description: Physical access to the protected equipment bay containing the Mission Computer (LRU-001), the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall require a second authorisation held separately from general facility access, and the bay reader shall refuse any credential absent from the bay-specific list even where that same credential opens the outer facility door. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The bay reader access list is a strict subset of the facility roster and is shorter than it.
A credential valid at the outer door but absent from the bay list is refused at the bay reader.
Each refusal is written to the reader event log with the credential identifier and timestamp.

requirements.title: Physical protection of internal data cabling between gateway and switch
requirements.description: The wiring runs carrying mission data between the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall be routed inside locked metal conduit or sealed cable tray for their entire length within the integration facility, with no accessible splice, patch panel or unterminated drop outside a controlled space. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The as-built cable route drawing shows conduit or sealed tray on every segment between LRU-007 and LRU-009.
A walk of the route finds no patch panel, junction box or spare drop outside a locked space.
Every conduit access cover on the route is fitted with a lock or a serialised seal.

requirements.title: Tamper-evident termination of RF feed and navigation sensor harness runs
requirements.description: The antenna feed between the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the facility test antenna, and the sensor harness runs entering the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006), shall terminate in sealed connectors whose disturbance is visible without instrumentation; a bench trial shall show that removing a connector breaks the seal and leaves a witness mark in 10 of 10 attempts. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 trial disconnections leave a broken seal or witness mark visible to the unaided eye.
Seal serial numbers for the installed feed and harness terminations are recorded against the airframe record.
No connector on either run is found finger-tight or unsealed during the trial.

requirements.title: Output-device lockdown on provisioning and maintenance endpoints
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall carry no enabled printer, removable-media writer or external display port in the approved configuration; an attempt to attach any of the three shall be refused by the endpoint and recorded, and a screen-visibility check shall confirm that provisioning output is not readable from outside the controlled area. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Attaching a USB mass-storage device, a printer and an external monitor to each endpoint is refused in all six attempts.
Each refusal produces a dated endpoint log entry naming the device class.
A viewing check from the corridor and from the adjacent bay finds no readable provisioning output on either screen.

requirements.title: Intrusion alarm and surveillance feed into the security log record
requirements.description: The facility intrusion alarm and the camera covering the WS-X90 integration bay shall export door-forced and after-hours motion events to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) so that they can be correlated with chassis-intrusion telemetry from the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013); the export shall be a one-way feed with no return path from the alarm system into WS-X90. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The interface design shows a data-diode or equivalent one-way path from the alarm system to LRU-018.
A forced-door event and an after-hours motion event both appear in the LRU-018 record with the bay identifier.
No route exists by which the alarm system can write to, or command, any WS-X90 component.

requirements.title: System-level physical access monitoring for the maintenance bay
requirements.description: Entry to the maintenance bay where the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is racked shall be monitored separately from the outer facility, and each badge-in event shall be forwarded to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) carrying the bay identifier, so that a maintenance session opened on LRU-014 can be matched against a person physically present at that time. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Badge events for the maintenance bay are distinguishable in LRU-018 from outer-door events.
For a sampled maintenance session on LRU-014, a badge-in event for the same bay precedes session open.
A session opened with no corresponding badge-in event is reportable as an anomaly.

requirements.title: Visitor access record retention, review and anomaly reporting
requirements.description: Visitor access records for the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall be retained for at least one year and reviewed at least every 90 days by the Platform Lead; any anomaly — an unescorted entry, a missing exit time, or a visit outside approved hours — shall be reported to the System Security Engineer within 2 working days and mirrored to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Visitor records older than 11 months and younger than 12 months are still retrievable.
The gap between consecutive signed reviews never exceeds 90 days over the last four cycles.
For each anomaly raised in the last cycle, a dated report to the System Security Engineer exists within 2 working days.

requirements.title: Automated visitor record capture and review prompting
requirements.description: Visitor sign-in for the WS-X90 areas shall be captured by the badge system rather than a paper book, exported nightly to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), and shall raise an automatic prompt to the Platform Lead once 90 days have elapsed since the last recorded review; a seeded test visit at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) area shall appear in the LRU-018 export within one nightly cycle. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded visitor record appears in the LRU-018 export on the next nightly run.
No paper visitor book is in use for the WS-X90 areas at the time of the check.
Setting the last-review date back 91 days causes a review prompt to be raised without operator action.

requirements.title: Minimised personal data in exported visitor records
requirements.description: The visitor record set exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall carry only badge identifier, escort identifier, area code and in/out timestamps, and shall not carry home address, personal telephone number, date of birth or citizenship data. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The export field list matches the four approved fields exactly, with no additional personal fields.
A sampled export record contains no home address, personal telephone number, date of birth or citizenship value.

requirements.title: Protection of power feeds serving the mission and payload racks
requirements.description: The power feeds serving the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall run in protected raceway, terminate on individually labelled breakers inside a lockable distribution panel, and shall not share a breaker with any load outside the WS-X90 programme. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three feeds terminates on a breaker labelled with the LRU identifier it serves.
The distribution panel door is fitted with a working lock and is found locked during the check.
The panel schedule shows no non-programme load on any breaker serving LRU-009, LRU-011 or LRU-013.

requirements.title: Emergency power cutoff at the payload interface bench
requirements.description: A single emergency cutoff at the payload interface bench shall remove power from the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) within 2 seconds of activation while leaving the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) monitoring rail energised for post-event readout; the cutoff shall be within 3 metres of the bench operator position and guarded against accidental strike. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Measured time from activation to loss of rail voltage on LRU-010 and LRU-011 is under 2 seconds in every trial.
The LRU-013 monitoring rail remains energised throughout each trial and the event is readable afterwards.
The cutoff is within 3 metres of the operator position and fitted with a strike guard or shroud.

requirements.title: Uninterruptible supply sized for orderly shutdown, not sustained operation
requirements.description: The integration bay uninterruptible supply shall hold the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) long enough for an orderly shutdown that flushes buffered audit records to LRU-015 — sized at 15 minutes of ride-through and explicitly not as a long-term alternate power source, consistent with the moderate availability categorisation of WS-X90. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The load calculation shows at least 15 minutes of ride-through at the measured rack draw.
The shutdown script flushes the LRU-015 audit buffer before power is dropped.
The design record states that sustained operation on alternate power is out of scope for this system.

requirements.title: Automatic emergency lighting over the provisioning area egress route
requirements.description: Automatic emergency lighting shall cover the egress route from the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and shall illuminate on loss of building power without any manual action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every segment of the marked egress route from the provisioning area is within the coverage of a fitting.
Dropping building power during a scheduled test illuminates all fittings on the route with no operator action.

requirements.title: Fire detection and suppression on an independent energy source
requirements.description: Fire detection and suppression covering the WS-X90 integration bay and the provisioning area shall draw on an energy source independent of the building supply, and shall be confirmed operable on that independent source during the annual facility check while the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) racks are installed and powered. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The detection and suppression systems remain functional with the building supply isolated.
The independent energy source has a service record dated within the last 12 months.
The annual check record names both the integration bay and the provisioning area as covered spaces.

requirements.title: Automatic fire detection notification and event capture
requirements.description: Fire detection in the WS-X90 areas shall activate without human action, notify the Platform Lead and the site fire response desk within the same alarm cycle, and emit a dated event record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) so that the alarm can be reconciled against Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shutdown telemetry. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A test activation notifies both the Platform Lead and the fire response desk without any operator step.
The test activation produces a dated record in LRU-018 carrying the area identifier.
The LRU-018 record and the LRU-013 shutdown telemetry for the same event can be matched on timestamp.

requirements.title: Automatic fire suppression during unstaffed periods
requirements.description: Fire suppression covering the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall activate automatically and notify the site fire response desk, and shall remain in automatic mode throughout the overnight and weekend periods during which the area is not staffed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The suppression system mode log shows automatic mode for every unstaffed period in the sampled month.
A test activation notifies the fire response desk without any local operator action.

requirements.title: Continuous environmental monitoring of the timing and payload bays
requirements.description: Bay temperature and humidity shall be monitored continuously, with the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) oven temperature and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) bay temperature sampled at no less than one reading per minute and forwarded to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013); an excursion outside the approved band shall raise an alarm within 5 minutes rather than at the next scheduled walk-round. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The telemetry record shows no gap longer than 60 seconds between readings over a 14-day window.
An injected out-of-band reading raises an alarm at LRU-013 within 5 minutes.
The approved temperature and humidity bands are stated numerically in the bay environmental record.

requirements.title: Water isolation valves for the integration bay
requirements.description: The water isolation valves serving the space above and adjacent to the WS-X90 integration rack holding the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall be identified on the bay drawing, reachable without a ladder, and known by location to the two named duty staff on each shift. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every relevant valve appears on the current bay drawing with a location reference.
Each valve can be reached and operated from floor level without a ladder or platform.
Both named duty staff on the sampled shift can point to each valve without consulting the drawing.

requirements.title: Authorisation and recording of LRU movement across the facility boundary
requirements.description: No WS-X90 line-replaceable unit shall enter or leave the integration facility without a movement authorisation naming the unit serial number and the receiving custodian, and the movement shall be posted against the asset entry in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) on the same working day — covering at minimum the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) spares pool. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every movement in the sampled month has an authorisation naming a serial number and a receiving custodian.
The LRU-020 asset entry posting date is no later than the working day of the physical movement.
No unit is found on site whose last recorded movement is an outbound one.

requirements.title: Alternate work site rules for the maintenance laptop
requirements.description: The Platform Lead shall be able to walk through the approved list of alternate work sites at which the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) may be used, the controls required at each — locked storage between sessions, no unattended session, and no network connection other than the link to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) — and the reporting path a technician uses to raise a security incident from such a site. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The interviewee names the approved alternate sites without reference to an uncontrolled list.
The interviewee states the storage, attendance and connectivity rules that apply at each site.
The interviewee names the incident reporting contact and the time limit for raising a report.

requirements.title: Classification marking on protected mission hardware
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall each carry a durable external marking stating the highest impact level of information the unit is approved to process, store or transmit, positioned so that it is readable with the unit installed and without removing a cover. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three units carries a marking that survives a solvent wipe and a scuff check.
Each marking is readable in situ, with the unit racked and all covers fitted.
The stated impact level on each marking matches the level recorded for that unit in the system record.

requirements.title: Classification and conditional-use marking on ground support hardware
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall each carry a durable marking stating the highest impact level of information they are approved to hold, and the Maintenance Laptop marking shall additionally state its conditional-use status so that it is not drawn from controlled storage for an activity outside its bounded maintenance role. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Both units carry a legible impact-level marking on an external surface.
The LRU-019 marking states conditional use and names the authority that releases it from storage.
No unmarked provisioning or maintenance endpoint is found in the controlled storage inventory.

requirements.title: Hazard assessment for the support facility location
requirements.description: The siting record for the facility holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the controlled storage for the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall state the flood, seismic and adjacent-industrial hazards considered, and any residual hazard that cannot be engineered out shall be carried in the WS-X90 risk register rather than closed out in the facility file. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The siting record names each of the three hazard classes and the assessment basis used.
Every residual hazard in the siting record has a matching entry in the WS-X90 risk register.
No hazard is recorded as closed in the facility file without a corresponding engineering change.

requirements.title: Supply chain risk management procedure set for WS-X90
requirements.description: Aurora Defense Systems shall maintain a WS-X90 supply chain risk management procedure set that names the accountable official and is issued to the engineering and procurement staff who release baselines through the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and provision hardware at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017); the set shall be reviewed and reissued at least annually and following any change of prime supplier for a criticality-ranked item. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The issued copy carries an approval date within the last 12 months.
The distribution record covers every named baseline releaser and provisioning operator.
A prime supplier change in the last cycle has a matching out-of-cycle review entry.

requirements.title: WS-X90 supply chain risk management plan and its protection
requirements.description: The WS-X90 supply chain risk management plan shall cover design, manufacture, delivery, integration, sustainment and disposal for the criticality-ranked items — at minimum the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) — shall be reviewed at least annually, and shall be held as a controlled item in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) readable only by the named SCRM distribution list. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The plan addresses each of the six life-cycle phases for LRU-003 and LRU-004 by name.
The last review entry is dated within 12 months of the assessment date.
An account outside the SCRM distribution list is refused read access to the plan in LRU-020.

requirements.title: Standing supply chain risk management team and its decision rights
requirements.description: A standing WS-X90 supply chain risk management team drawn from programme security, procurement and firmware engineering shall be able to state which of its members clears a new supplier into the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) signing chain, and who approves a baseline entering the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) from a newly qualified source. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The interviewee names the current team members and the function each represents.
The interviewee identifies the single role that clears a supplier into the LRU-002 signing chain.
The interviewee describes the approval step that gates a first baseline from a new source into LRU-020.

requirements.title: Second qualified source for navigation and timing critical items
requirements.description: The Navigation Processor (LRU-004), the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall each carry either a second qualified source or a documented and approved single-source risk acceptance, recorded against the item in the programme parts list before the next production lot is released. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three items has either a second qualified source or a signed single-source acceptance.
Every single-source acceptance names an approver and an expiry date.
No production lot has been released for an item whose parts-list entry is blank on this field.

requirements.title: Blind-buy and destination obfuscation for targeted procurement
requirements.description: Procurement of the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall be placed so that the supplier order record does not name WS-X90 or its end use, and the shipping destination on the order shall be a general receiving address rather than the programme integration facility. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No sampled purchase order for LRU-003 or LRU-008 names WS-X90, the programme code or the end use.
The ship-to address on each sampled order is the general receiving address.
The internal cross-reference tying the order back to the programme is held outside the supplier-visible record.

requirements.title: Flow-down of supply chain clauses to payload sub-tier suppliers
requirements.description: The supply chain security clauses in the prime contracts covering the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall appear unaltered in each sub-tier contract, and the prime shall be able to produce the sub-tier clause listing on request within 10 working days. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The clause text in each sampled sub-tier contract matches the prime contract text without amendment.
A clause listing request issued during the assessment is answered within 10 working days.
Every sub-tier supplier for the three payload items appears on the listing returned.

requirements.title: Unbroken provenance chain for signed release material
requirements.description: Every firmware release staged by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall trace back through the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) to a build record naming the source revision, the build host and the signing key identifier used by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) trust chain; a release whose provenance chain has a missing link shall be refused at staging rather than flagged after installation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each staged release resolves to a build record carrying all three provenance fields.
A release with a deliberately removed build record is refused by LRU-016 at staging.
The signing key identifier in the build record matches a key trusted by the LRU-002 chain.

requirements.title: Sustainment stock for long-lead navigation, timing and telemetry items
requirements.description: The programme shall hold, or have contractually committed, sustainment stock for the Timing Receiver (LRU-005), the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) sufficient to cover the quoted supplier lead time plus 6 months, and the holding shall be re-reviewed whenever a supplier issues an end-of-life or last-time-buy notice. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Held plus committed quantity for each item covers quoted lead time plus 6 months at the current consumption rate.
Each of the three items has a recorded quoted lead time no older than the last supplier review.
An end-of-life notice received in the last cycle has a matching dated stock re-review.

requirements.title: Pre-acceptance assessment of components, tools and updates
requirements.description: No component, development tool or firmware update shall be accepted into the WS-X90 baseline until an assessment record exists for it covering supplier standing, signature verification result and known-vulnerability check, and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall refuse to stage any package whose assessment record is absent from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every package accepted in the sampled period has an assessment record carrying all three fields.
A package with no assessment record in LRU-020 is refused at LRU-016 staging.
Assessment records are dated on or before the acceptance date of the package they cover.

requirements.title: Annual and event-driven supplier assessment and review
requirements.description: Suppliers of the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall be assessed and reviewed at least annually or as necessitated by events, where an event includes a change of supplier ownership, a reported compromise at the supplier, or a counterfeit finding elsewhere in the sector affecting the same part family. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three suppliers has a completed review dated within the last 12 months.
The review procedure lists the three event triggers explicitly.
An event that occurred in the last cycle has a matching out-of-cycle review record.

requirements.title: Independent testing of critical supplied elements before lot acceptance
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall each be subjected to independent third-party testing before first lot acceptance, covering as a minimum undocumented interface discovery and a comparison of delivered firmware against the supplier-declared hash. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An independent test report exists for each item and predates the lot acceptance date.
The report states the interfaces found and reconciles them against the supplier interface declaration.
The delivered firmware hash matches the supplier-declared value, or the mismatch is raised as a finding.

requirements.title: Operations security handling of WS-X90 supply chain information
requirements.description: Supply chain information for WS-X90 — parts lists, supplier names, lot quantities and delivery schedules — shall be handled at the sensitivity of the aggregate rather than of the individual item, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the programme parts list behind the same access rule as the signed release baselines. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The parts list in LRU-020 is subject to the same access rule as the release baselines.
The handling instruction states the aggregate sensitivity, not only the per-item sensitivity.

requirements.title: Compromise notification agreements with critical suppliers
requirements.description: The supply agreements for the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall oblige the supplier to notify the programme of a supply chain compromise affecting the delivered part family within 30 days of the supplier becoming aware, and to provide the results of any audit or assessment that identified it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Both agreements contain a notification clause with an explicit 30-day limit.
Each agreement names the programme contact to whom notification is sent.
Each agreement obliges the supplier to release the underlying audit or assessment result.

requirements.title: Tamper protection on the mission computing protected units
requirements.description: The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall each be enclosed so that opening the enclosure breaks a serialised tamper seal and, for LRU-003, zeroises key material held inside the protected boundary; seal serial numbers shall be recorded at build and re-checked at every depot induction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three units carries a seal whose serial matches its build record.
Opening an LRU-003 sample enclosure leaves no recoverable key material in the protected boundary.
The depot induction record shows a seal serial check for every unit inducted in the sampled period.

requirements.title: Latched tamper detection on the payload interface units
requirements.description: The Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011), the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall each raise a latched tamper indication on enclosure opening that survives a power cycle and remains readable at the next maintenance session; a bench trial shall show the latch set in 10 of 10 open-and-repower attempts. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The tamper latch is set in all 10 trials on each of the three units.
The latch state survives a full power cycle and is readable at the maintenance interface afterwards.
Clearing the latch requires an authorised maintenance action and is itself recorded.

requirements.title: Anti-tamper measures carried through the development life cycle
requirements.description: Anti-tamper measures for the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall be specified at design review, verified at first article inspection, and re-verified at each production lot acceptance, rather than added as a packaging step immediately before shipment. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design review record for each unit contains a specified anti-tamper section.
The first article inspection report records a verification result against that section.
Each accepted production lot has a re-verification entry referencing the same section.

requirements.title: Receiving inspection for tamper on delivered navigation and radio units
requirements.description: Every Navigation Processor (LRU-004), Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall be inspected on receipt against the supplier-supplied photograph and seal serial list before it is entered into stock, and a unit whose seal serial does not match the list shall be quarantined rather than reworked into the stream. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every unit received in the sampled period has a signed receiving inspection record before its stock entry date.
Each record states the seal serial read and the expected serial from the supplier list.
Any mismatch in the sampled period resulted in a quarantine record rather than a rework.

requirements.title: Field tamper inspection at maintenance induction
requirements.description: At every maintenance induction the technician shall check the tamper seals on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) and record the seal serial read against the expected value; a mismatch shall stop the maintenance action and raise an incident before any maintenance session is opened. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every induction in the sampled period carries a recorded seal serial for all three units.
A seeded mismatch stops the induction and produces an incident record before session open.
No maintenance session in the sampled period was opened without a preceding seal check record.

requirements.title: Counterfeit detection training for provisioning and maintenance staff
requirements.description: Staff who provision hardware at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or draw the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) from controlled storage shall be able to describe the marking, packaging and date-code checks that distinguish an authentic part from a counterfeit, and to name the route by which a suspect part is quarantined. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The interviewee describes at least three distinct authenticity checks without prompting.
The interviewee names the quarantine route and the person who is notified.
The interviewee's training record shows completion within the current training cycle.

requirements.title: Configuration control over components in the service and repair loop
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 line-replaceable unit awaiting service, in repair, or repaired and awaiting return to service shall hold an open custody record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) naming its physical location and configuration state; no unit shall be returned to service until the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) has reflashed it to the approved baseline and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) has recorded the closing check. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every unit in the repair loop at the time of the check has an open LRU-020 custody record with a location.
No unit returned to service in the sampled period lacks an LRU-016 reflash record to the approved baseline.
Each closing check in LRU-014 is dated on or after its matching reflash record.

requirements.title: Disposal of protected storage, key-bearing and maintenance units
requirements.description: A retired Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) or Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be zeroised and then physically destroyed, with a two-person destruction certificate naming the unit serial number and the method used; no such unit shall leave programme custody intact for resale or salvage. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each retired unit in the sampled period has a destruction certificate signed by two named people.
Each certificate states the zeroisation step and the physical destruction method separately.
The asset register shows no unit of these three types disposed of as intact salvage.

requirements.title: Access control policy and procedure baseline held under signature
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the approved WS-X90 access control policy and its associated procedures as a single signed, version-controlled baseline, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to issue a technician procedure package that cites a superseded policy revision. The policy and each procedure shall carry a review record dated at least annually, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-1, and an additional review shall be recorded within 30 days of any change to the effective control set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: LRU-020 holds exactly one approved revision of the access control policy, signed and dated within the last 12 months.
Every procedure package issued by LRU-017 in the last 90 days cites the current approved policy revision.
A review record exists dated on or after the 2026-09-08 change to the effective control set.

requirements.title: Account lifecycle actions synchronised to the log collector within 60 seconds
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall apply account create, modify, enable, disable and remove actions only through its account service, and shall publish each completed action as a structured record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 seconds with no operator step between the two. A direct write to the on-disk account store outside the account service shall be rejected and shall raise an integrity alarm inside the same 60-second window. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A create, a modify, a disable and a remove action each appear at LRU-018 within 60 seconds of execution at LRU-013.
A direct write to the LRU-013 account store outside the account service raises an integrity alarm and leaves the store unchanged.
No account action in a 30-day sample required an operator to re-enter it at LRU-018.

requirements.title: Temporary and emergency accounts expire and disable within 72 hours
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall stamp every temporary and emergency maintenance account with an expiry no more than 72 hours after creation, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(2), and shall automatically disable rather than delete the account at expiry so its history stays reviewable. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall reject a session offered by an expired account using the expiry carried inside the session credential, even when LRU-013 is unreachable. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No temporary or emergency account in the LRU-013 store carries an expiry more than 72 hours after its creation timestamp.
An expired temporary account is present and disabled, not absent, in the account store.
LRU-014 refuses an expired credential with the management link to LRU-013 disconnected.

requirements.title: Platform accounts disabled within 72 hours of expiry, disassociation or violation
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall disable a platform account within 72 hours of the account reaching its expiry date, of the holder ceasing to be associated with the WS-X90 programme, or of a recorded access policy violation, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(3), and shall stamp the triggering condition onto the disable record so the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) can report per-trigger counts. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every disable record in the sample carries exactly one of the three trigger codes.
The interval from trigger to disable is 72 hours or less for every account in the sample.
LRU-018 can produce a per-trigger disable count for a chosen 30-day window.

requirements.title: Ground support accounts disabled after 90 days without a successful authentication
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall run a daily inactivity sweep across ground support accounts and disable any account with no successful authentication in the previous 90 days, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(3)d, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall refuse offline logon with a cached credential older than the same 90 days so a disconnected laptop cannot outlive the sweep. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The sweep log shows one run per day for the last 30 days with no gap.
No enabled ground support account has a last-successful-authentication timestamp older than 90 days.
LRU-019 rejects a cached credential aged past 90 days with the network detached.

requirements.title: Account changes are abandoned rather than completed unaudited
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall emit an audit record for every account create, modify, enable, disable and remove action naming the actor, the target account, the action and the authorising role, shall write that record to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) before acknowledging the action to the operator, and shall notify the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). A failure to write the audit record shall cause the account action to be abandoned rather than completed unaudited. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every account action in a 30-day sample has a matching LRU-015 audit record with all four fields populated.
With LRU-015 write access removed, an attempted account change fails and leaves the account unchanged.
LRU-018 received a notification for every account action in the sample.

requirements.title: Technicians log out at the end of the standard work period
requirements.description: Provisioning and maintenance technicians shall log out of the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) at the end of their standard work period rather than leaving an authenticated session locked overnight, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(5), as directed in the WS-X90 ground support operating instruction. Each station shall display the count of sessions left open at the previous shift change to the next technician who signs on. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A technician can describe the end-of-shift logout step and name the instruction that carries it.
The sign-on banner on LRU-017 reports the count of sessions left open at the previous shift change.
The operating instruction that defines the standard work period is the current approved revision.

requirements.title: Platform privilege is carried by named roles, never attached to an account
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall assign platform privilege only through named roles held in the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), with no privilege attached directly to an individual account, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall accept a privileged operation only when the presented role is one of the four approved privileged roles. Any change to the membership of a privileged role shall be recorded with a reviewer name and date before the next mission load. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No account in the LRU-013 store carries a privilege bit outside a named role.
LRU-001 rejects a privileged operation presented with a role name outside the approved four.
Every privileged role membership change in the last 60 days carries a reviewer name and date.

requirements.title: Exactly one shared account exists and every action under it is individually attributed
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall permit exactly one shared account — the flight line pre-launch check account on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) — and only under two recorded conditions: a named technician signs the account out for a single sortie turn, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) tags every action taken under it with that technician's individual identifier. No other shared or group account shall exist on any WS-X90 LRU. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The account inventory on LRU-014 lists one shared account and no group accounts.
A technician can produce the sign-out record for a named sortie turn.
Every action in the LRU-019 log taken under the shared account carries an individual identifier.

requirements.title: Mission accounts bound to mission phase, ground station and time window
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall bind each privileged mission account to a usage condition set of permitted mission phase, permitted ground station identity and permitted time window, and shall refuse authentication outside that set; the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall reject a payload command from an account whose mission-phase condition does not include the current phase. The condition set is designed and under review, and enforcement is scheduled for the 4.4 mission software build. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved design record names the three condition types and the permitted values for each.
The 4.4 mission software build plan carries the enforcement work item with an accepted entry criterion.

requirements.title: Atypical account usage raised to the platform controller for analyst review
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall compare each authentication and each privileged action against the account's established pattern of ground station, time of day and command class, and shall raise an atypical-usage alert to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) for analyst review. Baselines and alert thresholds are defined in the WS-X90 log analytics design record; the correlation rules are not yet fielded. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The analytics design record defines the three pattern dimensions and the alert threshold for each.
A dated build item exists for the correlation rule set with a named owner.

requirements.title: High-risk determination disables all of an individual's accounts within 30 minutes
requirements.description: On receipt of a high-risk determination from the programme security office, the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall disable every account held by the named individual within 30 minutes, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(13), and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall revoke that individual's provisioning credential in the same run. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A rehearsed determination results in all of the individual's accounts disabled within 30 minutes of entry.
The individual's provisioning credential on LRU-017 is revoked in the same run.
Elapsed time from entry to last disable is recorded in the run log.

requirements.title: Discretionary sharing confined to draft ground mission plans
requirements.description: Discretionary sharing shall exist only in the ground mission-planning data area: the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall let a plan author grant read access on their own draft plan to another named author, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall refuse any discretionary grant on an approved release baseline, on signed configuration or on any airborne object. No LRU on the aircraft shall support a discretionary grant of any kind. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved design record states the covered object set as draft mission plans only.
The design record states that approved baselines and signed configuration in LRU-020 are non-discretionary.
No airborne LRU appears in the covered subject and object set.

requirements.title: Encrypted flows are inspected or blocked, never passed uninspected
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall block any outbound flow it cannot inspect, including an encrypted payload whose key is not held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), rather than passing it uninspected. Where the flow is one of the three approved encrypted tunnels, LRU-003 shall present the decrypted flow to the gateway inspection path before release, and a flow that fails inspection shall have its session terminated within 5 seconds of detection. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An outbound encrypted flow outside the three approved tunnels does not leave LRU-007.
An approved tunnel is visible to the LRU-007 inspection path in cleartext form.
A session carrying disallowed content is terminated within 5 seconds of detection.

requirements.title: Security functions authorised against the role table, re-checked at the crypto module
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall hold the enumerated list of WS-X90 security functions — key use requests to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), audit configuration, access policy load and boot policy change — and shall authorise each one only to the role named for it in the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) role table. LRU-003 shall independently check the presented role before performing a key operation rather than trusting the calling service. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The enumerated security function list on LRU-001 matches the approved list item for item.
LRU-003 refuses a key operation presented with a role not named for that function.
A role table change made at LRU-013 takes effect at LRU-001 without a software reload.

requirements.title: Privileged role holders use a separate non-privileged account for nonsecurity work
requirements.description: A person holding a WS-X90 privileged role shall hold a separate non-privileged account for nonsecurity work, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall refuse to open mission planning, telemetry review or documentation tasks under a privileged role, which is the class of function the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-6(2) reserves. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall issue the two accounts as a pair so a privileged role cannot be issued without its non-privileged counterpart. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every privileged role holder in the LRU-013 store has a matching non-privileged account.
LRU-001 refuses a mission planning session opened under a privileged role.
The exception list of dual-purpose legacy accounts is dated and carries a closure date.

requirements.title: Privileged commands cross the boundary on one approved path only
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall permit a privileged command to cross the external boundary only over the single approved maintenance path to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), and shall drop a privileged command arriving on any other interface without forwarding it. Each privileged command reaching LRU-014 over the network shall carry the operational need code recorded in the system security plan. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A privileged command offered on a non-maintenance interface is dropped at LRU-007 and logged.
The approved privileged network path list on LRU-007 contains exactly one entry.
Privileged commands in the LRU-014 session log carry an operational need code.

requirements.title: Privileged roles held only by individuals on the approved personnel list
requirements.description: Privileged roles on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall be held only by individuals on the current approved privileged-personnel list, and LRU-013 shall refuse a role assignment to an identity absent from that list at the moment of assignment rather than flagging it at a later review. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every privileged role holder on both LRUs appears on the current approved list.
An assignment to an off-list identity is refused at the point of assignment and logged.

requirements.title: Privileged assignments reviewed every 180 days against actual privileged activity
requirements.description: The System Security Engineer shall review every WS-X90 privileged role assignment at least every 180 days and on each change to a role definition, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall present the review worksheet with the preceding 180 days of privileged activity for each holder, drawn from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), so the reviewer can judge whether the privilege is still needed. An assignment not reconfirmed in a review shall be reduced to non-privileged. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A completed review worksheet exists dated within the last 180 days.
The worksheet shows per-holder privileged activity, not only the assignment list.
The reviewer can describe what happens to an assignment that is not reconfirmed.

requirements.title: Signed images run at the privilege ceiling carried in the boot manifest
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall record the maximum privilege level permitted for each signed mission software image in its manifest, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall start each image at that level and refuse any request from the image to raise its own privilege above the manifest value, including for the three third-party mission libraries. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each signed image in the LRU-002 manifest carries a maximum privilege level field.
An image requesting a level above its manifest value is denied and the denial is logged.
The list of images running without a manifest level is dated and shrinking release over release.

requirements.title: Every privileged execution is logged, denied ones at the same fidelity
requirements.description: Every execution of a privileged function on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall produce an audit record naming the function, the role, the account and the outcome, and that record shall reach the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) whether the execution succeeded or was denied. A denied privileged execution shall be logged at the same fidelity as a successful one. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of ten sampled privileged executions has a record at LRU-018 with all four fields populated.
A denied privileged execution produces a record carrying the same fields as a successful one.
No privileged function on the enumerated list is absent from the logged function set.

requirements.title: Non-privileged sessions cannot reach a privileged function on any path
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall refuse a privileged function invoked from a non-privileged session, including through the mission scripting interface and the payload command path, and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall independently reject a payload configuration command that arrives without a privileged role assertion rather than relying on LRU-001 to have filtered it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A privileged function called from a non-privileged session on LRU-001 is refused and logged.
The mission scripting interface cannot reach a privileged function from a non-privileged session.
LRU-010 rejects a payload configuration command carrying no privileged role assertion.

requirements.title: Every account is limited to three concurrent sessions
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall limit every account, with no exception for privileged or service accounts, to a maximum of 3 concurrent sessions, which are the CNSSI 1253 parameter values for AC-10, and shall refuse a fourth session with an explicit reason rather than displacing an existing session. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A fourth concurrent session for any account is refused on both LRUs.
The refusal names the concurrent session limit as the reason.
No account type is configured on either LRU with a session limit other than 3.

requirements.title: Locked stations show an opaque surface with no mission data or window titles
requirements.description: On session lock the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall replace the entire display with an opaque lock surface carrying no mission data, no account name and no window titles, and shall not restore any part of the previous display until reauthentication has completed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No mission data, account name or window title is readable on the locked display of either LRU.
The previous display is not rendered at any point between reauthentication and unlock.

requirements.title: User logout terminates the session against every resource it reached
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall offer a logout action from every authenticated screen, and that action shall terminate the session against all resources the session reached, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-12(1), including open handles in the Configuration Repository and any maintenance session held open on a downstream LRU. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A logout action is reachable from every authenticated screen on both LRUs.
After logout no downstream maintenance session remains open for that session identifier.
Repository handles held by the session are released within 5 seconds of logout.

requirements.title: Session termination is announced on screen with its cause
requirements.description: On termination of an authenticated session, whether by user logout, by inactivity or by administrative disconnect, the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall display an explicit message naming the session as ended and stating which of the three causes applied, and shall clear that message only on the next authentication attempt. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the three termination causes produces a distinct on-screen message.
The message persists on screen until the next authentication attempt.

requirements.title: Only two actions are permitted without identification or authentication
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall permit exactly two actions without identification or authentication: assertion of the payload-safe state at the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) using the physical safing lever, and read-only display of the payload built-in-test summary on the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) front panel. Every other action on every LRU shall require an authenticated identity, and both permitted actions and their rationale shall be recorded in the system security plan. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The system security plan lists exactly these two actions with a written rationale for each.
The safing lever action on LRU-011 completes with no operator authenticated.
No action other than the two listed can be started on any LRU without authentication.

requirements.title: Classification and releasability bound to stored and in-process mission data
requirements.description: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall bind a classification attribute and a releasability attribute to every stored mission data object at the moment of write, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall carry the same two attributes with the object while it is in process so the binding survives a copy between mission partitions. Permitted values shall be drawn from the approved WS-X90 marking set, each attribute change shall be audited, and the marking set shall be reviewed for applicability every 90 days, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-16f; the binding mechanism is designed and scheduled for the 4.4 build. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved design record names the two attribute types and the permitted value set for each.
The design record states that a copy between mission partitions preserves the binding.
A 90-day applicability review of the approved marking set is scheduled with a named owner.

requirements.title: Attributes travel with data across the gateway and the internal switch
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall carry the classification and releasability attributes with every data object crossing them, and LRU-007 shall drop an outbound object whose attributes are absent or outside the approved marking set rather than releasing it unmarked. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The design record defines the on-the-wire attribute encoding for both LRUs.
The design record states the drop behaviour for an absent or out-of-set attribute.

requirements.title: Provisioning personnel apply and maintain data marking attributes
requirements.description: Provisioning personnel shall associate the approved classification and releasability attributes with each mission data object and each subject record they create at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and shall maintain that association when the object is revised in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), in accordance with the WS-X90 marking policy. No personnel-applied attribute workflow exists today and this requirement is carried unimplemented in the plan of action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An approved marking procedure naming the personnel responsibility exists.
A provisioning technician can walk through applying an attribute and maintaining it across a revision.

requirements.title: One signed attribute dictionary shared by the payload and transport LRUs
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall interpret the classification and releasability attribute encoding identically, using a single shared attribute dictionary issued as one signed artefact, so an object marked at one LRU is not downgraded or re-interpreted at another. A dictionary version mismatch between two LRUs shall halt attribute-bearing traffic between them. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: One signed dictionary artefact with a version field is defined for all three LRUs.
The design record states the halt behaviour on a dictionary version mismatch.

requirements.title: Remote maintenance sessions are observable while they are still open
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall record the start, end, source identity and command set of every remote maintenance session and shall stream those records to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) while the session is live rather than at session close, so an in-progress session can be observed and cut. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A live session appears at LRU-018 within 10 seconds of its start.
Commands issued in the session appear at LRU-018 while the session is still open.
The list of session channels not yet streamed live is dated and tracked to closure.

requirements.title: Remote maintenance sessions are protected by keys that never leave the crypto module
requirements.description: Every remote maintenance session terminated at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall have its confidentiality and integrity protection performed by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) using keys that never leave LRU-003, and LRU-014 shall refuse to establish a session when LRU-003 reports a degraded key state. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No remote maintenance traffic is observable in cleartext on the LRU-014 external interface.
Session establishment fails when LRU-003 reports a degraded key state.
No session key material is present in LRU-014 storage after a session ends.

requirements.title: All remote access routes through one managed access control point
requirements.description: All remote access to WS-X90 shall route through a single managed access control point — the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) forwarding to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) — and no other LRU shall expose an externally reachable remote access service. That path shall be recorded in the approved network baseline and any deviation shall be raised as a configuration finding. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved network baseline shows exactly one external remote access path.
No LRU other than LRU-007 exposes an externally reachable listening remote access service.

requirements.title: Remote privileged maintenance commands pass three admission checks
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall permit a privileged maintenance command from a remote Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) only when the command appears on the approved remote-privileged command list, the laptop presents a current device attestation, and the session falls inside a scheduled maintenance window. A command failing any of the three shall be refused and logged with its reason code. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A command absent from the approved remote-privileged list is refused at LRU-014.
A laptop failing device attestation cannot open a privileged session.
Refusals and their reason codes are present in the LRU-014 session log.

requirements.title: Remote privileged access over the mission network is limited to two documented needs
requirements.description: Remote privileged access over the mission network to the Mission Computer (LRU-001) through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall be limited to the two operational needs documented in the system security plan — in-flight security policy reload and audit configuration recovery — and each use shall cite its need code in the session record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The system security plan documents exactly two operational needs with a rationale for each.
Session records for the sampled uses cite one of the two need codes.

requirements.title: Remote access design information is held where maintenance sessions cannot read it
requirements.description: Design and configuration information describing the WS-X90 remote access mechanism — the gateway rule set, the device attestation scheme and the approved command lists — shall be held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with access limited to the named security engineering and platform roles, and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall hold the on-platform copy in a partition that a maintenance session cannot read. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-020 access list for the remote access design area names only the approved roles.
A maintenance session cannot read the LRU-015 partition holding the on-platform copy.
The list of documents still held outside the repository is dated and carries a migration date.

requirements.title: One operator action disconnects and disables all remote access within 30 seconds
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall provide a single operator action that disconnects all live remote sessions and disables new remote access, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall stop forwarding remote access traffic within 30 seconds of that action without requiring a reboot of either LRU. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: All live remote sessions are terminated within 30 seconds of the disconnect action.
New remote access attempts are refused at LRU-007 after the action.
Neither LRU requires a reboot to execute the action.

requirements.title: Remote commands are authenticated at the radio and again at the payload controller
requirements.description: Every remote command arriving over the tactical data link shall carry an authentication tag verified by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) before the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) passes it on, and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall independently verify the same tag before acting on a payload command rather than trusting the radio's verification. A command failing either check shall be discarded and counted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A remote command carrying an invalid authentication tag is discarded at LRU-008 and counted.
A payload command that passes LRU-008 but carries an invalid tag is discarded at LRU-010.
Discard counters for both LRUs are readable in the maintenance download.

requirements.title: Maintenance laptop configuration and connection baseline held under signature
requirements.description: The approved configuration and connection requirements for the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), including its use outside controlled maintenance areas, shall be held as a signed baseline in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and LRU-019 shall report its configuration hash at each connection so a drifted laptop is identifiable before it is admitted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A signed configuration and connection baseline for LRU-019 exists in LRU-020.
LRU-019 reports its configuration hash at each connection attempt.
The out-of-area annex carries a named owner and a scheduled approval date.

requirements.title: Laptop connections are admitted only on register, hash and release
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall admit a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) only when the laptop appears on the approved device register, its reported configuration hash matches the signed baseline, and a named authorising engineer has released it for the current maintenance activity. An unregistered or drifted laptop shall be refused and the attempt logged. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unregistered laptop is refused at LRU-014 and the attempt is logged.
A laptop whose configuration hash differs from the signed baseline is refused.
The device register held by LRU-014 is the current approved revision.

requirements.title: Maintenance laptop storage is fully encrypted and hardware bound
requirements.description: The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall protect all stored WS-X90 data with full-device encryption bound to platform hardware, covering all mobile computers and devices that process organisation data, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-19(5), and shall present no readable programme data when the device is powered off and its storage is read on another host. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every enrolled maintenance laptop reports full-device encryption enabled.
Storage removed from a powered-off laptop yields no readable programme data on another host.
The encryption key is bound to device hardware, not to a user passphrase alone.

requirements.title: Releasing official can compare partner authorisations against record markings
requirements.description: Before the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) exports a security log extract to a partner programme, the authorised releasing official shall be able to see in one view the partner's access authorisations alongside the marking of every record in the extract, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the approved sharing circumstances against which that comparison is made. The comparison view is designed but not yet built. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The approved information sharing circumstances are recorded in LRU-020 and current.
The releasing official can describe the comparison required before an extract is released.

requirements.title: The only public release path is reviewed before staging and quarterly after
requirements.description: WS-X90 operates no publicly accessible system; the only public release path is the programme's unclassified support documentation set staged in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and released through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). A named release official shall review each item before staging and shall re-review the released set quarterly or as new information is posted, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-22, removing any nonpublic content found. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The release official is named in the current approved release procedure.
The quarterly re-review cadence is scheduled with a named owner.
The staged public documentation set is identified and separated from the controlled baseline.

requirements.title: Bulk extraction of mission data and baselines is detected and limited
requirements.description: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall detect and limit bulk extraction against mission data and configuration baselines through query rate ceilings, per-role extraction volume limits and alerting on sequential full-set reads, so an authorised account cannot quietly enumerate an entire store. No extraction-pattern detection is implemented today and the requirement is carried in the plan of action. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An approved technique set naming the rate ceiling and the per-role volume limit exists.
A dated work item exists to field extraction-pattern detection with a named owner.

requirements.title: Contingency planning policy and recovery procedure set held under signature
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 contingency planning policy and the recovery procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, and shall flag any artifact whose recorded review date is more than 12 months old, meeting the at-least-annual review interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-1. Publication of a new revision shall run only through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and each publication shall record the distribution list of cybersecurity personnel and contingency role holders who received it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current policy artifact and each procedure artifact in LRU-020 carry a valid signature and a review date within the last 12 months.
A publication attempt from any endpoint other than LRU-017 is refused and written to the repository event log.
The distribution record for the most recent revision names a recipient for every assigned contingency role.

requirements.title: Single declaration starts both the contingency and incident response plans
requirements.description: When the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) declares a platform state that matches a contingency activation trigger, it shall raise one correlated event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) carrying both the contingency plan activation reference and the incident response plan reference, so that a single declaration starts both plans rather than two independent calls. The System Security Engineer shall be able to walk an assessor through the trigger table and state, for each trigger, which related plan it is cross-referenced to and who owns that plan. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The trigger table names a related plan and a plan owner for every contingency activation trigger.
A rehearsed activation produces one correlated event in LRU-018 carrying both plan references.
The engineer can identify at least one trigger that is not yet cross-referenced and the open action that will close it.

requirements.title: Essential mission functions resume within the plan's four-hour objective
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall restore the approved mission application baseline onto the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and return the essential mission functions listed in the WS-X90 contingency plan to service within the four-hour resumption objective that plan defines, measured from contingency plan activation to the first successful mission-function self-test. Functions the plan classifies as non-essential may be deferred beyond that window and shall be reported as deferred rather than counted as restored. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A timed restoration exercise records elapsed time from activation to first passing mission-function self-test.
Every function the contingency plan lists as essential passes its self-test inside four hours.
Deferred non-essential functions are listed by name in the exercise record.

requirements.title: Critical asset list generated from mission-essential flags in the baseline
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall carry a mission-essential designation on each LRU baseline record, and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall carry that designation because the loss of either ends the position and timing function that the essential mission functions depend on. The critical asset list shall be generated from those designations rather than maintained as a separate document, so that a baseline change that adds, removes or re-scopes an LRU changes the list in the same commit. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
