acceptance_criteria: The critical asset list is produced by a repository query, and re-running the query reproduces the list byte for byte.
LRU-004 and LRU-005 carry the mission-essential designation with a recorded rationale.
A baseline commit that changes an LRU designation shows a matching change in the generated list.

requirements.title: Recovery-role sessions gated on current contingency training
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall refuse to open a recovery-role session for a technician whose contingency-role training record, held on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) credential, is absent, dated more than 12 months ago, or dated more than 10 working days after that technician assumed the role — the 10-working-day and annual intervals CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-3. A refused session shall state the reason to the technician and raise a training-currency event. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A session request with a training record older than 12 months is refused and the refusal reason is recorded.
A session request from a technician trained within 10 working days of role assignment is admitted.
The gateway's training-currency events can be reconciled against the training records held on LRU-019.

requirements.title: Semi-annual restore exercise from sealed backup on a representative article
requirements.description: The semi-annual recovery exercise defined in the WS-X90 contingency plan shall restore a representative platform article from a Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) backup set through the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), and shall be recorded as a failed exercise if any restored partition fails its integrity check or if the measured restore duration exceeds the plan's four-hour objective. Each failed exercise shall raise a corrective action with a named owner before the next scheduled exercise. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The two most recent exercise records exist, are no more than seven months apart, and carry a measured restore duration.
Every restored partition in the most recent exercise passed its integrity check, or a corrective action is open against it.
Corrective actions raised by a failed exercise name an owner and a target date.

requirements.title: Contingency, incident and maintenance rehearsals run on one schedule
requirements.description: Each contingency plan test shall be scheduled jointly with the incident response exercise and the maintenance continuity rehearsal, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall retain the correlated event set produced by all three so that one after-action review reads a single timeline built from Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) state changes. The System Security Engineer shall be able to name the owner of each related plan and the agreed joint schedule for the coming year. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A single published schedule shows the contingency test, the incident response exercise and the maintenance rehearsal with their dates and owners.
The engineer can name the related-plan owner for each of the three activities.
LRU-018 retains one correlated event set per joint exercise rather than three unlinked sets.

requirements.title: Alternate storage facility holds retrievable backup and baseline sets
requirements.description: Backup sets produced from the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the signed baselines held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall be retrievable from the designated Aurora alternate storage facility under a written storage and retrieval agreement that names the custodian, the release approver and the maximum retrieval time. The retrieval path shall apply the same access approval and two-person handling rules that govern the primary facility. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A signed storage and retrieval agreement exists and names a custodian, a release approver and a maximum retrieval time.
A retrieval rehearsal produced a usable backup set and a usable baseline set within the agreed time.
The alternate facility's access approval and handling rules are recorded and compared line by line against the primary facility's rules.

requirements.title: Alternate storage separation recorded with the hazards it decorrelates
requirements.description: The alternate facility holding the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) replica shall be recorded in the contingency plan with its separation distance from the primary facility and the specific hazards that separation is intended to decorrelate — utility feed, flood plain, transport corridor and site access control — and the replica shall be verified as a hash-identical copy of the primary set before it is counted as the alternate. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The contingency plan records a separation distance and names each hazard the separation addresses.
The most recent replica verification shows a hash match against the primary repository set.
Any hazard shared by both facilities is listed as a residual with an owner.

requirements.title: Retrieval obstacles at the alternate storage site and their mitigations
requirements.description: The contingency plan shall list the access obstacles that would delay retrieval of Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) backup media from the alternate facility during an area-wide disruption, and shall name a mitigation and a responsible role for each obstacle. The Platform Lead shall be able to walk an assessor through the retrieval sequence, including who authorises release of the media and how the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) instance at the alternate facility is brought into service. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The plan lists at least one obstacle per access route with a named mitigation and role.
The Platform Lead can walk through the retrieval sequence without reading from an unpublished note.
The release authorisation step names a specific role rather than an organisation.

requirements.title: Staged transfer of mission-support operations to a second integration facility
requirements.description: A written agreement shall make a second Aurora integration facility available to host a Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build and a Mission Computer (LRU-001) integration article sufficient to resume the mission-support operations named in the contingency plan within its five working-day transfer objective. Because WS-X90 is categorised A:moderate, the agreement covers a staged transfer with equipment delivered on call, not a continuously warm standby, and the plan shall say so explicitly. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A signed agreement names the alternate facility, the operations it must carry and the five working-day transfer objective.
The equipment list required to stand up LRU-017 and an LRU-001 integration article is recorded with a delivery commitment.
The contingency plan states that the alternate site is a staged transfer consistent with the moderate availability categorisation.

requirements.title: Alternate processing facility separated from the primary integration site
requirements.description: The alternate processing facility that would host the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build shall be recorded with its separation from the primary integration site and with the threat set that separation is intended to decorrelate, and shall not depend on the primary site's power feed, network entry or badge system. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The recorded separation distance and independent utility and network entries are documented for the alternate facility.
No dependency of the alternate facility on the primary site's badge system or network entry is listed as unresolved.

requirements.title: Accessibility analysis for the alternate processing facility
requirements.description: The contingency plan shall record the accessibility problems that would prevent staff and equipment from reaching the alternate processing facility during an area-wide disruption, with an explicit mitigation for each, so that the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build can actually be stood up rather than only nominated. No such analysis exists for WS-X90 today. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An accessibility analysis for the alternate processing facility exists and is referenced from the contingency plan.
Each identified accessibility problem carries a named mitigation and a responsible role.

requirements.title: Priority-of-service provisions in the alternate processing site agreement
requirements.description: The agreement covering the alternate processing facility shall carry priority-of-service provisions aligned to the recovery time objective in the contingency plan, so that the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build is not queued behind other tenants of the same facility. The current draft agreement carries no such provision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The executed agreement contains a priority-of-service clause referencing the contingency plan recovery time objective.
The clause names the recovery time objective it supports rather than a generic best-effort commitment.

requirements.title: Tactical data radio carries mission data when the primary bearer is lost
requirements.description: The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall carry the mission data operations the WS-X90 contingency plan names as essential when the primary ground bearer is unavailable, and shall reach the plan's 30-minute resumption objective for those operations, measured from loss-of-bearer declaration to the first acknowledged message on the alternate path. Operations the plan does not name shall stay suspended rather than compete for the reduced-capacity path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A bearer-loss test records the elapsed time to the first acknowledged message on the radio path.
Every operation the plan names as essential completes at least once on the alternate path during the test.
Non-essential traffic is observably suppressed while the alternate path is active.

requirements.title: Gateway fails over to the alternate bearer with an unchanged policy set
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall detect loss of the primary telecommunications bearer within 60 seconds and shall re-establish the protected tunnel over the alternate bearer without an operator re-keying step, applying the same policy set on both bearers so that no traffic class reaches a destination on the alternate path that it may not reach on the primary. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A bearer-loss test shows detection within 60 seconds and tunnel re-establishment without operator key entry.
A policy comparison across the two bearer profiles reports no permitted flow present on one and absent on the other.
The failover event is recorded with both bearer identifiers.

requirements.title: Priority-of-service provisions in both telecommunications agreements
requirements.description: Both the primary and the alternate telecommunications service agreements supporting the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall carry priority-of-service provisions consistent with the recovery time objective in the contingency plan, and the agreement file shall record, for each common-carrier service, whether a Telecommunications Service Priority request was submitted, its reference, or the reason the service is out of scope. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each executed telecommunications agreement contains a priority-of-service clause tied to the recovery time objective.
Every common-carrier service in the file carries either a submitted priority request reference or a recorded non-applicability rationale.

requirements.title: Primary and alternate communications paths proven disjoint end to end
requirements.description: The primary and alternate telecommunications paths shall not share a transmission line, a carrier point of presence, or an on-platform port group. A path-disjointness test shall trace both paths from the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) through the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) to the carrier demarcation and shall fail if any element appears on both traces. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Both path traces are produced from live configuration rather than from a drawing.
No transmission line or carrier point of presence appears on both traces.
Any shared on-platform element is recorded as an accepted single point of failure with a risk reference.

requirements.title: Monthly verification and partial restore of every sealed backup set
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall verify every backup set held on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) at least monthly by recomputing the set's hash tree and restoring at least one randomly selected partition to a scratch volume — the at-least-monthly interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-9(1). A verification that fails, or that has not run within 31 days of the previous one, shall raise a maintenance alert that cannot be cleared without a passing verification. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The three most recent verification records exist and no gap between consecutive records exceeds 31 days.
Each record names the partition selected for restore and reports its integrity result.
An induced hash mismatch raises a maintenance alert that survives a controller restart.

requirements.title: Sealed backup sets reach the alternate facility within five working days
requirements.description: A backup set sealed on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall reach the alternate storage facility within five working days of sealing, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall record the transfer with the set identifier, the sealing hash and the receiving custodian. A set with no transfer record after five working days shall be reported as a recovery-point gap against the contingency plan's recovery point objective. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every sealed set in the last quarter has a transfer record naming its sealing hash and receiving custodian.
No set in the last quarter took more than five working days from sealing to recorded receipt, or the exception is reported as a recovery-point gap.
The receiving custodian's recorded hash matches the sealing hash for each transferred set.

requirements.title: Backup sets encrypted and integrity-tagged before the set is sealed
requirements.description: Backup sets at rest on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall be encrypted and integrity-tagged as a whole set before sealing, and the module shall refuse to mark a set sealed unless both operations completed. A direct read of the raw backup partition shall yield no recoverable configuration, audit or key-shadow content. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A raw read of the backup partition returns no plaintext configuration or audit strings under inspection.
An attempt to seal a set with the integrity tag suppressed is refused and logged.
Altering one byte of a sealed set causes the integrity tag check to fail on the next verification.

requirements.title: Backup key material confined to the cryptographic services module
requirements.description: Backup encryption and integrity keys shall be generated, wrapped and used inside the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and shall never leave it in cleartext. The module shall serve a backup wrap or unwrap operation only to the storage role identity that seals and opens backup sets, and shall reject and log the request from any other role identity, including a maintenance role. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No interface on LRU-003 returns a backup key in cleartext under test.
A wrap request presented under a maintenance role identity is rejected and logged with the requesting identity.
Backup key generation events are recorded with the role identity that requested them.

requirements.title: Update transactions journalled and rolled back to an attested image
requirements.description: An update or configuration transaction staged by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall be journalled with a commit record, and an interruption before commit shall leave the platform on the previous known-good image with the partial transaction discarded. The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall attest the image the platform actually booted after the recovery, and the transaction shall be marked complete only when that attestation matches the intended image. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Power interruption during a staged update leaves the platform booting the previous known-good image.
The transaction journal shows the interrupted transaction as discarded, not as complete.
The post-recovery boot attestation from LRU-002 is recorded and compared against the intended image digest.

requirements.title: Payload command transactions replayed to a known state after reset
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall journal each payload command transaction with its authorization reference and the interlock state reported by the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) at the moment of issue, and after any reset shall replay the journal to reconstruct the last committed payload state before it accepts a new command. The Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall report the reconstructed state so it can be compared with observed payload behaviour. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A forced reset mid-sequence results in a reconstructed state that matches the last committed journal entry.
No new command is accepted by LRU-010 until replay has completed.
The reconstructed state reported by LRU-012 is recorded alongside the journal replay result.

requirements.title: Assessment and monitoring procedure set held under signature and review
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 assessment, authorization and continuous monitoring procedure set as signed artifacts, each carrying a named approver and a review date, and shall flag any artifact whose review date is more than 12 months old — the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CA-1. Publication shall run only through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) so that every revision carries an operator identity and a diff against the prior revision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every artifact in the set carries a named approver and a review date within the last 12 months.
The repository flags an artifact whose review date is deliberately aged past 12 months in test.
Each published revision carries an operator identity and a diff against its predecessor.

requirements.title: Assessor role separated from every engineering role
requirements.description: The independent assessment team shall hold an assessor role on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) that can read configuration and health state and can export the correlated record set from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), and that cannot change a configuration item, clear an audit record, or approve a remediation action. The assessor role shall be provisioned separately from every engineering role so that no individual both builds and assesses the same control. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The assessor role definition on LRU-013 grants no write, clear or approve permission.
No account holds both an assessor role and an engineering role at the same time.
An export from LRU-018 under the assessor role succeeds and is itself recorded as an access event.

requirements.title: Specialised data-leakage and malicious-user assessments each cycle
requirements.description: The assessment programme shall add, once per authorization cycle, an announced data-leakage assessment against the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) egress paths and an unannounced malicious-user exercise against a Mission Computer (LRU-001) operator account. Each shall produce a result naming the paths or accounts exercised and what was observed, not only a completion date. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The assessment plan schedules both activities within the current authorization cycle and marks which is announced.
The data-leakage result enumerates the egress paths exercised on LRU-007.
The malicious-user result names the operator account privileges exercised on LRU-001.

requirements.title: No external exchange enabled without a signed exchange agreement
requirements.description: Every external information exchange carried by the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) or the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall be covered by a signed exchange agreement recording the interface characteristics, the impact level of the information carried, the controls each party operates and the party responsible for each, and no exchange shall be enabled in the gateway policy set before that agreement exists. Agreements shall be reviewed at least annually and on any change to the interface. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each enabled exchange in the LRU-007 policy set maps to a signed agreement identifier.
Each agreement records the impact level of the information carried and the responsible party for each control.
Any exchange running under an interim approval is listed with its expiry and the agreement it awaits.

requirements.title: Write authorization verified before inbound data is accepted
requirements.description: Before accepting data written into WS-X90 from an interconnected system, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall verify that the sending identity holds a current write authorization for the destination data set, and shall reject and log the transfer when it does not. The Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) outbound path shall apply the same check in reverse, releasing telemetry only to a receiver holding a recorded read authorization. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A write from an identity with no recorded authorization is rejected by LRU-007 and logged with the identity and destination.
A write from an authorized identity to a data set outside its authorization is also rejected.
The LRU-012 release path checks a recorded read authorization rather than link-layer identity alone.

requirements.title: Authorization decision recorded, inherited controls accepted, expiry visible
requirements.description: The authorization decision for SYS-WSX90, the named authorizing official, and the set of common controls the system inherits shall be recorded as a signed artifact in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall report the authorization reference and its expiry as part of platform status. The record shall be updated at least every three years and on any significant change to the system or its operating environment, matching the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CA-6. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The signed authorization artifact names the authorizing official and lists each inherited common control accepted.
LRU-013 platform status reports the current authorization reference and expiry date.
A significant-change trigger since the last decision is either reflected in an updated authorization or carried as an open action.

requirements.title: Independent monitoring team receives the dataset directly
requirements.description: The independent monitoring team shall receive the continuous monitoring dataset directly from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) on the agreed cadence, rather than through the engineering organisation that operates the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013). The System Security Engineer shall be able to state which control families that team monitors independently and which remain self-assessed, and why. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The delivery path from LRU-018 to the independent team does not pass through an engineering-held staging step.
The engineer can list the families under independent monitoring and the families still self-assessed.
The cadence of the last four deliveries matches the agreed cadence.

requirements.title: Monitoring cadence changes justified by an observed trend
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall retain at least 12 months of control-monitoring outcomes in a form that supports comparison across periods, and each revision of the monitoring strategy shall cite the trend it responds to — a control whose failure rate is rising, or a check whose result has not changed across four consecutive periods — rather than restating the previous cadence. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: LRU-018 holds at least 12 months of period-comparable monitoring outcomes.
The most recent monitoring strategy revision cites a specific control and the trend that drove the change.
At least one check has had its frequency reduced on the strength of a stable trend, with the analysis recorded.

requirements.title: Monitoring dataset separates effectiveness, compliance and change
requirements.description: The continuous monitoring dataset shall carry three separable views for each in-scope control — whether the control is producing its intended effect, whether it remains configured as authorized, and what changed since the previous period — with the change view built from Configuration Repository (LRU-020) commits and the other two from Security Log Collector (LRU-018) outcomes, so that a rise in risk can be attributed to a change, a drift, or a degradation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each in-scope control carries an effectiveness result, a compliance result and a change result for the current period.
The change view is traceable to specific LRU-020 commits.
A control whose effectiveness fell while its configuration was unchanged is distinguishable from one whose configuration drifted.

requirements.title: Approved procedure compared against reported settings per family
requirements.description: A consistency check shall compare, for each control family, the approved procedure held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) against the settings the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) actually reports on each LRU, and shall list every divergence as a named item carrying the LRU, the setting and the approved value. A family with no divergence shall be recorded as consistent for that period rather than left silent. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every control family in scope has a consistency result for the current period, including families with no divergence.
Each divergence names the LRU, the setting and the approved value.
A divergence introduced deliberately in test appears in the next consistency result.

requirements.title: Monitoring results carry their age and stale feeds raise an alarm
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall present the current monitoring result for every in-scope control together with the time it was produced, shall mark any result older than 24 hours as stale, and shall raise a collection alarm when the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) feed has been silent for more than 15 minutes. No monitoring result presented to an assessor shall be assembled by hand. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every presented result carries a production timestamp and a stale flag computed from it.
Suppressing the LRU-013 feed for 20 minutes raises a collection alarm.
The presented dataset is reproducible from the collector without manual assembly.

requirements.title: Boundary and maintenance paths tested by a team with no build role
requirements.description: Penetration testing of the WS-X90 external boundary at the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and of the technician session path at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall be performed by a team holding no role in building or operating either LRU, working to written rules of engagement agreed before the test. The report shall name each attempted technique and its outcome, not only the findings that were raised. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The test team roster contains no individual with a build or operate role on LRU-007 or LRU-014.
Written rules of engagement are dated before the first test activity.
The report lists attempted techniques that did not succeed as well as those that did.

requirements.title: Unannounced physical attempts against provisioning and laptop custody
requirements.description: The penetration testing process shall include unannounced attempts, at the frequency set in the assessment plan, to reach the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) enclosure and to remove or connect a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) without passing facility access control, each attempt recorded as reached, blocked or detected. No facility-directed testing has been performed for WS-X90 to date. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The assessment plan sets a frequency for unannounced facility attempts and names the authorising official.
Each attempt is recorded as reached, blocked or detected with the time of detection where applicable.

requirements.title: Unregistered internal connections left unforwarding
requirements.description: Every internal connection carried by the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and every sensor connection aggregated by the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall appear in the authorized internal-connection register held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with its interface characteristics and the nature of the data it carries. A connection absent from the register shall be left in an unforwarding state, and the register shall be reviewed at least annually — the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CA-9. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Connecting an unregistered endpoint to LRU-009 leaves the port unforwarding and raises a register-mismatch event.
Every register entry records interface characteristics and the nature of the data carried.
The register carries a review record dated within the last 12 months.

requirements.title: Payload internal connections admitted by register and closed by interlock
requirements.description: The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall admit a payload-side internal connection only for an endpoint present in the authorized internal-connection register, and shall terminate that connection when the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) leaves the armed-permissive state or when the connection has been idle for more than 15 minutes. The Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) shall report each admission and termination so the register can be reconciled against what actually connected. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unregistered payload endpoint is refused admission by LRU-010 and the refusal is reported by LRU-012.
Driving LRU-011 out of the armed-permissive state terminates open payload-side connections.
A connection idle for more than 15 minutes is terminated without operator action.

requirements.title: Risk assessment policy set held under signed configuration control
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 risk assessment policy and its implementing procedures as one signed, version-controlled document set, each revision naming the designated risk-assessment official and the personnel roles it was issued to. The repository shall mark the set stale, and block promotion of any release package that cites it, once the approved revision is more than twelve months old, matching the CNSSI 1253 review parameter of at least annually for RA-1. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current policy revision in LRU-020 carries an approval date no more than twelve months before the review date.
Each revision record names exactly one designated risk-assessment official and the roles it was issued to.
A release package citing a policy set older than twelve months is refused promotion and the refusal is recorded against the package.

requirements.title: Approved H-H-M categorization record carried onto exported artifacts
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the approved WS-X90 categorization record stating confidentiality high, integrity high and availability moderate, with a separate impact rationale for each objective and a dated authorizing official approval, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall stamp that same three-value categorization onto every artifact it exports so a downstream consumer reads the categorization from the artifact rather than inferring it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The categorization record in LRU-020 states C high, I high, A moderate and carries one rationale paragraph per objective.
A dated authorizing official approval is present on the current revision of the record.
An artifact exported by LRU-001 carries a categorization label byte-identical to the record value.

requirements.title: Annual supply chain risk assessment for the three externally procured LRUs
requirements.description: Aurora shall hold a supply chain risk assessment for the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) covering counterfeit part risk, firmware provenance for vendor-loaded images and the identity of every sub-tier supplier of a programmable element, and shall reissue each assessment at least annually per the CNSSI 1253 parameter for RA-3(1) and within thirty days of a supplier, foundry or waveform-vendor change. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of LRU-003, LRU-005 and LRU-008 has an assessment reissued within the preceding twelve months.
Each assessment lists the sub-tier suppliers of every programmable element in that LRU.
A recorded supplier change is followed by a reissued assessment within thirty days.

requirements.title: All-source intelligence input to the WS-X90 risk analysis
requirements.description: The WS-X90 risk analysis shall draw on all-source intelligence reporting held by the Aurora program security office, with each analysed threat recorded against the affected LRU in the risk register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and, where the threat has an observable signature, translated into a detection rule loaded into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). No intelligence channel, register field or rule pipeline exists for WS-X90 today. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The System Security Engineer can name the intelligence channel and the clearance under which WS-X90 receives it.
The LRU-020 risk register carries an intelligence-source field on every threat entry.
At least one LRU-018 detection rule can be traced to a specific intelligence report identifier.

requirements.title: Current cyber threat state published to the boundary policy
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall maintain a named current threat state for WS-X90, refreshed on every ground-segment bulletin and at least weekly, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall load a distinct flow policy per threat state so that raising the state narrows the permitted external flow set without a software change. The state in force shall be recorded in the gateway audit stream at every policy load. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: LRU-018 holds a threat state with a refresh timestamp no older than seven days.
LRU-007 carries a separate named flow policy for each defined threat state.
Raising the threat state removes at least one permitted external flow and writes the transition to the gateway audit stream.

requirements.title: Vulnerability signature set refreshed within 24 hours before every scan
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refresh its vulnerability signature set from the approved feed mirrored in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) within 24 hours prior to running any scan of a WS-X90 baseline, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for RA-5(2), and shall abort the scan with an operator alert if the signature timestamp at scan start is older than that. The signature set identifier and timestamp shall be written into the header of every scan report. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A scan started with a signature set older than 24 hours aborts and records the abort reason and the signature timestamp.
Every scan report header carries the signature set identifier and its refresh timestamp.
A newly published signature added to the LRU-020 mirror appears in the LRU-017 set on the next refresh.

requirements.title: No identifying information discoverable on the external network interface
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall return no service banner, protocol version string, build identifier, host name or vendor product string on any externally reachable port, so that an unauthenticated survey from outside the boundary recovers only port state. Any field found by the quarterly external survey shall be suppressed or removed under a configuration change within ten working days of the survey report. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unauthenticated survey of every externally reachable port on LRU-007 returns no banner or version string.
The gateway host name and build identifier do not appear in any response to an unauthenticated request.
Every field reported by the previous quarterly survey is closed by a configuration change dated within ten working days of that report.

requirements.title: No airframe or build identity recoverable from the tactical radio emission
requirements.description: The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall carry no airframe identifier, tail number, unit designator or software build string in any unprotected link-layer field, in the acquisition preamble or in the idle keep-alive pattern, so that an off-platform receiver survey of the acquisition and idle states recovers no field that identifies the platform or its build. A discoverable field found by survey shall be removed or masked in the next scheduled waveform load. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A receiver survey of LRU-008 in the idle state recovers no airframe or unit identifier.
A receiver survey during link acquisition recovers no software build string.
Each field reported by the previous survey is shown closed in the waveform load notes for the following build.

requirements.title: Credentialed scanning only from a gateway-authorized privileged scan role
requirements.description: Credentialed vulnerability scanning of the Mission Computer (LRU-001) baseline shall be possible only from a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) session that the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) has authorized under the named privileged scan role. The gateway shall refuse the scan service to any session not holding that role, shall bind the role to a single scan window, and shall revoke it automatically when the maintenance session ends or the window expires, whichever is first. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A LRU-019 session without the privileged scan role is refused the credentialed scan service by LRU-014 and the refusal is logged.
The scan role is revoked within the session teardown sequence, verified by a second scan attempt failing on the same connection.
The scan account cannot authenticate to LRU-001 outside an open gateway-authorized scan window.

requirements.title: Scan, drift and audit output correlated into one attack-path view per build
requirements.description: Vulnerability scan output, configuration drift reports and audit alerts shall be correlated by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) into a single per-build attack-path view, from which a multi-hop finding is raised whenever two or more open findings on different LRUs are joined by a reachable path in the approved segmentation map. Each multi-hop finding shall name the ordered LRU sequence and the permitted flow that joins them. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Two seeded findings on LRUs joined by a permitted flow produce one multi-hop finding naming the ordered sequence.
Two seeded findings on LRUs with no permitted flow between them produce no multi-hop finding.
The attack-path view is regenerated on every baseline change and carries the build identifier it was computed from.

requirements.title: Public vulnerability reporting channel and intake register
requirements.description: Aurora shall operate a publicly reachable intake route by which anyone outside the program can report a suspected weakness in a WS-X90 component, with every submission entered into an intake register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) inside two working days, triaged against the affected LRU, and given a remediation or no-action decision with a named decision authority. No public channel or intake register exists for WS-X90 today; reports reaching Aurora by other routes are handled ad hoc by the Product Security Engineer. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A publicly reachable reporting address for WS-X90 components can be produced and reaches a monitored queue.
The LRU-020 intake register records receipt, affected LRU, triage outcome and decision authority for every report.
The Product Security Engineer can walk through the triage path from receipt to remediation decision.

requirements.title: Recorded response decision on every open assessment finding
requirements.description: Every finding raised against WS-X90 shall carry a response decision of mitigate, accept, transfer or avoid, recorded in the risk register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) within fifteen working days of the finding being raised, naming the accepting authority for any acceptance and the POA&M item for any mitigation. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall not report a baseline as compliant while a finding open against that baseline has no recorded response decision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every open finding in the LRU-020 register has a response decision dated within fifteen working days of the finding date.
Every acceptance names an accepting authority and every mitigation names a POA&M item.
LRU-013 reports a baseline with an undecided open finding as non-compliant rather than compliant.

requirements.title: Criticality analysis fixing the mission-critical function set at each design gate
requirements.description: The WS-X90 criticality analysis shall classify every LRU function as mission-critical, mission-essential or supporting at preliminary design review, at critical design review and at every baseline change board, and shall record the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) integrity-monitor function, the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) arm and inhibit function and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) root-of-trust verification as mission-critical, each with a named protection allocation and the supply chain measures applied to it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The analysis carries a classification for every function of every LRU with no unclassified entries.
The LRU-004 integrity monitor, LRU-011 arm and inhibit path and LRU-002 root-of-trust verification are each classified mission-critical with a named protection allocation.
The analysis revision date matches or follows the most recent baseline change board.

requirements.title: Continuous threat hunting across the exported platform telemetry
requirements.description: A threat-hunting capability shall run continuously on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) over exported WS-X90 telemetry, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency parameter for RA-10, searching for indicators of compromise the deployed detection rules do not cover and recording each hunt with its hypothesis, the data range searched and the outcome. LRU-018 today runs only fixed detection rules; no hunting workspace, hypothesis record or retained search corpus exists. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A hunt can be started against retained telemetry without disturbing the fixed detection rule set.
Each hunt records a hypothesis, the data range searched and a disposition.
A hunt that finds an uncovered indicator produces a new detection rule or a recorded decision not to add one.

requirements.title: Awareness and training policy issued to all WS-X90 account holders
requirements.description: The WS-X90 awareness and training policy and its implementing procedures shall be held as one signed document set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and issued to all personnel holding a WS-X90 account, which is the CNSSI 1253 dissemination parameter for AT-1, reviewed and re-approved at least annually and after any assessment finding against the AT family. Each account holder shall be recorded against the revision acknowledged and the date of acknowledgement. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current revision carries an approval date no more than twelve months before the review date.
Every WS-X90 account holder appears in the acknowledgement record against a specific revision.
An assessment finding against an AT control is followed by a policy review entry within the same review cycle.

requirements.title: Literacy training before first account enablement and annually thereafter
requirements.description: Every person holding a Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) account shall complete WS-X90 security literacy training before that account is first enabled and at least annually thereafter, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency parameter for AT-2, and again within thirty days of a platform change that alters how the operator handles mission data or removable media. Course content shall be updated at least annually and after any WS-X90 security incident, with the lesson learned named in the revision notes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No LRU-017 or LRU-019 account is enabled without a literacy training completion date on file.
Every current account holder has a completion date within the preceding twelve months.
The most recent course revision notes name the incident or platform change that prompted it.

requirements.title: Insider threat indicator recognition and reporting path for maintenance staff
requirements.description: Personnel authorized to hold a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be trained to recognise the WS-X90 insider-threat indicator set, which covers requests to bypass the maintenance session record, attempts to widen a bounded maintenance task, and removal of platform data outside the approved transfer path, and shall be able to name the reporting path without consulting a document. Training shall state that the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) retains the session record any report will be checked against. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A sampled technician names the reporting contact and route from memory.
A sampled technician names at least three indicators from the published WS-X90 indicator set.
The training record shows the insider-threat module completed for every current LRU-019 holder.

requirements.title: Social engineering refusal exercise for provisioning and maintenance roles
requirements.description: Holders of Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) accounts shall be trained to refuse out-of-band requests for provisioning material, session credentials or baseline identifiers regardless of the claimed requester, and shall take part in at least one exercise per year in which such a request is made and the refusal and the report are both recorded. Personnel shall also be trained on social mining, where unclassified fragments about WS-X90 roles and schedules are collected across separate conversations. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An annual exercise record exists naming the participants and the pretext used.
Each exercise participant either refused the request or is recorded with a follow-up action.
A sampled operator describes the approved channel for a legitimate credential request.

requirements.title: Operator recognition of the published anomalous-behaviour indicator set
requirements.description: Operators and maintenance staff shall be trained on the published WS-X90 anomalous-behaviour indicator set, which names the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) plausibility-reject classes, the out-of-envelope health values reported by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012), and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) alert classes that indicate suspicious code behaviour, and shall report any observed indicator through the incident channel within one hour of observation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The published indicator set names specific LRU-006, LRU-012 and LRU-018 conditions rather than generic categories.
A sampled operator classifies three presented conditions correctly against that set.
The training record shows the module completed before an operator is cleared for an unsupervised mission shift.

requirements.title: Advanced persistent threat literacy module for WS-X90 personnel
requirements.description: WS-X90 personnel shall receive literacy training on advanced persistent threat behaviour, covering long-dwell access, the use of legitimate maintenance paths for persistence, and the low-signal indicators that the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) surfaces rather than alerts on. No advanced persistent threat module has been written for WS-X90 and no personnel have received it; the topic is not covered by the general literacy course. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A written advanced persistent threat module exists and names WS-X90 maintenance and update paths as examples.
Completion is recorded for every person holding a privileged WS-X90 role.
A sampled person describes one low-signal indicator and where LRU-018 would surface it.

requirements.title: Quarterly threat bulletin reflected in the WS-X90 operating instructions
requirements.description: Aurora shall issue a WS-X90 cyber threat bulletin at least quarterly, drawn from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) alert history and the ground-segment threat feed, and shall carry each bulletin into the operating instructions held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) so that a change in the threat picture reaches the people running the system rather than stopping at the training record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A bulletin exists for each of the preceding four quarters.
Each bulletin is cross-referenced from a dated revision of the LRU-020 operating instructions.
A sampled operator states the current threat theme and the operating change it caused.

requirements.title: Maintenance account enablement gated on a current role-training record
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall enable a technician account only when the training record for that person shows the WS-X90 maintenance-role course completed within the preceding twelve months, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency parameter for AT-3, and shall disable the account within 24 hours of that record lapsing. A Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) session inherits the gateway decision and cannot be established against a lapsed record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An account whose training record is set to expired is disabled by LRU-014 within 24 hours without operator action.
A LRU-019 session attempt against a lapsed record is refused at the gateway and logged with the reason.
Every enabled technician account resolves to a completion date within the preceding twelve months.

requirements.title: Role curricula for the provisioning operator and log analyst roles
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) operator role and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) analyst role shall each have a documented curriculum naming the duties it covers, completed before first authorisation and at least annually thereafter, and reissued when a platform change alters those duties. The LRU-017 provisioning curriculum is written and in use; the LRU-018 analyst curriculum has not been written and analysts are currently authorized against the general literacy course alone. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A written curriculum exists for each of the two roles naming the duties it covers.
No person is authorized to either role without a completion date against that role curriculum.
A platform change altering either role is followed by a reissued curriculum in the same baseline.

requirements.title: Environmental control training for WS-X90 integration bay personnel
requirements.description: Personnel working in the WS-X90 integration bay, where the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is installed and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) units are held, shall receive initial and at least annual training in operating the bay fire detection and suppression equipment, the emergency power cut-off and the environmental alarms, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency parameter for AT-3(1). Training shall cover the shutdown order that protects platform state before power is removed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every person with unescorted integration bay access has an environmental training completion date within the preceding twelve months.
A sampled person locates the emergency power cut-off and states the shutdown order.
The training material matches the equipment currently installed in the bay.

requirements.title: Physical security training covering conditional custody of the maintenance laptop
requirements.description: Personnel authorized to draw a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) or to open a Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session shall receive initial and at least annual training in the WS-X90 physical security controls, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency parameter for AT-3(2), covering badge-reader use, intrusion alarm response and the custody procedure that governs LRU-019, which is a conditional asset released only for a named bounded activity and returned to controlled storage on completion. Training shall be repeated within thirty days of a significant change to the facility physical security systems. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A sampled technician describes the LRU-019 draw, custody and return procedure without reference to a document.
Every current LRU-019 custodian has a completion date within the preceding twelve months.
A recorded change to the facility physical security systems is followed by retraining within thirty days.

requirements.title: Training records exposed to the account gates as machine-readable status
requirements.description: Every person holding a WS-X90 account shall resolve to a training record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) giving the course, the completion date and the expiry date, retained for three years after the account is closed, and that record shall reach the maintenance and provisioning account gates as a machine-readable current-or-lapsed status rather than as a document a reviewer has to open. Completion dates are recorded today; the expiry field and the machine-readable status are not yet published to the gates. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every WS-X90 account holder resolves to a training record carrying course, completion date and expiry date.
Records for closed accounts are still retrievable for three years after closure.
The account gates read the status field directly and do not require a document lookup.

requirements.title: Training results reported to supervisors and the cybersecurity official
requirements.description: WS-X90 training results shall be reported to each person's supervisor and to the Aurora cybersecurity and privacy officials at least annually and again on discovery of a security incident or privacy breach, which are the CNSSI 1253 parameter values for AT-6, with failures in the maintenance, provisioning and analyst roles named individually rather than reported as an aggregate pass rate. Each report shall be filed against the training register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A report exists for the preceding twelve months addressed to supervisors and the cybersecurity official.
The report names individual failures in privileged roles rather than only a pass rate.
A WS-X90 security incident in the period is followed by an out-of-cycle report filed against the LRU-020 register.

requirements.title: Planning policy and procedure set under signed configuration control
requirements.description: The WS-X90 planning policy and its implementing procedures shall be held as a signed document set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), reviewed and re-approved at least annually per the CNSSI 1253 parameter for PL-1 and after any change to the system boundary or the authorization state, with each revision naming the designated planning official and the roles it was issued to. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current revision carries an approval date no more than twelve months before the review date.
A boundary or authorization state change in the period is followed by a policy review entry.
Each revision names one designated planning official and the roles it was issued to.

requirements.title: Account enablement gated on acknowledgement of the current rules of behaviour
requirements.description: No account on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be enabled until a dated acknowledgement of the current WS-X90 rules of behaviour revision is recorded against that person. The rules shall be reviewed at least annually, and every holder shall re-acknowledge at least annually or within ten working days of a revision, whichever falls first, after which an unacknowledged account is disabled rather than warned. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every enabled account on LRU-014, LRU-017 and LRU-019 resolves to an acknowledgement of the current revision.
A revision issued in the period shows re-acknowledgement by every holder or a disabled account.
The rules carry a review date no more than twelve months before the audit date.

requirements.title: External site and social media restrictions written into the rules of behaviour
requirements.description: The WS-X90 rules of behaviour shall state that build identifiers, subsystem and LRU names, imagery of the integration bay and schedule information may not be posted to social media, social networking sites or external applications, and that Aurora-issued identifiers and authentication secrets may not be used to create accounts on external sites. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall carry no general-purpose browsing path, so the restriction is enforced by configuration as well as stated in the rules. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The rules of behaviour contain a clause covering each of the three restriction areas.
LRU-019 and LRU-017 have no configured route to a general-purpose external browsing service.
The acknowledgement record shows holders acknowledged the revision containing these clauses.

requirements.title: Security concept of operations stating the degraded and abort posture
requirements.description: A WS-X90 security concept of operations shall be held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) describing how the system is operated across mission phases, which authority holds each decision, how maintenance and provisioning windows are entered and left, and how the Mission Computer (LRU-001) behaves on a security event. Consistent with the moderate availability objective, the concept of operations shall state a controlled mission abort and recover posture rather than continuous failover, and shall be reviewed at each baseline change board and at least annually. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The concept of operations names the decision authority for each mission phase and for entry into maintenance mode.
The security event response is stated as a controlled abort and recover sequence with no claim of continuous availability.
The document revision date is no earlier than the most recent baseline change board.

requirements.title: Security architecture description covering all six subsystems and their inheritance
requirements.description: The WS-X90 security architecture description held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall state, for each of the six subsystems, which security functions that subsystem carries itself, which it inherits from another subsystem, and which depend on an external system or service, together with the assumption made about each external dependency. It shall be reviewed and reissued at least annually per the CNSSI 1253 parameter for PL-8 and on any change to the external interface set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each of SUB-01 through SUB-06 has a carried, inherited and external-dependency list with no empty placeholders.
Every external dependency records the assumption made about it and who owns that assumption.
The issue date is within twelve months and no earlier than the last external interface change.

requirements.title: Every allocated security function resolves to a named element in the build manifest
requirements.description: Every security function the architecture allocates to the Mission Computer (LRU-001) or the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall resolve to a named software or hardware element in the approved build manifest for the baseline under review, and an allocation with no resolving element shall be carried as an open architecture gap with an owner and a target baseline rather than shown as covered. LRU-001 allocations resolve today; the LRU-007 flow-policy allocations are not yet mapped to manifest elements. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each allocated function on LRU-001 and LRU-007 names a manifest element or an open gap entry.
No allocation is shown as covered without a resolving manifest element.
Every open architecture gap carries an owner and a target baseline.

requirements.title: Two independent enforcement layers between the external world and mission compute
requirements.description: External traffic reaching WS-X90 mission compute shall cross two independently configured enforcement points, the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) link-layer admission policy and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) flow policy, neither of which derives its rule set from the other, so that a single misconfiguration on one layer cannot admit traffic the other layer would reject. The independence claim shall be re-checked by a configuration review at each baseline. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-007 and LRU-008 rule sets are generated from separate configuration sources with no shared derivation.
A rule deliberately widened on one layer does not widen the admitted flow set observed at mission compute.
The baseline configuration review records the independence check with a dated result.

requirements.title: Three-layer payload command path with no shared configuration source
requirements.description: A payload command shall pass the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) segment policy, the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) command validation and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) independent arm authorization before it reaches the payload, and a command rejected by any one of the three shall be rejected for the platform. No two of the three layers shall share a configuration source or a supplier-provided default rule set; LRU-009 and LRU-010 currently draw part of their segment definition from the same generated file. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A command blocked at any single layer does not reach the payload and the rejecting layer is identified in the audit record.
The three layers resolve to three distinct configuration sources with no shared generated file.
No layer is left at a supplier default rule set in the approved baseline.

requirements.title: Supplier diversity between the boundary and internal segmentation enforcement points
requirements.description: The boundary enforcement point in the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the internal segmentation enforcement point in the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall be obtained from different suppliers, so that a single vendor defect or a single vendor advisory cannot open both layers at once. Both enforcement points today derive from one vendor switching stack, and no second-source assessment or procurement action has been opened. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The LRU-007 and LRU-009 enforcement stacks resolve to two different named suppliers in the build manifest.
A vendor advisory affecting one enforcement point is shown not to apply to the other.
A second-source assessment exists with a decision and a target baseline.

requirements.title: Central management of flaw remediation and malicious code protection
requirements.description: Flaw remediation and malicious code protection shall be managed centrally for every WS-X90 LRU from the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), with the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) holding the single authoritative status view and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) the single alert path, so that no LRU carries a locally managed exception. The spam protection element of the CNSSI 1253 parameter for PL-9 has no applicable service on WS-X90, which carries no messaging or mail transfer function, and is recorded as not applicable with that rationale rather than claimed as met. Malicious code protection is centrally managed today; flaw remediation for the payload subsystem LRUs is still scheduled by hand. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every LRU appears in the LRU-013 status view with a centrally sourced flaw remediation and malicious code protection state.
No LRU carries a locally managed flaw remediation exception outside the LRU-016 schedule.
The not-applicable rationale for spam protection is recorded in the control implementation rather than left implicit.

requirements.title: One selected control baseline with its derivation visible
requirements.description: PROFILE-WSX90-TAILORED shall be the single selected control baseline for WS-X90, held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and recording SP 800-53B High as the starting baseline chosen from the C high, I high, A moderate categorization, together with the CNSSI 1253 allocation applied over it, so that a reviewer reads one selected baseline and the ordered reason it was selected rather than a hand-listed control set with no provenance. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Exactly one selected baseline is recorded for WS-X90 and it names SP 800-53B High as its starting point.
The selection record ties the starting baseline to the recorded categorization values.
No control appears in the selected baseline without an entry in the selection trail.

requirements.title: Every tailoring action reconstructible from the recorded event set
requirements.description: Every tailoring action applied to the WS-X90 baseline shall be recorded in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as an individual event naming the control, the action taken, the driver for it and the approving authority, so that the difference between SP 800-53B High and the effective control set is reconstructible from the event record alone. A control added to or withdrawn from the set without a matching event shall fail the baseline review rather than be accepted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Replaying the recorded events over SP 800-53B High reproduces the effective control set exactly.
Every event names a control, an action, a driver and an approving authority.
A control introduced without a matching event is rejected by the baseline review and recorded as rejected.

requirements.title: Configuration management policy and CM procedure set carried under signature with an annual review flag
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 configuration management policy and the CM procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, each bound to the named Aurora configuration management official who owns it, and shall raise a review-overdue flag on any artifact whose recorded review date is more than 12 months old, meeting the at-least-annual review interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-1. Publication of a revision shall run only from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and each publication shall record the engineering and cybersecurity role holders the revision was disseminated to. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current policy artifact and every procedure artifact in LRU-020 carry a valid signature and name a single accountable CM official.
A repository query returns the review-overdue flag set for any artifact whose review date is older than 12 months.
The dissemination record for the most recent revision names a recipient for each engineering and cybersecurity role listed in the policy.

requirements.title: Baseline record refreshed from the live platform inventory within 15 minutes of a state change
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall push each observed change of installed part number, firmware version or configuration set to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) within 15 minutes of the change taking effect, and LRU-020 shall mark the affected baseline record stale until the push is reconciled, so the recorded baseline configuration is maintained by machine rather than by a technician retyping it. Reconciliation shall run without operator intervention and shall record both the previous and the observed value. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate firmware version change on a monitored LRU appears in the LRU-020 baseline record within 15 minutes with no manual entry.
The baseline record shows a stale marker between the observed change and the completed reconciliation.
The reconciliation entry records the prior value, the observed value and the source LRU.

requirements.title: At least two prior baseline versions retained and provably restorable
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall retain at least two previous approved versions of each WS-X90 baseline configuration alongside the current one, matching the retention depth CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-2(3), and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall be able to stage and apply either retained version as a rollback without reaching outside the repository for any missing artifact. Retained versions shall keep their original approval signature; a version whose signature no longer verifies shall be reported rather than silently dropped from the retention set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: For every baseline held in LRU-020, at least two prior approved versions are present and their approval signatures verify.
A rollback exercise applies the second-most-recent retained version through LRU-016 using only repository content.
A tampered retained version is reported as a retention integrity fault rather than removed from the set.

requirements.title: Travel configuration and return sanitisation for the maintenance laptop
requirements.description: The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall be issued for off-site support at a reduced travel configuration that carries no mission data, no provisioning key material and no cached maintenance credentials, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall record the issue and the return of each travel instance. On return the laptop shall be re-imaged from the approved baseline and re-enrolled before it is permitted to open a maintenance session again; the record shall state which controls were applied on return. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The travel configuration definition exists in the approved baseline set and excludes mission data, provisioning keys and cached credentials.
Each issue and return of LRU-019 has a matching record on LRU-017 naming the traveller and the destination risk determination.
A returned laptop cannot open a maintenance session until the re-image and re-enrolment steps are recorded as complete.

requirements.title: Change record, approval routing and hard block on unapproved change
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall create a change record for every proposed WS-X90 configuration change, route it to the named approval authorities, highlight any record left neither approved nor disapproved for more than 10 working days, and refuse to release the change artifact for staging until the required approvals are recorded. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall reject any configuration set that does not carry a released change record identifier, and LRU-020 shall notify the change originator and the affected engineering lead when the change is recorded complete. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unapproved change artifact cannot be released for staging and the refusal is written to the change record.
A change record left undecided for more than 10 working days is returned by the aging query and shown as highlighted.
Completion of an approved change generates a notification to the originator and the affected engineering lead.

requirements.title: No change is finalised without a recorded test and validation result
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall accept a change package for operational application only when the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds, against that change record, a completed test result, a validation statement naming the security controls examined, and the identity of the engineer who signed the result. A change package presented without all three shall be held in the staging area and reported as incomplete rather than applied. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every change record applied in the last quarter carries a test result, a validation statement and a signer identity.
A change package whose record is missing any of the three is held in staging with an incomplete-record reason.
The validation statement names the specific controls examined, not a generic assertion of compliance.

requirements.title: Cybersecurity representative recorded as a voting member of the change control board
requirements.description: The WS-X90 configuration control board shall include the Aurora cybersecurity representative as a voting member, as CNSSI 1253 directs for CM-3(4), and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall record that representative's recorded vote against each board decision. The System Security Engineer shall be able to walk an assessor through the board charter, the named representative and alternate, and a decision where the representative's dissent was carried into the record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The board charter names the cybersecurity representative and an alternate, both designated as voting members.
Each board decision recorded in LRU-020 carries an explicit vote from the cybersecurity representative or the alternate.
The engineer can produce at least one decision record where a dissenting security vote is preserved in the outcome text.

requirements.title: Automatic response when a platform baseline is changed outside the change process
