requirements.description: When the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) or the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) observes a baseline configuration value that does not match a released change record, the platform shall automatically place the affected function in its restricted state, refuse the next mission-enable transition, and raise a priority event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 seconds, without waiting for an operator decision. Restoration to the normal state shall require an approved change record or an explicit recorded override. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An injected out-of-process baseline change drives the affected function to its restricted state automatically.
The priority event reaches LRU-018 within 60 seconds and names the changed value and the observing LRU.
Return to the normal state is refused until an approved change record or a recorded override is present.

requirements.title: Cryptographic mechanisms serving every crypto-dependent control held as configuration items
requirements.description: Every cryptographic mechanism WS-X90 relies on to satisfy a control that depends on cryptography — the algorithm suites, key strengths, certificate trust anchors and module firmware versions in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) — shall be registered as configuration items in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), as CNSSI 1253 scopes CM-3(6) to all controls that rely on cryptography. A change to any of these items shall be processed as a configuration change and shall not be settable from an operational console. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The repository configuration item list includes the algorithm suite, key strength, trust anchor set and module firmware version for LRU-003 and LRU-008.
Each crypto-dependent control in the WS-X90 control set resolves to at least one registered cryptographic configuration item.
An attempt to change an algorithm suite or trust anchor from an operational console is refused and logged.

requirements.title: Monthly change review against the high-integrity interval, plus event-driven review
requirements.description: Because WS-X90 is categorised I:high, the applied-change set shall be reviewed monthly — the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for high integrity under CM-3(7) — and additionally after any incident and once a planned change campaign has been performed, by reconciling the changes recorded in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) against the change-related events retained by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). Any applied change with no matching approved record, and any approved record with no matching applied change, shall be raised as a review exception. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A completed review record exists for each of the last three calendar months.
The reviewer can show the reconciliation output listing applied-without-record and record-without-applied exceptions.
At least one post-incident or post-campaign review is recorded outside the monthly cadence.

requirements.title: Configuration changes blocked while the platform is in an exercise or operational state
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall refuse to apply any configuration change while the platform is in an exercise or real-world operational state — the circumstance CNSSI 1253 names for CM-3(8) — and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall independently refuse to accept an interlock parameter change in those states regardless of what LRU-013 permits. A change request arriving in a blocked state shall be queued with the blocking state recorded, not discarded. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A configuration change submitted while the platform reports an operational or exercise state is refused by LRU-013.
LRU-011 refuses an interlock parameter change in those states even when the request carries a valid change record.
The refused request is queued and the record names the blocking platform state and the time it was asserted.

requirements.title: Changes analysed on a representative test rig before any operational application
requirements.description: Every WS-X90 change package shall be applied and analysed on the ground test rig driven from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) before it is released for operational application, and the analysis record held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall state the rig's configuration delta against the operational baseline so an assessor can judge how representative the test was. The record shall report findings under four headings — defect, weakness, incompatibility and suspected malicious content — rather than a single pass verdict. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each released change package has a rig analysis record naming the rig build and its delta against the operational baseline.
The analysis record reports separately on defect, weakness, incompatibility and suspected malicious content.
A change released without a rig analysis record is listed as an exception in the monthly change review.

requirements.title: Post-change control verification run before the platform is returned to mission service
requirements.description: After a configuration change is applied, the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall run the verification set associated with each control the change record marks as impacted, and shall hold the platform out of mission-ready state until every verification in that set reports a result to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). A verification that reports a failure or does not report at all shall keep the platform out of mission-ready state and shall name the control that could not be verified. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A change marked as impacting a named control triggers that control's verification set on the next platform bring-up.
A verification failure or timeout holds the platform out of mission-ready state and names the unverified control.
The verification results for the last three applied changes are retrievable from LRU-018 by change record identifier.

requirements.title: Change access enforced by the repository itself and audited on every enforcement decision
requirements.description: Access to modify WS-X90 baselines, change records and release artifacts shall be enforced by the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) against the authorised change role list rather than by convention, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall carry the same enforcement for any change action reaching the platform through a maintenance session. Every enforcement decision, permit and deny alike, shall produce an audit record forwarded to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) carrying the actor identity, the object and the decision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A user outside the authorised change role list is denied a repository write and a maintenance-session change action.
Both the permitted and the denied action produce an audit record in LRU-018 naming actor, object and decision.
No path exists to modify a released artifact that bypasses the LRU-020 or LRU-014 enforcement point.

requirements.title: Operational change privilege held by a small named set and re-evaluated annually
requirements.description: Privilege to change components or system information on the operational WS-X90 platform shall be held only by named individuals in the operational change role, granted through the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and honoured by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013); developers and integration staff shall not hold it by default. The holder list shall be reviewed and re-evaluated at least annually, the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-5(5), with each retained privilege re-justified by name. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The operational change role list is separate from the development role list and no individual holds both without a recorded exception.
A completed re-evaluation record exists within the last 12 months and re-justifies each retained holder by name.
The lead can identify at least one privilege withdrawn as a result of the most recent re-evaluation.

requirements.title: Write access to the mission software library restricted to the release pipeline identity
requirements.description: The mission software library on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall accept content only from the release pipeline identity issued by the Configuration Repository (LRU-020); no interactive account, including an administrative one, shall hold write access to library contents on the operational platform. An attempted write from any other identity shall be refused at the filesystem enforcement point and reported as a library privilege violation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An interactive administrative account is refused a write to the mission software library.
The release pipeline identity successfully writes a signed library update and the write is attributable to that identity.
Each refused write produces a library privilege violation record naming the attempting identity.

requirements.title: Automated setting application and drift verification across all security-relevant components
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall apply the approved configuration setting set to, and verify it on, every security-relevant WS-X90 component — at a minimum all cybersecurity and cybersecurity-enabled components, the scope CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-6(1) — including the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) integrity-check thresholds and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) holdover and source-authentication settings. Verification shall run at each bring-up and at least once every 24 hours in sustained operation, and shall report every deviation as a named setting rather than a pass/fail total. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The verified component list covers every component the system record marks as security-relevant, including LRU-004 and LRU-005.
A deliberately altered navigation integrity threshold or timing holdover setting is reported by name at the next verification pass.
Verification runs at bring-up and at least once in any 24-hour period of sustained operation.

requirements.title: Unauthorised setting change reverted to the approved value and reported
requirements.description: When the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) detects a security-relevant setting that differs from the approved value and carries no released change record, it shall restore the approved value, mark the affected function as having been reverted, and raise an event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) naming the setting, the observed value and the restored value. For the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) the revert shall be deferred until the current navigation solution is handed over, so a revert never drops the navigation output mid-solution. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unauthorised change to a security-relevant setting is restored to the approved value automatically.
The event in LRU-018 names the setting, the observed value and the restored value.
A revert on LRU-004 is deferred to a solution handover boundary and the deferral is recorded with its duration.

requirements.title: Annual and event-driven review of mission compute functions, software and services
requirements.description: The functions, software and services running on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall be reviewed at least annually and additionally as system changes or incidents occur — the trigger set CNSSI 1253 gives for CM-7(1) — against the approved function list held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). Everything identified as unnecessary or nonsecure shall be disabled or removed, and anything retained shall carry a recorded operational justification and a review date rather than remaining in place by default. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A review record exists within the last 12 months and at least one further review is tied to a change or incident.
Every function or service present on LRU-001 but absent from the approved list is marked for disable or removal with a target date.
Each retained item flagged as unnecessary or nonsecure carries a written operational justification and a review date.

requirements.title: External and sensor-facing ports and protocols reduced to the approved set
requirements.description: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) shall present only the ports, protocols and services named in the approved external interface set; anything else shall be disabled in the shipped configuration rather than left listening. The set shall be reviewed at least annually and after any change or incident affecting an external interface, and an enabled interface with no approved entry shall be treated as a configuration defect. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An interface enumeration of LRU-007, LRU-008 and LRU-006 returns only ports and protocols present in the approved external interface set.
Any interface found enabled without an approved entry is raised as a configuration defect with an owning engineer.
The approved external interface set carries a review date within the last 12 months.

requirements.title: Execution refused for any image outside the approved program set
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall refuse to execute any binary whose measurement is absent from the approved program set anchored by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002), and shall refuse it at load time rather than terminating it after start. A refusal shall name the attempted image path and its measurement, and the refusal path shall remain effective when the platform is running in maintenance mode as well as in mission mode. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unapproved binary placed on the platform is refused at load and never reaches an executing state.
The refusal record names the image path and the computed measurement.
The same refusal occurs when the platform is in maintenance mode.

requirements.title: Registered service and protocol identifiers reconciled against the gateway configuration
requirements.description: Every network service WS-X90 exposes through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall carry, in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), the registration identifier required by the Aurora ports, protocols and services registration process, and the gateway configuration shall be reconciled against that register before each release. A service present on the gateway with no registration identifier, or a registration whose recorded port no longer matches the gateway, shall be reported as a registration exception. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each service in the gateway configuration resolves to a registration identifier held in LRU-020.
The pre-release reconciliation output lists unregistered services and port mismatches separately.
A registration exception has a named owner and a target closure date.

requirements.title: Deny-all, permit-by-exception software list reviewed at least annually
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall run a deny-all, permit-by-exception software policy: only programs identified in the authorised software list held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall be permitted to execute on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and the list shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-7(5). Each entry shall name the program, its measurement and the mission function it supports; an entry with no current mission function shall be removed at review. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The authorised software list names a program, a measurement and a supporting mission function for every entry.
The enforcement policy on LRU-001 and LRU-013 is deny-all with the list as the only permit source.
The list carries a completed review within the last 12 months and shows entries removed for lack of a mission function.

requirements.title: Binary-only supplied code prohibited without an authorising official exception
requirements.description: WS-X90 shall not accept binary or machine-executable code from a supplier that provides no source code and no meaningful warranty, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall carry, for each software configuration item, a supplier warranty and source-availability determination. Where a compelling mission need requires such code, the item shall be marked as an exception carrying the authorising official's recorded approval, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to publish an unmarked binary-only item. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each software configuration item in LRU-020 carries a supplier warranty and source-availability determination.
A binary-only item without a recorded authorising official approval is refused publication from LRU-017.
The engineer can list current exceptions and name the authorising official who approved each.

requirements.title: Authorised hardware list enforced at the internal switch and reviewed annually
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall admit only hardware whose identity appears in the authorised hardware list maintained by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013); an unlisted device presenting itself on a port shall be refused a data path and reported within 30 seconds. The authorised hardware list shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-7(9), with each entry tied to a platform build. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unlisted device connected to an LRU-009 port or the LRU-014 maintenance port is refused a data path.
The refusal is reported to the platform log within 30 seconds and names the port and the presented device identity.
The authorised hardware list carries a review within the last 12 months and each entry names a platform build.

requirements.title: Inventory updated as part of the install or removal action, not after it
requirements.description: Installation, removal or replacement of a WS-X90 line replaceable unit shall not be recorded as complete until the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) has written the resulting inventory delta — part number, serial number, firmware version and slot — to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). A maintenance action closed without an accepted inventory delta shall be held open and reported to the maintenance supervisor. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A rehearsed LRU replacement writes the inventory delta before the maintenance action can be closed.
The delta carries part number, serial number, firmware version and slot for both the removed and the installed unit.
A maintenance action closed without an accepted delta remains open and is reported.

requirements.title: Inventory currency measured, not assumed
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall poll the platform for installed component identity at least once per operating day and publish the result to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which shall compute and expose an inventory currency figure — the proportion of inventory records confirmed by an automated observation within the last 24 hours — and forward it to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). Records not confirmed within that window shall be listed individually as unconfirmed rather than absorbed into the total. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The inventory currency figure is computed daily and retrievable for any of the last 30 operating days.
Unconfirmed records are listed individually with the age of their last confirmation.
No inventory record is marked confirmed on the basis of a manual entry alone.

requirements.title: Continuous detection of unauthorised software and firmware, with isolation of the affected function
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall continuously compare observed software and firmware measurements against the approved baseline — the frequency CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-8(3) — and, on detecting an unauthorised component, shall isolate the affected function from the mission network and notify the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and the on-duty security role within 5 minutes. Detection shall not depend on a scheduled scan window. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unauthorised firmware image introduced between scheduled maintenance windows is detected without waiting for a scan.
The affected function is isolated from the mission network and the notification reaches LRU-018 within 5 minutes.
The detection record names the measured value, the expected baseline value and the observing LRU.

requirements.title: Unauthorised hardware on an internal port loses its data path automatically
requirements.description: The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) shall continuously monitor port state and admitted device identity, and shall place any port presenting an unlisted device into a quarantine state that carries no mission traffic, while the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) refuses to forward traffic sourced from a quarantined segment. Quarantine shall apply without an operator decision and shall be recorded with the port, the presented identity and the time of quarantine. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An unlisted device on an LRU-009 port results in a quarantined port carrying no mission traffic.
LRU-007 refuses to forward traffic originating from the quarantined segment.
The quarantine record names the port, the presented device identity and the quarantine time.

requirements.title: Every inventory record names an accountable position or role
requirements.description: Each WS-X90 component record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall carry the position or role accountable for administering that component — at minimum a position or role, as CNSSI 1253 scopes CM-8(4) — drawn from the four engineering roles used on this programme, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall refuse to accept a new component record that leaves the accountability field empty. Where a role holder changes, the record shall be updated by role rather than by individual name so the record does not decay with personnel turnover. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every component record in LRU-020 carries a non-empty accountable position or role.
A new component record submitted without the accountability field is refused by LRU-013.
The accountability field holds a role rather than a personal name in every record.

requirements.title: Configuration management plan held as a protected, approved configuration item
requirements.description: The WS-X90 configuration management plan shall itself be a configuration item: held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) under signature, approved by the named programme and cybersecurity approvers, and mirrored to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) so a recovery does not lose it. The plan shall define the configuration item classes for the system, the identification process across the lifecycle, and the roles that may approve a change, and shall be readable only by holders of a configuration management role. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The plan exists as a signed configuration item with recorded programme and cybersecurity approvals.
The plan defines configuration item classes and the identification process across the system lifecycle.
Read access is refused to an account outside the configuration management roles, and the refusal is logged.

requirements.title: Open-source components admitted only under a recorded licence and provenance determination
requirements.description: An open-source software component shall be admitted to a WS-X90 build only when the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds, for that component and version, the licence determination, the upstream provenance reference and the named engineer who reviewed it, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to publish a build whose bill of materials contains an open-source component missing any of the three. Components carrying licences on the programme's prohibited list shall be refused outright. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every open-source entry in the current build bill of materials has a licence determination, a provenance reference and a reviewer.
A build containing an open-source component with a prohibited licence is refused publication.
The prohibited licence list is a versioned artifact in LRU-020 with a recorded owner.

requirements.title: Software installation possible only under an explicitly elevated maintenance session
requirements.description: Software installation onto the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall be possible only from a maintenance session that has been explicitly elevated to installation privilege for a bounded period, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall not be able to trigger an installation from an ordinary session. Elevation shall be requested per action, expire automatically at the end of the bounded period, and be recorded with the requesting identity and the installed package identifier. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An installation attempted from an unelevated maintenance session is refused.
An elevation expires automatically at the end of its bounded period without an operator action.
Each successful installation record names the requesting identity, the elevation window and the package identifier.

requirements.title: Documented location of protected mission information and the accounts that can reach it
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold, for each class of protected WS-X90 mission information, the specific components on which it is processed and stored — principally the Mission Computer (LRU-001) working set and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) at-rest set — together with the roles and accounts able to reach it on each. A change that moves a class of information onto a different component shall be recorded as a location change with a date and a reason, so the information map is a maintained record rather than a design-time snapshot. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each protected information class resolves to a named set of components and a named set of roles with access.
A rehearsed relocation of an information class produces a dated location-change record with a reason.
No protected information class is recorded as residing on a component absent from the system inventory.

requirements.title: Payload telemetry retention points documented and bounded
requirements.description: Payload health and status telemetry collected by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and relayed through the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) shall have every retention point documented in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) — which buffers hold it, for how long, and which roles can read it — and LRU-012 shall hold no telemetry beyond the documented buffer depth. Any new retention point introduced by a change shall be added to the record before the change is released. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The documented retention points match the buffers actually present on LRU-012 and LRU-010.
Telemetry older than the documented buffer depth is not recoverable from LRU-012.
A change introducing a new retention point is refused release until the record is updated.

requirements.title: Automated discovery of protected information types across platform components
requirements.description: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) shall run automated discovery over the exported platform data sets to identify occurrences of the protected WS-X90 information types on components not recorded as holding them, and shall report each occurrence to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as an information location exception naming the component, the information type and the detection basis. Discovery shall be scheduled, not run on request only, and an exception shall be closed only by a recorded relocation, removal or record correction. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Discovery runs on a defined schedule and its last three runs are evidenced.
An exception names the component, the information type and the detection basis.
Closure of an exception records a relocation, a removal or a corrected location record.

requirements.title: Firmware refused at boot unless signed by an approved certificate
requirements.description: The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) shall verify, against the approved certificate set held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the digital signature of every firmware component in the boot chain — any software and firmware component, as CNSSI 1253 scopes CM-14 — and shall halt the affected LRU in its recovery state rather than continue when verification fails. Signature verification shall be enforced by the boot controller itself and shall not be defeatable by a configuration setting reachable from the operational platform. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A firmware image signed by a certificate outside the approved set halts the LRU in its recovery state.
No operational configuration setting exists that disables signature verification on LRU-002.
The recovery-state record names the failing component and the certificate that presented the signature.

requirements.title: Update packages refused at staging unless every component is signed by an approved certificate
requirements.description: The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall verify the signature of every software and firmware component inside an update package against the approved certificate set before staging it, and shall reject the whole package if any single component fails, rather than staging the verifiable subset. The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall record the certificate identity used for each accepted component so the provenance of a staged update is reconstructible after the fact. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An update package containing one unsigned or wrongly signed component is rejected in full.
Each accepted component records the certificate identity that verified it in LRU-020.
No staging path exists that accepts a component without a signature check.

requirements.title: IA policy and procedure set held signed with an annual review flag
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 identification and authentication policy together with its IA procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, and shall raise a review-overdue flag on any artifact whose recorded review date is more than 12 months old, meeting the at-least-annual review interval CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-1. A revision shall be published only from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), which shall bind the approving official and the distribution list of cybersecurity and ground support role holders to the published revision. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The current IA policy artifact and every IA procedure artifact in LRU-020 carry a valid signature and a recorded review date inside the last 12 months.
A publication attempt from any endpoint other than LRU-017 is refused and written to the repository event log.
The distribution record for the most recent revision names a recipient for every assigned IA role holder.

requirements.title: Two distinct factors before any privileged administrative command
requirements.description: Every privileged session on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall require two distinct authentication factors before any administrative command is dispatched: a hardware credential whose private key is generated in and never leaves the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), and an operator-held PIN. A privileged login that presents only one factor shall be refused outright, with no reduced-privilege session offered as a fallback. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A privileged login presenting only the PIN, or only the hardware credential, is refused and the refusal reaches the security log within 5 seconds.
LRU-003 key attestation shows the privileged authentication private key marked non-exportable.
No administrative command executes on LRU-013 or LRU-014 inside a session whose second factor was not verified.

requirements.title: Hardware credential and PIN for non-privileged ground support sessions
requirements.description: Non-privileged operator sessions on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall require a hardware credential plus an operator PIN, including sessions established while the endpoint is disconnected from the ground support network, and shall offer no password-only fallback path. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A non-privileged logon attempt on LRU-017 with no hardware credential inserted is refused at the identifier prompt.
A disconnected logon on LRU-019 requires the hardware credential and records the credential serial in the local session log.
The build configuration of both endpoints exposes no password-only authentication method.

requirements.title: Individual identity bound to every action taken under a shared role account
requirements.description: Where a shared maintenance role account is used on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) or the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), the individual technician shall authenticate with their own credential first, and the platform shall bind that individual identity to every action taken under the shared account, so that no audit record resolves only to the shared account name. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every audit record produced under a shared role account carries a non-empty individual identity field.
An attempt to assume the shared role account with no prior successful individual authentication is refused.
The bound individual identity survives a privilege change inside the session without reverting to the shared account name.

requirements.title: One authentication factor from a device separate from the endpoint being accessed
requirements.description: Local, network and remote access to both privileged and non-privileged accounts on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall take one authentication factor from a hardware token physically separate from the endpoint being accessed, the token holding its authentication key inside a certified hardware boundary, with the token attestation validated by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) before the session opens. The CNSSI 1253 parameter for IA-2(6) sets both the access paths in scope, local, network and remote, and the account types in scope, privileged and non-privileged. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A session opened with both factors originating on the accessed endpoint is refused on the local, the network and the remote path.
LRU-003 records a token attestation result for every accepted session, for privileged and non-privileged accounts alike.
Removing the token during an open session terminates that session within 30 seconds.

requirements.title: Nonce-bound authentication that refuses a replayed exchange
requirements.description: Authentication to the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) shall be replay resistant for privileged accounts at a minimum, the level CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-2(8), by binding a gateway-issued nonce to the derived session key so that a captured and re-sent authentication exchange is refused, with the refusal recorded under a distinct replay-detected reason code. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded privileged authentication exchange replayed against LRU-007 is refused and no session key is derived.
Each accepted authentication carries a nonce that appears exactly once in the LRU-008 session log for the sortie.
Replay refusals appear in the exported security log under a distinct reason code.

requirements.title: Electronic verification of a PIV-compliant credential before account binding
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall accept a PIV-compliant credential as the hardware factor and shall verify it electronically, chaining the certificate up to a trust anchor on the WS-X90 accepted list and checking revocation status, before an operator account is bound to the session; a credential whose revocation status cannot be determined shall be refused rather than accepted on trust. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A PIV credential whose certification path cannot be built to an accepted anchor is refused with no account binding.
A revoked PIV credential is refused and the revocation source consulted is named in the session record.
A credential presented while no revocation data is reachable is refused, not accepted with a warning.

requirements.title: Mutual certificate authentication before a switch port joins the mission VLAN
requirements.description: Before the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) places a port into the mission VLAN, the switch and the attached device shall complete a mutual certificate-based authentication in which the device credential is anchored in the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and released only after a successful measured boot, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) shall drop mission traffic sourced from any port that has not completed that exchange. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A device presenting a valid certificate but a failed boot measurement is held in the quarantine VLAN.
The switch presents its own certificate and the device refuses the link when switch validation fails.
LRU-001 drops mission traffic sourced from a port whose authentication state is not authenticated.

requirements.title: Navigation and timing sources authenticate before their data is trusted
requirements.description: The Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) shall each complete a mutual cryptographic authentication with the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) at power-on and at every reconnection, and LRU-004 shall mark data arriving from an unauthenticated source as unusable for navigation solution formation and raise an operator advisory, rather than degrading the solution silently. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A simulated sensor injected on the LRU-006 bus without a valid credential produces no contribution to the navigation solution.
A timing message from LRU-005 that fails authentication is excluded and the holdover state is entered rather than accepting the message.
Each power-on cycle records an authentication result for every configured navigation and timing source.

requirements.title: Every individual identifier carries an approved affiliation attribute
requirements.description: Every individual identifier issued through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and held by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall carry a non-null affiliation attribute drawn from the approved set of government civilian, military, prime contractor, subcontractor and foreign national, and account creation shall fail closed when the attribute is absent or outside that set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An export of the LRU-013 identifier table shows an affiliation value from the approved set on every active identifier.
A registration submitted with an empty affiliation field is rejected at LRU-017 before an identifier is minted.
The affiliation value appears on the account record and on the audit records the account produces.

requirements.title: Single protected attribute store with an immutable revision record per write
requirements.description: Identity attributes for every user, device and service on WS-X90, covering identifier, affiliation, credential binding, issuing authority and status, shall be held in one protected attribute store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), writable only by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) over an authenticated channel, and every accepted write shall produce an immutable revision record naming the writer and the prior value. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A write to the attribute store from any source other than an authenticated LRU-013 channel is refused.
Each attribute change produces a revision record whose prior value matches the value read immediately before the change.
No second copy of the attribute set is discoverable on LRU-001 or LRU-017 after a provisioning cycle.

requirements.title: Quarterly refreshed compromised-password list screened at every password change
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall hold a list of commonly used, expected and compromised passwords, refresh it at least quarterly, the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-5(1)(a), and refresh it immediately on notification of a suspected compromise, and shall screen every password creation or change made through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) against that list, rejecting a match with a generic message that does not disclose which entry matched. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The list revision date held on LRU-013 is inside the last 3 months.
A password drawn from the list is rejected at LRU-017 and the rejection message names no list entry.
A list refresh triggered by a compromise notification is recorded with the notification reference.

requirements.title: Password composition, protected transport and salted keyed-hash storage
requirements.description: A password accepted on WS-X90 shall be a case-sensitive mix of at least 12 characters containing at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one number and one special character, and a password change shall alter at least 50 percent of the characters, the composition rule CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-5(1)(h). The credential shall reach the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) only over a cryptographically protected channel and shall be held on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) as a salted keyed-hash derivation whose derivation key never leaves LRU-003. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An 11-character password, and a 12-character password missing any one of the four character classes, are both rejected.
A password change that leaves more than half the characters unchanged in position is rejected.
A raw read of the LRU-015 credential region yields only salt and derivation output, with no recoverable plaintext.
A packet capture of the credential path shows no plaintext password on the wire between LRU-017 and LRU-003.

requirements.title: Certification path build and cached revocation check on public key authentication
requirements.description: For every public key-based authentication the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) shall confine use of the private key to the authorised subject and refuse export of that key, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall validate the presented certificate by building a path to an accepted trust anchor and checking status against a locally cached revocation set that is refreshed whenever an external link is available and treated as stale after 7 days. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A certificate that chains to an unrecognised anchor is refused with a path-build failure recorded.
A certificate listed in the cached revocation set is refused even with no external link available.
A revocation cache older than 7 days is reported stale and downgrades the session to refused rather than accepted.
An attempt to export the authentication private key from LRU-003 returns a refusal and an audit record.

requirements.title: Authenticator material confined to hardware or the encrypted credential region
requirements.description: An authenticator that permits access to WS-X90 mission data shall be protected at the highest security category that credential can reach, which for this system is confidentiality high, so authenticator material shall exist only inside the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) hardware boundary or in the encrypted credential region of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), and no process outside the identity service shall hold a read path to either location. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The access control export for the LRU-015 credential region lists only the identity service principal.
The LRU-003 key inventory records every authentication key as hardware-resident and non-exportable.
No authenticator material appears in a memory or storage image taken from LRU-001 or LRU-017.

requirements.title: No unencrypted static authenticator survives repository or update staging
requirements.description: No mission software image, update package or interface script accepted into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) or staged by the Update and Recovery Controller (LRU-016) shall contain an unencrypted static authenticator. LRU-020 shall run a credential-pattern scan over every submitted artifact and refuse to publish one that flags, and the scan shall cover the payload command scripts executed by the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An artifact seeded with a known static credential pattern is refused at publication and the refusal names the scan rule.
The scan coverage report lists every artifact class in the repository, including payload command scripts.
LRU-016 refuses to stage an update package that carries no passing scan verdict.

requirements.title: Acknowledged restriction on reusing a password across domains and privilege levels
requirements.description: A ground support user holding accounts on more than one WS-X90 related system shall be advised, and shall acknowledge in the account record held by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), that the same password must not be used across domains of differing classification levels, across more than one domain of a single classification level, or across more than one privilege level, which is the precaution CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-5(8), and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall present that acknowledgement at each credential set. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A ground support technician can describe the three reuse prohibitions and where the acknowledgement is recorded.
The account record for a multi-system user shows a dated acknowledgement.
The credential-set workflow on LRU-019 cannot be completed without the acknowledgement step.

requirements.title: Cached maintenance authenticator expires 12 hours after last online verification
requirements.description: Where the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) or the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) caches an authenticator so a disconnected flightline session can proceed, the cached authenticator shall expire 12 hours after the last successful online verification, after which the endpoint shall refuse the session and require reconnection to the identity service before work resumes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A disconnected logon attempted 12 hours and 1 minute after the last online verification is refused.
The cache expiry timer survives a power cycle of the endpoint and is not reset by it.
Expiry refusals are recorded locally and exported when the endpoint next reconnects.

requirements.title: One approved trust store manifest with power-on digest reporting
requirements.description: A single approved PKI trust store manifest shall be held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and shall be the only source of the trust anchors loaded by the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012); each of those LRUs shall report the digest of its installed trust store at power-on, and a digest that does not match the current manifest shall raise a configuration deviation rather than being accepted. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest in LRU-020 is signed and names every anchor, its purpose and its expiry.
The power-on digest reported by LRU-008 and LRU-012 matches the manifest digest of record.
An anchor added outside the manifest raises a deviation within one power-on cycle.

requirements.title: Privileged hardware authenticators issued in person against a recorded sponsor
requirements.description: A hardware authenticator for a WS-X90 privileged role shall be issued in person by the designated registration authority at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and the issuing officer identity and the authorising government sponsor shall both be recorded against the credential serial number before the credential is activated for use. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The registration authority can walk through the in-person issuance sequence end to end without consulting an undocumented step.
Every activated privileged credential serial resolves to an issuing officer and a named sponsor.
A credential activated without both records present is quarantined at the next reconciliation.

requirements.title: Masked authenticator entry and a single generic failure message
requirements.description: During authentication on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) the entered PIN or password shall be masked on the display, shall not appear in any log, crash dump or diagnostic buffer, and a failed authentication shall return one generic message that does not reveal whether the identifier or the authenticator was wrong. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Entry is masked on both endpoints, including on the recovery console.
A failure with a valid identifier and a failure with an invalid identifier return the identical message and take the same time to within 50 milliseconds.
A diagnostic capture taken immediately after a failed logon contains no authenticator characters.

requirements.title: Role-bound operator authentication before any keyed cryptographic operation
requirements.description: An operator or service shall authenticate to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and be bound to a specific module role before the module performs any keyed operation, and the module shall refuse a role transition without re-authentication; the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall accept a key-wrapping request only from a session that carries a valid LRU-003 role binding. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A keyed operation requested before role authentication is refused with a module status code.
A transition from the user role to the crypto officer role without re-authentication is refused.
LRU-015 refuses a key-wrapping request that carries no LRU-003 role binding.

requirements.title: Time-boxed non-organisational account bound to a verified other-agency PIV
requirements.description: When a technician from another federal agency requires temporary access, the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall accept that agency PIV credential, verify it electronically against the issuing agency trust anchor and revocation source captured in the support authorisation, and bind it to a non-organisational account that expires automatically with that support authorisation and cannot be extended in place. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each non-organisational account record names the issuing agency, the credential identifier and the authorisation reference.
The account expiry date equals the support authorisation end date with no manual extension path.
A credential from an agency with no captured trust anchor is refused at registration.

requirements.title: Only listed external authenticators accepted at the support interface
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the maintained list of external authenticators approved for non-organisational access to WS-X90 support interfaces, recording type, assurance level and approval date for each, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) shall accept only an authenticator present on that list, refusing any external credential whose type or assurance level is not listed. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The list in LRU-020 is signed, dated and names an approver for every entry.
An external authenticator type absent from the list is refused at LRU-007 with the refusal logged.
The gateway configuration references the list revision it is enforcing.

requirements.title: External identity assertions checked against the identity management profile in force
requirements.description: Non-organisational identity handling on WS-X90 shall conform to the identity management profile recorded in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall reject an external identity assertion whose attribute set, binding method or assurance level does not match the profile revision in force at the time of the assertion. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The profile artifact in LRU-020 names the required attributes and the accepted assurance levels.
An assertion missing a required attribute is rejected and the missing attribute is named in the rejection record.
The profile revision enforced by LRU-013 matches the current repository revision.

requirements.title: Per-service certificates on every cross-LRU mission connection
requirements.description: Every mission service that opens a cross-LRU connection, specifically the service mesh on the Mission Computer (LRU-001), the telemetry publisher on the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and the navigation solution service on the Navigation Processor (LRU-004), shall present a per-service certificate whose subject names both the service and the hosting LRU, and shall refuse a peer that offers only a device credential or an unnamed service identity. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A connection attempt carrying only a device certificate is refused by all three services.
Every accepted service session records the peer service name and hosting LRU in the session log.
A service certificate whose subject does not match the hosting LRU inventory entry is refused.

requirements.title: Supplemental factor demanded when a maintenance session looks anomalous
requirements.description: When the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) observes a maintenance session opening outside the authorised support window or from a ground network address not on the approved list, the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall require a supplemental authentication factor from the technician before the session is allowed to continue, and shall terminate the session if the supplemental factor is not supplied within 2 minutes. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A session opened outside the authorised support window triggers a supplemental factor prompt at LRU-014.
A session that does not supply the supplemental factor within 2 minutes is terminated and recorded.
The circumstance list that drives the prompt is held as approved configuration, not embedded in code.

requirements.title: Re-authentication at privilege escalation, role change and 30 minutes idle
requirements.description: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall require the technician to re-authenticate before any privilege escalation, before any change to the maintenance role assignment, and after 30 minutes of session inactivity, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall discard its session key at each of those points so a resumed session cannot inherit the earlier authorisation. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An escalation request inside an authenticated session prompts for the full factor set again before it is granted.
A session idle for 30 minutes and 1 second requires re-authentication before the next command is accepted.
The LRU-019 session key is not recoverable from memory after a re-authentication trigger fires.

requirements.title: Fresh two-person re-authentication within 5 minutes of a payload arming release
requirements.description: The Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) shall require a two-person re-authentication completed within the 5 minutes preceding an arming command before it releases an arming state to the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), shall reject an arming command backed by an older authentication, and shall revert to the safe state when the re-authentication is not renewed for a subsequent arming command. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An arming command presented 5 minutes and 1 second after the re-authentication is rejected and the interlock stays safe.
An arming release requires two distinct authenticated identities, and the same identity twice is rejected.
A second arming command without a renewed re-authentication leaves LRU-010 in the safe state.

requirements.title: Identity proofing to the assurance level of the requested role before account creation
requirements.description: Before an account is created on WS-X90 the registration authority operating the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall identity-proof the applicant at the assurance level recorded for the requested role, resolve the applicant to a single individual with no shared or role-only registration accepted, and record the collected, validated and verified identity evidence against the account before the account is enabled. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The registration authority can state the assurance level required for each WS-X90 role and where it is recorded.
Every enabled account resolves to exactly one named individual with no shared registration.
The registration record shows a collection, a validation and a verification step for the identity evidence.

requirements.title: Named sponsor authorisation before an account is enabled
requirements.description: An account registration submitted at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall not be enabled by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) until a named government sponsor or supervisor has authorised it, and the authorisation record naming the sponsor, the role requested and the date shall be retained with the account for its whole life, including after the account is disabled. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: No account in the LRU-013 account table is in the enabled state without a sponsor authorisation record.
The authorisation record names a sponsor who is not the applicant.
Disabling an account leaves the authorisation record intact and retrievable.

requirements.title: Physical identity evidence presented to the registration authority
requirements.description: The registration authority at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall require the applicant to present physical identity evidence, at minimum one government-issued photo credential plus one supporting document, and shall record the evidence type, issuer and reference in the registration record, never an image or a scanned copy of the document. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The registration authority can name the acceptable evidence types without consulting an unwritten convention.
Each registration record lists at least two evidence items with type, issuer and reference.
No document image is present anywhere in the registration store.

requirements.title: Two approved validation and verification methods recorded per evidence item
requirements.description: Identity evidence presented at registration shall be validated for genuineness and currency and verified as belonging to the applicant using the two approved methods, issuer or authoritative-source confirmation and a biometric comparison against the presented credential, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall record the method used and the outcome for each item of evidence. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each evidence item in a registration record carries a validation method and a verification method with an outcome.
A registration in which either method returned an inconclusive outcome does not reach the enabled state.
The approved method list is held as a controlled artifact and referenced by revision in the record.

requirements.title: In-person proofing before a privileged account is enabled
requirements.description: Validation and verification of identity evidence for a WS-X90 privileged role shall be conducted with the applicant physically present before the designated registration authority at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and a remote or delegated proofing session shall not enable a privileged account regardless of the evidence quality presented. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The registration authority can identify which roles require in-person proofing and why.
Every privileged account record carries an in-person proofing attestation naming the registration authority and the date.
A registration marked remote cannot be promoted to a privileged role without a new in-person session.

requirements.title: Media protection policy and procedure set held signed with an annual review flag
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the WS-X90 media protection policy and its five subordinate procedures (media access, marking, storage, transport, sanitization) as signed, version-tagged artifacts, shall name the designated media protection official in the policy header, and shall raise a review-overdue flag on any artifact whose recorded review date is more than 12 months old, meeting the at-least-annual review interval CNSSI 1253 sets for MP-1. A revision shall become effective only when published from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and each publication shall record the custodians and maintenance role holders who received it. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The policy artifact and each of the five procedure artifacts in LRU-020 carry a valid signature, a named approver and a recorded review date.
An artifact whose review date is older than 12 months is listed on the LRU-020 review-overdue report.
A publication attempt from any endpoint other than LRU-017 is refused and recorded in the repository event log.
The distribution record for the current revision names a recipient for every assigned media custodian role.

requirements.title: Media library check-out restricted to named custodians for all non-releasable media
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall gate check-out of every digital and non-digital media item carrying information not cleared for public release - including the removable audit and recovery cartridges written by the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) - on an identity present in the current media custodian list, shall record custodian, item serial and purpose on each successful check-out, and shall refuse and report any request from an identity outside that list. Each refusal shall reach the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 seconds. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A check-out attempt by an identity absent from the custodian list is refused and no media serial is released.
The refusal record is queryable in LRU-018 within 60 seconds of the attempt.
Every LRU-015 cartridge held outside the library at the time of test resolves to an open check-out record naming a current custodian.

requirements.title: Handling markings applied to every removable volume released from provisioning
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall apply a human-readable handling label to every removable volume it writes, carrying the distribution limitation, the handling caveat and the release record identifier held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and shall refuse to close a release record whose label was not printed and confirmed. Volumes exempted from marking shall be limited to media that never leaves the controlled provisioning area, and each exemption shall be recorded against a named area in LRU-020. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Each closed release record in LRU-020 carries a label-confirmed flag and the marking text that was printed.
Every recorded marking exemption names the controlled area the media is confined to.
A sample of released volumes bears a label whose release record identifier resolves in LRU-020.

requirements.title: Removable audit and recovery cartridges accountable from removal to sanitization
requirements.description: Every removable cartridge written by the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) shall be stored in the key-controlled media library inside the controlled maintenance area when not in use, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall keep an inventory entry for each cartridge that stays open - and is reconciled at least monthly against a physical count - until a completed sanitization or destruction record closes it. No cartridge shall be released to storage outside that area without a transport record. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The most recent monthly reconciliation shows a physical count equal to the open inventory entries, or a documented discrepancy with an assigned action.
Each open inventory entry names the cartridge serial, its storage location and the date it left LRU-015.
No inventory entry is closed without a referenced sanitization or destruction record.

requirements.title: Media leaving the controlled area encrypted and bound to a transport record
requirements.description: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) shall refuse to release any volume for transport outside the controlled maintenance area unless the volume is encrypted under a key issued by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and a transport record naming the authorized custodian, the destination, the seal number and the release time is bound to the volume serial. Release shall be permitted only to identities on the transport-authorized list, and the release event shall be exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: An attempt to release an unencrypted volume for transport is refused and produces no transport record.
A released volume's serial resolves to a transport record carrying custodian, destination, seal number and release time.
A release attempt by an identity absent from the transport-authorized list is refused and the attempt appears in LRU-018.

requirements.title: Two-person sanitization record with verification before disposal
requirements.description: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shall host a sanitization record for each media item that captures the reviewer who approved sanitization, the media serial and category, the sanitization method applied, the operator who performed it, the verification result and the disposal action, shall refuse to mark a record complete while the approver and the operator are the same identity or while the verification result is absent, and shall export each completed record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). The designated media custodian shall be able to walk an assessor through that review, approval, verification and disposal sequence end to end. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: The media custodian can name the approver, operator and verifier for the most recent sanitization action and show the record that holds them.
The custodian can demonstrate that a record with the same approver and operator identity cannot be completed.
The custodian can show where a completed record is retained and how it reaches LRU-018.

requirements.title: Annual coupon test of the fielded sanitization tooling
requirements.description: At least annually, and again within 30 days of any change to the sanitization utility version fielded on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), a coupon test shall write a known marker pattern to a sample cartridge of each media type in service, sanitize it with the fielded tooling and procedure, and read the device back; the test passes only when no instance of the marker pattern is recoverable and the tool version, operator and result are recorded. Failure shall suspend use of that tool version for WS-X90 media. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A coupon test record exists for each media type in service dated within the last 12 months.
Read-back of a sanitized coupon recovers no instance of the marker pattern.
Each coupon record names the sanitization tool version, the operator and the pass or fail result.

requirements.title: Nondestructive wipe of portable storage at intake before first connection
requirements.description: A portable storage device shall be nondestructively sanitized on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) intake station, and the wipe result recorded against its serial, before its first connection to any WS-X90 component in either of two circumstances: the device is newly received from a vendor or distributor, or its chain of custody shows a gap since the last recorded WS-X90 use. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall refuse to mount a device in either circumstance until an intake wipe record exists for that serial. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A newly received device with no intake wipe record is refused a mount on LRU-019.
An intake wipe record exists for every portable storage serial that has been connected since the capability was fielded, naming the wipe method and the operator.

requirements.title: Mass-storage devices refused on airborne maintenance ports unless allow-listed
requirements.description: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) shall refuse mass-storage class enumeration on their maintenance ports unless the device serial appears in the signed removable-device allow-list distributed from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), shall leave the port electrically enabled but the storage function unbound on refusal, and shall emit a refusal record naming the device serial and port within 60 seconds. Write access to an allow-listed device shall remain disabled on LRU-001 in flight configuration. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: A non-allow-listed mass-storage device inserted into a maintenance port on LRU-001 or LRU-014 does not enumerate as a storage volume.
The refusal record naming the device serial and the port is retrievable within 60 seconds of insertion.
A write to an allow-listed device from LRU-001 in flight configuration fails and is recorded.

requirements.title: Portable storage devices bound to a named custodian or refused
requirements.description: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) shall hold the approved portable-storage registry, binding each device serial to a named custodian, an issue date and a device category, and shall mark a registry entry vacant when its custodian record lapses. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) shall refuse to mount any portable storage device whose serial has no registry entry or whose entry is marked vacant, so that no device without an identifiable owner is used on WS-X90 equipment. This is fictional example language and not the text of the NIST control.
acceptance_criteria: Every entry in the LRU-020 portable-storage registry names a current custodian, an issue date and a device category.
The mount policy exported to LRU-017 and LRU-019 matches the registry as of its last publication timestamp.
No mount record on LRU-017 or LRU-019 exists for a serial absent from the registry or marked vacant.

control_implementations.narrative: Aurora holds the WS-X90 system and services acquisition policy and its supporting procedures as a controlled document set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020); the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is the only workstation authorised to publish a new revision, and each revision carries signed release metadata naming the designated acquisition security official and the roles the issue was disseminated to. What is missing is enforcement of the review cadence: the repository stores the review date but does not yet block an expired procedure from being cited in a procurement package, and the last full reissue predates the expansion of the tailored profile from 74 to 546 controls, so the procedure set does not yet describe the acquisition actions the new SA, SR and CM enhancements require. Remediation is tracked against the acquisition procedure refresh. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the acquisition policy and procedure set as controlled configuration items, stamps each revision with signed release metadata, and records the review date and the designated official for every issue.
Sole authorised publication point for a new procedure revision; captures the dissemination acknowledgement from each acquisition role before the revision is marked current.

control_implementations.narrative: Aurora intends to carry WS-X90 security engineering as a discrete funded line rather than as overhead absorbed into subsystem budgets. The planned build is a resourcing record, maintained alongside the program work breakdown, that names the security effort allocated to each of the six subsystems and the ground support toolchain refresh covering the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019). Nothing is in place today beyond the draft: the line item has not been established in the programming submission and no subsystem allocation has been agreed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Planned as a named funded item in the security resourcing record, covering the provisioning toolchain refresh and its recurring assurance cost.
Planned as a named funded item covering the conditional maintenance endpoint's sustainment and its periodic re-baselining.

control_implementations.narrative: Every WS-X90 build is admitted to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) through an intake gate that requires a life-cycle phase tag — design, development, integration, qualification or sustainment — and the named security role accountable for that phase; the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) refuses to provision an LRU from a build that lacks either field. Risk decisions taken during a phase are attached to the same build record, which is what makes the risk process part of the life cycle rather than a parallel activity. The gap is coverage: the intake gate is enforced for mission computing, communications and platform management builds, but payload interface firmware is still delivered by the supplier as a sustainment drop without a phase tag, so those builds are admitted under a manual waiver. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs the build intake gate that requires a life-cycle phase tag and an accountable security role, and stores the phase risk decisions against the build record.
Refuses to provision any LRU from a build whose repository record lacks a phase tag or accountable role, which is where the gate is felt operationally.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 preproduction integration bench is today an engineering asset built by hand and protected informally. The planned change is to treat the bench as a controlled environment: provision it from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) using the same signed baseline that flight units receive, and physically bar the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) from bridging the bench to any operational network segment. Neither is in place — bench builds are still assembled from developer images, and the laptop is currently permitted on both sides. This narrative is synthetic demo content.
