by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller triggers and holds the restricted state on a mission software set violation; it does not yet act on violations reported by navigation, timing or payload firmware.
Update & Recovery Controller exposes the last known-good signed image for controlled recovery, requiring an authenticated technician action rather than reimaging on its own.

control_implementations.narrative: Three unauthorized-change classes are raised by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) as incident-class events — unexpected boot measurements, configuration drift from the signed baseline, and the appearance of an unapproved service — and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) incident workflow opens a record for each, so integrity detections enter the same response path as reported incidents rather than a separate engineering queue. The handoff is automated in one direction only: an incident closed in the workflow does not clear the originating detection at the collector, so detections must be reconciled by hand, and the response procedure has not been reissued to describe the new detection-originated entry point. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector classifies the three unauthorized-change detection classes as incident-class events and hands them to the incident workflow.
Platform Management Controller opens and tracks the incident record; closure in the workflow does not yet propagate back to clear the originating detection.

control_implementations.narrative: Every potential integrity violation produces an audit record carrying the failing component, the expected and observed measurement identifiers and the action taken. The record is written to the write-protected region of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), where it cannot be modified or deleted from a maintenance session, and exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), giving an on-platform copy that survives tampering attempts and an off-platform copy that survives loss of the LRU. The two copies are comparable field for field, which is what makes a discrepancy between them meaningful. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Storage Module holds the integrity-violation audit records in a write-protected region that maintenance sessions cannot alter or erase.
Security Log Collector holds the exported copy of each record for off-platform retention and comparison against the on-platform original.

control_implementations.narrative: Boot verification covers all devices capable of verification of the boot process, the CNSSI 1253 scope for this enhancement, in two forms. In mission computing, the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) verifies the Mission Computer (LRU-001) boot from an immutable root of trust, extending one measurement per stage and publishing the resulting platform state for attestation; the root of trust is not writable through the maintenance path. Outside mission computing, the Navigation Processor (LRU-004), Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) each verify their own boot image against a stored signature before enabling any external interface, and report boot verification status at every start, so a failed verification leaves the LRU present but silent on the bus. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller is the immutable root of trust for the mission computing boot chain and extends a distinct measurement at each stage.
Mission Computer boots under stage-by-stage measurement and exposes the resulting platform state for attestation.
Navigation Processor verifies its own boot image against a stored signature and holds its interfaces down until verification passes.
Navigation Sensor Interface performs the same self-verification before it will accept any sensor message.
Payload Interface Controller performs the same self-verification before enabling the payload command and telemetry interfaces.

control_implementations.narrative: Boot firmware on all capable devices sits in a hardware write-protected region. The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) is the only agent that can lift the protection, and only inside an authenticated update sequence staged by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016); protection re-asserts automatically when the sequence ends, so an interrupted update does not leave firmware writable. Any write attempt outside that sequence is blocked at the device and logged, and the write-protect state is reported as part of the platform state so an unprotected device is visible rather than assumed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller gates the write-protect state, re-asserting it at the end of an update sequence and logging blocked write attempts.
Update & Recovery Controller stages the authenticated update sequence that is the only condition under which boot firmware becomes writable.

control_implementations.narrative: All software and firmware from vendors or sources that provide cryptographic mechanisms to enable validation of code authenticity and integrity — the CNSSI 1253 scope here — is signature-verified before installation. The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) performs the check using verification keys held in and never exported from the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), against release metadata drawn from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). An unsigned package, or one signed by a key outside the approved set, is refused with a recorded reason; the refusal is at the controller, so it applies equally to a bundle staged from the provisioning pipeline and to a single-component recovery image. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Update & Recovery Controller performs the pre-installation signature verification and refuses any package that fails or lacks a signature, recording the reason.
Cryptographic Services Module holds the vendor verification keys and performs the verification operation; the keys are not exportable to the controller.
Configuration Repository supplies the signed release metadata that names the approved key set and expected package identity for each release.

control_implementations.narrative: The intent is for mission applications on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) to carry in-process runtime protections that detect control-flow and memory-corruption attempts, terminate the affected process and raise a security event rather than continuing in a corrupted state. The mechanisms are selected in the design record and a security event class is reserved in the monitoring rule set, but the build configuration that enables them is not yet applied to any mission application and no application has been rebuilt or re-qualified under them. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Mission Computer will host the runtime-protected mission applications; mechanism selection is recorded but no application build currently enables them.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 runs no messaging service of its own, so spam protection is scoped to content screening at the points where message and file content enters or leaves the platform: the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) for network-borne content, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) for content transferred from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019). The content policy and the rejection-and-log disposition are drafted, but no screening engine is installed at either point and nothing is being screened today; deliberately, the design places screening at the gateways rather than inside mission applications. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway will screen network-borne message and file content against the approved content policy at the external entry and exit point.
Maintenance Access Gateway will screen content transferred into the platform during a maintenance session before it reaches any platform LRU.
Maintenance Laptop is the source of maintenance-borne content; screening is applied at the gateway rather than trusting the endpoint.

control_implementations.narrative: There is no automatic weekly refresh of a content-screening rule set, because there is no screening engine on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) to refresh — see SI-8. The signed rule package build on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) does not exist either, and no active rule-set version or refresh timestamp is reported to the platform monitoring path. This is recorded as not implemented rather than partial; the at-least-weekly cadence from CNSSI 1253 becomes a requirement on the build once SI-8 is fielded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway has no content-screening rule set installed, so there is nothing to refresh and no active version to report.
Provisioning Workstation has no signed rule-package build pipeline for content screening.

control_implementations.narrative: Behaviour on invalid input is specified per input class — reject, clamp to a documented safe value, or hold current state — for the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006), the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011), and the qualification campaign runs the defined invalid-input set three times to confirm the outcome is identical each time and that no LRU resets, hangs or enters an undocumented mode. Coverage is uneven: the payload interface and interlock have a complete documented action per input class, while several navigation sensor message types are still documented only as "reject" without stating the resulting output state, so predictability there is asserted rather than demonstrated. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Sensor Interface applies per-class invalid-input handling to sensor messages; several message types lack a documented resulting output state.
Payload Interface Controller has a documented action for every invalid command class and is exercised across the full invalid-input set.
Payload Safety Interlock holds its current safe state on any invalid input rather than acting on it, which is its documented behaviour for every input class.

control_implementations.narrative: Two input paths are restricted to trusted sources and approved formats. The Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) accepts navigation messages only from sensor identifiers in the approved sensor configuration and only in approved formats, discarding anything with an unlisted source identifier, an unexpected format version or a non-conforming length before it reaches the Navigation Processor (LRU-004), which therefore never parses an unscreened message. On the payload path, the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) accepts commands only from the authorised mission-compute source on the designated channel and in the approved format, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) independently rejects any command lacking a matching authorisation token, so a single compromised path cannot deliver a payload command on its own. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Sensor Interface screens source identifier, format version and length and discards non-conforming messages before forwarding, counting each discard.
Navigation Processor consumes only screened messages from the interface and has no independent external navigation input path.
Payload Interface Controller restricts payload commands to the authorised mission-compute source, the designated channel and the approved command format.
Payload Safety Interlock applies an independent authorisation-token check, providing the second, separately implemented restriction on the payload command path.

control_implementations.narrative: Mission software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and command handling on the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) treat externally sourced data as untrusted, decoding it through fixed-length structured parsers and passing it across internal interfaces as typed parameters rather than assembling it into command, query or path syntax. The payload command path has been reviewed end to end under that rule. The mission computing side has not: the static analysis injection rule set is configured but its findings on the mission application code base are not yet fully dispositioned, so some legacy log-formatting and configuration-lookup paths remain unreviewed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Mission Computer uses structured decoding and parameterised internal interfaces for external data; injection findings on legacy log and configuration paths are still open.
Payload Interface Controller decodes payload commands with fixed-length structured parsing and has been reviewed end to end for injection paths.

control_implementations.narrative: Errors surfaced off the platform carry a stable error code and a corrective-action class and nothing else — no memory addresses, key identifiers, file paths or account names — with the full diagnostic detail kept on the platform log path where a privileged maintenance role can retrieve it. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) generates the errors and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) is the surface that carries them to the operator. The screening is enforced in the telemetry formatter, which means new error strings added to mission software are only caught when they pass through it; error text emitted on the maintenance console path is not yet subject to the same screening, and closing that second path is the open work. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Mission Computer produces the error condition and the full diagnostic entry, which stays on the platform log path for privileged retrieval.
Payload Telemetry Unit formats and transmits the externally visible error, enforcing the code-and-action-class-only rule on everything it carries.

control_implementations.narrative: Protected configuration, audit and key material in the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is disposed of by cryptographic erase — destroying the wrapping key held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) — followed by an overwrite pass of the affected region, with the disposal recorded by object class and date. The technique is implemented and has been exercised. The retention side is not: retention periods are documented for audit records and key material but not for protected configuration objects, so disposal of that class is triggered by hand at a technician's judgement rather than by an expiry the module can enforce. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Storage Module performs the overwrite pass and writes the disposal record with object class and date; it cannot yet trigger disposal automatically for protected configuration objects.
Cryptographic Services Module holds and destroys the wrapping key, which is the operative step that renders the stored material unrecoverable.

control_implementations.narrative: Telemetry and status output produced by mission and payload software on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) is validated by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) against the published output schema and range set before transmission, and a field outside the expected content is suppressed and logged rather than forwarded, with the schema version reported alongside the stream. Validation today is structural and range-based; semantic consistency checks — a reported payload state that cannot follow from the previous state, for instance — are specified but not implemented, so an in-range but implausible value is still transmitted. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Payload Telemetry Unit applies schema and range validation to every outgoing field, suppresses and logs violations and reports the active schema version.
Mission Computer is the producer of the mission and status content being validated; it carries no independent transmission path that bypasses the telemetry unit.

control_implementations.narrative: Navigation and timing caches are refreshed rather than allowed to age indefinitely. The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) refresh cached almanac, ephemeris and timing correction data at least every 24 hours of operation, and both delete cached navigation state at the recorded mission-end transition, so a subsequent sortie starts without the previous mission's position solution available to it. This both keeps navigation data current and prevents stale mission-associated position information persisting on the platform between sorties. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Timing Receiver refreshes timing correction and almanac data on the 24-hour cadence and clears its cached timing state at mission end.
Navigation Processor refreshes ephemeris data on the same cadence and deletes cached navigation state, including the last position solution, at mission end.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 inherits the Aurora Defense Systems incident response policy and adds a system-level procedure set that names the WS-X90 escalation chain, the declarable incident classes and the containment actions available on each subsystem. Both documents are held as signed revisions in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which is the only source from which a controlled copy may be drawn, and each approved revision is republished to the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) for technician use. What is missing is the review cadence under the expanded scope: the organisation-level policy was last approved before the control set grew to 546 controls, and the WS-X90 procedure set has not yet completed its first at-least-annually review against the new set, so the procedures do not yet name the insider-threat branch or the spillage roles introduced by IR-4(6) and IR-9. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the signed, version-controlled revisions of the WS-X90 incident response policy and procedure set and enforces that a controlled copy can only be drawn from an approved revision.
Provisioning Workstation carries the staged working copy issued to ground support technicians and fails its baseline check when the staged digest differs from the current repository revision.

control_implementations.narrative: Incident response training is delivered by role. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) holds each individual's training record and acts as the gate on responder account issue: no responder account is created on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) without a completion date inside the annual window, and the 30-working-day clock starts from the provisioning record's role-assignment date. Scenario and checklist material is staged to the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) for delivery at operating locations. The core responder cadre is trained and current; what is missing is coverage of the ground support technicians who acquired WS-X90 access during the scope expansion, several of whom are past the 30-working-day bound, and continuous enforcement of the annual refresh — today currency is checked at recertification rather than at each session, so an account can outlive its training record by up to one recertification cycle. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation stores the per-individual incident response training record and refuses responder account issue when the completion date is absent or older than twelve months.
Security Log Collector holds the responder accounts that the training gate protects; its account roster is the list reconciled against training currency at each recertification.
Maintenance Laptop carries the offline scenario and checklist bundle used when training is delivered away from the program facility.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned design injects scripted WS-X90 scenarios — navigation spoofing seen from the Timing Receiver and Navigation Sensor Interface, and maintenance-session abuse seen from the Maintenance Access Gateway — into the annual training cycle. Recorded and sanitised event sets are staged from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and replayed to the responder on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), which times each decision and scores the run against the expected containment sequence. The scenario library and the scoring rubric are drafted and reviewed; no scenario has yet been run against a responder, and the replay tooling is scheduled against the expanded-scope remediation plan. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation will hold the sanitised scenario event sets and the scoring rubric, and will stage a scenario to a laptop only after the scenario is approved.
Maintenance Laptop will replay the scenario to the responder and record decision timing locally, returning the scored run to the provisioning record.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. WS-X90 has no automated incident response training environment; training is delivered from written scenario material rather than from a replay environment. A standalone replay capability hosted on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) with no route to any operational interface has been scoped but is unfunded, and the program has accepted delivering IR-2 and IR-2(1) without it for the current cycle. No claim of partial coverage is made. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation is the intended future host for the isolated replay environment; today it carries only static scenario documents and no replay capability.

control_implementations.narrative: The annual WS-X90 incident response test injects a controlled detection case into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and a controlled privileged-account-abuse case into the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and records elapsed time from event generation to responder acknowledgement and to first containment action. The 2026 test ran both cases and the report is signed. What is missing is coordination with the recovery rehearsal: the controlled-recovery path on the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) was not exercised inside the incident window, so the joint case covering an incident that also requires a controlled restart has not been demonstrated. Because WS-X90 availability is categorised moderate, the joint case is scoped to an orderly bounded restart rather than to failover. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector receives the injected detection case and provides the acknowledgement and containment timestamps the test measures.
Platform Management Controller receives the injected privileged-account-abuse case and supplies the account-change record the responder must find.
Update & Recovery Controller holds the controlled-recovery path that the joint incident-and-recovery case is intended to exercise; it has not yet been included in an incident response test window.

control_implementations.narrative: The plan is to schedule the annual incident response test and the contingency and recovery rehearsal into one window so that a declared incident drives the controlled-recovery path on the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) restart sequence is walked through jointly by the responder and the recovery operator. The joint scenario is written and the two plan owners have agreed the scope; the combined window is booked for the next annual cycle and has not yet run. WS-X90 availability is moderate, so the rehearsal objective is a bounded, orderly restart with a stated duration rather than continuity of service. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller supplies the restart sequence and the platform state checkpoints that both plan owners will walk through in the joint window.
Update & Recovery Controller provides the authenticated controlled-recovery path that the joint rehearsal will exercise against a declared incident.

control_implementations.narrative: Incident handling on WS-X90 is machine-driven from detection to containment. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) evaluates the platform security event stream against the WS-X90 detection rule set and opens an incident record in the protected incident store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) within five minutes, carrying the rule identifier, the originating LRU and a reference to the raw event. Containment is then dispatched to the enforcement points: the Mission Computer (LRU-001) suspends the named non-essential mission service and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) drops the named external session, each inside thirty seconds and each written back to the record as a separate timestamped entry. No step in that chain requires an operator to transcribe an identifier. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector runs the detection rule set over the platform event stream and is the only component that may open an incident record.
Secure Storage Module holds the protected incident store; records are appended and state transitions written, and the store is not writable from the mission network.
Mission Computer executes the service-suspend containment action against a named non-essential mission service and reports the resulting service state back to the incident record.
Protected Network Gateway executes the session-drop containment action at the external boundary and refuses re-establishment of the dropped session without a new authorisation.

control_implementations.narrative: Two WS-X90 incident classes bear directly on mission continuation, and the planned response is a defined safe state rather than continued full capability. On payload command-path compromise the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) stops accepting payload commands and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) latches to inhibit; on navigation integrity loss the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) reverts to its last validated navigation solution and raises a degraded-integrity flag. The class definitions and the latch semantics are agreed and captured in the interface control documents; the firmware changes on LRU-010 and LRU-011 are scheduled into the next load and no build carries them yet. Given moderate availability, the design deliberately accepts a reduced but safe capability rather than attempting to sustain full mission function through the incident. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Payload Interface Controller will reject payload commands for the duration of a declared payload command-path compromise and record each rejection against the incident.
Payload Safety Interlock will latch independently to the inhibit state so that payload authorisation cannot be restored by the compromised command path alone.
Navigation Processor will publish the last validated navigation solution with a degraded-integrity flag instead of a solution derived from suspect inputs.

control_implementations.narrative: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) builds one incident timeline per incident from every reporting subsystem, keyed to platform time rather than to each source's local clock, so that mission compute, navigation, communications, payload, platform management and ground support events are read in a single ordering. Payload health and status records forwarded by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) join that timeline directly rather than being reconciled by hand afterwards. Where a contributing source has been silent for more than fifteen minutes the timeline carries an explicit silence marker, so an analyst distinguishes an absence of events from an absence of reporting. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector normalises source timestamps to platform time, merges the streams onto one incident timeline and emits the silence markers when a source stops reporting.
Payload Telemetry Unit forwards payload health and status records into the correlation stream so payload state is visible on the incident timeline without a separate retrieval.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned insider-threat branch of the WS-X90 incident handling procedure is entered on privileged-session anomalies observed at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) — out-of-window sessions, credential use from an unassigned endpoint — and on out-of-policy account changes made on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013). A case in that branch is routed to a restricted responder list and is not visible to the standard on-call rotation. The trigger conditions are defined and the restricted list has a named approver; the case-visibility partition in the incident tooling is not yet built, so today such a case would be worked in the ordinary queue. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway supplies the privileged-session anomaly conditions that enter the branch and holds the session captures the restricted case will reference.
Platform Management Controller supplies the out-of-policy account-change events that enter the branch and records which administrative identity made each change.

control_implementations.narrative: Coordination for WS-X90 insider-threat cases is planned around a fixed roster that includes, at a minimum, the Senior Agency Official for Privacy or designee and key cybersecurity personnel. The roster is to be bound to the restricted case record so that retrieval of Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session captures and Security Log Collector (LRU-018) extracts is authorised by roster membership rather than by ordinary responder role. The roster composition is agreed with the privacy and security functions; the access binding in the incident tooling is not implemented, so retrieval is currently controlled by ordinary role membership. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway holds the privileged-session captures whose retrieval will be restricted to the coordination roster.
Security Log Collector holds the correlated extracts for the case and will enforce roster membership as the retrieval condition once the binding is built.

control_implementations.narrative: For at a minimum a known or suspected compromise or unauthorized access, the program will share a sanitised WS-X90 incident summary with the National Manager through the appropriate Federal Cyber Center or other designated central department point of contact. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) assembles the summary from the incident record and strips mission payload and navigation content; the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) is the sole egress for that package and applies release review before transmission. The sanitisation profile and the release-review step are specified; the external reporting channel registration is outstanding, so no summary has yet been shared through it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector assembles the sanitised incident summary from the incident record and applies the content-exclusion profile before release.
Protected Network Gateway is the only egress path for incident summaries and enforces release review, so no summary can leave the platform unreviewed.

control_implementations.narrative: Where an incident implicates a supplied component or a delivered software load, the planned handling identifies the affected release from the signed release metadata in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), notifies the supplying organisation, and places a staging hold on the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) so the implicated release cannot be pushed to a platform while the supplier response is outstanding. The metadata needed to make the identification is already present in LRU-020; the staging-hold flag on LRU-016 and its release-by-decision path are designed but not built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository provides the signed release metadata that identifies which delivered load and which supplier a given incident implicates.
Update & Recovery Controller will honour a staging hold on an implicated release and record each refused staging attempt against the incident.

control_implementations.narrative: A named integrated incident response team is planned, drawn from program security engineering, platform engineering and ground support, able to deploy to a WS-X90 operating location within 72 hours. The deployment kit is a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) built from the current approved image held on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and provisioned with credentials scoped to the declared incident class and expiring on return. The roster and the call-out procedure are drafted; the deployment kit build has not been rehearsed and the scoped-credential profile does not yet exist on LRU-017. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Laptop is the deployment endpoint and must be rebuilt from the current approved image immediately before each deployment.
Provisioning Workstation holds the approved deployment image and will issue the incident-class-scoped credentials that expire when the deployment closes.

control_implementations.narrative: After containment the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) retains a read-only forensic capture of the affected Mission Computer (LRU-001) executable region and loaded module list, together with the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) platform integrity state word recorded at the time of the incident, and each capture is hashed at collection so a later analyst can prove the artifact was not altered in storage. What is missing is the analysis side: the program has no offline malicious-code analysis environment approved for WS-X90 artifacts, so captures are retained and hashed but are examined only by inspection of the module list rather than by execution or disassembly. Retention today is set at 90 days against a required 180. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Storage Module holds the read-only forensic captures and the collection-time digests; captures cannot be modified after write.
Mission Computer provides the executable region image and loaded module list at containment, taken before any recovery action changes the state.
Secure Boot Controller supplies the platform integrity state word recorded at the time of the incident, which fixes whether the boot chain was already suspect.

control_implementations.narrative: Anomalous behaviour in the navigation and timing environment is captured at source. The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) emits an anomaly record when holdover is entered without a commanded cause, and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) emits one when cross-sensor divergence exceeds the configured navigation integrity threshold. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) retains those records as a behaviour-analysis stream held separately from routine navigation telemetry, so a pattern can be examined without sampling the full telemetry volume. What is missing is analysis over time: the stream is retained and queryable but no baseline of normal divergence has been established, so an analyst can retrieve anomalies but cannot yet say whether a rate is abnormal. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Timing Receiver raises an anomaly record on uncommanded holdover entry, which is the platform's earliest indicator of a timing-source attack.
Navigation Sensor Interface raises an anomaly record when cross-sensor divergence passes the configured integrity threshold, naming the diverging sensors.
Security Log Collector retains the anomaly records as a separate behaviour-analysis stream with its own retention and query path.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. There is no staffed security operations centre watching the WS-X90 exported event feed from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) outside program working hours, and no delegated authority to declare a WS-X90 incident sits outside the program engineering chain. Events raised overnight are queued and reviewed at the start of the next working day. Standing up a watch, or contracting one, is a program decision that has not been taken and no partial coverage is claimed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector already exports the security event feed a watch would consume; no consumer exists outside program working hours.

control_implementations.narrative: Incident tracking is a machine function on WS-X90. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) mints one tracking identifier per incident at the moment the record opens and carries it through open, contained, eradicated and closed with no manual re-keying at any transition. Every transition is written to the protected incident store on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) with the acting identity and the transition timestamp, and the store rejects a transition whose timestamp precedes its predecessor, so the state history cannot be rewritten to look tidier than it was. Collection and analysis queries run against that store rather than against exported copies. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector mints and owns the incident tracking identifier and performs every state transition; no other component may change incident state.
Secure Storage Module holds the append-only transition history with acting identity and timestamp, and refuses out-of-order transitions.

control_implementations.narrative: Reporting is generated rather than typed. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) renders the initial WS-X90 incident report straight from the incident record — reportable-incident category, affected LRU list, detection time, containment time — and presents it for release review inside fifteen minutes of declaration, leaving unpopulated fields explicitly absent rather than blank-filled. Once released, the report leaves the platform through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) on the approved reporting path; where that path is unavailable the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) carries an abbreviated form under the same release approval. Both paths write a delivery acknowledgement back against the tracking identifier, so an unacknowledged report is visible as such. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector renders the report from the incident record with no manual transcription and holds it in a released or unreleased state.
Protected Network Gateway carries the released report on the approved reporting path and records the delivery acknowledgement against the tracking identifier.
Tactical Data Radio carries the abbreviated report when the gateway path is unavailable, under the same release approval and with its own acknowledgement.

control_implementations.narrative: Where an incident is traced to an exploitable weakness in a fielded configuration, the incident record on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) names the affected baseline item held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) so the weakness is anchored to a specific configuration revision rather than described in prose. The report then goes to the WS-X90 system security engineering lead and to the responsible design authority. What is missing is the timing discipline and the second recipient: the routing to the design authority is manual and two of the four cases worked since the scope expansion reached it later than five working days after containment. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector holds the incident record and the field that names the implicated baseline item, and is the source of the containment timestamp the five-working-day bound is measured from.
Configuration Repository supplies the baseline item identifier and revision so the weakness is attached to a specific fielded configuration.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned supplier notice draws the affected part number and release identifier from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) rather than from free text, and carries no mission data, no navigation data and no operating location. The template and the content-exclusion rules are drafted and have been reviewed by the program security function; the supplier distribution list and the transmission route are not yet established, so no notice has been issued under this control. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository is the authoritative source for the part number and release identifier that a supplier notice must name, and the notice template reads them from it.

control_implementations.narrative: A named WS-X90 incident response support contact is reachable during program working hours and advises operators and technicians on reporting and on the bounded containment actions a technician may take from the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) without escalation. The current contact details are carried in the approved ground support procedure staged on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). What is missing is cover outside program hours and a defined deputy: when the primary contact is unavailable the route falls back to the general engineering queue, which has no defined response expectation, and this is the same gap that IR-4(14) records at the watch level. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway is the surface on which the bounded technician containment actions are performed, so the support contact advises against its specific action set.
Provisioning Workstation stages the approved ground support procedure that carries the current support contact details.

control_implementations.narrative: The current incident reporting procedure, contact roster and containment checklist are packaged as a signed bundle and held offline on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019), refreshed from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) so a responder at a remote location does not need a network path to obtain them. The bundle signature verifies against the LRU-017 signing key before the laptop will render it. What is missing is refresh on roster change: the bundle is rebuilt on the quarterly image cycle rather than when the roster changes, so a deployed laptop can carry contact details up to three months stale. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation builds and signs the offline bundle and holds the roster revision the bundle is built from.
Maintenance Laptop stores the signed bundle, verifies its signature before rendering, and is usable with no network path available.

control_implementations.narrative: The plan establishes a named working relationship with the external providers of the protected transport and network protection services behind the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), with WS-X90 responders identified to those providers by role and by name and an agreed first action for a cross-boundary event. Contact records are drafted on the program side; the provider side has not been formally engaged and no joint exercise has been held, so a cross-boundary event today would begin with an introduction. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway is the boundary at which a provider-side event and a WS-X90 event meet, and the relationship exists to work events observed on either side of it.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 incident response plan describes the responder structure, the declarable incident classes, the reportable-incident definitions, the metrics the program tracks and the resources committed to the capability. It is held as a signed release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with a protected working copy on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) so that the plan is still readable during an incident that affects program information technology, and both copies are protected from unauthorised change. What is missing is the approval and distribution cycle under the expanded scope: the current revision predates the move to the 546-control set, has not been re-approved by the CISO/SAISO or equivalent, and its distribution list does not yet cover the ground support personnel who took on response roles with the expansion. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the signed plan revisions and the approval record, and is the source for any controlled copy.
Secure Storage Module holds the protected on-platform working copy so the plan survives loss of program information technology during an incident.

control_implementations.narrative: Spillage response on WS-X90 is split between containment and eradication. On declaration the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) blocks external sessions for the affected enclave and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) isolates the contaminated LRU port, both inside ten minutes, and the responder alert is issued on a path that does not traverse the contaminated segment. Eradication overwrites the affected regions of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) with the approved sanitisation routine and produces a record naming every region cleared, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) is queried for every baseline that carried a copy of the affected artifact so that subsequently contaminated components are identified rather than assumed absent. What is missing is the assignment step and the alerting path: responsibility for spillage response is named in the procedure by role but not by individual, and the out-of-band alert route has been walked through on paper rather than exercised. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway blocks external sessions for the affected enclave on declaration, cutting the outward path before eradication begins.
Internal Ethernet Switch isolates the contaminated LRU port so the spilled artifact cannot propagate across the internal segments.
Secure Storage Module is overwritten region by region with the approved sanitisation routine and produces the cleared-region completion record.
Configuration Repository is queried to enumerate every baseline, including superseded revisions, that received a copy of the affected artifact.

control_implementations.narrative: Spillage response training is planned on a cycle consistent with IR-2 for every individual authorised to handle WS-X90 mission data, covering the declaration route, the prohibition on discussing a spill over the contaminated path and the individual's own containment obligations. Completion will be recorded against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) alongside the incident response training record. The material is drafted; delivery is scheduled with the next IR-2 cycle and no completions have been recorded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation will hold the spillage training completion date on the same provisioning record that gates account issue, so currency is visible in one place.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. WS-X90 has no documented degraded-operations procedure for continuing assigned tasks while contaminated storage is under corrective action. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) does support partitioned execution and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) can enforce a partition boundary, so the mechanism exists, but no procedure defines which tasks may continue, for how long, or at what point operations stop. Because WS-X90 availability is categorised moderate, the program has not treated continuation through a spill as a priority and has accepted a stop-and-remediate posture for now. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Mission Computer provides the partitioned execution capability a future continuation procedure would use; no partition is currently designated as the uncontaminated working partition.
Platform Management Controller can enforce a partition boundary but has no configured boundary policy for post-spill operation.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. There is no defined handling for an individual exposed to WS-X90 information outside their access authorisation. Suspension of that individual's sessions on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), quarantine and imaging of the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) used in the exposure, and a signed exposure acknowledgement as a precondition of access restoration are all specified in the draft spillage procedure but none is in force, and the draft has not been approved. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway can suspend an individual's sessions on demand but has no exposure-driven trigger configured.
Maintenance Laptop would be the quarantined and imaged endpoint; no quarantine holding process or imaging destination is established.

control_implementations.narrative: The Aurora personnel security policy and the WS-X90 supporting procedures set the screening levels, national eligibility gating, access agreement terms and termination and transfer handling that the program applies. The approved revision is held as a signed release in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and disseminated to every role that provisions accounts from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and a named official is designated to manage it. What is missing is currency: the last approved revision predates the national eligibility gating change made during the scope expansion, so the enforced behaviour on LRU-017 is stricter than the published procedure describes, and the at-least-annually review is overdue. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the signed personnel security policy and procedure revisions and their approval records.
Provisioning Workstation is where the policy is operationally enforced and where the dissemination record for provisioning roles is kept.

control_implementations.narrative: Every WS-X90 position that can obtain a privileged account carries a recorded risk designation with the screening criteria that follow from it, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) refuses to issue a privileged account for a position whose designation record is absent. What is missing is the review trigger set: designations are reviewed on the annual cycle, but the additional triggers — position description update and position vacancy — are not wired into the personnel process, so a description rewritten mid-year does not force a designation review until the next annual pass. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation holds the position risk designation records and enforces their presence as a precondition of privileged account issue.

control_implementations.narrative: Screening is a hard precondition of WS-X90 account creation. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) holds each individual's completed screening record and the level it was completed at, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) will not create an account until LRU-017 confirms a completed screening at the level the position risk designation requires. The record is re-verified at each account recertification cycle rather than checked once at issue, so an account whose holder's screening lapses is caught at the next cycle and refused renewal. Refusals are recorded with the reason. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation is the authoritative store for screening completion and level, and answers the account-creation precondition query.
Platform Management Controller creates no account without a positive screening answer from LRU-017 and records each refusal with its reason.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 mission data and privileged maintenance sessions are restricted to individuals whose citizenship status is recorded and verified against the program's national eligibility requirement. The verification is held on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), is set by the program security function rather than by the requesting individual or the provisioning technician, and is enforced as a hard gate: the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) privileged maintenance roster is built only from individuals carrying a verified eligibility record, and an account request without one is refused rather than issued with an advisory flag. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation holds the verified national eligibility record and restricts who may set it to the program security function.
Maintenance Access Gateway builds its privileged maintenance roster only from individuals with a verified eligibility record and rejects sessions from anyone else.

control_implementations.narrative: Termination processing disables WS-X90 access on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) within the same day for an involuntary termination and within five working days for a voluntary one, updates the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), places the issued credential on the revocation list held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) so the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) rejects it at the next session attempt, and records recovery of any assigned Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) or issued token. What is missing is the exit interview content and the retention step: exit interviews are held but do not follow a defined security topic list, and there is no documented process for retaining program access to information formerly controlled by the terminated individual, which has left two orphaned data sets on the ground support share. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller applies the account disable within the applicable time bound and stamps the disable action for later measurement.
Provisioning Workstation closes the individual's provisioning record and holds the disable reference and the property return record.
Cryptographic Services Module places the individual's issued credential on the WS-X90 revocation list so the credential fails at the next use.
Maintenance Access Gateway checks the revocation list on each session attempt and rejects a revoked credential at first presentation.
Maintenance Laptop is the assigned support property recovered and recorded as returned before the termination record is closed.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned exit process notifies departing individuals who held WS-X90 access of the legally binding post-employment obligations for protecting program information and takes a signed acknowledgement, filed against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) as a precondition of closing that record. The obligation text has been settled with the legal function; the exit interview script has not been updated to include it and no acknowledgement has yet been captured. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation will hold the signed post-employment acknowledgement reference and will not report a provisioning record as fully closed without it.

control_implementations.narrative: Termination is machine-driven. A termination action entered in the Aurora personnel feed disables the individual's mapped WS-X90 accounts on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and raises a notification to the security operations distribution held by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) inside sixty minutes, with no technician performing the disable by hand. A feed entry that maps to no WS-X90 account produces a recorded no-op rather than a silent drop, so a mapping error is visible as an unmatched entry rather than as an account that was never disabled. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller consumes the personnel feed termination action and disables every mapped account automatically.
Security Log Collector receives the termination notification onto the security operations distribution and retains it with the individual identifier and action time.

control_implementations.narrative: On reassignment or transfer, the WS-X90 access set is reviewed against the operational need of the new position and accesses no longer required on need-to-know grounds are removed or disabled on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), with the change confirmed against the individual's provisioning record on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). What is missing is the ten-working-day discipline and the notification step: transfers are worked in the monthly provisioning batch, so three of the seven transfers since the scope expansion exceeded ten working days, and no automatic notification is raised to the receiving and losing managers. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller applies the access removal or modification and records which accesses were retained against the new position's need.
Provisioning Workstation holds the operational-need record for the new position and the confirmation entry naming the confirming role.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 access agreement is signed before any account is issued and re-signed at least annually or whenever the agreement text is updated. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) holds the signed agreement date and treats it as a precondition of both account issue and each recertification, so an account cannot be renewed against a lapsed agreement. Publishing a new agreement revision automatically raises a re-sign requirement against every holder of the superseded revision rather than waiting for their next anniversary. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation stores the signed access agreement date and revision per individual and enforces it at issue and at recertification.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned change adds the legally binding post-employment obligations to the WS-X90 access agreement itself and takes the individual's acknowledgement at initial access rather than only at exit, recorded on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) beside the signed agreement. The clause is drafted and agreed with the legal function; it has not yet been published as an agreement revision, so no current holder has acknowledged it at grant. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation will hold the acknowledgement reference alongside the access agreement record and will require it before initial access is granted.

control_implementations.narrative: External providers whose personnel hold WS-X90 credentials or maintenance access carry contractual personnel security requirements, including a duty to notify the organizational security manager of any transfer or termination of those personnel as soon as possible and not to exceed one working day. Compliance is monitored by reconciling the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session roster and the issued Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) inventory against each provider's personnel list. What is missing is coverage and cadence: two of the five current provider agreements predate the one-working-day clause and carry a five-day term instead, and the reconciliation has been run twice in the last six months rather than monthly. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway session roster is the list of external personnel actually able to open a privileged session and is the primary reconciliation input.
Maintenance Laptop inventory records which issued endpoint is held by which external individual, so an unreturned unit surfaces a stale provider record.

control_implementations.narrative: A formal sanctions process for WS-X90 policy breaches is planned, triggered by defined conditions including bypassing the maintenance session controls on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and suppressing or deleting records on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), with notification to the program security manager and the individual's line manager within five working days of initiation, naming the individual and the reason. The organisation has a general disciplinary process; the WS-X90 trigger conditions and the notification path have been drafted but not adopted, so no program-specific initiation has occurred. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway supplies the session-control bypass evidence that would initiate the process.
Security Log Collector supplies the record-suppression evidence and holds the audit trail a sanctions case would rest on.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned update states the security responsibilities carried by each WS-X90 role that can provision accounts from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or sign a configuration baseline into the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and references the applicable position description revision from the individual's provisioning record so the responsibilities in force at the time of a grant can be reconstructed. Draft text exists for the two provisioning roles; the baseline-signing roles have not been drafted and no position description has been reissued. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation holds the provisioning-authority role list whose position descriptions must state security responsibilities, and will carry the revision reference on each record.
Configuration Repository holds the baseline-signing role list, which is the second population whose position descriptions are in scope.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 audit and accountability policy and its implementing procedures are held as a signed record set in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which carries the approving official, the revision number and the review date, and pushes the approved revision to the platform role dissemination list. What is missing is the procedure half: the policy was re-approved in the current annual cycle, but the procedures still describe the original 74-control audit scope and have not been rewritten for the expanded 546-control set or for the correlation and reviewer-queue behaviour now running on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). The procedure rewrite is carried on the plan of action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed, version-controlled audit policy and procedure records, the approving official and review dates, and drives the dissemination list to all WS-X90 platform role holders.
Is the audit pipeline the procedures govern; a change to its ingest, correlation or reviewer-queue configuration is the event that triggers an out-of-cycle procedure review.

control_implementations.narrative: Payload command records generated by the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) carry four fields beyond the AU-3 base set: the command opcode, the originating crew-station identifier, the commanded payload state and the Payload Safety Interlock state sampled at command time. LRU-010 populates each field or writes an explicit null marker rather than omitting it, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) parses the extended schema natively so an analyst sees the payload context without joining to a second source. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Generates the extended payload command audit record and samples the interlock state at command time so the record is self-describing.
Ingests and indexes the extended schema, exposing the four additional fields as searchable columns rather than opaque payload text.

control_implementations.narrative: Audit segments written on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) are closed on a 24-hour timer or on reaching their size limit, whichever comes first, and transferred to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which is a physically separate component in a different subsystem. LRU-015 keeps the local copy until LRU-018 acknowledges receipt, so a failed transfer retries rather than losing the segment; the retry is itself recorded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Closes, seals and queues audit segments for transfer, and retains each local copy until receipt is acknowledged.
Receives transferred segments off the recording component, acknowledges receipt and holds the platform-external copy.

control_implementations.narrative: The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) reports audit partition utilisation to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), which raises an operator warning within 60 seconds of the partition crossing 75% of its allocated capacity — the CNSSI 1253 parameter for this system — and repeats at each further 5% of consumption. The warning is written to the on-platform maintenance log as well as the operator display, so a warning raised while the crew station is unattended is still recoverable. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Measures audit partition utilisation and reports the 75% crossing with the crossing timestamp.
Raises and repeats the operator warning within 60 seconds and writes the maintenance log entry naming the partition and percentage.

control_implementations.narrative: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) runs the approved correlation rule set against records as they are ingested, with no operator step in the job definition, and builds a weekly reviewer queue covering the preceding seven days for the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) — the at-least-weekly cadence carried by the CNSSI 1253 parameter for AU-6. What is missing is the downstream automation: an analyst who accepts a queue item still opens the incident ticket by hand, so the review process is automated but the hand-off into incident handling is not. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Executes the correlation rule set on ingest and assembles the weekly reviewer queue with full seven-day coverage.
Presents the reviewer queue to the on-platform administrator and records queue disposition; the ticket hand-off from this point is still manual.

control_implementations.narrative: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) joins the on-platform audit store copied from the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) with the configuration-change history held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), keyed on actor identity and time, so a configuration change and the audit records it produced resolve to a single correlated event and an unmatched change is reported rather than dropped. The maintenance session transcript store was the third repository sitting outside that key space; it was brought inside it on 2026-10-28, so a change made during a maintenance session now resolves to the session that carried it as well as to the change record, and the analysis view can say under whose hands a change was made. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Performs the join on actor identity and time across the audit store, the configuration-change history and, since 2026-10-28, the maintenance session transcript store, and publishes the correlated analysis view.
Supplies the on-platform audit record repository as one correlation input.
Supplies the configuration-change history as the second correlation input, including the approving identity for each change.

control_implementations.narrative: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) is the single central review surface for WS-X90 audit content: an analyst reviews platform-wide activity from LRU-018 without logging in to a source component, and an LRU that misses its expected reporting interval shows as silent rather than simply absent. What is missing is live coverage of the Navigation and Timing Subsystem — records from the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) reach the central view through a batch export taken at mission close rather than the live path, so intra-mission navigation activity is not centrally reviewable until the mission ends. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Hosts the central review interface, the reporting-component register and the silent-source detection.
Emits navigation processing audit content that reaches the central view only through an end-of-mission batch export.
Emits sensor-interface audit content on the same end-of-mission batch path, so it is absent from the live central view.

control_implementations.narrative: The design places the vulnerability scan results and the host monitoring stream produced for the Mission Computer (LRU-001) into the same analysis view on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), with a source-type column that keeps audit, scan and monitoring rows distinguishable while allowing one time-window query to return all three. Neither feed is ingested yet; the ingest adapters and the extended view schema are scheduled work and no correlated analysis across the three sources is available today. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will host the extended analysis view and the two new ingest adapters; today it holds audit records only.
Is the source of the host monitoring stream and the scan target whose results will be joined; it produces both today for separate consumers.

control_implementations.narrative: The design correlates each provisioning session on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) with the facility badge entry that preceded it, so a provisioning session with no matching physical entry is raised as an exception on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). The facility physical-access feed is owned outside the program and is not yet delivered to LRU-018; the data-source agreement, the feed format and the matching window are drafted but the correlation rule is not built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will ingest the physical-access feed and run the session-to-entry matching rule; the rule is not yet built.
Produces the provisioning session records that will form one side of the correlation; those records exist today.

control_implementations.narrative: Audit reduction and report generation run on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) from stored queries against a read-only view of the segment store, so a report run leaves the source records byte-identical and preserves their relative order; each report header carries the query text, the requesting operator and the record count. What is missing is scope: approved report templates exist only for the original 74-control assessment scope, and templates for the expanded 546-control set are not yet written, so reporting against the new controls is done with ad-hoc queries that are not repeatable between analysts. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs reduction and report generation against a read-only view, preserves source content and ordering, and stamps each report header; its approved template set still covers only the original control scope.

control_implementations.narrative: The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) indexes event type, actor identity, source LRU identifier, outcome and event timestamp, and processes, sorts and searches on any of the five. A seven-day query over the full retained platform volume returns inside 30 seconds, and sorting on event timestamp is stable so records sharing a timestamp keep a deterministic order between runs. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintains the five field indexes, executes the sort and search, and holds the 30-second seven-day query budget as a tested performance requirement.

control_implementations.narrative: Every closed audit segment on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is copied to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which sits in the Ground Support Subsystem on a different chassis from the LRUs being audited. The CNSSI 1253 parameter for this system is at least weekly; the fielded cadence is daily, and a calendar week that closes with no acknowledged copy raises a maintenance alert so the floor cannot be silently missed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the audit segments being copied and tracks the per-week copy acknowledgement that drives the missed-copy alert.
Is the physically separate repository that receives and retains the copy, on a different chassis from every audited LRU.

control_implementations.narrative: Audit records and the tools that read them are integrity-protected by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003): it signs each audit segment as the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) closes it, and signs each audit tool binary before release. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) verifies both against the current platform trust anchor, quarantining a segment that fails verification rather than ingesting it and refusing execution of an unsigned or mis-signed tool. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Performs the segment and tool signing operations and holds the signing keys inside the protected boundary.
Presents each segment for signature at close and stores the signature alongside the segment.
Verifies segment and tool signatures against the platform trust anchor and quarantines or refuses on failure.

control_implementations.narrative: Audit logging configuration is owned by a dedicated audit-management group of no more than three named individuals, kept disjoint from the general platform administration group. On the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) that separation is enforced by the access control policy on the audit configuration objects. What is missing is the same enforcement on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013): the platform administration group there can still alter local audit configuration, so the subset restriction holds off-platform but not on the controller itself. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces audit-management group ownership of the audit configuration objects and holds the group membership export.
Hosts local audit configuration that the general platform administration group can still modify; the split is not yet enforced here.

control_implementations.narrative: The design requires two distinct authenticated approvals from the audit-management group, recorded in one transaction, before any audit information — the CNSSI 1253 parameter is any audit information, not a subset — is moved or deleted on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) or the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), with a single-approval attempt failing closed and being logged as a denied action. The dual-approval transaction does not exist yet on either component; today both accept a single approval from that group. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will require the two-approval transaction before a segment can be moved or deleted; today a single approval suffices.
Will require the same two-approval transaction for its record store and will log denied single-approval attempts.

control_implementations.narrative: Read-only analysis accounts reach audit content on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) through an interface that exposes no write, edit or delete verb, so read-only access is enforced by the interface surface rather than by convention. What is missing is the storage layer: the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) still exposes a maintenance write path to the segment store that is not restricted to the audit writer service identity, so a maintenance identity can in principle write to a store that should be read-only to everything but the writer. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Presents the read-only analysis interface, whose surface offers no mutating verb to any account that reaches it.
Holds the segment store; its maintenance write path is not yet restricted to the audit writer service identity.

control_implementations.narrative: Non-repudiation for payload actions is built from two halves. The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) attaches a signature produced by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) to every arm and release command, covering the command, the operator identity and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) state sampled at command time, so an altered replay fails verification. LRU-003 holds the signing keys with no export path. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) verifies each signature on ingest and marks a record it cannot verify rather than discarding it. What is missing is key history: the retired-key identifier list is not yet published to LRU-018, so records signed under a rotated key verify as unknown-key and land in the unverifiable bucket even though they were validly signed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Assembles and signs the arm and release command structure, binding command, operator identity and interlock state into one signed object.
Supplies the independent interlock state that is bound into the signature, so the interlock reading cannot be substituted after the fact.
Holds the non-repudiation signing keys in protected storage with no export path and performs the signing operation.
Verifies command signatures on ingest and marks unverifiable records; it lacks the retired-key identifier history needed to resolve rotated keys.

control_implementations.narrative: The CNSSI 1253 parameter for this enhancement is a retention of the capability to access audit records for the duration of the required retention period, which for WS-X90 means keeping the reader tooling, the record schema version and the verification key for each segment for as long as the segment itself is retained. The design places tooling and schema versions in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and the per-epoch verification keys on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015). Neither store is populated for historical epochs yet, and a segment older than the current schema version cannot today be read without an out-of-configuration tool. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will retain the per-epoch verification keys needed to check an old segment; today it retains only the current key set.
Will hold the reader tooling and record schema version applicable to each retention epoch; the historical entries are not yet loaded.

control_implementations.narrative: The system-wide audit trail is time-correlated to the platform time reference distributed by the Timing Receiver (LRU-005), which holds the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) inside the AU-8 tolerance and declares holdover with a degraded-time marker on emitted records when it cannot.
