The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) compiles records from every reporting LRU into one trail ordered on that reference, carrying the degraded-time marker through rather than interleaving silently. The relay path was the last ordering exception and it closed on 2026-11-05, when the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) began stamping its own source time; switch-origin events are ordered on origin from that date and stay inside the tolerance while the internal segment is congested. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Distributes the single platform time reference used both to bound navigation timestamps and to order the compiled system-wide trail, monitors holdover and drives the degraded-time marker.
Consumes the platform time reference and stamps its navigation audit records inside the AU-8 tolerance.
Consumes the same reference for sensor-interface audit records and marks them degraded during declared holdover.
Relays audit records from segmented internal paths and, since 2026-11-05, stamps each one with its own source time, so relayed events are ordered on origin instead of on arrival at the collector.
Compiles the system-wide trail on the platform time reference and preserves the degraded-time marking.

control_implementations.narrative: The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) exposes the logging-selection function to the audit-management group only, offering a fixed approved event-criteria set rather than free-form configuration, and every accepted or refused change is itself audited with requester, target LRU and criteria selected. Changes reach the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within seconds. What is missing is the payload path: the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) only reads new logging configuration at a mission-mode transition, so a change can take substantially longer than 15 minutes to take effect there if the platform is mid-mission. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Hosts the logging-selection function, enforces audit-management group ownership and audits every change request and refusal.
Applies a logging change within seconds of receipt and reports the applied criteria back to LRU-013.
Reads logging configuration only at a mission-mode transition, so it does not meet the 15-minute threshold mid-mission.

control_implementations.narrative: The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) captures the full command and response content of every nonlocal maintenance session, whichever maintenance account opened it, and forwards the transcript to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) at session close, including for sessions that terminate abnormally. What is missing is the second half of the control: the legal-review record required before session content may be retained and used for personnel-conduct purposes is not complete, so transcripts are currently retained for security analysis only, under a narrower retention rule than the design assumes. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Records session command and response content, marks the recorded state to the technician and forwards the transcript at close.
Receives, indexes and retains session transcripts under the narrower security-analysis retention rule pending the legal review.

control_implementations.narrative: Session auditing on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is enabled by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) as an ordered step of the authenticated boot sequence, ahead of the step that brings the maintenance port up. If the enable step fails, the boot sequence leaves the maintenance port down, so there is no window in which a maintenance session can be opened with session auditing off and no operator action is available to reorder the two steps. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Sequences session-audit enablement ahead of maintenance port bring-up in the authenticated boot chain and fails the port closed if enablement fails.
Receives the enable at boot and refuses to accept a session while session auditing is not active.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has no capability for an authorized supervisor to view an in-progress maintenance session in real time. Sessions on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) are reviewable only after close, from the forwarded transcript, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) carries no observation path. A design naming the observation path, the supervisor authorization and the technician notification is not yet approved. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provides post-close transcript review only; no live observation interface exists.
Carries no maintenance-observation policy or path today.

control_implementations.narrative: The design restricts release of WS-X90 audit information across an organizational boundary to a single approved coordination method bound to a named egress policy on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), with the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) recording the receiving organization, the record set released and the releasing authority for each transfer. The coordination method is drafted but not approved, the egress policies are not written, and no transfer register exists on LRU-018. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will enforce the named egress policy for cross-boundary audit release; no such policy is configured today.
Will apply the same restriction to audit content leaving over the tactical data path; today it carries no audit egress path at all.
Will hold the transfer register naming receiving organization, record set and releasing authority; the register is not built.

control_implementations.narrative: The design carries the originating individual identity through unchanged in any audit record exported to a partner organization, resolving it from the platform identity binding held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) rather than substituting a locally reassigned or per-session identifier on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). Since no cross-organizational export path is built, the export mapping that would preserve identity does not exist and no transform has been written or reviewed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will apply the identity-preserving export mapping; no export transform exists today.
Holds the platform identity binding that the mapping will resolve against; the binding exists and is in use for on-platform verification.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 does not share audit information with external organizations. There is no sharing-agreement record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and no agreement check on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), because there is no release path to gate. The gap is carried on the plan of action with a named owner rather than being closed by an unused mechanism. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds no cross-organizational audit sharing agreements today.
Has no cross-organizational release path and therefore no agreement check on release.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 maintenance policy and its implementing procedures are held as signed, version-controlled records in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with a named approving official and an at-least-annual review, the CNSSI 1253 parameter for this control. The policy was re-approved inside the current cycle. What is missing is the procedure set: it still describes the local maintenance path only and has not been updated for the nonlocal maintenance path implemented on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) in build 4.2, so technicians work that path from an engineering work instruction rather than an approved procedure. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed maintenance policy and procedure records, the approving official and the annual review dates.
Implements the nonlocal maintenance path that the current approved procedure set does not yet cover.

control_implementations.narrative: Maintenance, repair and replacement actions are scheduled, dispatched and closed out through the automated workflow on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) refuses any maintenance action that does not carry an open work order, so the workflow is a gate rather than a record. Closed-out actions are written to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with the acting technician and the parts fitted. What is missing is coverage of the payload LRUs: maintenance records for the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) are still entered by hand after the fact and are not subject to the 30-day stale-record flag, so the record set is accurate for the platform management subsystem and incomplete for the payload interface subsystem. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs the automated scheduling, dispatch and close-out workflow and stamps each state change with an actor identity.
Enforces the work-order gate, refusing to apply any maintenance action with no open order.
Holds one maintenance record per LRU carrying the raise, booking, work-under-way and close-out timestamps, and runs the 30-day stale-record flag.
Is maintained under hand-entered records that bypass the automated workflow and are excluded from the stale-record flag.

control_implementations.narrative: Before a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is issued, the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) compares its tool image against the approved tool baseline and blocks issue on any difference in file set, version or signature, recording the comparison against the laptop serial number. What is missing is the return leg: a laptop coming back from the field is re-shelved without re-inspection, so an unauthorized modification made during field use is only caught at the next issue rather than at return, and the record does not distinguish the two. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs the pre-issue baseline comparison and holds the approved tool baseline and the per-serial inspection record.
Is the inspected endpoint; it is checked at issue but not re-inspected on return from the field.

control_implementations.narrative: Diagnostic and test media are scanned on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) with a signature set no more than seven days old before the media reaches any WS-X90 interface, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) records the scan result and the signature-set date against the media serial number. Media presented at a platform interface without a current recorded scan is refused, so the scan is enforced at the point of use rather than only at the point of issue. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Performs the malicious-code scan with a signature set inside the seven-day currency window and blocks media that fails.
Records the scan result, the signature-set date and the media serial number, and is the source the platform interface checks against.

control_implementations.narrative: The design requires maintenance equipment that has held WS-X90 information — principally the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) — to be verified clear, sanitized, destroyed or covered by a recorded exemption from a named authorizing official before it leaves the facility, with the release record joined to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session history that shows what the equipment was used for. The disposition procedure is drafted; there is no release record store, no join to session history, and no check today that prevents equipment leaving with no disposition recorded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Is the equipment the release control will cover; it currently leaves the facility on a manual sign-out with no disposition record.
Holds the maintenance session history the release record will be joined to; the join is not built.

control_implementations.narrative: Maintenance tool use is restricted at both ends. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) accepts a tool invocation only from an authenticated technician present on the current authorized-maintainer list, and revocation takes effect within one session. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) will not launch a platform maintenance tool without a valid session token issued by LRU-014, so a laptop separated from the gateway is not a usable tool platform. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Authenticates the technician against the authorized-maintainer list, issues the session token and refuses invocations from revoked identities.
Refuses to launch a platform maintenance tool without a valid LRU-014 session token.

control_implementations.narrative: Every maintenance tool invocation that runs with elevated platform privilege produces an audit record from the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) naming the tool, the technician identity and the privilege level, so privileged tool use is fully visible after the fact. Detection caught up with that visibility on 2026-11-14, when the rule raising an alert for a privileged invocation that falls outside an open work order was built on LRU-018; out-of-order privileged use now surfaces on its own rather than waiting for someone to go looking for it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Emits the privileged-invocation audit record with tool, technician and privilege level for every elevated tool run.
Receives and retains those records and, since 2026-11-14, raises the out-of-work-order alert when a privileged invocation has no open work order standing behind it.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 maintenance tools are baselined at first issue and are not inspected against a current approved patch level. The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds no per-tool approved patch level, and the issue workflow for the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) has no patch-level check or withhold action, so a tool can be issued with software older than the approved level without that being visible. The gap is carried on the plan of action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds no approved patch level per maintenance tool today.
Is issued without a patch-level inspection; there is no withhold action in the issue workflow.

control_implementations.narrative: Nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) are logged with the event set defined in the WS-X90 audit policy for AU-1 — the CNSSI 1253 parameter points at that policy rather than a local list — covering session start, authentication outcome, every privileged command, every file transfer and session end. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) places each closed session in the review queue within one working day, so anomalous behaviour is reviewed against a defined queue rather than on request. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Generates the five logged event classes for each nonlocal session, drawn from the audit policy event set in force.
Queues each closed session for review within one working day and holds the reviewer disposition.

control_implementations.narrative: The control is met on two paths. For in-place service, a session may be opened only from a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) whose baseline provides authentication, session encryption, endpoint integrity checking and audit forwarding at the platform level, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) requires a baseline attestation before establishing the session. For off-platform service, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) clears mission information from the removed LRU while the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) retains its recovery material, and LRU-016 re-verifies the component image against the approved baseline before reconnection. Two gaps remain: contractor-supplied endpoints are still accepted on a manual waiver rather than an attestation, and the clear-and-verify path is automated only for Platform Management Subsystem LRUs — payload and navigation LRUs are removed under a manual procedure. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Attests to the comparable-security baseline before a session is established; government-issued images attest, contractor-supplied endpoints run on a manual waiver.
Enforces the attestation requirement at session establishment and records any waiver with an expiry date.
Clears mission information from a removed LRU and re-verifies its image against the approved baseline before reconnection, automated for SUB-05 LRUs only.
Retains the recovery material for a removed LRU so its configuration can be restored after service.

control_implementations.narrative: Nonlocal maintenance sessions are authenticated on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) with a replay-resistant authenticator, so a captured exchange replayed against the gateway is refused. The session is carried on a dedicated VLAN on the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and a dedicated policy on the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), logically separated from mission traffic; maintenance frames observed on the switch carry the maintenance VLAN tag only. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Performs the replay-resistant authentication and binds the resulting session to the maintenance path.
Provides the dedicated maintenance VLAN that keeps maintenance frames off the mission VLANs.
Applies a maintenance-specific policy distinct from the mission traffic policy at the external boundary.

control_implementations.narrative: Nonlocal maintenance traffic between the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is protected for integrity and confidentiality with the approved algorithms listed in CNSSP 15 Annex B, the CNSSI 1253 parameter for this enhancement. Session keys are issued and held by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and appear in the platform key inventory by identifier. Negotiation is constrained to the approved set: a client offering only algorithms outside it is refused rather than downgraded, so the session fails closed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Issues and holds the maintenance session keys and records each key identifier in the platform key inventory.
Terminates the protected maintenance session and refuses a negotiation that resolves outside the approved algorithm set.
Enforces the same constrained negotiation at the external boundary so no downgrade path exists on either end.

control_implementations.narrative: At session close the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) destroys the session context and records a confirmed-terminated state, and a session context queried after close returns not found. What is missing is the network half: LRU-014 learns the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) connection state from a periodic poll rather than an explicit teardown acknowledgement, so a connection left established on LRU-007 can be reported as terminated for up to 60 seconds before the next poll corrects it, and the alert for an unconfirmed teardown fires on that delayed evidence. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Destroys the session context, records the confirmed-terminated state and raises the unconfirmed-teardown alert.
Tears down the network connection but returns no explicit acknowledgement; its state is read by a 60-second poll.

control_implementations.narrative: The design covers maintenance by personnel without the required clearance or access approval: a cleared, technically qualified escort supervises the work, the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is placed in a restricted maintenance mode that withholds mission-data and configuration functions, the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is booted from an uncleared-session image, and volatile mission information on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is cleared before work starts. The restricted maintenance mode and the uncleared-session image are specified but not built, the escort procedure is drafted and not approved, and no alternate control has been written for a component that can be neither cleared in place nor physically detached. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will host the restricted maintenance mode that withholds mission-data and configuration functions; the mode is not built.
Will boot from a separate uncleared-session image for escorted work; that image does not exist yet.
Will have volatile mission information cleared before escorted work begins; the clear step is manual and unverified today.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 is categorized moderate for availability, so the maintenance response target is set proportionately: support or a serviceable spare for a failed Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) or Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) within 30 days of the failure being reported, with elapsed time recorded per failure. No continuous-availability or hot-spare commitment is made or implied. The support agreement covering the 30-day period is in negotiation and the failure register that would record report and arrival dates is not yet in service. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Is one of the three components the 30-day support target will cover; no spares holding is contracted yet.
Will host the failure register recording report and arrival dates, and is itself inside the covered set.
Is the third covered component; radio spares are held at depot today with no contracted turnaround period.

control_implementations.narrative: The preventive maintenance schedule sets a 12-month interval for the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) — retention-battery and recovery-media checks — the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) — oscillator ageing and holdover calibration — and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) — connector and calibration checks — each recorded against the LRU serial number. The schedule is drafted but not approved, no serial-number due dates have been loaded, and no preventive check has yet been performed under it; maintenance on all three LRUs is currently corrective only. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will receive 12-month retention-battery and recovery-media checks; no due dates are loaded against its serial numbers.
Will receive 12-month oscillator ageing and holdover calibration checks, which bound the time tolerance the compiled audit trail depends on; no checks have been performed under the schedule.
Will receive 12-month connector and calibration checks; today it is maintained correctively only.

control_implementations.narrative: Physical and environmental protection for WS-X90 is carried at the facility level by Aurora Defense Systems and inherited by the system, so PE-1 is being written as a programme-specific procedure set rather than adopted wholesale from the corporate estate policy. The drafted set names the Platform Lead as accountable official, scopes the integration bay around the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the provisioning area around the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and fixes an annual reissue cadence plus an event trigger on any facility move. Nothing has been issued yet; the draft is with programme security for first review and the annual review clock starts at first issue. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — the integration bay housing this unit is one of the two spaces the drafted procedure set scopes; its rack location fixes the bay boundary used in the procedures.
Provisioning Workstation — the provisioning area housing this unit is the second scoped space, and its operators are named in the drafted distribution list.

control_implementations.narrative: A facility access roster is maintained for the three WS-X90 controlled spaces: the provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), the maintenance bay holding the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), and the controlled storage from which the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is drawn. Badge credentials are issued against roster entries and the roster is reviewed annually by the Platform Lead. What is missing is the removal side: roster strike-off and badge revocation are done manually on notification from the personnel function, and two sampled leavers were removed 9 and 12 working days after departure against the 5-working-day target. A POA&M action to drive removals from the personnel system feed rather than from manual notification is open. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway — the maintenance bay holding this unit is a rostered space; entry requires a bay-scoped credential separate from the outer door.
Provisioning Workstation — the provisioning area holding this unit is the most heavily rostered space, with the largest visitor and escort load.
Maintenance Laptop — held in controlled storage; the roster governs who may sign this conditional-status unit in and out.

control_implementations.narrative: The protected equipment bay holding the Mission Computer (LRU-001), the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is behind a second reader with its own access list, so a credential that opens the outer facility door does not open the bay. The bay list is a strict subset of the facility roster and refusals are logged at the reader. What is not yet in place is the reconciliation: the bay list is maintained by hand against the facility roster rather than derived from it, so a facility-roster removal does not automatically remove bay access, and the reader event log is not yet exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) for correlation. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Mission Computer — racked inside the protected bay; the second reader is the only physical route to its front panel and maintenance connector.
Cryptographic Services Module — the reason the bay carries a second authorisation at all; its key-bearing status sets the bay access list membership.
Secure Storage Module — co-located in the bay so that protected configuration, audit and recovery material sits behind the same second authorisation.

control_implementations.narrative: Transmission media are protected in two distinct ways because they are two distinct problems. Copper mission-data runs between the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) are carried in locked conduit and sealed tray inside the facility. RF and sensor runs — the antenna feed at the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the harness entering the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) — are protected by sealed, witness-marked connectors instead, because conduit is not available on the flight-side runs. Both are partial: two conduit access covers on the LRU-007 to LRU-009 route are currently secured with a padlock rather than a serialised seal, and the connector seal serials for the LRU-006 harness are recorded on the bench sheet but not yet posted to the airframe record. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Sensor Interface — its sensor harness entries are the flight-side terminations carrying witness-marked seals in place of conduit.
Protected Network Gateway — the boundary end of the protected copper run; its patch field sits inside the locked cabinet.
Tactical Data Radio — its antenna feed to the facility test antenna is the longest unconduited run and carries the sealed connector treatment.
Internal Ethernet Switch — the internal end of the protected copper run; all drops terminate in the same locked cabinet with no spare live ports.

control_implementations.narrative: Output control on WS-X90 is achieved by removing the output paths rather than by controlling access to them. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) ship in a hardened build with print spooling, removable-media write and external display output disabled at the driver policy level; device attachment attempts are refused and written to the endpoint log. Screen placement in the provisioning area was surveyed and both positions face away from the corridor glazing. No printer exists in either controlled space. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — hardened build blocks print, USB mass-storage write and external display; the only sanctioned output is the signed provisioning bundle written to the Configuration Repository.
Maintenance Laptop — same hardened output policy, plus a screen privacy filter because it is used at alternate work sites where placement cannot be surveyed in advance.

control_implementations.narrative: The facility already runs intrusion alarms and cameras over the WS-X90 spaces, but they are a facility service with no interface to the system. The planned build adds a one-way export of forced-door and after-hours motion events into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) across a data diode, so that a physical event can be correlated against chassis-intrusion telemetry from the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013). The one-way direction is the design constraint: nothing from the alarm estate may reach a WS-X90 component. Diode procurement is on the sustainment order and the LRU-018 ingest schema for physical events is drafted but not built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — supplies the chassis-intrusion telemetry that the facility alarm events will be correlated against once the export exists.
Security Log Collector — the intended sink for exported alarm and camera events; needs a new physical-event source type and retention rule.

control_implementations.narrative: Monitoring today stops at the outer facility door, which cannot tell whether the person who opened a maintenance session on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) was in the bay at the time. The planned design gives the maintenance bay its own reader and forwards bay-scoped badge events to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) carrying a bay identifier, so LRU-018 can raise a session-without-presence anomaly. The reader and cabling are specified; the LRU-018 correlation rule is designed but the bay reader has not been installed and no bay-scoped events exist yet. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway — the unit whose sessions are to be matched to physical presence; its session-open records supply one half of the correlation.
Security Log Collector — will hold the bay badge events and run the session-without-presence rule that raises the anomaly.

control_implementations.narrative: Visitor records for the provisioning area around the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) are kept for a full year and reviewed by the Platform Lead on a quarterly cycle, with anomalies reported to the System Security Engineer. Retention and reporting are working. The gap is review cadence discipline and export: the last four review intervals were 88, 90, 97 and 84 days, so the 90-day ceiling was breached once, and the records are still reviewed in the badge system rather than mirrored to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which means a visitor anomaly cannot be correlated with system events. Both items are carried in the remediation plan. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — the area holding this unit is the space whose visitor records are retained and reviewed on the quarterly cycle.
Security Log Collector — intended mirror for visitor anomalies so they can be correlated with provisioning session activity; the mirror is not yet built.

control_implementations.narrative: Visitor sign-in for the WS-X90 areas is currently a paper book kept at the provisioning area desk, which is why review is manual and anomaly detection is retrospective. The planned change moves sign-in onto the site badge system, adds a nightly export into the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), and drives an automatic review prompt to the Platform Lead once 90 days have elapsed since the last recorded review. The badge system already supports visitor enrolment; the work is the export job and the prompt rule, neither of which is built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — the area desk where the paper book sits today and where the badge enrolment terminal will replace it.
Security Log Collector — target of the planned nightly visitor export and host of the 90-day review-prompt rule.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. Visitor records are held in the site badge system in its default schema, which carries personal fields beyond what WS-X90 needs, and no minimised export view has been defined. This is a privacy-driven enhancement on a system whose privacy analysis has not yet been run, so no programme work has started. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector — would hold the minimised visitor export once a field-limited view is defined; today it receives no visitor data at all.

control_implementations.narrative: Power feeds to the mission rack run in protected raceway from a lockable distribution panel, with the breakers serving the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) labelled to the LRU identifier. The panel schedule was cleaned up during the last integration stand-down. Two gaps remain: the LRU-011 feed still shares a breaker with the bench lighting circuit for the payload interface bench, which is a non-programme load, and the panel lock is a common-key type rather than a programme-controlled key. Availability here is treated proportionately — the categorisation for WS-X90 is moderate, so this is about protecting the feeds from damage and mis-operation, not about redundant supply. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Internal Ethernet Switch — fed from a dedicated labelled breaker; the raceway to the switch cabinet is shared with no other service.
Payload Safety Interlock — currently the one feed still sharing a breaker with a non-programme load; separation is the open corrective action.
Platform Management Controller — fed from a dedicated labelled breaker and additionally carried on the bay uninterruptible supply for orderly shutdown.

control_implementations.narrative: The payload interface bench carries a guarded emergency cutoff within arm's reach of the operator position that drops the supply to the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) while leaving the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) monitoring rail up, so the state at the moment of the cut can be read back afterwards. Measured drop time across ten activations was between 0.6 and 1.1 seconds. The cutoff is mushroom-head with a strike shroud and is keyed to reset, so it cannot be re-armed by a passer-by. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Payload Interface Controller — de-energised by the cutoff; its command path to the payload dies with it, which is the point of the interlock ordering.
Payload Safety Interlock — de-energised by the same action so the interlock cannot hold an authorisation open after the cut.
Platform Management Controller — deliberately excluded from the cut so its monitoring rail stays up and the pre-cut state can be read out.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 is categorised moderate for availability, so the emergency power design targets an orderly shutdown rather than transition to long-term alternate power, and the narrative deliberately claims nothing more. The planned uninterruptible supply covers the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) for 15 minutes of ride-through, long enough to flush the LRU-015 audit buffer and bring the rack down cleanly. Load calculations are done and the unit is specified; procurement is against the next sustainment order and no shutdown script yet exists that sequences the buffer flush. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — initiates and sequences the orderly shutdown once the supply signals loss of primary power.
Secure Storage Module — the reason ride-through is needed at all; buffered audit records must reach it before power is dropped.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented at programme level. Emergency lighting on the egress route from the provisioning area is a facility service that WS-X90 inherits, and the programme has neither surveyed the route against the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) position nor obtained a coverage or test record from the facility. No programme action has started. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — its position defines the egress route that would need coverage; no survey has been carried out against it.

control_implementations.narrative: Fire detection and suppression over the integration bay and the provisioning area is a facility system, and the programme's planned work is to establish that it holds up on an energy source independent of the building supply while the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) racks are installed and powered. That means obtaining the independent-source service record, adding both spaces by name to the annual facility check scope, and witnessing the check once. None of the three has been done; the request to the facility is raised. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — its rack defines the integration bay that must appear by name in the annual facility check scope.
Provisioning Workstation — its area is the second space to be added to the check scope; it is currently covered only as general office space.

control_implementations.narrative: Detection in the WS-X90 spaces activates automatically today and notifies the site fire response desk, but it does not notify the Platform Lead in the same alarm cycle and it emits nothing that WS-X90 can consume. The planned change adds the Platform Lead to the notification group and emits a dated event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) so the alarm can be reconciled against Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) shutdown telemetry — which matters because a thermal event and an unexplained shutdown currently appear as two unrelated records. Both changes ride on the same facility interface work as PE-6(1). This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — its shutdown telemetry is the system-side record that a fire event must be reconcilable against.
Security Log Collector — will receive the dated detection event over the same one-way facility feed planned for intrusion events.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. The provisioning area holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is unstaffed overnight and at weekends, and the programme has not confirmed whether suppression in that space runs in automatic mode during those periods or is switched to manual by the facility out of hours. No mode log has been requested and no test activation has been witnessed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — the unstaffed space in question; no suppression mode evidence has been obtained for the hours it sits unattended.

control_implementations.narrative: Environmental monitoring is genuinely continuous on the system side and only periodic on the facility side. The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) reports oven temperature and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) reports bay temperature to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) once per second, and LRU-013 alarms on an out-of-band reading within seconds — which is why the timing holdover budget is defensible at all. Humidity, by contrast, is read from a facility gauge on the twice-daily walk-round, so a humidity excursion between walk-rounds is invisible. Fitting a humidity sensor onto the LRU-013 telemetry loop is the open corrective action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Timing Receiver — its oven temperature is the most sensitive environmental parameter on the platform; drift outside band degrades holdover before anything else shows.
Payload Telemetry Unit — supplies payload bay temperature at one-second cadence over the same telemetry path.
Platform Management Controller — collects both temperature streams, applies the approved bands and raises the excursion alarm; carries no humidity input today.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. There are wet services in the ceiling void above the integration bay holding the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), but the isolation valves have not been identified on the bay drawing, their reachability has not been checked, and duty staff have not been briefed on their location. No programme action has started. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — the rack under the wet services; the valve identification work would be scoped to the void directly above and adjacent to it.

control_implementations.narrative: Movement of line-replaceable units across the facility boundary is authorised on a movement docket naming serial number and receiving custodian, and the movement is posted against the asset entry in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). The spares pool for the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is fully covered. The gap is timeliness and closure: postings are batched weekly rather than same-day, so LRU-020 lags physical reality by up to five days, and three units in the last quarter show an outbound movement as their last posting while being physically present on site. A same-day posting rule and a reconciliation sweep are the open actions. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Platform Management Controller — spares for this unit are the highest-turnover movements and the ones most affected by the weekly posting lag.
Provisioning Workstation — moves between the provisioning area and the vendor depot for periodic rebuild; each leg needs its own docket.
Configuration Repository — holds the asset entry and movement history that the docket is posted against; it is the system of record for where a unit is.

control_implementations.narrative: Alternate work site use is real for WS-X90 because the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is a conditional-status endpoint that travels to depot and field locations. The planned control set fixes an approved site list, requires locked storage between sessions, forbids unattended sessions, and permits no network connection other than the link to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014). Draft rules exist and have been walked with two technicians, but the approved site list has not been signed off, no effectiveness assessment has been run at any site, and the incident reporting path from a field site is still the general corporate line rather than a programme contact. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway — the only endpoint LRU-019 is permitted to reach from an alternate site; all other connectivity is to be blocked by the endpoint policy.
Maintenance Laptop — the unit that actually goes off site; its conditional status is what makes the alternate work site rules necessary.

control_implementations.narrative: Hardware marking is done at two levels because the two populations are handled by different people. Mission-side protected units — the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) — carry an etched nameplate marking stating the highest impact level they may process, positioned for in-situ reading with covers fitted, and the marking is on the issue-C nameplate drawing so it is reproduced at every build. Ground support units — the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) — carry an equivalent label, and the LRU-019 label additionally states conditional-use status so it is not signed out of storage for an unrelated task. A marking survey of the controlled storage inventory found no unmarked endpoint. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module — etched nameplate marking on the front face, readable racked; it is the highest-marked unit on the platform.
Tactical Data Radio — marked on the chassis side rather than the face because the face is obscured by the feed when installed.
Secure Storage Module — marked to the same level as LRU-003 because it holds protected audit and recovery material at rest.
Provisioning Workstation — labelled with the highest level of provisioning material it may hold; the label is checked at each rebuild.
Maintenance Laptop — carries both the impact-level label and a conditional-use statement, which is what stops it being drawn for out-of-scope work.

control_implementations.narrative: The facility holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the controlled storage for the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is an existing site, so PE-23 for WS-X90 is a hazard-consideration exercise rather than a siting decision. The planned work is to obtain the site flood, seismic and adjacent-industrial assessments, record which hazards cannot be engineered out, and carry those forward into the WS-X90 risk register instead of leaving them closed in the facility file. The assessments have been requested from the estates function; none have been received and no register entries exist. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — its location fixes which building and floor the hazard assessment must cover.
Maintenance Laptop — its controlled storage is in the same building; the storage location is included in the requested assessment scope.

control_implementations.narrative: Supply chain risk management for WS-X90 currently runs on the corporate procurement policy, which does not address programme-specific concerns such as who may clear a source into the signing chain. The planned procedure set is programme-scoped, names an accountable official, is issued to the engineering and procurement staff who release baselines through the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and provision hardware at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and carries an annual reissue plus an event trigger on prime supplier change for a criticality-ranked item. Drafting has started against the criticality analysis; nothing has been issued. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — the provisioning point the procedures govern; its operators handle received hardware first and are the second named audience.
Configuration Repository — the release point the procedures govern; baseline releasers are the primary named audience for the issued set.

control_implementations.narrative: A WS-X90 supply chain risk management plan exists at revision 2 and is held as a controlled item in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) under an access rule limited to the SCRM distribution list, which satisfies the protection requirement. Coverage is the gap: the plan addresses design, manufacture, delivery and integration for the criticality-ranked items including the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Navigation Processor (LRU-004), but the sustainment and disposal phases are stubbed with a forward reference and carry no supplier-specific content. Revision 3 closing those two phases is scheduled and is the open remediation item. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module — top of the criticality ranking; the plan carries named-source, blind-buy and testing content for it through integration.
Navigation Processor — second in the ranking; covered through integration but with no sustainment or disposal content in the current revision.
Configuration Repository — holds the plan as a controlled item and enforces the SCRM distribution list as its read rule.

control_implementations.narrative: Supply chain decisions on WS-X90 are made today by whoever is nearest the problem, which is why the decision rights around the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) signing chain and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) baseline gate are not written down. The planned standing SCRM team draws named members from programme security, procurement and firmware engineering, and its first task is to fix those two decision rights explicitly: who clears a new supplier into the signing chain, and who approves a first baseline from a newly qualified source. Membership has been proposed and not yet appointed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller — the signing chain it anchors is the asset whose supplier-clearance decision the team must own.
Configuration Repository — the baseline gate the team must own; today a first baseline from a new source enters on engineering judgement alone.

control_implementations.narrative: The navigation and timing chain is where WS-X90 is most exposed to a single source. The Navigation Processor (LRU-004), the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) each come from one supplier today, and there is no signed single-source risk acceptance for any of them. The planned action is a second-source qualification study covering all three, with the fallback of a signed and expiry-dated acceptance where a second source is not economically available, both to be recorded against the parts-list entry before the next production lot is released. The study is scoped and unstarted. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Processor — single-sourced; a second source would need re-qualification of the integrity-check firmware, which is the main cost driver in the study.
Timing Receiver — single-sourced and the hardest to dual-source because holdover performance is specific to the supplier's oscillator.
Navigation Sensor Interface — single-sourced but the most tractable of the three; the interface is documented and a second source is credible.

control_implementations.narrative: Nothing currently prevents a supplier of the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) or the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) from inferring the programme from the order record and the ship-to address. The planned measures are blind-buy placement — order records that name neither WS-X90 nor its end use — and consolidation of deliveries onto a general receiving address, with the programme cross-reference held only in the internal purchasing record. The purchasing function has agreed the approach in principle; no order has yet been placed under it and the general receiving address has not been designated. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module — the item whose order pattern most clearly signals a protected programme; first candidate for blind-buy placement.
Tactical Data Radio — order quantities and cadence for this item currently correlate with programme milestones and would be masked by consolidation.

control_implementations.narrative: Supply chain security clauses are present in the prime contracts for the payload chain — the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) — and the primes are contractually obliged to flow them to sub-tier suppliers. Verification is where this is incomplete: the programme has confirmed flow-down for the LRU-010 and LRU-012 chains, but the LRU-011 prime has not returned its sub-tier clause listing, and one returned sub-tier contract carried an amended notification period rather than the clause unaltered. Both are open with the contracting officer. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Payload Interface Controller — flow-down confirmed to two sub-tier suppliers with clause text matching the prime contract.
Payload Safety Interlock — the outstanding case; the prime has not produced its sub-tier clause listing on request.
Payload Telemetry Unit — flow-down confirmed, but one sub-tier contract carries an amended notification period that is being corrected.

control_implementations.narrative: Provenance is enforced as a staging gate rather than as a record-keeping habit. Every firmware release staged by the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) must resolve, through the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), to a build record carrying source revision, build host identity and the signing key identifier; the key identifier must match a key trusted by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) chain. A release whose chain is incomplete is refused at staging, so a provenance gap becomes a staging failure rather than a post-installation discovery. Forty-two releases have been staged under this rule with no bypass path. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller — supplies the trusted key set the build record's signing key identifier is checked against.
Update & Recovery Controller — enforces the gate at staging; it refuses any package whose provenance chain does not resolve.
Configuration Repository — holds the build records and the release-to-build linkage that the chain is walked through.

control_implementations.narrative: Sustainment stock for the long-lead items — the Timing Receiver (LRU-005), the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) — is planned at quoted lead time plus six months of consumption, held or contractually committed, with a re-review trigger on any supplier end-of-life or last-time-buy notice. Quoted lead times have been collected for all three and the consumption model exists, but no stock has been placed on order and no re-review trigger is wired into the supplier notification handling, so an end-of-life notice today would not prompt a stock decision. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Timing Receiver — longest quoted lead time of the three and the item that sets the overall stock horizon.
Navigation Sensor Interface — moderate lead time but the highest attrition rate in integration, so consumption dominates the calculation.
Payload Telemetry Unit — included because its supplier has already issued one last-time-buy notice on a subordinate assembly.

control_implementations.narrative: Acceptance into the WS-X90 baseline is gated on an assessment record covering supplier standing, signature verification result and known-vulnerability check, and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) refuses to stage a package whose record is absent from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). Firmware and software packages are fully covered by this gate. What is not covered is hardware and development tooling: a replacement component or a new build tool is accepted on the engineering acceptance sheet with no assessment record, so the LRU-016 gate never sees it. Extending the record requirement to those two categories is the open action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Update & Recovery Controller — enforces the pre-acceptance gate for firmware and software; has no visibility of hardware or tooling acceptance.
Configuration Repository — holds the assessment records; hardware and tooling entries are absent from it today.

control_implementations.narrative: The three suppliers behind the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) are on an annual assessment cycle, and the LRU-004 and LRU-010 suppliers have current reviews. The LRU-008 supplier review is 14 months old and therefore out of cycle. The event-driven half is weaker still: the review procedure names change of ownership as a trigger but not a reported compromise at the supplier or a sector counterfeit finding on the same part family, so two of the three triggers have no procedural hook. Adding them and clearing the overdue review are the open actions. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Processor — supplier review current; assessment covered ownership, financial standing and sub-tier visibility.
Tactical Data Radio — supplier review is 14 months old and overdue against the annual cadence.
Payload Interface Controller — supplier review current, carried out jointly with the sub-tier flow-down check.

control_implementations.narrative: Independent testing of supplied elements is planned for the two items where a hidden interface or a substituted firmware image would be hardest to detect downstream: the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005). The planned scope is undocumented interface discovery and a comparison of delivered firmware against the supplier-declared hash, carried out by a third-party laboratory before first lot acceptance. A laboratory has been shortlisted and the test scope drafted; no testing has been commissioned and both items were accepted on supplier declaration alone for the current lot. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module — first candidate for independent test because a hidden debug interface here would bypass the protected boundary entirely.
Timing Receiver — second candidate; a substituted firmware image would show as a slow holdover drift rather than an obvious fault.

control_implementations.narrative: Not implemented. WS-X90 supply chain information — the parts list, supplier names, lot quantities and delivery schedules — is handled at the sensitivity of each individual item, and the aggregate is not treated as more sensitive than its parts. The parts list sits in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) under a broader read rule than the signed release baselines. No operations security analysis of the aggregate has been carried out. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository — holds the parts list under a broader read rule than the release baselines it sits beside; no aggregation rule is applied.

control_implementations.narrative: Notification agreements are in place for the two suppliers whose compromise would be hardest to detect from the platform side. The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) agreement obliges notification of a supply chain compromise affecting the delivered part family within 30 days of the supplier becoming aware, and obliges release of the underlying audit result. The Timing Receiver (LRU-005) agreement carries the notification clause but no audit-release obligation and names no programme recipient, so a notification would arrive at the general contracts mailbox. Both gaps are with the contracting officer for the next agreement amendment. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Timing Receiver — notification clause present at 30 days but with no audit-release obligation and no named programme recipient.
Tactical Data Radio — full clause in place: 30-day notification, named programme recipient and audit-result release.

control_implementations.narrative: Tamper protection is implemented as two different mechanisms for two different threat pictures. On the mission computing side, the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) sit inside enclosures whose opening breaks a serialised seal, and LRU-003 additionally zeroises key material inside its protected boundary on enclosure breach; seal serials are captured at build and re-read at every depot induction. On the payload side, the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011), the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) and the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) carry a latched electronic tamper indication that survives a power cycle and is read at the next maintenance session, because those units are opened in the field where a broken seal alone would be ambiguous. Clearing a latch requires an authorised maintenance action and is itself recorded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller — serialised seal on the enclosure; a broken seal invalidates the platform integrity attestation until the unit is re-inducted.
Cryptographic Services Module — serialised seal plus active zeroisation of key material on enclosure breach; the only unit with a destructive response.
Payload Interface Controller — latched electronic tamper indication surviving power cycle, read at the maintenance interface.
Payload Safety Interlock — same latched indication; because it is the independent authorisation path, a set latch blocks payload authorisation until cleared.
Payload Telemetry Unit — latched indication forwarded in the health telemetry stream so a field tamper shows without a maintenance session.
Secure Storage Module — serialised seal; opening is expected only at depot, so seal-only treatment is proportionate.

control_implementations.narrative: Anti-tamper for the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) is specified in the design review record and verified at first article inspection, so it is not a packaging afterthought. The life-cycle gap is at the far end: production lot acceptance does not re-verify the anti-tamper section, so a change in the supplier's enclosure process between lots would not be caught until the next design review. Adding a lot-acceptance re-verification step referencing the same design review section is the open action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Secure Boot Controller — anti-tamper specified at design review and verified at first article; no per-lot re-verification.
Update & Recovery Controller — same position; its enclosure is produced by a different supplier, so per-lot drift is the more likely risk of the two.

control_implementations.narrative: Inspection for tampering happens twice, at receipt and in the field. At receipt, every Navigation Processor (LRU-004), Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) and Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) is checked against the supplier photograph and seal serial list before stock entry, and a serial mismatch sends the unit to quarantine rather than back into the stream. In the field, every maintenance induction checks and records the seal serials on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) before any session is opened, so a mismatch stops the maintenance action rather than being noticed afterwards. Both checks are recorded against the unit serial and both have been exercised with seeded mismatches. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Processor — receiving inspection against supplier photograph and seal serial list before stock entry.
Navigation Sensor Interface — same receiving inspection; its harness connector seals are checked as well as the enclosure seal.
Tactical Data Radio — same receiving inspection, extended to the feed connector seals fitted at the supplier.
Payload Safety Interlock — field seal check at maintenance induction; a mismatch blocks the induction outright.
Maintenance Access Gateway — field seal check before any technician session is opened through it.
Maintenance Laptop — field seal check at sign-out from controlled storage as well as at induction, because it travels off site.

control_implementations.narrative: Counterfeit detection knowledge on WS-X90 is currently carried informally by two long-serving provisioning staff, which is not a training programme. The planned course covers the marking, packaging and date-code checks that separate an authentic part from a counterfeit, and the quarantine route for a suspect part, and is aimed at everyone who provisions hardware at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or draws the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) from controlled storage. Course material has been drafted against the anti-counterfeit procedure; no session has been delivered and no training records exist. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation — its operators handle incoming parts first and are the primary training audience.
Maintenance Laptop — staff drawing this unit handle field-replaceable parts and form the second training audience.

control_implementations.narrative: Every WS-X90 line-replaceable unit in the service and repair loop holds an open custody record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) naming its physical location and configuration state, from the moment it comes off the platform to the moment it is returned to service. Return is gated: the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) must reflash the unit to the approved baseline, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) must record the closing check, before the custody record can be closed. That closes the gap a repaired unit otherwise leaves — a unit that went to a vendor depot cannot re-enter service carrying whatever configuration the depot left on it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway — records the closing check that must exist before a custody record can be closed and the unit returned to service.
Update & Recovery Controller — reflashes every returning unit to the approved baseline regardless of what the depot installed.
Configuration Repository — holds the open custody record with location and configuration state for every unit in the loop.

control_implementations.narrative: Disposal for the key-bearing and storage-bearing units is zeroise-then-destroy with a two-person certificate naming serial number and method. The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) are fully covered and no unit of either type has left programme custody intact. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is the gap: two units retired in the last quarter were wiped to the corporate endpoint standard and returned to the corporate asset pool rather than destroyed, because the disposal procedure treats them as standard IT assets rather than as WS-X90 protected units. Correcting the procedure and recovering the two units are the open actions. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module — zeroised inside its protected boundary and then physically destroyed under two-person control.
Secure Storage Module — same treatment; the storage media is destroyed separately from the chassis and certified separately.
Maintenance Laptop — currently disposed of as a standard IT asset rather than a protected unit; this is the open non-conformance.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 access control policy and its procedures exist as one signed baseline in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which rejects an unsigned or superseded revision at check-in, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) assembles every technician procedure package from the current approved revision so a field package cannot carry stale policy. The policy carries an annual review record, matching the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-1, and the profile change of 2026-09-08 triggered an out-of-cycle review. What is missing: the AC-family procedures were written against the previous 74-control scope and have not been reissued for the 546-control effective set, so seven procedures currently lack a current owner signature. REQ-436 stays partially satisfied until that reissue lands. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed, version-controlled access control policy and procedure baseline and refuses unsigned or superseded revisions at check-in.
Assembles technician procedure packages from the current approved policy revision and blocks issue when the cited revision has been superseded.

control_implementations.narrative: Account create, modify, enable, disable and remove actions on WS-X90 exist only as calls into the account service on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013); the on-disk account store is sealed and a direct write raises an integrity alarm rather than taking effect. Each completed action is published as a structured record to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) over the platform management bus within 60 seconds and with no operator step, which is what removed the manual re-entry the previous ground toolchain required. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs the only account service on the platform, seals the account store against direct writes, and emits a structured record for each account lifecycle action.
Receives, timestamps and indexes the account action stream and is the single reporting point for account lifecycle queries.

control_implementations.narrative: Temporary and emergency maintenance accounts are created by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) with a hard expiry no more than 72 hours out, the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(2), and are disabled rather than deleted at expiry so their history remains reviewable during an investigation. The expiry is also carried inside the session credential, so the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) refuses an expired account even when the management link to LRU-013 is down. What is missing: emergency accounts opened directly at LRU-014 during a communications-out recovery are still stamped by the technician rather than by the controller, so on that one path the 72-hour bound is procedural rather than enforced. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Stamps every temporary and emergency account with a 72-hour expiry at creation and disables, rather than deletes, the account when the expiry passes.
Reads the expiry carried in the session credential and refuses an expired account independently of the management link to LRU-013.

control_implementations.narrative: Two disable paths carry AC-2(3). On the platform side the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) disables an account within 72 hours of expiry, of loss of programme association or of a recorded policy violation, the CNSSI 1253 parameter value, and stamps the triggering condition onto the disable record so the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) can report per-trigger counts. On the ground support side the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) runs a daily inactivity sweep and disables any account idle for 90 days, the CNSSI value for AC-2(3)d, while the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) refuses offline logon with a cached credential older than the same 90 days so a laptop kept off the network cannot outlive the sweep. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Disables platform accounts within 72 hours of expiry, disassociation or policy violation and stamps the trigger code onto the disable record.
Aggregates disable records by trigger code and produces the per-trigger counts used in the monthly account review.
Runs the daily 90-day inactivity sweep across ground support accounts and disables the accounts it finds idle.
Refuses offline logon with a cached credential older than 90 days so a disconnected laptop cannot bypass the sweep.

control_implementations.narrative: The audit write is on the critical path of the account change. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) builds an audit record naming the actor, the target account, the action and the authorising role, writes it to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), and only then acknowledges the change to the operator; if the LRU-015 write fails the account action is rolled back rather than completed unaudited. LRU-013 then notifies the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which is the off-platform read path for account history. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Builds the four-field account audit record and rolls the account change back if the record cannot be written.
Provides the write-before-acknowledge audit store for account lifecycle records and returns the write receipt LRU-013 waits on.
Receives the account audit notification and holds the queryable off-platform copy of account history.

control_implementations.narrative: End-of-work-period logout on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is directed by the WS-X90 ground support operating instruction, which names the end of a technician's standard work period as the logout point, matching the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(5). LRU-017 makes the behaviour visible by showing the next technician how many sessions were left open at the previous shift change. What is missing: the requirement is carried procedurally. Neither station enforces a shift-boundary logout, and the open-session count is informational rather than blocking, so REQ-442 is verified by interview and by the shift-change count rather than by an enforced control. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Displays the count of sessions left open at the previous shift change on sign-on; the logout itself is performed by the technician, not enforced by the station.
Carries the same shift-boundary logout direction for field use; no automated end-of-shift termination is fielded.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 carries privilege in named roles rather than on accounts. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) holds the four approved privileged roles and refuses to set a privilege attribute directly on an account, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) accepts a privileged operation only when the presented role is one of those four. What is missing: membership change review is a manual checklist held by the System Security Engineer rather than a gate in the tooling, so a membership change can reach a mission load before its review entry is written. Closing that is tracked against the same work item as REQ-454. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the four approved privileged role definitions and their membership, and refuses a privilege attribute set directly on an account.
Checks the presented role name against the approved four before executing any privileged operation and logs a mismatch.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 runs one shared account and no group accounts: the flight line pre-launch check account terminated at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014). Its two permitted conditions are that a named technician signs it out for a single sortie turn and that the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) tags every action taken under it with that technician's individual identifier, so the shared credential never breaks individual attribution. What is missing: the sign-out register is electronic at one of the three support sites and on paper at the other two, so the reviewer cannot reconcile sign-out to action without a site visit. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Terminates the single approved shared account, holds its usage conditions, and rejects any attempt to create a second shared or group account.
Tags every action taken under the shared account with the signed-out technician's individual identifier before the action is forwarded.

control_implementations.narrative: Usage conditions are designed and not yet enforced. The approved design binds each privileged mission account to a permitted mission phase, a permitted ground station identity and a permitted time window, held with the account record and evaluated by the Mission Computer (LRU-001) at authentication; the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) will apply the mission-phase condition a second time at the payload command boundary so a session that survives a phase change cannot keep commanding. Enforcement is scheduled for the 4.4 mission software build with an accepted entry criterion; nothing is fielded today. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will evaluate the three usage conditions at authentication; the condition schema is approved and the evaluation code is scheduled for build 4.4.
Will re-check the mission-phase condition at the payload command boundary so a stale session cannot command across a phase change.

control_implementations.narrative: Atypical usage detection is a design on paper. The WS-X90 log analytics design record defines the per-account pattern as ground station, time of day and command class, with a threshold for each, to be evaluated by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) against the account action and authentication streams it already receives, and to be raised to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) as an analyst review item. The correlation rule set has a dated build item and a named owner; no rules are fielded and no alerts are produced today. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Already ingests the authentication and privileged action streams the detection will run over; the correlation rules themselves are not fielded.
Will present the atypical-usage alert queue to the analyst; the queue surface is designed and not yet built.

control_implementations.narrative: A high-risk determination from the programme security office is entered against the individual on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), which then disables every account that individual holds within 30 minutes, the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-2(13), and drives the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) to revoke their provisioning credential in the same run. What is missing: the determination arrives by email and is keyed in by an operator, so the 30-minute clock is measured from entry rather than from issue. An authenticated intake feed from the security office is the open item behind REQ-447. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Disables every account held by a named individual within 30 minutes of the determination being entered and records the elapsed time per run.
Revokes the individual's provisioning credential in the same run so a ground support credential cannot outlive the platform disable.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 is a non-discretionary system everywhere it matters. The approved design confines discretionary grants to draft mission plans held on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), where a plan author may grant read access on their own draft to another named author and nothing else; the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) refuses a discretionary grant on an approved release baseline, on signed configuration or on any airborne object, and no LRU on the aircraft implements a discretionary grant at all.
