The draft-plan grant mechanism is designed and scheduled; today plan sharing is done by copying, which the design replaces. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will hold the draft mission plan grant mechanism, the only place in WS-X90 where a subject may pass access to another subject; the design is approved and the build is scheduled.
Will refuse discretionary grants on approved baselines, signed configuration and airborne objects, keeping the covered object set to drafts only.

control_implementations.narrative: The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) is a default-deny inspection point: a flow it cannot inspect does not leave the boundary. Three encrypted tunnels are approved, and for those the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) terminates the tunnel and presents the plaintext to the gateway inspection path before release, so approved encryption does not become an inspection bypass; a flow whose key is not held by LRU-003 is blocked outright. What is missing: the terminate-on-failure path is implemented for TCP-bearing tunnels only. A UDP-bearing tunnel that fails inspection is dropped packet by packet but the session is not torn down inside the 5-second bound REQ-449 states. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Blocks any flow it cannot inspect, holds the three-entry approved tunnel list, and terminates a TCP-bearing session within 5 seconds of a failed inspection.
Terminates the approved tunnels and presents the decrypted flow to the gateway inspection path; holds the keys that decide which flows are inspectable at all.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 enumerates its security functions rather than inferring them. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) holds the list — key use requests to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), audit configuration, access policy load and boot policy change — and authorises each one only to the role named against it in the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) role table, which LRU-001 reads live so a role change takes effect without a software reload. LRU-003 does not trust that decision: it re-checks the presented role against its own copy of the authorisation map before performing a key operation, so a compromise of the mission partition does not by itself yield key use. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the enumerated security function list and authorises each function against the live role table before dispatching it.
Independently re-checks the presented role against its own authorisation map before performing any key operation.
Publishes the authoritative role table that both LRU-001 and LRU-003 evaluate against, and versions each change.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged role holders on WS-X90 are issued two accounts, not one: the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) creates the privileged role account and its non-privileged counterpart in a single transaction, so a privileged role cannot exist without the everyday account that keeps it out of nonsecurity work. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) then refuses to open mission planning, telemetry review or documentation under a privileged role, which is the class of function the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-6(2) reserves. What is missing: eleven legacy engineering accounts predate the paired issue and still carry both uses. They are on a dated exception list with a closure date and are the residual behind REQ-451. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses to open mission planning, telemetry review or documentation tasks under a privileged role and logs the refusal.
Issues privileged and non-privileged accounts as one transaction and holds the dated exception list of eleven legacy dual-use accounts.

control_implementations.narrative: Only one network path may carry a privileged command across the WS-X90 boundary: the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) forwards privileged traffic solely to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and drops a privileged command arriving on any other interface without forwarding it, so there is one place to review rather than a policy per interface. Each privileged command that reaches LRU-014 over the network carries the operational need code recorded in the system security plan. What is missing: LRU-014 records the need code but does not yet validate it against the approved list, so an unrecognised code is logged rather than refused. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the single-entry approved privileged path list and drops privileged commands offered on any other interface.
Terminates the one approved privileged path and records the operational need code on each command; validation of that code against the approved list is not yet fielded.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged roles on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) are restricted to the approved privileged-personnel list, and the check happens at assignment rather than at review: LRU-013 refuses to bind a role to an identity that is not on the current list, so an off-list assignment cannot exist even briefly. LRU-014 accepts privileged role assertions only for identities LRU-013 has bound. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses a privileged role assignment to any identity absent from the current approved personnel list at the moment of assignment.
Accepts a privileged role assertion only for an identity LRU-013 has bound, so the gateway cannot become a second assignment authority.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged assignment review on WS-X90 is evidence-led rather than list-led. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) builds the review worksheet by joining each holder's assignment to the preceding 180 days of their privileged activity drawn from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), so the System Security Engineer judges continued need against what the holder actually did rather than against the role name. Reviews run at least every 180 days and on each role definition change. What is missing: reduction to non-privileged on non-reconfirmation is a manual action today; the tooling flags the unreconfirmed assignment but does not itself downgrade it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Generates the 180-day review worksheet and flags assignments that were not reconfirmed; it does not yet perform the reduction automatically.
Supplies the per-holder privileged activity history the worksheet is built from, which is what makes the review a judgement rather than a sign-off.

control_implementations.narrative: Execution privilege on WS-X90 is fixed at signing time, not at load time. The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) records a maximum privilege level for each signed mission software image in its manifest, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) starts the image at that level and denies any request the image makes to raise its own privilege above it, so a library invoked by a low-privilege user cannot execute above that user. What is missing: two of the three third-party mission libraries ship without a manifest privilege level and still run at the mission service level. Both are on a dated list and the supplier manifests are scheduled for the next delivery. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Records the maximum privilege level for each signed image in the boot manifest and refuses to sign an image whose level is undeclared for first-party code.
Starts each image at its manifest level and denies and logs an in-process request to raise privilege above it.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged function use is logged at the point of execution on both LRUs that host privileged functions. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) each emit a record naming the function, the role, the account and the outcome, and the record is produced on the denial path with the same fields as on the success path, so a probing sequence of refused privileged calls is as visible as a successful one. Records reach the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which is where the enumerated privileged function list is reconciled against what was actually observed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Emits a four-field privileged execution record for every mission-side privileged call, on both the success and the denial path.
Emits the same record shape for platform administrative privileged functions, including refused attempts.
Reconciles the observed privileged function set against the enumerated list and reports any function never seen.

control_implementations.narrative: The Mission Computer (LRU-001) refuses a privileged function invoked from a non-privileged session on every path into it, including the mission scripting interface, which is checked at dispatch rather than at parse so a script cannot smuggle a privileged call through a data argument. The Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) enforces the same rule again at its own boundary: a payload configuration command with no privileged role assertion is rejected there, so the payload side does not inherit its safety from LRU-001 having filtered correctly. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses privileged functions from non-privileged sessions at dispatch, covering the mission scripting interface and the payload command path.
Independently rejects a payload configuration command that carries no privileged role assertion, without relying on upstream filtering.

control_implementations.narrative: Both WS-X90 session terminators cap concurrency at three. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) apply a maximum of 3 concurrent sessions to all accounts, the CNSSI 1253 parameter values for AC-10, with no privileged or service account exemption, and they refuse the fourth session with an explicit reason rather than displacing an existing one, so an attacker cannot use a new session to evict an operator mid-task. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Counts live maintenance sessions per account and refuses the fourth with an explicit limit reason; no account type carries an exemption.
Applies the same three-session cap to provisioning sessions and never displaces an existing session to admit a new one.

control_implementations.narrative: On session lock the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) hand the whole framebuffer to an opaque lock surface that renders no mission data, no account name and no window titles, and the compositor does not present the prior framebuffer between successful reauthentication and unlock, which closes the brief-flash exposure found on the previous ground software build. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Replaces the entire display with an opaque lock surface on lock and holds it until reauthentication completes.
Applies the same lock surface in field use, including on external displays attached during maintenance.

control_implementations.narrative: Logout on WS-X90 is a session-wide teardown, not a screen change. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) expose the logout action on every authenticated screen, and the action terminates the session against all resources it reached, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-12(1): downstream maintenance sessions the session opened on other LRUs are closed by session identifier, and Configuration Repository handles are released within 5 seconds. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Propagates logout by session identifier to every downstream maintenance session the session opened, then closes its own.
Offers logout from every authenticated screen and releases held repository handles as part of the teardown.

control_implementations.narrative: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) display an explicit termination message on every session end and distinguish the three causes — user logout, inactivity and administrative disconnect — so a technician who returns to a station can tell an idle timeout from an administrator cutting the session. The message is held on screen until the next authentication attempt rather than cleared on a timer. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Renders a distinct termination message per cause and holds it until the next authentication attempt.
Renders the same three messages in field use, including when the disconnect arrives from the gateway rather than locally.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 permits two actions without identification or authentication, both on the payload side and both chosen because an authentication dependency would be a safety hazard: assertion of the payload-safe state at the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) through the physical safing lever, which must work with the platform unpowered, and read-only display of the payload built-in-test summary on the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) front panel. Both are recorded in the system security plan with their rationale. What is missing: the LRU-012 front panel also renders the last commanded payload state, which is outside the approved action set. Its removal is scheduled and is the residual behind REQ-462. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Accepts the physical safing lever assertion with no operator authenticated and with the platform unpowered, and records the assertion for later review.
Presents the read-only built-in-test summary on the front panel; the panel currently also shows the last commanded payload state, which is outside the approved set and scheduled for removal.

control_implementations.narrative: Attribute binding is designed across two boundaries and fielded at neither. At rest and in process, the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) will bind classification and releasability attributes to each mission data object at write, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) will carry the pair with the object so the binding survives a copy between mission partitions, with attribute changes audited on the existing account-audit path. In transmission, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) will carry the same attributes with every object crossing them, and LRU-007 will drop an outbound object whose attributes are missing or outside the approved marking set rather than releasing it unmarked. Permitted values are the approved WS-X90 marking set, which is reviewed for applicability every 90 days per the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-16f; the mechanism is scheduled for the 4.4 build. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will bind classification and releasability attributes at the moment of write for stored mission data objects; the store schema change is designed and not yet fielded.
Will carry the attribute pair with the object in process so a cross-partition copy preserves the binding.
Will drop an outbound object whose attributes are absent or outside the approved marking set instead of releasing it unmarked.
Will carry attributes with objects crossing the internal transport so an object does not lose its marking between LRUs.

control_implementations.narrative: No personnel-applied attribute association workflow exists on WS-X90. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) will carry it once the attribute mechanism behind REQ-463 and REQ-464 is fielded, since there is nothing for a person to associate or maintain until an attribute exists to hold. REQ-465 is carried unimplemented in the plan of action and no coverage is claimed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: No attribute association workflow is implemented; the marking procedure that would direct personnel is not yet approved.
No attribute maintenance is performed on revision; objects are versioned without a marking attribute today.

control_implementations.narrative: Consistent interpretation is a single-artefact problem on WS-X90 and is designed as one. A single signed attribute dictionary, carrying a version field, will be issued to the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009), so the encoding cannot drift per LRU as it did across the earlier payload builds; a version mismatch between two LRUs halts attribute-bearing traffic between them rather than letting one side guess. The dictionary format is approved and its distribution rides the existing signed configuration path; nothing is fielded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will resolve attributes through the shared signed dictionary and halt attribute-bearing traffic to a peer on a version mismatch.
Will mark telemetry objects using the same dictionary so payload health data is not downgraded on the way out.
Will refuse to bridge attribute-bearing traffic between two LRUs holding different dictionary versions.

control_implementations.narrative: Remote maintenance is watched live rather than reconstructed afterwards. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) records the start, end, source identity and command set of every remote session and streams those records to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) while the session is open, which is what makes the AC-17(9) cut action useful — an analyst can see a session and end it. What is missing: live streaming covers the command channel; the file transfer channel is still written to the session record and shipped at close, so a transfer in progress is not visible at LRU-018 until it finishes. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Streams remote session start, identity and commands to LRU-018 while the session is live; file transfer records are still shipped at session close.
Presents live remote sessions to the analyst and is the surface from which a session is selected for the disconnect action.

control_implementations.narrative: Remote maintenance sessions terminate at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) inside a protected session whose confidentiality and integrity protection is performed entirely by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003); key material never leaves LRU-003 and no session key is written to LRU-014 storage, so recovering the gateway yields no way to replay a captured session. LRU-014 refuses to establish a session when LRU-003 reports a degraded key state rather than falling back to a weaker protection profile. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Terminates the protected session, holds no key material after the session ends, and refuses establishment on a degraded key report.
Performs the confidentiality and integrity protection for every remote maintenance session and reports its key state to LRU-014.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has one way in. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) is the only externally reachable LRU and forwards remote access solely to the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014); no other LRU exposes an externally reachable listening service, which is asserted in the approved network baseline and verified by the boundary scan that runs against each release. A deviation is raised as a configuration finding against CM rather than being absorbed as a gateway rule change. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Is the single managed access control point for all remote access and forwards only to LRU-014.
Is the sole termination point behind the access control point; it does not accept remote access from any other route.

control_implementations.narrative: Remote privileged access exists on two paths, both bounded. On the maintenance path the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) admits a privileged command from a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) only when the command is on the approved remote-privileged list, the laptop presents a current device attestation, and the session falls inside a scheduled maintenance window; the window test was promoted from advisory to a blocking admission decision on 2026-11-14, so a command failing any one of the three is now refused with a reason code rather than logged and executed. On the mission network path, remote privileged access to the Mission Computer (LRU-001) through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) is limited to two documented operational needs, in-flight security policy reload and audit configuration recovery. One gap keeps this record short of complete: the need code is written into the LRU-007 session record by convention and is not a required field, so a session can still be recorded without one. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Applies the approved-list, attestation and scheduled-window checks to remote privileged commands and refuses on any one of the three with a reason code; the window check has been a blocking decision rather than an advisory note since 2026-11-14.
Presents the device attestation the gateway checks and carries the technician identity attached to each privileged command.

Carries the mission network privileged path for the two documented needs; the need code is still recorded by convention rather than enforced as a required field on the session record, and that is the gap keeping this control short of complete.
Accepts remote privileged operations only for in-flight security policy reload and audit configuration recovery, and logs each with its role.

control_implementations.narrative: Information about how WS-X90 remote access works is held as controlled material, not as engineering reference. The gateway rule set, the device attestation scheme and the approved command lists live in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) behind an access list naming only the security engineering and platform roles, and the on-platform copy sits in a Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) partition that a maintenance session cannot read, so a technician with a live session cannot read the rules that constrain them. What is missing: two supplier design packages describing the attestation scheme are still on the general engineering share; they are listed with a migration date. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the remote access rule set, attestation scheme and command lists behind a role-limited access list, and logs reads.
Holds the on-platform copy in a partition outside the reach of any maintenance session.

control_implementations.narrative: One operator action cuts remote access. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) terminates every live remote session and stops accepting new ones, and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) stops forwarding remote access traffic within 30 seconds of the same action, with neither LRU requiring a reboot, so the cut is usable during a mission rather than only on the ground. What is missing: restoring access requires a manual configuration edit at LRU-007, so the action is not reversible from the operator control that issued it, and a restore therefore needs a second person. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provides the single disconnect-and-disable operator action and terminates all live sessions on it without a reboot.
Stops forwarding remote access traffic within 30 seconds of the action; re-enabling still requires a manual configuration edit.

control_implementations.narrative: Remote commands over the tactical data link are authenticated twice on WS-X90. The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) hands each command's authentication tag to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and passes the command on only if the tag verifies, and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) verifies the same tag again before acting on a payload command, so a compromised radio cannot inject payload commands on its own authority. Failures are discarded and counted at both points, and the counters are readable in the maintenance download. What is missing: the second verification at LRU-010 covers payload commands but not payload configuration reads, which are still verified only at LRU-008. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Verifies each remote command's authentication tag through LRU-003 before forwarding, and counts discards by failure reason.
Re-verifies the tag on payload commands before acting; payload configuration reads are not yet covered by the second check.
Performs the tag verification for both LRUs and holds the command authentication keys.

control_implementations.narrative: The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is the only mobile device in the WS-X90 boundary and is treated as one. Its configuration and connection requirements are held as a signed baseline in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020); LRU-019 reports its configuration hash at each connection, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) admits it only when it is on the approved device register and the reported hash matches the signed baseline, refusing and logging otherwise. What is missing: the baseline covers in-hangar use fully but the annex governing use outside controlled maintenance areas is drafted and unapproved, and the per-activity release by a named authorising engineer is recorded in the maintenance plan rather than enforced at the gateway. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Reports its configuration hash at each connection and holds the signed baseline it was provisioned against.
Holds the signed configuration and connection baseline for the maintenance laptop fleet and the drafted out-of-area annex.
Checks the device register and the reported configuration hash before admitting a laptop; the per-activity engineer release is not yet a gateway check.

control_implementations.narrative: Every enrolled Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) uses full-device encryption with the key bound to platform hardware rather than to a user passphrase alone, covering all mobile computers and devices that process organisation data, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-19(5). Storage lifted from a powered-off laptop yields no readable programme data on another host, which is the acceptance condition the fleet is checked against at each provisioning cycle. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Encrypts all storage with a hardware-bound key and reports encryption state at each connection so a non-compliant laptop is refused rather than merely flagged.

control_implementations.narrative: Information sharing on WS-X90 is a log-export question, not a mission-data one: the only outbound sharing path is a security log extract from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) to a partner programme. The approved design gives the releasing official one view showing the partner's access authorisations beside the marking of every record in the extract, so the comparison is made against the extract in hand rather than a policy memory, with the approved sharing circumstances held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). The circumstances are recorded; the comparison view is designed and not yet built, and it depends on the AC-16 marking work. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Produces the partner log extract and will host the comparison view; today the extract is released against a manual check.
Holds the approved information sharing circumstances the comparison is made against.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 operates no publicly accessible system. The only public release path is the programme's unclassified support documentation set, staged in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and released through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and the approved approach names a single release official who reviews each item before staging and re-reviews the released set quarterly or as new information is posted, which is the CNSSI 1253 parameter value for AC-22. The release official is named and the staged set has been identified; the quarterly re-review has an owner and a scheduled first run but has not yet been performed on the expanded scope. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Stages the unclassified support documentation set separately from the controlled baseline so the reviewable public set is unambiguous.
Is the only route by which staged content is released outward; release is gated on the named official's review record.

control_implementations.narrative: No data mining or bulk extraction detection is implemented on WS-X90. The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) both enforce per-role access but neither applies a query rate ceiling, a per-role extraction volume limit, nor alerting on a sequential full-set read, so an authorised account can enumerate a whole store within its own authorisation without raising anything. The technique set is drafted, REQ-480 is carried in the plan of action, and no coverage is claimed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces per-role access but applies no extraction rate ceiling or volume limit; sequential full-set reads are not detected.
Enforces per-role access to baselines but does not detect or limit bulk enumeration of the repository.

control_implementations.narrative: Contingency planning direction for SYS-WSX90 is not a shelf document: the policy and the recovery procedure set are held as signed, version-tagged artifacts in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which flags any artifact whose recorded review date passes 12 months and refuses an unsigned revision. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is the only publication path, so every revision carries an operator identity, a diff against its predecessor and the distribution list of contingency role holders who received it. Review runs on the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-1. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the contingency planning policy and the recovery procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, computes the 12-month review flag, and refuses to accept an unsigned or unapproved revision.
Sole publication endpoint for a policy or procedure revision; binds the operator identity, the predecessor diff and the recipient distribution list to each published revision.

control_implementations.narrative: The contingency plan and the incident response plan are coupled at the trigger rather than at the document. When the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) declares a platform state matching a contingency activation trigger, it emits one correlated event carrying both plan references, and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) retains that correlation so an after-action review reads one timeline. What is missing is breadth: the trigger table cross-references the incident response plan for every trigger, but the depot supply and maintenance continuity plans are cross-referenced for only four of nine triggers, and the remaining five are carried as an open action against REQ-482. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Declares the platform state that matches a contingency activation trigger and emits the single correlated activation event carrying both the contingency and incident response plan references.
Retains the correlated activation event set and links subsequent plan-driven actions to it so one after-action review reads a single timeline.

control_implementations.narrative: The design intent is that the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) restores the approved mission application baseline onto the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and returns the essential mission functions named in the contingency plan to service inside the plan's four-hour objective, with non-essential functions explicitly deferred and reported rather than counted. Nothing is built yet: the essential-function list has been drafted but not baselined, the per-function self-test set that would measure resumption does not exist, and no timed restoration exercise has been run. Consistent with the moderate availability categorisation, the intended approach is a measured staged restoration, not a hot standby. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will drive the restoration sequence from a sealed backup set and timestamp each restored function against the four-hour objective; the sequencing logic is designed but not implemented.
Will host the restored mission application baseline and run the per-function self-tests that mark a mission function as resumed; the self-test set is not yet written.

control_implementations.narrative: The critical asset list is generated, not maintained. Each LRU baseline record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) carries a mission-essential designation with a recorded rationale, and the list is produced by querying those designations, so a baseline commit that adds, removes or re-scopes an LRU changes the list in the same commit and cannot drift from it. The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) carry the designation because loss of either ends the position and timing function on which the essential mission functions depend. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Carries the mission-essential designation and rationale on every LRU baseline record and generates the critical asset list on demand from those designations.
Designated mission-essential: its loss ends navigation data processing and therefore the essential mission functions that depend on a valid position solution.
Designated mission-essential: its loss removes trusted timing input, and holdover margin bounds how long the essential mission functions can continue.

control_implementations.narrative: Contingency training is enforced by the platform rather than tracked on a spreadsheet. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) reads the contingency-role training record bound to the technician's Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) credential and refuses to open a recovery-role session when that record is absent, older than 12 months, or dated more than 10 working days after the technician assumed the role — the intervals CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-3. The gap is population: the gate is enforced for depot technicians, while field maintenance sessions still open on a supervisor override that records the override but does not check training currency. Closing that override is tracked against REQ-485. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Evaluates the technician's contingency-role training currency before opening a recovery-role session and refuses the session with a stated reason when the record is absent or stale; the field-maintenance supervisor override still bypasses this check.
Carries the technician credential that the training record is bound to, and holds the local copy of the record the gateway reads at session request.

control_implementations.narrative: The contingency plan is exercised semi-annually by restoring a representative platform article from a sealed Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) backup set through the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), with the exercise recorded as failed if any restored partition fails integrity or the measured duration exceeds the plan's four-hour objective. Two tabletop reviews and one partial restore have been completed. What is missing is the full-article exercise: the most recent run restored the mission software partition only, because the flight-configuration article was not released for test, so the platform management and payload interface partitions have never been restored end to end and the measured duration covers a partial scope. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Executes the exercise restore sequence, measures elapsed time against the four-hour objective, and records the exercise result and any corrective action.
Supplies the sealed backup set under exercise and verifies each restored partition's integrity tag as it is read out.

control_implementations.narrative: The intent is one schedule and one after-action review: the contingency plan test, the incident response exercise and the maintenance continuity rehearsal run as a single joint activity, with the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) retaining one correlated event set built from Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) state changes rather than three unlinked sets. Today the three activities are scheduled by different owners and reviewed separately. The joint schedule, the named related-plan owners and the correlation key that would tie the three event sets together are all still to be established. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will emit the exercise state changes that give the three related-plan activities a common timeline; no exercise correlation key is defined yet.
Will retain the correlated event set for the joint exercise so one after-action review reads all three plans; currently retains each activity's events independently.

control_implementations.narrative: Backup sets produced from the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and the signed baselines held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) are stored at a designated Aurora alternate facility under a written storage and retrieval agreement naming the custodian, the release approver and a maximum retrieval time, and one retrieval rehearsal has returned a usable backup set and a usable baseline set inside that time. The equivalence obligation is not met: the alternate facility's access approval and handling rules have been collected but not yet assessed line by line against the primary facility's rules, so the claim that the alternate provides equivalent controls is asserted rather than demonstrated. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Produces the sealed backup sets that are stored at and retrieved from the alternate facility, and re-verifies each set's integrity tag on return.
Provides the signed baseline set replicated to the alternate facility and holds the storage and retrieval agreement, custodian record and retrieval rehearsal results.

control_implementations.narrative: The alternate facility holding the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) replica is recorded in the contingency plan with its separation distance from the primary facility, its independent utility feed and its own site access control, and each replica set is verified as hash-identical to the primary before it counts as the alternate. What is incomplete is the decorrelation argument: the plan names the hazards separation is intended to address, but the regional-event analysis — shared transport corridor and shared regional power provider — has not been finished, so a residual shared-threat exposure is neither quantified nor formally accepted. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the primary repository set and the hash-verification record proving the alternate replica is identical; carries the recorded separation distance and hazard list in the site annex of the contingency plan.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned approach lists, for each access route to the alternate facility, the obstacle that would delay retrieval of Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) backup media during an area-wide disruption, with a named mitigation and a responsible role, and walks the retrieval sequence through to standing up the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) instance at that facility. Nothing has been written down yet: no obstacle list exists, the media release authorisation names an organisation rather than a role, and no retrieval walkthrough has been rehearsed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will be stood up at the alternate facility to read retrieved media into a usable provisioning workflow; no alternate-facility build or media-ingest procedure exists yet.
Supplies the backup media whose retrieval the accessibility analysis must cover; the media release authorisation step is not yet assigned to a named role.

control_implementations.narrative: The intended alternate processing arrangement is a written agreement making a second Aurora integration facility available to host a Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build and a Mission Computer (LRU-001) integration article, sufficient to resume the mission-support operations the contingency plan names within its five working-day transfer objective. Because WS-X90 is categorised A:moderate, the design is a staged transfer with equipment delivered on call — not a continuously warm standby, and the plan says so rather than implying capability the programme does not fund. The agreement is in negotiation, the equipment list is drafted but carries no delivery commitment, and no transfer has been rehearsed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will be rebuilt at the alternate facility from the signed baseline as the first step of a transfer; the alternate-site build procedure is drafted but untested.
An integration article would be stood up at the alternate facility to carry mission-support operations during a staged transfer; no article is currently allocated to that role.

control_implementations.narrative: The candidate alternate processing facility is separated from the primary integration site and, on the survey completed to date, draws its power and network entry from different providers and runs its own badge system. The record that would make this a control rather than a fact — the separation entry in the contingency plan, the threat set the separation is intended to decorrelate, and a signed confirmation of the independent utility and network entries — has not been produced, so the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) alternate build is still nominated rather than assured. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Would be rebuilt at the separated alternate facility; the dependency survey covering that facility's power, network entry and badge system is complete but not recorded in the plan.

control_implementations.narrative: No accessibility analysis exists for the alternate processing facility. The obstacles that would prevent staff and equipment from reaching it during an area-wide disruption, and the mitigations for each, have not been identified, so the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) alternate build is nominated in the plan without any assurance it could be reached. This is tracked as an open gap. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: No accessibility analysis covers reaching the alternate facility to stand up this build; no mitigation actions are defined.

control_implementations.narrative: The draft agreement for the alternate processing facility carries no priority-of-service provision, so the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) build could be queued behind other tenants of the same facility with no contractual basis to object. No clause referencing the contingency plan's recovery time objective has been proposed to the facility owner. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: The alternate-site build has no contractual priority of service; the draft facility agreement is silent on recovery time objectives.

control_implementations.narrative: The intended alternate telecommunications design uses the two bearers the platform already carries: the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) takes the mission data operations the contingency plan names as essential when the primary ground bearer is lost, reaching a 30-minute resumption objective, while the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) detects bearer loss within 60 seconds and re-establishes the protected tunnel over the alternate bearer under an identical policy set. Neither behaviour is fielded: the essential-operations list is not baselined, bearer-loss detection is manual today, and no failover has been timed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will carry the named essential mission data operations on the alternate path and suppress non-essential traffic while that path is active; the operation classification and the timed resumption test do not exist yet.

Will detect primary bearer loss within 60 seconds and re-establish the protected tunnel on the alternate bearer without operator re-keying, applying the same policy set on both; detection is presently an operator action.

control_implementations.narrative: The intent is that both the primary and the alternate telecommunications service agreements supporting the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) carry priority-of-service provisions tied to the recovery time objective in the contingency plan, and that the agreement file records, for each common-carrier service, either a submitted national security emergency preparedness priority request reference or the reason the service is out of scope. Today neither agreement contains such a clause and no priority request has been submitted or ruled out in writing. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Depends on the primary common-carrier service whose agreement is to carry the priority-of-service clause; the clause is not in the executed agreement.
Depends on the alternate bearer service whose agreement is to carry the matching clause and priority request record; neither exists yet.

control_implementations.narrative: Carrier-side disjointness has been established and demonstrated: the primary and alternate services traverse different transmission lines and different carrier points of presence, and a path trace built from live configuration rather than from a drawing shows no shared carrier element between the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) path and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) path. On-platform the two paths still converge — both transit the same port group on the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009), which is the single point of failure the control is meant to remove. Re-homing the radio path onto a separate port group is the open item behind REQ-498. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Terminates the primary bearer and generates one of the two traced paths from live interface and routing state.
Terminates the alternate bearer and generates the second traced path; carrier-side disjointness from the primary is confirmed.
Carries both traced paths through a single port group today; this shared element is the remaining on-platform single point of failure and is recorded as such.

control_implementations.narrative: Backup reliability is verified rather than assumed. At least monthly — the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CP-9(1) — the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) recomputes the hash tree of every backup set held on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) and restores at least one randomly selected partition to a scratch volume, recording which partition was chosen and its integrity result. A verification that fails, or that has not run within 31 days of its predecessor, raises a maintenance alert that cannot be cleared without a subsequent passing verification and that survives a controller restart. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Schedules and runs the monthly verification, selects the partition to restore, performs the scratch restore, and owns the maintenance alert that a failed or overdue verification raises.
Holds the sealed backup sets and their hash trees, serves the partition read for the scratch restore, and re-verifies each set's integrity tag as it is read.

control_implementations.narrative: Every backup set sealed on the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) is transferred to the alternate storage facility, and the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) records the transfer with the set identifier, the sealing hash and the receiving custodian's confirmed hash, so a mismatch is visible on receipt. The transfer itself is a signed-media courier run staged from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), which meets the five working-day objective in practice but is not measured against it automatically: no check compares elapsed time from sealing to recorded receipt, so a missed run is found at the next audit rather than reported as a recovery-point gap when it happens. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Seals each backup set with its hash and hands it to the transfer workflow; re-verifies the set on any return from the alternate facility.
Records the transfer entry — set identifier, sealing hash, receiving custodian and confirmed hash — and is where the missing elapsed-time check against the five working-day objective will be added.
Stages the signed media for the courier run and captures the custodian handover record; the run is initiated by an operator rather than by a scheduled trigger.

control_implementations.narrative: Backup material is protected as a unit and its keys never leave hardware. The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) encrypts and integrity-tags a backup set as a whole before it will mark the set sealed, and refuses to seal a set on which either operation was suppressed; a raw read of the backup partition yields no recoverable configuration, audit or key-shadow content. The wrapping and integrity keys are generated and used inside the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), which serves a backup wrap or unwrap only to the storage role identity that seals and opens backup sets and rejects and logs the request under any other identity, including maintenance roles. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Encrypts and integrity-tags each backup set before sealing, refuses to seal an untagged or unencrypted set, and fails the integrity check on any post-seal modification.
Generates, wraps and uses the backup encryption and integrity keys internally, never exporting them in cleartext, and enforces the storage role identity check on every wrap and unwrap request.

control_implementations.narrative: Recovery is transactional on both of the platform's transaction-shaped paths. The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) journals each staged update or configuration transaction with a commit record, discards a partial transaction on interruption, and marks a transaction complete only when the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) attests that the image the platform actually booted matches the intended image. On the payload side the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) journals each command with its authorization reference and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) state at issue, and replays the journal after a reset before accepting a new command. Two gaps remain: the platform management configuration partition still requires a technician to select the rollback point rather than rolling back automatically, and the reconstructed payload state reported by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) is compared with observed behaviour by hand. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Journals staged update and configuration transactions, discards partial transactions on interruption, and marks completion only on a matching boot attestation; automatic rollback-point selection is missing for the platform management configuration partition.
Attests the image actually booted after a recovery and supplies the digest that gates transaction completion.
Journals each payload command transaction with its authorization reference and interlock state, and replays the journal to the last committed state before accepting a new command after a reset.
Supplies the interlock state recorded with each command transaction, which bounds what the replay may treat as committed.
Reports the reconstructed payload state after replay; the comparison of that report against observed payload behaviour is still a manual step.

control_implementations.narrative: The assessment, authorization and continuous monitoring procedure set for SYS-WSX90 is held as signed artifacts in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), each carrying a named approver and a review date, with any artifact past a 12-month review date flagged automatically — the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CA-1. Publication runs only through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), so each revision carries the publishing operator's identity and a diff against its predecessor, and the recipient list for each revision is retained with it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed assessment, authorization and monitoring procedure set with approver and review date on each artifact, and computes the 12-month review flag.
Sole publication path for a revision; binds operator identity, predecessor diff and recipient list to each published artifact.

control_implementations.narrative: Assessment independence is enforced by the access model rather than by assertion. The independent assessment team holds a dedicated assessor role on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) that can read configuration and health state but holds no permission to change a configuration item, clear an audit record or approve a remediation action, and can export the correlated record set from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) — an export that is itself recorded as an access event. The role is provisioned separately from every engineering role, and no account holds both, so nobody assesses a control they built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Defines and enforces the read-only assessor role, denying write, clear and approve permissions, and prevents an account from holding an assessor role and an engineering role simultaneously.
Serves the correlated record export the independent team works from and records each export as an access event attributable to the assessor identity.

control_implementations.narrative: The programme intends to add two specialised assessments to each authorization cycle: an announced data-leakage assessment against the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) egress paths, and an unannounced malicious-user exercise against a Mission Computer (LRU-001) operator account, each producing a result that enumerates the paths or privileges exercised and what was observed rather than a completion date. Neither is scheduled yet — the assessment plan carries no specialised-assessment frequency, no announced-versus-unannounced determination has been made, and no rules of engagement exist for the malicious-user exercise. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Target of the planned data-leakage assessment; the egress path inventory the assessment would exercise exists but has not been scoped into an assessment procedure.
Target of the planned unannounced malicious-user exercise against an operator account; no rules of engagement or account provisioning for the exercise exist yet.

control_implementations.narrative: External exchanges are gated on agreements. Each exchange enabled in the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) policy set maps to a signed exchange agreement identifier recording interface characteristics, the impact level of the information carried, the controls each party operates and the responsible party for each, and the gateway will not enable an exchange with no agreement identifier. The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) tactical data link agreement is signed and current. The gap is the ground-support telemetry exchange, which is running under a time-bounded interim approval while its agreement is in draft; the interim approval has an expiry recorded but the exchange is live without a signed agreement. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses to enable an external exchange whose policy entry carries no signed agreement identifier, and reports the agreement identifier with each enabled exchange; carries the one exchange currently running under interim approval.
Carries the tactical data link exchange, which is covered by a signed and current agreement recording its impact level and control responsibilities.

control_implementations.narrative: Inbound transfer authorization is checked at the boundary: before accepting data written into WS-X90 from an interconnected system, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) verifies that the sending identity holds a current write authorization for the specific destination data set, and rejects and logs a transfer from an unauthorized identity or one directed at a data set outside its authorization. The reverse direction is weaker — the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) releases telemetry on link-layer identity alone, with no check against a recorded read authorization, so a receiver that has been de-authorized on paper can still be served until the link configuration is changed. That gap is carried by REQ-509. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Verifies the sending identity's current write authorization for the destination data set before accepting inbound data, and rejects and logs unauthorized or out-of-scope writes.
Releases telemetry on link-layer identity only; the recorded read-authorization check on the outbound path is not implemented.

control_implementations.narrative: The authorization decision for SYS-WSX90, the named authorizing official and the list of inherited common controls accepted are recorded as a signed artifact in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) surfaces the authorization reference and its expiry as part of platform status so the authorization state is visible on the platform rather than only in a file. What is outstanding is currency: the expansion of the in-scope control set from 74 to 546 controls is a significant change under the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CA-6, and the resulting reauthorization package has not been submitted, so the recorded decision covers a narrower scope than the system now claims. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed authorization artifact naming the authorizing official and each accepted inherited common control, and is where the pending reauthorization package will be recorded.
Reports the current authorization reference and expiry in platform status so an operator or assessor can see the authorization state without opening the artifact.

control_implementations.narrative: The independent monitoring team pulls the continuous monitoring dataset directly from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) on the agreed cadence, with no engineering-held staging step between the collector and the team, so the data they analyse is not curated by the organisation that operates the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013). Coverage is partial: independent monitoring today spans the audit, boundary and configuration families, while the contingency, maintenance and payload-interface families remain self-assessed by the engineering organisation, which is recorded in the monitoring strategy but not yet remediated. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Serves the monitoring dataset directly to the independent team on the agreed cadence and records each delivery, with no engineering staging step in the path.
Produces the underlying control state the dataset is built from; the families it reports that are not yet under independent monitoring are listed in the monitoring strategy.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned trend capability keeps at least 12 months of period-comparable control-monitoring outcomes in the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and requires each monitoring-strategy revision to cite the trend that drove it — a control whose failure rate is rising, or a check whose result has been unchanged across four consecutive periods that can therefore be run less often. Today the collector retains the outcomes but not in a period-comparable form: the check identifiers were re-scoped when the control set expanded, so periods before that change cannot be compared, and no strategy revision has yet cited empirical data. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Retains control-monitoring outcomes but not yet in a stable, period-comparable form; the identifier remapping needed to make historical periods comparable is the outstanding work.

control_implementations.narrative: Risk monitoring is intended to be readable as three separable views for each in-scope control — effectiveness, compliance with the authorized configuration, and what changed since the previous period — with the change view built from Configuration Repository (LRU-020) commits and the other two from Security Log Collector (LRU-018) outcomes, so that a rise in risk can be attributed to a change, a drift or a degradation rather than reported as a single score. The dataset today carries a compliance result only; the effectiveness view has no defined measure per family, and the change view is not joined to repository commits. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Produces the compliance results today; the effectiveness measure per control family that the risk view needs is undefined.
Holds the commit history the change view will be built from; no join between commits and monitoring periods exists yet.

control_implementations.narrative: The consistency check is designed to compare, for each control family, the approved procedure held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) against the settings the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) actually reports on each LRU, listing every divergence with the LRU, the setting and the approved value, and recording a family with no divergence as consistent for the period rather than leaving it silent. The comparison exists only as a manual spot check on two families; the machine-readable expression of the approved settings that would make it repeatable has not been authored. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the approved procedures; the machine-readable expected-settings expression the comparison needs does not exist for most families.
Reports the actual per-LRU settings the comparison would read; the reporting interface is available and already used by the manual spot check.

control_implementations.narrative: Monitoring results are machine-produced and carry their own age. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) presents the current result for every in-scope control with the time it was produced, marks any result older than 24 hours as stale so an assessor cannot mistake an old pass for a current one, and raises a collection alarm when the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) feed has been silent for more than 15 minutes. The presented dataset is reproducible from the collector on demand, so no monitoring result reaches an assessor through manual assembly. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Assembles, timestamps and ages every monitoring result, marks stale results, raises the feed-silence alarm, and regenerates the presented dataset on demand.
Supplies the continuous control-state feed whose silence beyond 15 minutes triggers the collection alarm.

control_implementations.narrative: Penetration testing of the WS-X90 external boundary at the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and of the technician session path at the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) is performed by a team holding no build or operate role on either LRU, under written rules of engagement agreed and dated before the first test activity. The report names each attempted technique and its outcome — including techniques that did not succeed — rather than listing only the findings raised, so the coverage of the test is assessable and not just its results. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: External boundary under test; the gateway's policy set, tunnel termination and egress paths were exercised by the independent team.
Technician session path under test; session establishment, privilege boundaries and the supervisor override path were exercised by the independent team.

control_implementations.narrative: No facility-directed penetration testing has been performed for WS-X90. Unannounced attempts to reach the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) enclosure or to remove or connect a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) without passing facility access control are not part of the assessment process, the assessment plan sets no frequency for them, and no authorising official has been named for such attempts. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Its enclosure has never been the target of an authorised physical bypass attempt; no facility-directed test procedure exists.
Custody and connection controls on this conditional endpoint have not been tested by attempted physical removal or unauthorised connection.

control_implementations.narrative: Internal connections are governed by a register rather than by convention. The authorized internal-connection register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) records each internal connection with its interface characteristics and the nature of the data it carries; the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) leaves a port unforwarding when the endpoint on it is absent from the register and raises a register-mismatch event, and the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) admits a payload-side connection only for a registered endpoint and terminates it when the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) leaves the armed-permissive state. Three things are missing: the sensor connections aggregated by the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) are documented in the register but not yet enforced against it, the 15-minute idle termination on payload-side connections is not implemented, and the annual review of the register has not run once since the register was expanded. Admission and termination events reported by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) are available for reconciliation but are reconciled by hand. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Leaves a port unforwarding when its endpoint is absent from the authorized internal-connection register and raises a register-mismatch event naming the port and endpoint.
Aggregates the navigation sensor connections; these are documented in the register but the interface does not yet refuse an unregistered sensor connection.
Holds the authorized internal-connection register with interface characteristics and data nature per connection; the at-least-annual review record for the expanded register is outstanding.
Admits a payload-side internal connection only for a registered endpoint and terminates it on loss of the armed-permissive interlock state; the 15-minute idle termination is not implemented.
Supplies the armed-permissive state whose loss terminates open payload-side internal connections.
Reports each payload-side admission and termination for reconciliation against the register; the reconciliation itself is manual today.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 inherits the Aurora enterprise risk management policy but has no system-level risk assessment policy of its own, so the annual review parameter is currently met at the enterprise level only. The planned build places the system-level policy and its procedures in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as a signed set, adds the designated risk-assessment official and dissemination list as record fields rather than prose, and wires the twelve-month staleness flag into the release promotion gate so a lapsed policy stops a build rather than being caught at audit. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository is the single store for the signed risk assessment policy and procedure set, and will carry the staleness flag that blocks promotion of a release package citing a policy revision older than twelve months.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 is categorized confidentiality high, integrity high, availability moderate. The record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) carries a separate impact rationale per objective and a dated authorizing official approval, and it is the same record that selects SP 800-53B High as the starting baseline and drives the CNSSI 1253 allocation, so the categorization cannot drift away from the control set derived from it. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) stamps the three-value categorization into every artifact header it emits. A conflicting H-M-M figure in an older configuration example was rejected during the reference rebuild and the resolution is recorded with the profile derivation. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the approved categorization record with the per-objective rationale and the dated authorizing official approval, and is the source the security plan and the tailoring pipeline both read.
Mission Computer reads the categorization value at build time and stamps it into the header of every artifact it exports, so a consumer of an export does not have to look the categorization up.

control_implementations.narrative: Supply chain risk for WS-X90 is currently assessed once at procurement and not refreshed. The planned build produces a standing assessment for each of the three externally procured LRUs, the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008), covering counterfeit part risk, firmware provenance and named sub-tier suppliers for every programmable element, reissued at least annually and within thirty days of a supplier, foundry or waveform-vendor change. What is missing is the assessment itself, the supplier-change trigger and the link from the assessment into the criticality analysis; nothing is fielded yet. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cryptographic Services Module is the highest-consequence procured item; its assessment will cover foundry provenance for the security controller and the vendor-loaded firmware image chain.
Timing Receiver is a commercial GNSS receiver with vendor-loaded firmware, so its assessment covers firmware provenance and the sub-tier suppliers of the receiver front end.
Tactical Data Radio carries a programmable waveform from a separate vendor, so its assessment covers the waveform supply chain and the identity of the waveform signing authority.

control_implementations.narrative: No all-source intelligence channel supports the WS-X90 risk analysis. Threat input today is limited to open vendor advisories handled by the Product Security Engineer. Neither the intelligence-source field on the risk register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) nor the path from an intelligence report to a Security Log Collector (LRU-018) detection rule exists, and no clearance arrangement for receiving such reporting on the program has been established. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector would be the point where a threat with an observable signature becomes a detection rule; no intelligence-derived rule exists on it today.
Configuration Repository holds the risk register that would carry the intelligence-source field; the field is not defined and no entry cites a report identifier.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has no representation of the current threat environment inside the platform; boundary policy is static between baselines. The planned design keeps a named threat state on the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), refreshed on each ground-segment bulletin and at least weekly, and gives the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) a distinct flow policy per state, with every policy load written to the gateway audit stream. The state machine, the policy set and the bulletin ingest are all still to be built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector will hold the named current threat state and refresh it on each ground-segment bulletin, at least weekly, as the single value the rest of the platform reads.
Protected Network Gateway will carry one named flow policy per threat state so a state change narrows the permitted external flow set by policy load rather than by software change.

control_implementations.narrative: The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) pulls its vulnerability signature set from the approved feed mirrored in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and the mirror is refreshed on a weekly schedule with a signed timestamp. What is missing is the enforcement: the workstation does not yet compare the signature timestamp against the 24-hour window the CNSSI 1253 parameter for RA-5(2) sets before a scan starts, so a scan can currently run on a stale set, and the signature identifier is written into the scan log but not into the scan report header a reviewer reads. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation runs the baseline scan and holds the signature set; the freshness check at scan start and the abort path are the parts still to be added.
Configuration Repository mirrors the approved signature feed and stamps each mirrored set with a refresh timestamp that the workstation compares against.

control_implementations.narrative: Discoverable information is handled as two separate exposures. On the network side the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) has been stripped of service banners and version strings and is surveyed quarterly from outside the boundary; one host-name leak on an error path remains open and is tracked for the next configuration change. On the RF side the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) protects mission traffic, but the acquisition preamble and idle keep-alive pattern have not been surveyed by an off-platform receiver, so no statement can yet be made about what a passive listener recovers from those states. Corrective action timing is defined for the network survey and not for the RF survey. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway has had service banners and version strings suppressed on the externally reachable ports; the host name still appears in one error response path found by the last quarterly survey.

Tactical Data Radio carries no airframe identifier in the protected traffic path, but the acquisition preamble has not yet been surveyed off-platform and the idle keep-alive pattern is unchanged from the vendor default.

control_implementations.narrative: Credentialed scanning of the Mission Computer (LRU-001) baseline runs only from a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) session that the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) has authorized under a named privileged scan role. The role is issued per scan window, never held standing on the laptop, and is revoked as part of session teardown, so the scan credential is only meaningful while the gateway is holding the window open. Refusals are written to the gateway audit stream with the requesting session identity. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway holds the privileged scan role, binds it to a single scan window, refuses the credentialed scan service to any session without it and revokes it in the session teardown sequence.
Maintenance Laptop is the only endpoint from which a credentialed scan may be run, and it obtains the scan role from the gateway rather than holding a standing credential.
Mission Computer accepts credentialed scan authentication only inside an open gateway-authorized window, so a captured scan credential is not usable on its own.

control_implementations.narrative: The three input streams a multi-hop view needs, vulnerability scan output, configuration drift reports and audit alerts, all reach the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) today but are read separately by an analyst. The planned build joins them per build identifier against the approved segmentation map and emits a multi-hop finding naming the ordered LRU sequence and the permitted flow that connects them. Neither the join nor the finding type exists yet, and the segmentation map is not currently machine-readable to LRU-018. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector already receives scan output, drift reports and audit alerts separately; the correlation engine, the segmentation-map join and the multi-hop finding type are the new work.

control_implementations.narrative: Aurora operates no public reporting channel for vulnerabilities in WS-X90 components. Reports arriving by other routes are handled case by case by the Product Security Engineer with no intake register, no receipt commitment and no recorded decision authority. Establishing the channel is an Aurora-level action that the program has not yet raised, and the intake register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) has not been specified. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository would hold the intake register that records receipt, affected LRU, triage outcome and decision authority; no register schema has been defined.

control_implementations.narrative: Every finding from the completed assessment carries a response decision in the risk register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), with an accepting authority named on each acceptance and a POA&M item on each mitigation, so the response practice itself is established. Two things are missing: the fifteen working day decision clock is tracked in a spreadsheet rather than enforced by the register, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) still reports a baseline as compliant when an open finding against it has no decision, which removes the signal that should stop that baseline from shipping. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the risk register carrying the response decision, the accepting authority and the POA&M link for each finding; the fifteen working day clock is tracked manually rather than by the register.

Platform Management Controller reports baseline compliance and is intended to withhold a compliant verdict while an open finding on that baseline has no recorded response decision; that interlock is not yet wired.

control_implementations.narrative: A criticality analysis exists for WS-X90 baseline 4.2 and classifies the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) integrity monitor, the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) arm and inhibit path and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) root-of-trust verification as mission-critical with a named protection allocation for each. What is missing is coverage and cadence: functions in the ground support subsystem are unclassified, the supply chain measures column is populated for only two of the three mission-critical entries, and the analysis is refreshed at design reviews but not at every baseline change board. This narrative is synthetic demo content.
