by_component.description: Navigation Processor integrity-monitor function is classified mission-critical with the protection allocation named; the supply chain measures column for it is empty.
Payload Safety Interlock arm and inhibit function is classified mission-critical and is the reference case for an independently powered, independently configured critical function.
Secure Boot Controller root-of-trust verification is classified mission-critical and its protection allocation is the anti-tamper and provisioning control set.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has no threat hunting capability. The Security Log Collector (LRU-018) evaluates fixed detection rules against the exported telemetry stream and retains alerts, but retains no searchable corpus behind them, so an analyst cannot run a hypothesis-driven search over past data. The continuous employment frequency the CNSSI 1253 parameter for RA-10 sets is therefore not met in any degree, and neither the workspace nor the retention needed to start is funded in the current baseline. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector runs fixed detection rules only; there is no hunting workspace, no hypothesis record and no retained corpus over which an analyst-driven search could run.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 relies on the Aurora enterprise awareness and training policy and has no system-level policy or procedure set of its own. The planned build issues a WS-X90 policy set to all personnel holding a WS-X90 account, the dissemination scope the CNSSI 1253 parameter for AT-1 sets, holds it signed in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), reviews it at least annually and after any AT-family assessment finding, and records the acknowledged revision per account holder so dissemination is a record rather than an assertion. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository will hold the signed awareness and training policy set and the per-account-holder acknowledgement record tying each person to the revision they acknowledged.

control_implementations.narrative: Aurora runs general security awareness training that WS-X90 personnel attend, but no WS-X90-specific literacy content exists and no account gate reads a completion date. The planned build makes completion a precondition for first enablement of a Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) or Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) account and at least annually thereafter, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency for AT-2, adds a thirty-day retraining trigger on platform changes that alter mission data or removable media handling, and requires the course revision notes to name the incident or change that prompted each update. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation account enablement will be conditioned on a literacy training completion date, and its operators are the population the removable-media and mission-data handling content is written for.
Maintenance Laptop holders are the second training population; the thirty-day retraining trigger is driven by platform changes that alter how they handle mission data in the field.

control_implementations.narrative: No WS-X90 insider threat module has been written. The planned content is specific rather than generic: it names the indicators that arise in this system, requests to bypass the maintenance session record, attempts to widen a bounded maintenance task, and removal of platform data outside the approved transfer path, and it states that the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) retains the session record a report will be checked against. Recognition and the reporting path are both to be tested by sampling rather than by course completion alone. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Laptop holders are the trained population, because the bounded maintenance activity is where a request to widen scope or bypass the session record would be made.
Security Log Collector retains the maintenance session record that any insider-threat report is checked against, which is the fact the training has to convey so reporting is not deterred.

control_implementations.narrative: Social engineering content is covered only by the Aurora enterprise course and no exercise has been run against WS-X90 personnel. The planned build trains Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) account holders to refuse out-of-band requests for provisioning material, session credentials or baseline identifiers regardless of the claimed requester, adds social mining content covering the collection of unclassified fragments about roles and schedules, and runs at least one recorded refusal exercise per year in which both the refusal and the report are scored. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation operators hold the material a social engineering attempt against this program would target, so they are the primary exercise population.
Maintenance Laptop holders work at forward locations where an out-of-band request is most plausible, and are the second exercise population.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has no published anomalous-behaviour indicator set, so operators are trained on generic guidance that does not map to what this platform actually shows them. The planned build publishes an indicator set drawn from the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) plausibility-reject classes, the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) out-of-envelope health values and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) alert classes, trains against it with a one-hour reporting expectation, and gates unsupervised mission shifts on completion. Publishing the indicator set is the prerequisite and has not started. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Navigation Sensor Interface plausibility-reject classes are one of the three indicator sources the training material draws its concrete examples from.
Payload Telemetry Unit out-of-envelope health values are the second indicator source, and are the indicators an operator is most likely to see first during a mission shift.
Security Log Collector alert classes are the third source; the training distinguishes the classes that indicate suspicious code behaviour from routine operational alerts.

control_implementations.narrative: No advanced persistent threat literacy content exists for WS-X90 and the topic is not covered by the general Aurora literacy course. Long-dwell access and the abuse of legitimate maintenance and update paths for persistence are the two behaviours most relevant to this platform and neither is taught. No material has been drafted and no personnel have received training on it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector surfaces the low-signal indicators an advanced persistent threat module would teach people to look at, but no training material references it and no analyst has been trained against it.

control_implementations.narrative: Threat information reaches the WS-X90 engineering team but does not reach the people operating the system, and no bulletin is issued. The planned build produces a quarterly WS-X90 threat bulletin from the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) alert history and the ground-segment feed, and requires each bulletin to be reflected in a dated revision of the operating instructions in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), so the current threat picture shows up in how the system is run and not only in a training record. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Security Log Collector alert history is one of the two inputs to the quarterly bulletin, and is what keeps the bulletin specific to what this platform has actually seen.
Configuration Repository holds the operating instructions each bulletin has to be carried into, which is the step that turns a bulletin into an operating change.

control_implementations.narrative: Role-based training is real for two of the four privileged roles. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) checks a current maintenance-role completion date before enabling a technician account, and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) sessions inherit that decision, so an untrained technician cannot get in. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) operator curriculum is written and authorisations are recorded against it. Two gaps remain: LRU-014 does not disable an account when the training record lapses after enablement, so the twelve-month CNSSI 1253 frequency for AT-3 is enforced at the door and not continuously, and no curriculum has been written for the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) analyst role. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway holds the account gate; it checks the maintenance-role completion date at enablement today but does not yet disable an account when the record lapses.
Maintenance Laptop sessions inherit the gateway decision, so the lapse behaviour on LRU-014 is what determines whether a lapsed technician can still establish a session.
Provisioning Workstation operators have a written role curriculum in use, and account authorisation is recorded against it.
Security Log Collector analysts have no role curriculum; they are currently authorized against the general literacy course alone, which is the open gap for this control.

control_implementations.narrative: Integration bay personnel receive a facility induction that mentions fire and power equipment but is not recorded as environmental control training and is not repeated. The planned build gives everyone with unescorted access to the bay holding the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) units initial and at least annual training on the fire detection and suppression equipment, the emergency power cut-off and the environmental alarms, which is the CNSSI 1253 frequency for AT-3(1), and adds the shutdown order that protects platform state before power is removed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Provisioning Workstation is installed in the integration bay whose fire, power and environmental alarm equipment the training covers.
Maintenance Laptop units are held in the same bay, and the shutdown order the training teaches is what protects platform state before bay power is cut.

control_implementations.narrative: Physical security training for WS-X90 is currently the site induction only, which does not cover the custody procedure specific to this program. The planned build trains everyone authorized to draw a Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) or open a Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) session, initially and at least annually per the CNSSI 1253 frequency for AT-3(2), on badge-reader use, intrusion alarm response and the draw, custody and return procedure that governs LRU-019 as a conditional asset, with retraining within thirty days of a significant change to the facility physical security systems. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway session holders are one of the two trained populations, because opening a session is the point at which physical and logical custody meet.
Maintenance Laptop is a conditional asset drawn for a named bounded activity and returned to controlled storage, and its custody procedure is the core of the training.

control_implementations.narrative: Training records for every WS-X90 account holder are kept in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with the course and completion date, and records survive account closure for the three-year retention period. Two gaps stop the record from doing its job: there is no expiry field, so lapse has to be computed by hand from the course cadence, and the record is published as a document rather than as a machine-readable status, which is why the account enablement gates on the maintenance and provisioning paths check a date at enablement and cannot re-check it afterwards. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the training records with course and completion date; the expiry field and the machine-readable current-or-lapsed status the account gates need are not yet published.

control_implementations.narrative: Training results for WS-X90 personnel are not reported to anyone; completion is recorded and not read. The planned build reports results to each person's supervisor and to the Aurora cybersecurity and privacy officials at least annually and again on discovery of a security incident or privacy breach, which are the CNSSI 1253 parameter values for AT-6, names individual failures in the maintenance, provisioning and analyst roles rather than reporting an aggregate pass rate, and files each report against the training register in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the training register each feedback report is filed against, which is what makes the report retrievable at assessment rather than living in mail.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has a system security plan but no system-level planning policy and procedure set governing how that plan and the architecture, concept of operations and rules of behaviour are produced and maintained. The planned build holds the set signed in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), reviews it at least annually per the CNSSI 1253 parameter for PL-1 and after any boundary or authorization state change, and names the designated planning official on every revision. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository will hold the signed planning policy and procedure set with the designated planning official and the dissemination roles as record fields.

control_implementations.narrative: Rules of behaviour exist for WS-X90, are acknowledged before account enablement on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014), the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) accounts, and are reviewed annually. The gap is in re-acknowledgement: LRU-014 checks that an acknowledgement exists but not that it is against the current revision, so a holder who acknowledged an earlier version keeps access after a revision, and there is no automatic disablement at the ten working day mark. LRU-017 enforces the current revision correctly and is the pattern the gateway will be brought to. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Access Gateway checks an acknowledgement exists before enabling a technician account, but accepts an acknowledgement of any revision rather than the current one.
Provisioning Workstation account enablement is gated on a current acknowledgement and is the path where the gate works as intended.
Maintenance Laptop accounts inherit the gateway decision, so the revision-matching weakness on LRU-014 carries through to laptop sessions.

control_implementations.narrative: The current WS-X90 rules of behaviour say nothing about social media, external sites or the reuse of Aurora-issued identifiers off-platform. The planned revision adds clauses covering the posting of build identifiers, subsystem and LRU names, integration bay imagery and schedule information, and the use of Aurora identifiers or authentication secrets to create external accounts. The configuration half already holds: neither the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) nor the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) has a general-purpose browsing path, so the rule will be backed by the absence of the route. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Maintenance Laptop is the asset most likely to be used near a personal device, and carries no general-purpose browsing path, which is the configuration half of the restriction.
Provisioning Workstation likewise has no route to an external browsing service, so the rule and the configuration agree rather than the rule standing alone.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 has no security concept of operations; operating intent is spread across the security plan and the maintenance procedures. The planned document describes operation across mission phases, the decision authority at each phase, entry to and exit from maintenance and provisioning windows, and Mission Computer (LRU-001) behaviour on a security event. Consistent with the moderate availability objective it will state a controlled mission abort and recover posture rather than continuous failover, which is what the platform actually does, and will be reviewed at each baseline change board and at least annually. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository will hold the security concept of operations under the same review cadence as the security plan and the architecture description.
Mission Computer behaviour on a security event is the part of the concept of operations that has to be written against actual platform behaviour rather than intent.

control_implementations.narrative: A WS-X90 security architecture description exists in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and states which security functions each subsystem carries. Two things are incomplete. The description records carried and inherited functions for four of the six subsystems and does not yet record the assumptions made about external dependencies, so PL-8a is met in part. And while every function allocated to the Mission Computer (LRU-001) resolves to a named element in the approved build manifest, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) flow-policy allocations do not, and they are currently shown as covered rather than carried as open gaps with an owner and a target baseline. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds the architecture description; the carried and inherited function lists are complete for four subsystems and the external dependency assumptions are not recorded.
Mission Computer allocations resolve to named elements in the approved build manifest, so the architecture claim and the build agree for this LRU.
Protected Network Gateway flow-policy allocations are described in the architecture but not yet mapped to manifest elements, which is the open architecture gap for this control.

control_implementations.narrative: Defense in depth is real on both paths but the independence claim does not fully hold. Externally, the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) link-layer admission policy and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) flow policy are generated from separate configuration sources and neither derives its rules from the other. On the payload command path the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) segment policy, the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) command validation and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) arm authorization form three layers, and a rejection at any one stops the command, but LRU-009 and LRU-010 currently draw part of their segment definition from the same generated file, so a single error in that file can weaken two layers at once. Separating those sources is the open item. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway is the outer of the two external enforcement layers and holds the flow policy, generated from a configuration source separate from the radio.
Tactical Data Radio link-layer admission policy is the first external layer, so admitted RF traffic still faces an independently written gateway policy.

Internal Ethernet Switch segment policy is the first payload-path layer; part of its segment definition is generated from the same file as the payload interface controller, which breaks the independence claim.
Payload Interface Controller command validation is the second payload-path layer and rejects malformed or out-of-scope commands before they reach the interlock.
Payload Safety Interlock arm authorization is the third and independently powered layer; a command it rejects is rejected for the platform regardless of the other two.

control_implementations.narrative: Supplier diversity between the boundary and internal enforcement points is not achieved. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) and the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) both derive their enforcement from one vendor switching stack, so a single vendor defect or advisory reaches both layers at once and the depth described under PL-8(1) is shallower than it appears. No second-source assessment has been performed and no procurement action has been opened. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Protected Network Gateway boundary enforcement derives from the same vendor switching stack as the internal segmentation point, so a vendor advisory applies to both.
Internal Ethernet Switch segmentation enforcement is the second instance of that same stack; no second-source alternative has been assessed.

control_implementations.narrative: Malicious code protection is centrally managed for every WS-X90 LRU from the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016), with the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) holding the authoritative status view and the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) the single alert path. Flaw remediation is centrally managed for the mission computing, navigation, communications and platform management LRUs but the payload subsystem LRUs are still scheduled by hand, which is the open gap. The spam protection element of the CNSSI 1253 parameter for PL-9 has no applicable service on WS-X90, which carries no messaging or mail transfer function, and is recorded as not applicable with that rationale rather than claimed as met. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Update & Recovery Controller is the central point that stages malicious code protection updates for every LRU; payload subsystem flaw remediation is still scheduled outside it.
Platform Management Controller holds the authoritative per-LRU status view for both processes, which is what makes a locally managed exception visible.
Security Log Collector is the single alert path for both processes, so a locally handled event on any LRU still surfaces centrally.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 selects one control baseline, PROFILE-WSX90-TAILORED, held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). SP 800-53B High is recorded as the starting baseline, selected from the high water mark of the C high, I high, A moderate categorization, with the CNSSI 1253 allocation applied over it and three named overlays after that. Every control in the resulting set carries an ordered selection trail, so the baseline can be read as a derivation rather than as an asserted list. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository holds PROFILE-WSX90-TAILORED as the single selected baseline together with the ordered selection trail behind every control in it.

control_implementations.narrative: Tailoring of the WS-X90 baseline is recorded as individual events in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), each naming the control, the action, the driver and the approving authority. Replaying the recorded events over SP 800-53B High reproduces the effective control set exactly, so the difference between the published baseline and what WS-X90 actually carries is reconstructible from the record without reference to anyone's memory. A control introduced into the set without a matching event fails the baseline review and the rejection is recorded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Configuration Repository records each tailoring action as an individual event naming control, action, driver and approving authority, and rejects a baseline whose contents cannot be replayed from those events.

control_implementations.narrative: Configuration management direction for SYS-WSX90 lives as data, not as a shelf binder. The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds the CM policy and the CM procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, each bound to the named Aurora CM official who owns it, and computes a review-overdue flag against the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-1. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is the only publication endpoint, so every revision carries an operator identity, a diff against its predecessor and the dissemination list of engineering and cybersecurity role holders who received it. What is missing is coverage: the policy and the seven procedures that supported the original 74-control scope are current and signed, but the procedures for the configuration management enhancements the expanded set introduced — automated change prohibition, automated security response, information location and signed components — are drafted and unsigned, so four of the eleven required procedures show as review-overdue in the repository today. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the CM policy and the eleven CM procedures as signed, version-tagged artifacts bound to the named CM official, and computes the review-overdue flag against the at-least-annual interval; currently reports four unsigned draft procedures for the newly added enhancements.
Sole publication endpoint for a policy or procedure revision; binds the operator identity, the predecessor diff and the engineering and cybersecurity dissemination list to each published revision.

control_implementations.narrative: Baseline currency is machine-maintained on the platform side and manual on the ground side. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) pushes each observed change of part number, firmware version or configuration set to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) inside a 15-minute window, and LRU-020 marks the affected baseline record stale until the push is reconciled, recording the prior value alongside the observed one. The gap is scope: LRU-013 observes the platform LRUs it manages directly, but the Ground Support Subsystem items — the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) and the repository host itself — are still reconciled by a technician on a weekly cadence, so their baseline records can sit stale for up to seven days. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Marks the affected baseline record stale on receipt and clears the marker only when the reconciliation completes; the ground support items it does not receive pushes for are still reconciled by hand on a weekly cadence.

Observes installed part number, firmware version and configuration set on the platform LRUs it manages and pushes each change to the repository inside a 15-minute window with the prior and observed values.

control_implementations.narrative: Rollback depth is held at three: the current approved baseline plus at least two prior approved versions, matching the retention CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-2(3). The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) keeps each retained version with its original approval signature and re-verifies those signatures on a weekly integrity sweep, reporting a retention integrity fault rather than quietly dropping a version that no longer verifies. The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) can stage and apply any retained version as a rollback using repository content alone, which is what makes the retention meaningful — the rollback path was exercised in the last integration campaign and completed without reaching outside LRU-020 for a missing artifact. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Retains the current baseline plus at least two prior approved versions with their original approval signatures, and re-verifies those signatures on a weekly sweep, reporting a retention integrity fault rather than dropping a version.
Stages and applies any retained baseline version as a rollback using repository content alone, which is what makes the retained depth operationally real rather than archival.

control_implementations.narrative: The travel configuration for the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) is designed and not yet built. The intent is a reduced image that carries no mission data, no provisioning key material and no cached maintenance credentials, issued and returned through a recorded transaction on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), with mandatory re-imaging and re-enrolment before LRU-019 may open a maintenance session again. The image definition and the issue/return record schema are drafted; the enforcement that prevents a returned laptop from opening a session before re-enrolment is not built, and today the return step is a procedural instruction rather than a technical gate. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Target of the reduced travel configuration — no mission data, no provisioning key material, no cached maintenance credentials — and subject to mandatory re-image and re-enrolment on return; the enforcement gate is not yet built.
Will record the issue and return of each travel instance with the traveller, the destination risk determination and the controls applied on return; the record schema is drafted and not in use.

control_implementations.narrative: Change automation runs in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020): every proposed change gets a record, the record is routed to its named approval authorities, and the release of the change artifact for staging is refused until the required approvals are present — the prohibition is enforced by the repository, not by discipline. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) refuses any configuration set that arrives without a released change record identifier, which closes the second path onto the platform. Two of the six behaviours the enhancement asks for are weak: the aging highlight for records left undecided beyond 10 working days is computed but only surfaced in a weekly report rather than pushed to the approvers, and completion notification reaches the originator but not yet the affected engineering lead. Both are carried against REQ-563. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Creates the change record, routes it to the named approval authorities, refuses to release the change artifact for staging until approvals are recorded, and computes the aging highlight for records left undecided beyond 10 working days.
Second enforcement point on the platform side: refuses any configuration set that arrives without a released change record identifier, closing the path that would bypass the repository.

control_implementations.narrative: No WS-X90 change reaches an operational platform without a recorded test and validation. The Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) will accept a change package for application only when the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) holds three things against that change record: a completed test result, a validation statement naming the specific security controls examined, and the identity of the engineer who signed it. A package presented with any of the three missing is held in the staging area and reported as an incomplete record, which is the mechanism that keeps the requirement from degrading into a checkbox — the validation statement has to name controls, and a statement that merely asserts compliance is rejected at review. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Accepts a change package for operational application only when the test result, the control validation statement and the signer identity are all present; otherwise holds the package in staging and reports it as an incomplete record.

Holds the test result, the validation statement naming the specific controls examined and the signing engineer's identity against the change record, and rejects a validation statement that only asserts compliance.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 configuration control board exists and meets, but the cybersecurity representative currently attends in an advisory capacity rather than as the voting member CNSSI 1253 directs for CM-3(4). The planned change amends the board charter to designate the representative and a named alternate as voting members, and extends the decision record the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) writes so that the representative's vote is a required field on every board decision, with dissent carried into the outcome text rather than summarised away. Neither the charter amendment nor the decision-record change has been made. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Records the board decision and the cybersecurity representative's vote against each change; the vote is not yet a required field and dissent is not yet carried into the outcome text.

control_implementations.narrative: Automatic response to an out-of-process baseline change is designed around the two components that already hold platform state. The Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) both detect a baseline value with no released change record today, and both raise it; what they do not yet do is act on it. The planned build drives the affected function to its restricted state, refuses the next mission-enable transition and raises a priority event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) within 60 seconds, with return to normal gated on an approved change record or a recorded override. Because availability is categorised moderate, the restricted state is scoped to the affected function rather than a whole-platform halt. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Detects a boot-chain baseline value with no released change record and will drive the affected function to its restricted state; today it raises the condition without acting on it.

Detects an out-of-process platform baseline change and will refuse the next mission-enable transition until an approved change record or a recorded override is present; the refusal is designed, not built.
Receives the priority event for an unauthorised baseline change within 60 seconds of detection and retains it for the monthly change review.

control_implementations.narrative: Every cryptographic mechanism WS-X90 depends on is a configuration item, which is what CNSSI 1253 asks for when it scopes CM-3(6) to all controls that rely on cryptography. The algorithm suites, key strengths, certificate trust anchors and module firmware versions of the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) are registered in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and each crypto-dependent control in the tailored set resolves to at least one of those items. Changing any of them is a configuration change with a board decision behind it — there is no operational console path to set an algorithm suite or add a trust anchor, and an attempt is refused and logged. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the algorithm suites, key strengths and certificate trust anchors registered as configuration items; refuses a trust anchor or suite change that does not arrive as an approved configuration change.

Contributes its transmission crypto suite selection and module firmware version as registered configuration items, so a radio waveform crypto change is a board decision rather than an operator setting.
Holds the cryptographic configuration item register and the cross-reference that resolves each crypto-dependent control in the tailored set to at least one registered item.

control_implementations.narrative: Applied changes are reviewed against a monthly cadence, the interval CNSSI 1253 sets for a high-integrity system under CM-3(7), by reconciling the change records in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) against the change-related events retained by the Security Log Collector (LRU-018). The reconciliation reports two exception classes separately: applied-without-record and record-without-applied. Three monthly reviews are complete. The event-driven half is weaker — a post-incident review was run after the August integration incident, but there is no automatic trigger that opens a review once a planned change campaign completes, so that leg currently depends on the engineer remembering. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Supplies the applied and approved change records for the monthly reconciliation and records the review outcome, including the record-without-applied exception class.
Supplies the retained change-related event stream the change records are reconciled against, which is what surfaces the applied-without-record exceptions.

control_implementations.narrative: Blocking configuration change during exercises and real-world operations — the circumstance CNSSI 1253 names for CM-3(8) — is designed as two independent refusals so that neither is a single point of bypass. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) will refuse to apply any configuration change while the platform reports an operational or exercise state, and the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) will independently refuse an interlock parameter change in those states even when the request carries a valid change record. Requests arriving in a blocked state are queued with the blocking state recorded rather than discarded. The platform state signal exists; neither refusal is implemented yet. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Independent second refusal: will reject an interlock parameter change in an exercise or operational state regardless of the change record it carries, so the block cannot be lifted from the platform management path alone.

Will refuse to apply a configuration change while the platform reports an exercise or operational state and queue the request with the blocking state recorded; the platform state signal exists, the refusal does not.

control_implementations.narrative: The ground test rig driven from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is a separate environment from the operational platform and every change package is applied there first, with the analysis record filed against the change in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020). Two things are short of the intent. The analysis record reports a single verdict rather than the four separate headings — defect, weakness, incompatibility and suspected malicious content — that would let an assessor see what was actually looked for; and the rig does not yet include a Payload Interface Subsystem representative, so payload-affecting changes are analysed against a simulated interface and the record does not state that limitation. Both gaps are carried against REQ-570. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Drives the ground test rig on which every change package is applied and analysed before operational release; the rig has no Payload Interface Subsystem representative, so payload-affecting changes are analysed against a simulated interface.

Holds the rig analysis record against the change, including the rig build and its delta against the operational baseline; the record still reports a single verdict rather than the four separate finding headings.

control_implementations.narrative: Post-change verification is wired to the change record: the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) reads the controls the record marks as impacted, runs the verification set associated with each and reports results to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), holding the platform out of mission-ready state until every verification in the set reports. The limitation is coverage of the verification library — verification sets exist for 41 of the controls in the expanded set, concentrated in AC, AU, CM and SI, so a change marked as impacting a control with no verification set is currently recorded as unverifiable and released on an engineering judgement rather than a test. Building out the remaining sets is the open work behind REQ-571. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Reads the impacted controls from the change record, runs each associated verification set at bring-up and holds the platform out of mission-ready state until every set reports.
Receives and retains the verification results so a post-change verification can be retrieved later by change record identifier, including the sets recorded as unavailable.

control_implementations.narrative: Change access is enforced at two points and audited at both. The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) checks every write against the authorised change role list before it touches a baseline, a change record or a release artifact, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) applies the same list to change actions that arrive through a maintenance session, so there is no second path that reaches a released artifact without passing an enforcement point. Every decision, permit and deny alike, produces an audit record carrying actor identity, object and decision, forwarded to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) — the deny records matter more than the permits here, because they are what shows the enforcement is live rather than nominal. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces the authorised change role list on every write to a baseline, change record or release artifact, and emits an audit record for each permit and each deny.
Applies the same authorised change role list to change actions arriving through a maintenance session, so no maintenance path reaches a released artifact unenforced.
Receives the enforcement audit records from both enforcement points and retains actor identity, object and decision for each.

control_implementations.narrative: Privilege to change components on the operational platform is issued through the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and honoured by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and the operational change role is held separately from the development role. The annual re-evaluation CNSSI 1253 requires under CM-5(5) has been performed once and withdrew two dormant holders. Two weaknesses remain: three integration engineers hold both the development and the operational change role under an exception that has no expiry date, and the re-evaluation is currently a spreadsheet exercise against an exported list rather than a review inside the tool that grants the privilege, so the record and the grant can drift between reviews. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Issues the operational change privilege to named holders for the session and refuses a change action from an identity outside the operational change role list.

Honours only privileges issued through the maintenance access gateway for component changes on the operational platform; the annual re-evaluation of holders is still run against an exported list rather than inside this grant path.

control_implementations.narrative: The mission software library on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) accepts content from exactly one identity — the release pipeline identity issued by the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) — and from no interactive account, administrative accounts included. Enforcement sits at the filesystem enforcement point rather than in the application, so an attempted write from any other identity is refused before it reaches library contents and is reported as a library privilege violation naming the attempting identity. This is the narrower of the two library protections on the platform: it constrains who may write, while the execution policy constrains what may run. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces at the filesystem enforcement point that the mission software library accepts content only from the release pipeline identity, refusing interactive and administrative writes and reporting each as a library privilege violation.
Issues the release pipeline identity that is the sole permitted writer to the mission software library and holds the signed library update artifacts it delivers.

control_implementations.narrative: Configuration settings are applied and verified by machine across the security-relevant component set — at minimum all cybersecurity and cybersecurity-enabled components, the scope CNSSI 1253 gives CM-6(1). The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) pushes the approved setting set and then reads it back at every bring-up and at least once in any 24-hour period of sustained operation, reporting each deviation as a named setting rather than a count. The scope deliberately reaches into the Navigation & Timing Subsystem: the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) integrity-check thresholds and the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) holdover and source-authentication settings are verified on the same cycle as the mission compute settings, because a silently loosened navigation threshold is an integrity failure, not a tuning choice. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Pushes the approved setting set to every security-relevant component and reads it back at bring-up and at least once in any 24-hour period of operation, reporting each deviation as a named setting.
Carries its navigation integrity-check thresholds as managed settings verified on the platform cycle, so a loosened threshold is reported by name rather than absorbed into a pass count.
Carries its holdover behaviour and timing source authentication settings as managed settings on the same verification cycle, so a weakened timing source policy surfaces as a named deviation.

control_implementations.narrative: Response to an unauthorised setting change is automatic restoration plus a named event: the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) writes back the approved value, marks the affected function as reverted, and raises an event to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) carrying the setting, the observed value and the restored value. The Navigation Processor (LRU-004) case is handled specially and correctly — a revert is deferred to a navigation solution handover boundary so the revert never drops the solution mid-computation, and the deferral is recorded with its duration. What is missing is the equivalent handling for the Communications Subsystem: a revert on the Protected Network Gateway currently resets the affected session, which is why REQ-576 remains partially satisfied. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Restores the approved value on detecting an unauthorised security-relevant setting change, marks the affected function as reverted and raises the event; the equivalent handling for the Communications Subsystem still resets the affected session.
Defers an applied revert to a navigation solution handover boundary so restoring the approved value never drops the navigation output mid-solution, and records the deferral with its duration.
Retains the revert event carrying the setting name, the observed value and the restored value so the response is reconstructible during the monthly change review.

control_implementations.narrative: The least-functionality review runs on two fronts. Inside the platform, the functions, software and services on the Mission Computer (LRU-001) are reviewed against the approved function list in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) at least annually and after a change or incident, the trigger set CNSSI 1253 gives for CM-7(1); anything unnecessary or nonsecure is disabled or removed, and anything retained carries a written justification and a review date. Outward, the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007), the Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) and the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) are constrained to the approved external interface set. The shortfall is on the sensor interface: LRU-006 still exposes two vendor diagnostic services that are enabled in the shipped configuration with no approved entry, and disabling them is blocked on a vendor firmware release. That is the open item behind REQ-578. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Subject of the annual and event-driven review of functions, software and services; unnecessary or nonsecure items are disabled or removed and retained items carry a written justification and a review date.
Holds the approved function list and the approved external interface set the reviews are run against, and records each retained-item justification and review date.
Presents only the ports, protocols and services in the approved external interface set; anything outside it is disabled in the shipped configuration rather than left listening.
Constrains its exposed data services to the approved external interface set, which is what keeps the radio's management and diagnostic surfaces off the operational configuration.
The open gap in this control: still exposes two vendor diagnostic services with no approved interface entry, pending a vendor firmware release that allows them to be disabled.

control_implementations.narrative: Execution prevention is anchored in measurement, not in file permissions. The Mission Computer (LRU-001) computes the measurement of every image at load and refuses it if that measurement is absent from the approved program set anchored by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002); the refusal happens at load, so an unapproved binary never reaches an executing state rather than being killed after start. The refusal record names the image path and the computed measurement, and the same path is enforced in maintenance mode — a mode switch does not relax the policy, which was the specific weakness the design set out to avoid. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Computes the measurement of every image at load and refuses execution when the measurement is absent from the approved program set, in mission and in maintenance mode alike.

Anchors the approved program set that the mission computer's load-time check is evaluated against, so the permit source is rooted in the boot integrity state rather than in the running operating system.

control_implementations.narrative: Registration compliance for ports, protocols and services is currently a paper reconciliation performed at release review. The planned build gives every service exposed through the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) a registration identifier recorded against its configuration item in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and runs an automated reconciliation of the gateway configuration against that register before each release, reporting unregistered services and port mismatches as separate exception classes with a named owner and a target date. The register schema is agreed; the reconciliation is not built and no gateway service carries a registration identifier in the repository yet. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Exposes the network services that must each carry a registration identifier; its configuration is the object of the planned pre-release reconciliation against the register.
Will hold the registration identifier against each service configuration item and run the pre-release reconciliation reporting unregistered services and port mismatches; the register is empty today.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 runs deny-all, permit-by-exception. The authorised software list in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) is the only permit source for the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), and each entry names the program, its measurement and the mission function it supports — the third field is what makes the annual review CNSSI 1253 requires under CM-7(5) more than a rubber stamp, because an entry with no current mission function is removed rather than carried forward. The most recent review removed four entries on that basis, two of them development-era diagnostic utilities that had survived three baselines. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs deny-all execution against the authorised software list, so a program absent from the list is refused rather than permitted by default.

Holds the authorised software list — program, measurement and supporting mission function per entry — as the only permit source, and records the annual review including entries removed for lack of a mission function.
Applies the same deny-all policy to platform management software, which is where the development-era diagnostic utilities removed at the last review had persisted.

control_implementations.narrative: No supplier warranty or source-availability determination is recorded against WS-X90 software configuration items, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) applies no publication check for binary-only content. The control is unimplemented; the determination field and the authorising-official exception record are scoped against REQ-582 and not yet built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Would hold the supplier warranty and source-availability determination against each software configuration item and mark authorising-official exceptions; neither field exists today.
Would refuse to publish a build containing an unmarked binary-only component; no such publication check is implemented.

control_implementations.narrative: The authorised hardware list is maintained by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) with each entry tied to a platform build, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) enforces it on the maintenance port - an unlisted device is refused a session and reported. The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) was the weaker half until 2026-11-11, when the four of its twelve ports still running firmware that predated the enforcement build were reflashed; all twelve now refuse an unlisted device a data path and report it inside the thirty-second bound, instead of four of them raising the report while the traffic continued. The annual list review CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-7(9) has been completed once. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses an unlisted device identity a data path on all twelve ports and reports it within 30 seconds; the four ports left on pre-enforcement firmware were reflashed to the enforcement build on 2026-11-11.
Refuses a maintenance session to a device whose identity is absent from the authorised hardware list and reports the refusal with the presented identity.
Maintains the authorised hardware list with each entry tied to a platform build and supplies it to the enforcement points; the annual review of the list has been completed once.

control_implementations.narrative: The inventory update is part of the maintenance action rather than a follow-up to it. A maintenance action that installs, removes or replaces an LRU cannot be closed until the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) has written the inventory delta — part number, serial number, firmware version and slot, for both the removed and the installed unit — to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and had it accepted. An action closed without an accepted delta stays open and is reported to the maintenance supervisor, which is what stops the inventory decaying between formal audits. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Writes the inventory delta — part number, serial number, firmware version and slot for the removed and the installed unit — as part of the maintenance action, and holds the action open until the delta is accepted.
Accepts or rejects the inventory delta and is the record that closes the maintenance action; a rejected delta leaves the action open and reported to the maintenance supervisor.

control_implementations.narrative: Inventory currency is measured rather than assumed. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) polls the platform for installed component identity at least once per operating day and publishes the result to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which computes an inventory currency figure — the proportion of records confirmed by an automated observation inside 24 hours — and forwards it to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) so the trend is visible alongside the security event stream. Records outside the window are listed individually with the age of their last confirmation instead of being absorbed into a percentage, and no record is marked confirmed on a manual entry alone. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Polls the platform for installed component identity at least once per operating day and publishes the observation set that the currency figure is computed from.
Computes the inventory currency figure from automated observations only and lists each unconfirmed record individually with the age of its last confirmation.
Receives the daily currency figure so inventory drift is visible on the same timeline as the security event stream.

control_implementations.narrative: Detection of unauthorised components is continuous rather than scheduled, which is the frequency CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-8(3). On the software and firmware side the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) and the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) compare observed measurements against the approved baseline as they change, isolate the affected function from the mission network and notify the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) inside 5 minutes. On the hardware side the Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) quarantines a port presenting an unlisted device and the Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) refuses traffic sourced from a quarantined segment. Two gaps remain: the firmware comparison does not yet cover the Payload Interface Subsystem controllers, whose measurements are read only at bring-up, and switch quarantine is enforcement-capable on eight of twelve ports. Both are tracked against REQ-586 and REQ-587. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Compares observed software measurements against the approved baseline as they change and isolates the affected function from the mission network on a mismatch.
Supplies the firmware measurement comparison for the boot chain; the Payload Interface Subsystem controllers are still measured only at bring-up rather than continuously.
Receives the unauthorised component notification within 5 minutes with the measured value, the expected baseline value and the observing LRU.
Quarantines a port presenting an unlisted device so it carries no mission traffic; quarantine enforcement is available on eight of its twelve ports.
Refuses to forward traffic sourced from a quarantined internal segment, which is what stops an unlisted device reaching an external path even from an advisory-only port.

control_implementations.narrative: Component records in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) carry an accountability field holding the position or role responsible for administering the component — at minimum a position or role, as CNSSI 1253 scopes CM-8(4) — drawn from the four engineering roles this programme uses, and the field holds a role rather than a personal name so it does not decay when staff move. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) refuses a new component record with the field empty. The gap is historical: 6 of the 20 component records were created before the field was mandatory and still carry an inherited default of Platform Lead that has not been confirmed against the current engineering assignment. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the accountability field on each component record as a position or role rather than a personal name; six of the twenty records still carry an inherited default not confirmed against the current engineering assignment.
Refuses to submit a new component record with the accountability field empty, so the gap cannot grow beyond the historical six records.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 configuration management plan is itself a configuration item: signed, version-tagged and held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with recorded programme and cybersecurity approvals, mirrored to the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) so a recovery does not lose it, and readable only by holders of a configuration management role, with refused reads logged. The plan defines the configuration item classes and the identification process across the lifecycle. What is not current is the content: the plan still describes the original 74-control scope and does not yet address the configuration item classes the expanded set introduces — cryptographic mechanism items under CM-3(6), signed component certificate sets under CM-14, and information location records under CM-12. The revision is drafted and awaiting board approval. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the configuration management plan as a signed configuration item with recorded programme and cybersecurity approvals, restricts read access to configuration management roles and logs refused reads; the held revision still describes the original control scope.
Mirrors the approved plan so a platform recovery restores the configuration management plan alongside the baselines rather than leaving it dependent on the ground repository.

control_implementations.narrative: Open-source admission is gated on three recorded facts per component and version — the licence determination, the upstream provenance reference and the named reviewing engineer — held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), with a versioned prohibited licence list carrying its own owner. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) refuses to publish a build whose bill of materials contains a component with a prohibited licence. The incomplete half is provenance: licence determinations are recorded for every open-source entry in the current bill of materials, but upstream provenance references are recorded for roughly two thirds, mostly missing on transitively pulled build-time dependencies, and the publication check does not yet fail a build for a missing provenance reference. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the licence determination, upstream provenance reference and reviewing engineer per open-source component and version, plus the versioned prohibited licence list; provenance references are recorded for roughly two thirds of entries.
Refuses to publish a build whose bill of materials contains a prohibited licence, but does not yet fail a build for a missing provenance reference.

control_implementations.narrative: Software installation onto the Mission Computer (LRU-001) requires a maintenance session that has been explicitly elevated to installation privilege for a bounded period; an ordinary session from the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) cannot trigger an installation at all. Elevation is requested per action rather than per session, expires automatically at the end of its window with no operator step, and is recorded with the requesting identity, the elevation window and the installed package identifier — so an installation is always attributable to a person and a time-boxed grant rather than to a standing privilege. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Cannot trigger an installation from an ordinary maintenance session; each installation requires a per-action elevation that expires automatically without an operator step.

Accepts an installation only from a maintenance session explicitly elevated to installation privilege for a bounded period, and records the requesting identity, the elevation window and the package identifier.

control_implementations.narrative: The information location record in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) maps each class of protected WS-X90 information to the components that process and store it and to the roles and accounts that can reach it on each — principally the Mission Computer (LRU-001) working set and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) at-rest set — and a relocation is captured as a dated location-change record with a reason, so the map is maintained rather than a design-time snapshot. The payload side is thinner: the retention points for telemetry collected by the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and relayed through the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010) are documented for the primary buffers but not for the diagnostic ring buffer LRU-012 holds during fault capture, and no release gate yet refuses a change that introduces a new retention point. Both are open against REQ-593. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the at-rest set of protected mission information; its entry in the location map is the anchor for the access-role listing and for relocation records.
Holds the working set of protected mission information; its component entry in the location map names the roles and accounts that can reach that information on the platform.
Holds the information location map, the access-role listing and the dated location-change records, and is where a new payload retention point would have to be recorded before release.
Collects payload health and status telemetry; its primary buffers are documented retention points, but the diagnostic ring buffer it holds during fault capture is not yet in the record.
Relays payload telemetry and holds a transient relay buffer that is documented as a retention point with its depth and the roles able to read it.

control_implementations.narrative: Automated discovery of protected information types is designed to run inside the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which already holds the exported platform data sets, and to report each occurrence found on a component not recorded as holding that information type to the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as an information location exception naming component, information type and detection basis. Discovery is to be scheduled rather than on-request, and an exception closes only on a recorded relocation, removal or corrected location record. The information type definitions exist; the discovery capability and the exception record are not built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will run the scheduled automated discovery over the exported platform data sets and report each protected information type found on a component not recorded as holding it; the discovery capability is not built.
Will hold the information location exceptions naming component, information type and detection basis, and close one only on a recorded relocation, removal or corrected record.

control_implementations.narrative: Signature verification for any software and firmware component — the scope CNSSI 1253 sets for CM-14 — is enforced at two independent points. At boot, the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) verifies each firmware component in the chain against the approved certificate set held in the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) and halts the affected LRU in its recovery state on failure; there is no operational configuration setting that disables the check. Before that, the Update & Recovery Controller (LRU-016) verifies every component inside an update package at staging and rejects the whole package if one component fails, rather than staging the verifiable subset, with the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) recording the certificate identity that verified each accepted component so provenance is reconstructible after the fact. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Verifies the signature of every firmware component in the boot chain against the approved certificate set and halts the affected LRU in its recovery state on failure; the check has no operational configuration path that disables it.
Holds the approved certificate set the boot chain signatures are verified against and refuses a certificate addition that does not arrive as an approved configuration change.
Verifies every software and firmware component inside an update package at staging and rejects the entire package if one component fails, rather than staging the verifiable subset.
Records the certificate identity that verified each accepted component so the provenance of a staged update is reconstructible after the fact.

control_implementations.narrative: The WS-X90 identification and authentication policy and its procedure set are not shelf documents: both are held as signed, version-tagged artifacts in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), which computes a review-overdue flag once an artifact passes 12 months since its recorded review and refuses to publish an unsigned revision. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is the only publication path, so each revision carries the approving official, a diff against its predecessor and the distribution list of cybersecurity and ground support role holders who received it. Review runs on the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-1, and the designated official for the IA policy is the System Security Engineer. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the IA policy and the IA procedure set as signed, version-tagged artifacts, computes the 12-month review-overdue flag, and refuses an unsigned or unapproved revision.
Sole publication endpoint for an IA policy or procedure revision; binds the approving official, the predecessor diff and the recipient distribution list to each published revision.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged access to WS-X90 runs through two enforcement points. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) opens no administrative session and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) dispatches no maintenance command until both factors verify: a hardware credential whose private key is generated inside and never leaves the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), and an operator PIN entered at the endpoint. There is no reduced-privilege fallback session, so a single-factor attempt ends at refusal rather than at a degraded grant, and every refusal reaches the security log with the credential serial but not the PIN. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Gates every administrative session on a verified two-factor result and refuses to dispatch a privileged command inside a session whose second factor did not verify.
Applies the same two-factor gate to technician maintenance sessions and terminates a session whose hardware credential is withdrawn mid-session.
Generates and holds the privileged authentication private keys as non-exportable hardware objects and returns the attestation result the two gates consume.

control_implementations.narrative: Non-privileged operator access on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) requires a hardware credential plus PIN on every path, and the workstation build exposes no password-only authentication method. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) enforces the same pair when it is attached to the ground support network. What is missing is the disconnected case: when LRU-019 operates on the flightline with no path to the identity service, a local password-only logon remains available as an availability concession, and that path is the open gap. Closing it needs the offline credential verifier that is being built for the LRU-019 baseline, tracked in the POA and M for this control. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces hardware credential plus PIN when network-attached; still permits a local password-only logon when disconnected, which is the residual gap for this control.
Enforces hardware credential plus PIN on every non-privileged session and exposes no password-only method in the approved build configuration.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 keeps two shared role accounts, a flightline maintenance role on the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and a provisioning operator role on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017). On LRU-014 the technician authenticates individually first and the gateway stamps that individual identity onto every action taken under the shared role, so no audit record resolves to the role name alone. LRU-017 authenticates the individual but does not yet propagate the identity into records written by the provisioning batch tooling, which still attributes to the role account. The fix is a change to the batch tool session context and is the open half of this control. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Requires an individual authentication before the shared maintenance role can be assumed and binds that identity to every command recorded under the role.
Authenticates the individual at logon but does not yet carry the identity into provisioning batch tool records, which remain attributed to the shared role account.

control_implementations.narrative: The separate-device factor is a hardware token issued to each technician; its authentication key lives inside a certified hardware boundary on the token, and the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) validates the token attestation before a session opens on either endpoint. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) applies this on its local console, its network path and its remote support path, and terminates the session within 30 seconds of token removal. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) applies it on the network and remote paths only; its local console still accepts a factor pair that both originate on the laptop, so the scope CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-2(6), local, network and remote access for privileged and non-privileged accounts alike, is not yet fully met. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Requires the separate hardware token on the local, network and remote paths for both account types and drops the session within 30 seconds of token removal.
Requires the separate token on the network and remote paths; the local console still accepts two factors originating on the laptop itself, which is the residual gap.
Validates the token attestation, checks the token against the issued-token inventory, and records an attestation result for every accepted session.

control_implementations.narrative: Replay resistance on the communications path is structural rather than procedural. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) issues a single-use nonce at the start of each authentication and binds it into the session key derivation, so a captured exchange re-sent later derives no usable key and is refused under a distinct replay-detected reason code. The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) applies the same construction to link authentication and records the nonce in its sortie session log, where each value appears exactly once. Coverage exceeds the privileged-accounts-at-a-minimum level CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-2(8): every account type on both LRUs is covered because the mechanism is in the protocol, not in an account policy. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Issues the single-use nonce, binds it into session key derivation, and refuses a replayed exchange with a distinct reason code before any key is established.
Applies the same nonce-bound authentication to link establishment and records each nonce once per sortie in the session log.

control_implementations.narrative: PIV acceptance is a ground support capability on WS-X90. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) reads a PIV-compliant credential, chains the certificate up to a trust anchor on the WS-X90 accepted list and checks revocation status before binding an operator account, and refuses a credential whose status cannot be determined rather than accepting it with a warning. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) reads the credential and chains it to an anchor but relies on the workstation for revocation data, so when the laptop is used disconnected it is operating on a revocation snapshot rather than a live check. Making the laptop enforce the same staleness refusal is the open work. Airborne LRUs do not read PIV credentials and are out of scope for this enhancement. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Reads the PIV credential, chains the certificate to an accepted anchor, checks live revocation status, and refuses a credential whose status is indeterminate.
Reads the credential and builds the path but consumes a revocation snapshot when disconnected; the staleness refusal is not yet enforced there.

control_implementations.narrative: Bidirectional device authentication is in place on the internal data path and partly in place on the sensor path. The Internal Ethernet Switch (LRU-009) and each attached device complete a mutual certificate exchange before the port leaves the quarantine VLAN, with the device credential released by the Secure Boot Controller (LRU-002) only after a successful measured boot, and the Mission Computer (LRU-001) drops mission traffic from any port not in the authenticated state. On the navigation side the Navigation Sensor Interface (LRU-006) authenticates mutually with the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) at power-on, but the Timing Receiver (LRU-005) currently authenticates in one direction only, so LRU-004 proves itself to the receiver without the receiver proving itself back on every reconnection. The mutual exchange for the timing link is the open item. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs the mutual certificate exchange per port, holds an unauthenticated port in the quarantine VLAN, and presents its own certificate for the device to validate.
Anchors the device authentication credential and releases it to the network stack only after the measured boot result matches the approved reference.
Refuses application traffic sourced from a switch port whose authentication state is not authenticated, regardless of link status.
Completes mutual cryptographic authentication with the navigation processor at power-on and at every reconnection before sensor data is offered.
Authenticates the processor but does not yet present its own credential on every reconnection; the reverse direction of the timing link is the residual gap.
Marks data from an unauthenticated source as unusable for solution formation and raises an operator advisory rather than degrading the solution silently.

control_implementations.narrative: Individual identifiers on WS-X90 carry an affiliation attribute drawn from an approved set of government civilian, military, prime contractor, subcontractor and foreign national. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) collects the attribute at registration and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) stores it on the identifier record and stamps it onto audit records the account produces. Two gaps remain: the interactive registration path fails closed on a missing attribute but the bulk import path used for the initial ground support roster does not, and roughly 30 identifiers imported before the check was added still carry a legacy unspecified value. A reconciliation sweep and the import-path check are the open work. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Collects the affiliation attribute at registration and fails the interactive path closed when it is absent; the bulk import path does not yet apply the same check.
Holds the affiliation on the identifier record and stamps it onto audit records; still carries legacy unspecified values on identifiers imported before the check existed.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 keeps one attribute store, not a set of per-LRU copies.
