Identifier, affiliation, credential binding, issuing authority and status for every user, device and service live in a protected region of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015). The only writer is the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) over an authenticated channel, and each accepted write appends an immutable revision record naming the writer, the timestamp and the prior value, so attribute history is reconstructible without depending on the audit pipeline. Read access is granted to the identity service principal alone; provisioning tooling queries through that service rather than reading the region. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Hosts the single protected attribute store, enforces the write path restriction, and appends an immutable revision record for every accepted attribute change.
Sole writer to the attribute store; authenticates to the storage module per write and supplies the prior value for the revision record.

control_implementations.narrative: Passwords remain in use on WS-X90 only as the knowledge factor inside multi-factor authentication, and they are handled in two places. The Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) holds the commonly used, expected and compromised password list and screens every creation and change made through the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), rejecting a match without naming the entry. The Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) receives the candidate over a cryptographically protected channel and the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) holds only a salted keyed-hash derivation, with the derivation key resident in LRU-003. The composition rule CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-5(1)(h), a case-sensitive 12-character mix with at least one uppercase, lowercase, numeric and special character and at least 50 percent of characters changed on update, is enforced at creation. Two gaps stand: the list refresh has been running on an ad hoc cadence rather than the at-least-quarterly interval the parameter sets, and the automated strength-assistance tool for operators has not been fielded. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds and applies the compromised-password list and the composition and change-percentage rules; list refresh is not yet on a scheduled quarterly cadence.
Submits every password creation and change for screening and returns a generic rejection message that names no list entry; offers no automated strength-assistance tool yet.
Terminates the cryptographically protected credential channel and holds the keyed-hash derivation key as a non-exportable hardware object.
Stores only salt and derivation output in the credential region, with no plaintext or reversible representation present.

control_implementations.narrative: Public key authentication is the primary mechanism on WS-X90 and the private key never leaves hardware: the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) generates each authentication key as a non-exportable object bound to a single subject, refuses export requests and audits them. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) performs the relying-party half, chaining the certificate up to a trust anchor on the WS-X90 accepted list and checking status against a locally cached revocation set. That cache is refreshed whenever an external link is available, which suits a system whose availability category is moderate and which spends long periods disconnected; a cache older than 7 days is declared stale and the session is refused rather than accepted on an assumption. The authenticated identity is mapped to a single account, never to a group. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Generates and confines the authentication private keys to hardware, refuses and audits export attempts, and maps the authenticated identity to one account.
Chains the certificate to an accepted anchor, checks the locally cached revocation set, refreshes it on external link availability, and refuses on a cache older than 7 days.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 is categorised confidentiality high, so every authenticator that can reach mission data is protected at that level with no per-credential downgrade. Authenticator material exists in exactly two places: inside the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) hardware boundary, or in the encrypted credential region of the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) whose key is itself held in LRU-003. The access control list on that region names only the identity service principal, and mission or provisioning software reaches credentials through the service interface rather than the storage path, so a memory or storage image taken from the Mission Computer or the Provisioning Workstation yields no authenticator material. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds every authentication key as a hardware-resident non-exportable object and wraps the key that protects the storage module credential region.
Keeps credential material only in the encrypted region whose access control list names the identity service principal alone.

control_implementations.narrative: The Configuration Repository (LRU-020) runs a credential-pattern scan across every artifact submitted for publication and refuses to publish one that flags, and the Update and Recovery Controller (LRU-016) refuses to stage a package that carries no passing scan verdict, so the normal software path cannot deliver an embedded unencrypted authenticator. The gap is coverage rather than mechanism: the scan rules were written for compiled images and configuration files and do not yet parse the payload command script format executed by the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), so those scripts are published on the strength of a manual review. A script-aware rule set is in development and is the open item for this control. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Scans every submitted artifact for credential patterns and blocks publication on a flag; its rule set does not yet parse the payload command script format.
Refuses to stage any update package that does not carry a passing scan verdict from the repository.
Executes payload command scripts that are currently cleared by manual review rather than by the automated credential-pattern scan.

control_implementations.narrative: The design is an acknowledgement gate rather than a technical control, because WS-X90 cannot see the other systems on which a ground support user holds accounts. At each credential set the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) will present the reuse prohibition CNSSI 1253 sets for IA-5(8), that the same password must not be reused across domains of differing classification levels, across more than one domain of a single classification level, or across more than one privilege level, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) will hold the dated acknowledgement on the account record and block the credential-set workflow until it is present. Neither the prompt nor the account record field has been built; both are scheduled with the ground support tooling drop. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will hold the dated reuse acknowledgement on the account record and gate the credential-set workflow on its presence; the record field is not yet built.
Will present the reuse prohibition text at each credential set and refuse to complete the workflow without an acknowledgement; not yet implemented.

control_implementations.narrative: Disconnected flightline work needs a cached authenticator, so WS-X90 bounds how long one stays usable. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) expires a cached authenticator 12 hours after the last successful online verification, holds the expiry timer in monotonic form so a power cycle does not reset it, and refuses the session afterwards until the endpoint reconnects to the identity service. The Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) applies the same 12-hour bound but stores the timer in a form that a full power cycle resets, so a technician can extend a cached credential past its intended life by rebooting. Moving the laptop timer onto the trusted counter is the open item. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Expires the cached authenticator 12 hours after the last online verification using a monotonic timer that survives a power cycle, then refuses the session.
Applies the same 12-hour bound but its expiry timer resets on a full power cycle, which is the residual gap for this control.

control_implementations.narrative: One signed trust store manifest in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) is the sole authority for the anchors any WS-X90 LRU may load, naming each anchor with its purpose and expiry. The Tactical Data Radio (LRU-008) reports the digest of its installed trust store at power-on and a mismatch raises a configuration deviation. The Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) reports its digest only during a maintenance download rather than at power-on, so a trust store drift on that unit can go unnoticed until the next maintenance cycle. Bringing LRU-012 onto power-on reporting is the open item; the distribution of new manifests to both units also remains a manual maintenance action rather than an automated push. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the single signed trust store manifest listing each anchor, its purpose and expiry, and is the only approved source for anchor distribution.
Reports its installed trust store digest at every power-on and raises a configuration deviation when it does not match the manifest of record.
Reports its trust store digest only during a maintenance download, so drift on this unit is detected a maintenance cycle late.

control_implementations.narrative: The intended process issues every privileged-role hardware authenticator in person at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), before the designated registration authority, with the issuing officer identity and the authorising government sponsor recorded against the credential serial number before activation. Today credentials are issued in person by local practice but the sponsor authorisation is captured on a separate form and is not bound to the serial number in the provisioning record, so the binding cannot be verified from the system. The work is procedural documentation plus a provisioning record field, scheduled with the identity proofing drop. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will record the issuing officer and the authorising sponsor against the credential serial before activation; the serial-to-sponsor binding field is not yet in the provisioning record.

control_implementations.narrative: Authentication feedback is suppressed at both ground support endpoints. The Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) mask PIN and password entry on every surface including the recovery console, keep the entered characters out of logs, crash dumps and diagnostic buffers by never copying them out of the credential input buffer, and return one generic failure message whether the identifier or the authenticator was wrong. The two failure paths were also equalised in timing to within 50 milliseconds so response latency does not become the disclosure channel the masked display closes. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Masks credential entry on the operator console and the recovery console, returns a single generic failure message, and keeps entered characters out of the diagnostic buffer.
Applies the same masking and generic message locally, and equalises the failure response timing so a wrong identifier and a wrong authenticator are indistinguishable.

control_implementations.narrative: Access to the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003) is role-bound, not merely session-bound. An operator or service authenticates to the module and is bound to a defined module role before any keyed operation is accepted, a keyed request arriving before role authentication returns a module status refusal, and a transition between roles requires a fresh authentication rather than inheriting the earlier one. The Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) participates by refusing a key-wrapping request that does not carry a valid LRU-003 role binding, so the storage module cannot be used as a path around the module role check. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Authenticates the operator or service to a defined module role before any keyed operation and refuses a role transition without re-authentication.
Accepts a key-wrapping request only from a session carrying a valid module role binding, closing the storage path around the role check.

control_implementations.narrative: Other-agency technician support is an anticipated case for WS-X90 rather than a current one. The design has the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) accept the visiting agency PIV credential, verify it electronically against the issuing agency trust anchor and revocation source captured as part of the support authorisation, and bind it to a non-organisational account whose expiry equals the authorisation end date with no in-place extension. Nothing is built: the workstation reads only anchors from the WS-X90 trust store manifest today, and the non-organisational account type does not exist in the account model. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will accept and electronically verify another agency PIV credential and bind it to a time-boxed non-organisational account; neither the external anchor path nor the account type exists yet.

control_implementations.narrative: A list of external authenticators approved for non-organisational access to WS-X90 support interfaces is held as a signed artifact in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) with type, assurance level, approver and approval date per entry. The Protected Network Gateway (LRU-007) enforces the list on the support interface and refuses an unlisted authenticator type. The gap is currency and completeness: the list was populated from the initial support agreements and has no scheduled review, and the gateway configuration pins a list revision rather than tracking the current one, so an approval added in the repository does not reach enforcement until a configuration change is pushed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the signed list of accepted external authenticators with type, assurance level and approver; the list has no scheduled review cycle yet.
Refuses any external authenticator type absent from the list revision it is configured with, and logs the refusal; it pins a revision rather than tracking the current one.

control_implementations.narrative: The intent is that non-organisational identity handling on WS-X90 conforms to one recorded identity management profile, held in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) and enforced by the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), which would reject an external identity assertion whose attribute set, binding method or assurance level does not match the profile revision in force. The profile has not been selected or written, and LRU-013 has no external assertion path in the current build, so this is design only. Selection is being held until the external authenticator list under IA-8(2) settles, because the two constrain each other. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will hold the selected identity management profile as a controlled, revisioned artifact; the profile has not yet been selected or authored.
Will validate an external identity assertion against the profile revision in force; no external assertion path exists in the current build.

control_implementations.narrative: WS-X90 authenticates services, not just the boxes hosting them. Each mission service holds a per-service certificate whose subject names both the service and its hosting LRU, issued during provisioning and renewed at each software baseline. The service mesh on the Mission Computer (LRU-001), the telemetry publisher on the Payload Telemetry Unit (LRU-012) and the navigation solution service on the Navigation Processor (LRU-004) all present that certificate on connection and refuse a peer that offers only a device credential or a certificate whose subject does not match the hosting LRU inventory entry. The effect is that a compromised but authenticated device still cannot impersonate a service it does not host. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Presents and validates per-service certificates for every mesh connection and refuses a peer offering only a device credential.
Authenticates as the named telemetry publisher service before forwarding payload health data and refuses an unnamed consumer identity.
Authenticates as the named navigation solution service and validates the subject against the hosting LRU inventory entry before accepting a peer.

control_implementations.narrative: No adaptive authentication capability exists on WS-X90. The circumstance detection that would drive it, a maintenance session opening outside the authorised support window or from a ground network address not on the approved list, is within reach of the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) but is not implemented, and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) has no supplemental factor prompt to raise. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: No anomalous-session detection is implemented; the collector correlates exported logs but raises no adaptive authentication trigger.
No supplemental authentication factor prompt exists in the current build.

control_implementations.narrative: Re-authentication is enforced at the two points where authorisation would otherwise be inherited across a change of context. On the ground support side the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) demands the full factor set again before any privilege escalation, before any maintenance role reassignment, and after 30 minutes of session inactivity, and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) discards its session key at each of those triggers so a resumed session cannot carry the earlier grant. On the payload side the Payload Safety Interlock (LRU-011) requires a two-person re-authentication completed within the preceding 5 minutes before it releases an arming state to the Payload Interface Controller (LRU-010), rejects an arming command backed by an older authentication, and reverts to the safe state when a subsequent arming command arrives without a renewed authentication. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Triggers full re-authentication on privilege escalation, on maintenance role reassignment and after 30 minutes idle before accepting a further command.
Discards the session key at each re-authentication trigger so a resumed session cannot inherit the previous authorisation.
Requires a two-person re-authentication inside a 5-minute window before releasing an arming state and reverts to safe when it is not renewed.
Accepts an arming state only from an interlock release backed by a current re-authentication and holds the safe state otherwise.

control_implementations.narrative: Identity proofing for WS-X90 accounts runs at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) before an account is enabled: the registration authority proofs the applicant, resolves them to a single named individual with no shared or role-only registration accepted, and records the identity evidence collected against the account. Two things are short of the intent. The assurance level required per role is documented in the ground support handbook rather than held as a controlled artifact the workstation can enforce, so the level applied depends on the registration authority reading it correctly, and the record captures collection and validation but treats verification as an implicit step with no separate outcome field. Both are addressed by the identity proofing drop that also carries IA-12(3). This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Runs registration-time identity proofing, resolves each applicant to one individual, and records collected evidence; assurance level per role is not yet an enforceable controlled artifact and verification has no separate outcome field.

control_implementations.narrative: No WS-X90 account reaches the enabled state without a named sponsor. A registration submitted at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) sits in a pending state until a government sponsor or supervisor authorises it, and the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) refuses to enable an account whose authorisation record is absent or names the applicant as their own sponsor. The record naming the sponsor, the role requested and the date is retained with the account for its whole life, including after the account is disabled, so a later review can reconstruct who vouched for a privilege that has since been removed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds a submitted registration in a pending state until a named sponsor authorises it and captures the sponsor identity, role requested and date.
Refuses to enable an account whose sponsor authorisation record is missing or self-referential, and retains the record after the account is disabled.

control_implementations.narrative: The registration authority at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) requires physical identity evidence at registration and records the type, issuer and reference for each item, deliberately storing no document image so the registration store never becomes a collection of scanned credentials. The shortfall is enforcement of the minimum: the workflow accepts a registration with a single evidence item, so the one photo credential plus one supporting document minimum currently rests on registration authority discipline rather than on the tool. Adding the two-item minimum check is the open work for this enhancement. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Captures evidence type, issuer and reference and stores no document image; does not yet enforce the two-item minimum at the registration workflow.

control_implementations.narrative: The planned approach fixes two approved methods for identity evidence, issuer or authoritative-source confirmation for validation and a biometric comparison against the presented credential for verification, and has the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) record the method and outcome per evidence item, holding a registration out of the enabled state when either returns an inconclusive outcome. Neither method is in use today: validation is a visual inspection by the registration authority and verification is not separately recorded, so the record fields, the approved method artifact and the biometric comparison step all remain to be built. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will record a validation method, a verification method and an outcome per evidence item and block enablement on an inconclusive outcome; currently performs visual inspection only.

control_implementations.narrative: Privileged-role applicants are proofed with the applicant physically present before the designated registration authority at the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017), and that is the standing practice for new privileged registrations. What is missing is the systemic guard: the registration record has no in-person attestation field, so a registration originally taken remotely for a non-privileged role can be promoted to a privileged role without a new in-person session, and the completed privileged accounts cannot be shown to have been proofed in person from the record alone. The attestation field and the promotion block are the open work. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Conducts in-person proofing for privileged-role registrations as standing practice but carries no in-person attestation field and does not block promotion of a remotely proofed registration.

control_implementations.narrative: Media protection direction for SYS-WSX90 is held as data, not as a shelf document: the policy and its five subordinate procedures - media access, marking, storage, transport and sanitization - sit in the Configuration Repository (LRU-020) as signed, version-tagged artifacts, each with a named approver and a recorded review date, and LRU-020 raises a review-overdue flag once a date passes 12 months, which is the at-least-annual interval CNSSI 1253 sets for MP-1. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) is the only endpoint that can publish a revision, so each effective revision carries an operator identity, a diff against its predecessor and the list of custodians and maintenance role holders it was distributed to. What is missing: the transport and sanitization-verification procedures are still drafts and carry no approver signature, so two of the five artifacts fail the signature check; and the media protection official is named in the policy header but the delegation has not been countersigned, leaving MP-1b evidenced by the policy text alone. Both gaps are carried as open media-protection remediation actions. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Stores the WS-X90 media protection policy plus the five procedure artifacts under signature with approver and review date, computes the 12-month review-overdue flag, and refuses to record an unsigned artifact as effective.
Sole publication endpoint for a media protection revision; binds the publishing operator, the predecessor diff and the custodian distribution list to each revision it makes effective.

control_implementations.narrative: Access to WS-X90 media is a check-out decision, not a cabinet key. The scope CNSSI 1253 sets for MP-2 - all digital and non-digital media carrying information not cleared for public release - resolves on this program to the removable audit and recovery cartridges written by the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015), the provisioning volumes cut for field load, and the printed configuration and key-handling worksheets held with them. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) holds the media library register and gates every check-out on an identity present in the current custodian list, recording custodian, item serial and stated purpose; a request from any other identity is refused, no serial is released, and the refusal reaches the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) inside 60 seconds, where it is retained with the rest of the ground-support security record. LRU-015 writes a cartridge only against an open check-out, so a cartridge outside the library always resolves to a named holder. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Holds the media library register and the custodian list; authorizes or refuses each check-out and records custodian, item serial and purpose on the ones it grants.
Writes removable audit and recovery cartridges only against an open check-out record, so every cartridge in circulation is attributable to a named custodian.
Receives check-out grants and refusals from LRU-017 within 60 seconds and retains them as the queryable media-access record off the maintenance floor.

control_implementations.narrative: Marking is currently manual and is being moved into the release path. The design puts label generation inside the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) write flow: when a removable volume is cut, LRU-017 will print a human-readable label carrying the distribution limitation, the handling caveat and the release record identifier issued by the Configuration Repository (LRU-020), and will refuse to close the release record until the label print is confirmed, so an unmarked volume cannot be signed out as released. Exemptions will be narrow by construction - only media that never leaves the named controlled provisioning area - and each exemption will be recorded against that area in LRU-020 rather than left to custodian judgement. Today custodians apply pre-printed caveat labels by hand against a paper log, which satisfies the intent of MP-3a inconsistently and gives no queryable exemption record; the label printer integration and the LRU-020 release-record field are scheduled work. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will generate and print the handling label during the volume write flow and block closure of a release record whose label print is unconfirmed; today the operator applies a pre-printed caveat label by hand.
Will issue the release record identifier that appears on the label and hold the marking text and any exemption against a named controlled area.

control_implementations.narrative: Removable cartridges written by the Secure Storage Module (LRU-015) carry audit and recovery material and are the only WS-X90 media that regularly sits outside a running LRU. When not in use they are held in the key-controlled media library inside the controlled maintenance area, and the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) opens an inventory entry the moment a cartridge is removed from LRU-015 - serial, storage location, removal date - which stays open until a completed sanitization or destruction record closes it, which is how MP-4b protection-until-sanitized is carried on this program. What is missing: the monthly physical reconciliation is still a manual count transcribed into a spreadsheet rather than a count taken against the LRU-017 inventory, so a discrepancy is found late; the off-site spares cabinet at the support facility is not yet inside the same count; and nothing feeds cartridge inventory state to the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013), so there is no platform-side view of outstanding media. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Source of the removable audit and recovery cartridges; records the write event and cartridge serial that opens the accountability chain when a cartridge is removed.
Holds the cartridge inventory entry from removal to closure and the key-controlled library register; reconciliation against a physical count is still performed by hand outside this record.

control_implementations.narrative: Nothing leaves the controlled maintenance area in the clear. The Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) will not release a volume for transport unless the volume is encrypted under a key issued by the Cryptographic Services Module (LRU-003), and will not complete the release until a transport record - authorized custodian, destination, seal number, release time - is bound to the volume serial; release is offered only to identities on the transport-authorized list, and the release event is exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018), which is where transport activity is reconstructed for an assessor. That covers MP-5a protection, MP-5d restriction to authorized personnel, and the outbound half of MP-5b and MP-5c. What is missing is the inbound half: courier hand-off and delivery receipts are still paper forms filed at the support facility and are not reconciled back into the transport record, so an open transport has no automated overdue or non-arrival alert and accountability during transit rests on the courier's signature alone. The receipt reconciliation feed is an open remediation action. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Enforces the encrypt-before-release gate, creates the transport record binding custodian, destination, seal number and release time to the volume serial, and checks the releasing identity against the transport-authorized list.
Issues and holds the volume encryption keys used for media in transit, so a volume outside the controlled area is unreadable without a key that never leaves the module.
Retains the release and refusal events that document transport activity; does not yet receive the courier delivery receipts that would close each transport.

control_implementations.narrative: MP-6 sanitization itself is fielded and evidenced on this program; the review, approval, tracking and verification wrapper that MP-6(1) adds is designed and not yet built. The design hosts a sanitization record on the Platform Management Controller (LRU-013) carrying the approving reviewer, the media serial and category, the method applied, the operator who performed it, the verification result and the disposal action, and refuses completion while the approver and operator are the same identity or while the verification result is empty - a two-person rule enforced by the record rather than by the custodian. Completed records are to be exported to the Security Log Collector (LRU-018) and referenced from the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) inventory entry so a cartridge cannot be retired without one. Today the same sequence runs on a paper sanitization form with a wet signature, which is auditable only by pulling the binder and gives no automatic check that verification actually happened before disposal. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Will host the sanitization record and enforce the approver-not-operator and verification-present rules that block completion; hosts no such record today.
Will reference the completed sanitization record from the media inventory entry so a cartridge cannot be closed out or retired without one.
Will receive completed sanitization records as the retained, queryable disposal history off the maintenance floor.

control_implementations.narrative: Sanitization tooling on WS-X90 is software: the wipe utility fielded on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) for library cartridges and the reduced field utility on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019). The planned test is a coupon: write a known marker pattern to a sample cartridge of each media type in service, sanitize it with the fielded utility and the published procedure, then read the device back through a raw path and confirm no instance of the pattern is recoverable, recording tool version, operator and result. The interval is the at-least-annual frequency CNSSI 1253 sets for MP-6(2), with a re-test inside 30 days of any utility version change, and a failing coupon suspends that version for WS-X90 media. The procedure is drafted and the coupon media has been identified; no coupon test has been executed yet, so no assurance is claimed that the intended sanitization is achieved. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Hosts the library sanitization utility that the coupon test will exercise and will hold the coupon result record with the tool version under test.
Hosts the reduced field wipe utility, which is a separate build and therefore needs its own coupon result before it is used on WS-X90 media.

control_implementations.narrative: No intake sanitization capability is fielded. Portable storage devices arriving from a vendor or returning with a gap in their chain of custody are handled today only by the MP-7 registry restriction - an unregistered or unowned serial will not mount - and by malware scanning on receipt, neither of which is the nondestructive wipe before first connection that MP-6(3) calls for. The intake station on the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the corresponding mount block on the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) are scoped but unfunded, and no partial credit is claimed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Intended host of the intake wipe station and the per-serial wipe record; provides no intake sanitization function today.
Intended enforcement point that would refuse a mount until an intake wipe record exists for the serial; enforces only the MP-7 registry check today.

control_implementations.narrative: Media use on WS-X90 is restricted in two independent places. On the platform, the Mission Computer (LRU-001) and the Maintenance Access Gateway (LRU-014) refuse mass-storage class enumeration on their maintenance ports unless the device serial is in the signed removable-device allow-list distributed from the Configuration Repository (LRU-020); the port stays electrically enabled for diagnostic use but the storage function is never bound, and a refusal record naming the serial and port is emitted within 60 seconds. LRU-001 additionally holds write access to an allow-listed device disabled in flight configuration, so removable media is a read path only. On the ground, the approved portable-storage registry in LRU-020 binds every serial to a named custodian, an issue date and a category, and marks an entry vacant when the custodian record lapses; the Provisioning Workstation (LRU-017) and the Maintenance Laptop (LRU-019) mount nothing whose serial is absent or vacant, which is how the no-identifiable-owner prohibition in MP-7b is enforced rather than asserted. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

by_component.description: Refuses mass-storage enumeration on its maintenance port for serials outside the signed allow-list and keeps write access to allow-listed devices disabled in flight configuration.
Applies the same allow-list check on the technician-facing maintenance port and emits the refusal record naming the device serial and port within 60 seconds.
Holds the approved portable-storage registry and the signed allow-list it publishes, binds each serial to a named custodian and category, and marks entries vacant when custody lapses.
Enforces the registry at mount time on the provisioning bench, refusing any serial that is unregistered or whose custodian entry is vacant.
Applies the same mount-time registry check on the conditional-use maintenance endpoint, so a device carried into the field still resolves to a named owner.

findings.title: SC policy baseline carries an issue date but no recorded review decision in the Configuration Repository (SC-1)
findings.description: Examining the LRU-020 baseline object export for SCP-BASE-3 recorded in EVD-146, the assessor found issue date, owner and both superseded revisions present, and watched LRU-017 refuse to assemble a provisioning package against a baseline older than twelve months. What the export does not contain is any trace of the annual review itself: the reissue is carried as a calendar reminder held by a person rather than as a repository workflow step that lodges a decision, so the freshness of the artifact is enforced while the review REQ-193 asks for leaves nothing behind. No protection is absent — the policy and its implementing procedures are current and the build gate demonstrably works — and the shortfall is that the assessor has to take the review on trust. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Session-table occupancy missing from the gateway counter export, leaving low-rate state exhaustion undetectable (SC-5(3))
findings.description: Across the one-hour capture in EVD-151 the 60-second export cadence from LRU-007 held with no sequence gap, and an injected connection-rate excursion sustained for three intervals produced exactly one alert at LRU-018 while a two-interval excursion produced none. The exported set is nevertheless link-level only: interface utilisation, connection rate and drop counters are published, session-table and buffer occupancy are not, so an adversary who exhausts gateway state at a packet rate under the profiled threshold leaves no mark in anything the collector evaluates. REQ-200 counts that occupancy counter as part of the exported set, so the objective is unmet even though the alerting behaviour it also specifies was correct in every trial. Adding the counters is queued behind the next gateway telemetry change, and until then detection on the platform's only external mediation point stops at the link layer. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Egress denial records attribute maintenance-origin traffic to a device instead of an operator (SC-7(9))
findings.description: The 2026-10 threat-rule sample in EVD-157 shows matching outbound traffic dropped at LRU-007 and a denial record reaching LRU-018 inside the 60-second bound, with originating LRU and partition resolved on every row. On rows whose traffic began in a maintenance session the operator field is unpopulated and the origin resolves to the Maintenance Access Gateway, because the session identity is not carried forward into the record the gateway emits. REQ-207 asks the record to name where denied traffic came from, and a device name does not answer that when several technicians reach the platform through the same appliance, so an attempted exfiltration from a maintenance session cannot afterwards be pinned to anyone. Losing attribution on the one path with the widest reach is what lifts this above a routine logging omission. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Maintenance Access Gateway service connector locked but unsealed, so an unauthorized connection leaves no trace (SC-7(14))
findings.description: The platform inventory extract in EVD-161 accounts for every boundary-crossing interface: both LRU-007 external terminations carry keyed locks recorded against a key holder, and unused LRU-009 ports are blanked with the blank noted per port. The LRU-014 service connector carries its lock and no tamper-evident seal, which makes it the one interface where a cable can be seated and pulled between scheduled inspections with nothing left for an inspector to find. REQ-212 was written to make an unauthorized physical connection visible rather than merely inconvenient, and a keyed lock delivers only the second of those. Seals are specified and on order so the window is bounded, but it sits on the connector that reaches the maintenance path directly. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Provisioning Workstation tooling screened for interpreted-code technologies by review rather than at build (SC-18)
findings.description: EVD-172 carries a dated acceptable and unacceptable technology list with a named owner, and an LRU-001 load module containing a listed unacceptable technology failed its build with the technology named in the failure text. Tooling built for LRU-017 reached that same list only through a control board reading, so whether an unacceptable technology was caught turned on a reviewer noticing it rather than on a gate refusing the module. REQ-229 puts the rejection in the build for both endpoints, and a review path cannot support that assertion for the workstation however diligent the reviewer is. Aurora Defense Systems extended the existing build scan over the LRU-017 tooling pipeline inside the assessment window and the objective retested to a pass, so the finding is recorded closed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: In-partition failures never reach the Secure Boot Controller, so the platform does not enter its defined secure state (SC-24)
findings.description: Induced boot integrity failures and watchdog expiries in EVD-178 drove LRU-001 into the defined secure state comfortably inside five seconds, with every external interface down and no key material resident in memory afterwards. A failure detected inside a running mission partition takes a different route entirely: it is handed to that partition's own handler and never reaches LRU-002, so the platform can carry on with other partitions live while one has already failed its own checks. REQ-240 describes the secure state as a whole-platform condition, and a per-partition handler has no means of bringing the platform to it. The uncovered case is also the airborne case rather than the power-on one, which is why on an integrity-high system this is not treated as a bounded shortfall. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Audit procedures still written to the original 74-control scope in the Configuration Repository (AU-1)
findings.description: The approval record in EVD-242 shows the audit policy re-approved within the current annual cycle, signed, numbered and disseminated in LRU-020 to every WS-X90 platform role holder on the list. Read next to it, the procedure half of the set still describes the audit scope as it stood before the effective control set reached 546 controls and is silent on the correlation and reviewer-queue behaviour now running on LRU-018. REQ-344 binds policy and procedures together and calls for both to be re-approved after a change to the audit pipeline, so an approved policy sitting over stale procedures leaves the objective short by half. The pipeline itself was observed working throughout, so what is defective is the written direction rather than anything the platform does. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Maintenance session transcripts sat outside the correlation key space on the Security Log Collector (AU-6(3))
findings.description: In the walkthrough recorded in EVD-247, a seeded configuration change in LRU-020 and the platform audit records it produced in the copy taken from LRU-015 resolved to one correlated event keyed on actor identity and time, and a change with no matching audit record surfaced as unmatched rather than being dropped. Maintenance session transcripts lived in a third store the join did not read, so a change made during a maintenance session correlated to the change record and not to the session that carried it, and the analysis view could say what had changed without saying under whose hands. REQ-349 asks for one view across the repositories holding the change and its audit trail, and a join that omits one of them cannot build it. The transcript store was brought into the correlation key space during the window and the requirement retested to a pass, closing the finding. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Payload arm and release commands signed under a rotated key cannot be verified at all (AU-10)
findings.description: Every arm and release command in the mission run captured in EVD-253 carried a signature from LRU-003 binding the command, the operator identity and the LRU-011 interlock state, and a replay with an altered operator identity failed verification exactly as intended. Verification breaks on key history instead: no list of retired key identifiers has been published to LRU-018, so a validly signed command whose signing key has since rotated resolves as unknown-key and is filed among the records that genuinely cannot be trusted. REQ-360 exists so that whoever originated a payload command through LRU-010 cannot later disown it, and a signature nobody can resolve to a key offers no more attribution than no signature at all. The records this strands are arm and release commands, so the objective the platform currently cannot meet is the one covering its most consequential action, and the affected population grows with every rotation until the retired-key history is published. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Switch-relayed audit records ordered on arrival rather than origin in the compiled trail (AU-12(1))
findings.description: The trail extract in EVD-255 covered every LRU in the reporting-component register for the sampled window, reproduced the known order of a seeded event sequence against the LRU-005 reference, and carried degraded-time markers through visibly instead of interleaving marked records in silence. Records relayed through LRU-009 were the exception: the switch passed them on without stamping a source time, so LRU-018 ordered them by the moment they arrived, which drifts outside the platform tolerance whenever the internal segment is congested. REQ-364 asks for one trail ordered on the platform time reference, and an arrival-ordered subset sitting inside it is a second ordering wearing the same column heading. A source-time stamp was added to the relay path and the retest reproduced the seeded order across every source, so this is recorded closed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Seven access control procedures in field packages carry no current owner signature (AC-1)
findings.description: The signed export in EVD-286 holds a single approved revision of the access control policy in LRU-020, an annual review record against it, and the out-of-cycle review triggered by the 2026-09-08 change to the effective control set, all as REQ-436 lays out. Seven of the fourteen procedures published alongside that policy were written against the previous control scope and carry no current owner signature, and LRU-017 will still assemble a technician procedure package containing them because the issue check tests the policy revision cited and not the signature state of each procedure inside. Unsigned direction therefore reaches the people performing the work, which is a materially different condition from stale direction resting in a repository. Reissue of the seven is the outstanding work, and the finding is carried on the packages already in the field rather than on the policy, which is current. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: UDP-bearing approved tunnel outlives a failed inspection past the five-second termination bound (AC-4(4))
findings.description: EVD-293 records all three approved tunnels presented to the LRU-007 inspection path in cleartext by LRU-003, and an encrypted flow whose key LRU-003 does not hold blocked outright rather than passed uninspected. Termination on a failed inspection measured inside the bound for the TCP-bearing tunnels and did not occur at all for the UDP-bearing one, where offending packets are discarded individually while the session itself stays established indefinitely. REQ-449 sets a five-second teardown on detection precisely so a flow that has already proved itself disallowed stops being available to try again, and dropping packet by packet leaves that door standing open. No content crosses the boundary meanwhile, which is what keeps the exposure contained, but the session state the requirement asks to be removed is still there. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Unreconfirmed privileged assignments flagged on the Platform Management Controller but never reduced (AC-6(7))
findings.description: The signed worksheet in EVD-298 falls inside the 180-day interval and sets each holder's assignment beside their preceding 180 days of privileged activity drawn from LRU-018, so the review was a judgement against what people actually did rather than a signature against a role name. Two assignments emerged from that review unreconfirmed and both were still privileged when the assessor asked, because LRU-013 raises a flag on a non-reconfirmation and leaves the downgrade to somebody remembering to perform it. REQ-454 states the reduction as the outcome of the review rather than an action available afterwards, so an assignment that survives its own review through inattention undoes the reason for holding one. The review discipline itself is sound and evidenced, which confines the shortfall to the enforcement step at the end of it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Out-of-window remote privileged commands logged and then admitted by the Maintenance Access Gateway (AC-17(4))
findings.description: Two of the three admission checks REQ-470 names held under test: EVD-309 shows a command absent from the approved remote-privileged list refused at LRU-014 with its reason code, and an LRU-019 laptop failing device attestation unable to open a privileged session at all. The third did not hold, because the scheduled-window test was wired as advisory rather than as an admission decision, so a privileged command issued outside a maintenance window was written to the session log and then executed. A refusal that records itself and proceeds regardless is not a refusal, so the rule that a command failing any one of the three checks is rejected was unsatisfied on the window leg. Aurora Defense Systems promoted the window test to a blocking check during the assessment window and the retest showed the out-of-window command refused with its reason code, so the finding is closed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Disconnected Maintenance Laptop still offers a password-only logon on the flightline (IA-2(2))
findings.description: The method inventory in EVD-372 shows LRU-017 offering no authentication path that does without a hardware credential and a PIN, and LRU-019 enforcing the same pair on every session while it is attached to the ground support network. Taken off that network the laptop falls back to a local password-only logon left in place as an availability concession, and REQ-599 forecloses it in terms: the credential-and-PIN pair extends to sessions established while the endpoint is disconnected, and no password-only fallback is to exist. That fallback is reachable in exactly the setting the platform is worked on most, by anyone holding the laptop at the aircraft with no path to the identity service, so the multi-factor property this control was selected to provide is not a property of the platform today. The offline credential verifier being built for the LRU-019 baseline is the only thing that closes it, and nothing compensates in the meantime. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Timing Receiver port admitted to the mission VLAN on a one-sided certificate exchange (IA-3(1))
findings.description: The per-port export in EVD-376 confirms the behaviour REQ-604 turns on across the mission computing ports: a device presenting a valid certificate but a failed LRU-002 boot measurement stays in the quarantine VLAN, and LRU-001 refuses mission traffic sourced from any port whose state is not authenticated. The port serving the Timing Receiver is nonetheless carried as authenticated with a certificate subject recorded for one end of the link only, because that device validates the switch credential without presenting its own on reconnection, so LRU-009 admitted it to the mission VLAN on an exchange that ran in a single direction. The requirement is written around a mutual exchange because a port that has proved the switch to the device tells the switch nothing whatever about what is attached to it. Every other port is correct and the quarantine mechanism works, so this is one link rather than a broken mechanism, but it is the link distributing the reference the whole audit trail is ordered on. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Compromised-password screening list refreshed ad hoc, so an accepted credential may already be public (IA-5(1))
findings.description: Storage and transport held under test in EVD-380: a raw read of the LRU-015 credential region returned salt and derivation output with nothing reversible in it, a packet capture of the path into LRU-003 carried no plaintext, and the composition rules rejected an eleven-character candidate, a twelve-character candidate missing a class, and a change leaving more than half the characters in position. What the assessor could not establish is that an accepted password is one worth accepting, because the compromised and commonly used list every candidate is screened against has been refreshed whenever somebody got to it rather than on the at-least-quarterly interval the parameter for this control sets, and the latest refresh sits well outside that interval. A candidate meeting every composition rule REQ-609 states and appearing on a list published since that refresh is accepted today without objection. The mechanism is sound and the remedy is a schedule, which bounds this, but the fielded consequence is that a public credential is a valid credential on WS-X90. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Monitoring and boot-integrity enhancement procedures still marked draft in the signed SI set (SI-1)
findings.description: Edition 3 of the integrity policy set in EVD-206 is signed inside the last twelve months, names the official accountable for it, enumerates the SI controls it implements, and the LRU-017 release manifest cites the same version identifier the LRU-020 copy carries, so a fielded image traces to the policy edition it was built under. The procedures covering the monitoring and boot-integrity enhancements the expanded control set introduced are marked draft in that same edition, and the set names no event other than the annual date that would force a reissue, so the arrival of those enhancements triggered nothing. REQ-251 requires reissue after any change to the SI control allocation, which is exactly the change that occurred, leaving the objective unmet on its event-driven leg while its calendar leg is satisfied. The engineering behind those enhancements is fielded and assessed on its own objectives; what is missing is issued direction for operating it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Mission data sessions over the tactical radio never presented to platform monitoring (SI-4(10))
findings.description: The design record in EVD-209 has the management and telemetry session classes terminated at LRU-007 so their content reaches the monitoring path inside the gateway boundary, with session keys generated and held in LRU-003 and no plaintext content written to gateway persistent storage. Mission data sessions carried over the Tactical Data Radio fall outside that arrangement completely: they are neither terminated nor inspected, so monitoring sees flow-level metadata and nothing of what the platform's primary operational link is actually carrying. REQ-261 carves out no session class, and the decision on whether to terminate the mission link or formally accept metadata-only visibility remains open, so the objective is unmet rather than deliberately tailored away. That blind spot covers the highest-volume external path on a confidentiality-high system, which is why it is not recorded as a contained shortfall. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Navigation, timing and payload firmware violations raise an alert without driving the restricted state (SI-7(5))
findings.description: An induced violation in the mission software set behaved as REQ-280 asks in EVD-213: LRU-002 put the platform into the restricted state with no operator action, mission functions were unavailable while it was held, and recovery from the last known-good image on LRU-016 demanded an authenticated technician instead of an automatic reimage. That automatic response is scoped to a single measurement domain. A violation reported by navigation, timing or payload firmware raises an alert and leaves the platform in whatever mode it was in, so a component that has already failed its own integrity check keeps contributing to the mission while somebody reads the alert. The requirement attaches the restricted state to an integrity violation in the platform rather than in one partition of it, and the three domains left out are the ones whose output the mission depends on most directly. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Four of eleven configuration management procedures unsigned and flagged review-overdue (CM-1)
findings.description: Revision 4.0 in EVD-345 shows the CM policy and seven procedures signed, version-tagged and bound to the single official who owns them, with the engineering and cybersecurity dissemination list recorded against the publication and the review-overdue flag computing correctly in LRU-020 against the annual interval. That flag is set on four procedures — those covering automated change prohibition, automated security response, information location and signed components — which were drafted when the enhancements were added and never signed. REQ-559 requires every artifact in the set to carry a valid signature and name an accountable owner, so a repository correctly reporting four unsigned procedures is reporting the objective as unmet rather than satisfying it. The enforcement machinery is doing precisely what it should, which is why this is raised against the content of the set and not against the repository holding it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Post-campaign change review has no trigger and runs only when somebody remembers (CM-3(7))
findings.description: The reconciliation output in EVD-351 covers the September and October cycles and keeps its two exception classes apart, listing applied changes with no approved record separately from approved records with no applied change, with the post-incident review raised after the August integration incident present beside them. REQ-568 asks for the same review once a planned change campaign has been performed, and nothing opens one: LRU-020 records the campaign closing and no reconciliation against the LRU-018 event stream is scheduled off that event, so the review happens if the engineer running the campaign thinks to ask for it. A change campaign is when the applied set diverges furthest from the approved set in the shortest time, so the review with no trigger behind it is the review covering the widest divergence. The monthly cadence is being met and evidenced, which caps how long an unreviewed campaign can sit unnoticed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Four Internal Ethernet Switch ports reported unlisted hardware without refusing it a data path (CM-7(9))
findings.description: EVD-360 records an unlisted device refused a maintenance session at LRU-014 with its presented identity named, and refused a data path on eight of the twelve LRU-009 ports, the refusal reaching the platform log inside the thirty-second bound every time. On the four remaining ports detection ran and the report was raised while the data path stayed up, because those ports carry firmware predating the enforcement build and can act on a device identity only by reporting it. REQ-583 requires the unlisted device to be refused a path as well as reported, so a port that announces the problem and then carries the traffic delivers half of what is asked. The four ports were reflashed to the enforcement build inside the assessment window and the retest showed all twelve refusing, so this is recorded closed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Payload Telemetry Unit maintained on retrospective paperwork outside the work-order gate (MA-2(2))
findings.description: The workflow export in EVD-259 shows scheduling, dispatch and close-out each producing a state change on LRU-013 stamped with an actor identity, the work-order gate on LRU-016 refusing any action carrying no open order, and no manual override path anywhere in the configuration. Maintenance on the Payload Telemetry Unit does not travel that route: its records are typed in by hand after the work is finished, so no work order gated the action while it was happening and the thirty-day stale-record flag never examines them. REQ-373 treats the workflow as the thing that authorises a maintenance action rather than the thing that describes it afterwards, so a subsystem maintained on retrospective paperwork sits outside the requirement however complete that paperwork is. Everything inside the platform management subsystem is gated correctly, which makes this a coverage boundary between subsystems rather than a defect in the gate itself. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Out-of-work-order privileged tool use discoverable only by query on the Security Log Collector (MA-3(5))
findings.description: Every privileged invocation in the sampled period reconciled one-to-one against the LRU-014 invocation register in EVD-262, each record naming the tool, the technician identity and the privilege level, so visibility of privileged tool use after the fact was complete. The extract carries no alert rows whatever, and the reason is that the rule REQ-379 asks for — an alert whenever a privileged invocation falls outside an open work order — had been specified for LRU-018 and not built, leaving out-of-order use something a person would find only by going to look for it. A record that exists and is never read detects nothing, which is the distinction the requirement draws between logging and alerting. The rule was implemented on the collector inside the assessment window and a seeded out-of-order invocation raised the alert on retest, closing the finding. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Recovery exercise restored one partition, leaving the four-hour objective unproven for the article (CP-4)
findings.description: The exercise record in EVD-323 shows a restore run through LRU-016 from a sealed LRU-015 backup set, with the mission software partition coming back and passing its integrity check inside the elapsed time measured. The flight-configuration article was not released for test, so the platform management and payload interface partitions were left out of the run and have never been restored end to end, which also makes the measured duration a figure for part of the article rather than the whole of it. REQ-486 defines the exercise as restoring a representative platform article and judges it against a four-hour objective for that article, so a partial restore can neither pass nor fail against the objective it was measured for. Availability is categorised moderate and a corrective action is open with a named owner against the untested partitions, so what is exposed is demonstrated readiness rather than the recovery path. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Primary and alternate bearers converge on one Internal Ethernet Switch port group (CP-8(2))
findings.description: The traces in EVD-325 were built from live interface and routing state rather than from a drawing, and they settle carrier-side disjointness cleanly: the LRU-007 primary and the LRU-008 alternate reach the demarcation over different transmission lines through different points of presence with no carrier element shared between them. On the platform they meet, both transiting the same LRU-009 port group, and REQ-498 fails a trace on any element appearing twice whichever side of the demarcation it sits on. The shared port group is the single point of failure the alternate path exists to remove, so the alternate is disjoint everywhere except the place that decides whether it helps. Availability is categorised moderate and the convergence is already recorded as an accepted single point of failure against a risk reference, which is why it is carried lightly while the radio path is re-homed. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Expired acquisition procedures can still be cited in a live procurement package (SA-1)
findings.description: The revision index in EVD-120 carries signed release metadata for the acquisition policy and its supporting procedures, names the designated official on each issue, and records the dissemination acknowledgements taken at LRU-017 before an issue was marked current. Two things hold the objective short: the last full reissue was made before the tailored profile grew from 74 to 546 controls, so the procedures describe none of the acquisition actions the added supply chain and configuration enhancements call for, and LRU-020 stores a review date without acting on it, so an expired procedure can be cited in a live procurement package and nothing intervenes. REQ-121 asks for an annual reissue and for publication to record who received it, and the second of those is evidenced while the first is not. A stale procedure that downstream work can still consume is what separates this from the other policy shortfalls, where the direction is out of date but nothing reads it. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Payload Safety Interlock carries an asserted trustworthiness basis with no supplier assurance case (SA-8(9))
findings.description: The dependency map at revision B in EVD-130 resolves every security-decision dependency in the mission computing chain to a component with a recorded basis: LRU-002 to its hardware root of trust and reviewed verification path, LRU-003 to its module validation and reviewed key release precondition. LRU-011 stands in that map as the component payload authorization depends upon, and its basis is an assertion, because the supplier assurance case has not been delivered and nothing behind the entry has been reviewed. REQ-148 turns that entry into a rule — the interlock must refuse an authorization from a component whose declared basis is weaker than its own — and a rule cannot be evaluated while one side of the comparison is a placeholder. The component nobody can characterise is the one standing between a payload command and the payload itself, so the least understood dependency in the architecture carries the most consequence. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Six LRUs fall back to a maintenance-record serial number for hardware identity at power-on (SA-10(3))
findings.description: EVD-142 shows LRU-013 reading the supplier-provisioned identity at power-on and raising a fault within one cycle for a substituted unit, the comparison anchored to the LRU-002 platform measurement so that a matched identity on an unmeasured platform is not accepted as valid. Six units across the navigation, timing and payload interface subsystems carry no identity part, their suppliers having been on contract before the requirement was placed, and for those the comparison falls back to a serial number read out of a maintenance record. A record-based check catches a substitution only when whoever performed it also updated the record, which is the single thing an adversary swapping hardware will not do. REQ-182 asks for the identity to be read from the unit itself, so this fallback is not a weaker form of the same check but a different check answering a different question. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Ground-support telemetry exchange carrying traffic on an interim approval with no signed agreement (CA-3)
findings.description: The register in EVD-328 maps each exchange enabled in the LRU-007 policy set to a signed agreement identifier and shows the LRU-008 tactical data link covered by a current agreement recording its impact level and the party responsible for each control. One entry resolves instead to a dated interim approval: the ground-support telemetry exchange is enabled and carrying traffic while its agreement remains in draft. REQ-508 makes the signed agreement the precondition for enabling an exchange rather than a record to be caught up afterwards, so an interim approval with an expiry on it is a plan to comply and not compliance. The exchange is time-bounded and listed openly rather than hidden, and what nobody has yet signed for is the division of control responsibilities with the other party. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Baseline scan ran to completion on a thirty-hour-old signature set without aborting (RA-5(2))
findings.description: The test run in EVD-333 drove LRU-017 against baseline 4.2.1 with signature sets aged six, twenty-three and thirty hours. The thirty-hour case completed and produced a clean report, because the workstation never compares the refresh timestamp on the LRU-020 mirrored set against the twenty-four-hour window the parameter for this control sets, and the abort path REQ-525 describes does not exist to be triggered. The signature identifier reached the scan log and not the report header, so a reviewer holding that report has no way to tell how old the set behind it was. A scan that silently runs stale returns an absence of findings indistinguishable from a clean result, which is what makes this more than a scheduling matter even though the weekly mirror refresh is working. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Incident response procedures name no insider-threat branch or spillage roles after the scope expansion (IR-1)
findings.description: The manifest in EVD-231 shows the incident response policy and the WS-X90 procedure set held as signed revisions in LRU-020 with their approval dates and signatures, and the copy staged on LRU-017 matching the current repository digest, so ground support is working from the controlled copy. That procedure set has completed no review since the effective control set expanded, and it shows: no insider-threat branch is named and nobody is assigned the spillage roles the added incident response enhancements introduce, so two declarable incident classes have an escalation path in the control set and none in the direction people actually follow. REQ-298 calls for review at least annually and after any incident that changes the escalation chain, and widening that chain by two branches is the change no review has been run against. Published containment actions for the existing subsystems remain accurate, which keeps this short of the response capability itself. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Two of four weakness reports reached the second recipient past the five-working-day bound (IR-6(2))
findings.description: All four cases worked since the scope expansion name the implicated baseline item on the LRU-018 incident record, so every weakness in EVD-235 is anchored to a specific LRU-020 configuration revision instead of being described in prose. Measured from the recorded containment timestamp, two of those four reports reached the second recipient REQ-319 names after five working days had elapsed, because that route is walked by hand while the first is dispatched automatically. The requirement sets one bound covering both recipients, so a report that is timely to one and late to the other is simply late. Four cases is a thin sample to reason from, and it is also every case the platform has produced since the scope grew. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Protected bay access list transcribed by hand, so a facility removal leaves bay access standing (PE-3(1))
findings.description: The export in EVD-267 shows the bay reader list as a strict subset of the facility roster and shorter than it, a credential valid at the outer door refused at the bay reader, and every refusal in the preceding thirty days written to the reader log with its credential identifier and timestamp. That list is transcribed from the roster rather than derived from it, so removing somebody from the facility does not remove them from the bay, and the reader log is not exported for correlation, so nothing checks a bay entry against whether the holder still has platform access at all. REQ-392 asks for a second authorisation held separately from general facility access, and a hand-maintained list is separate in the wrong direction, because it can outlive the access it exists to narrow. Behind that door sit LRU-001, LRU-003 and LRU-015, so a stale entry is standing physical access to the key, configuration and recovery material the rest of the control set is built on. This narrative is synthetic demo content.

findings.title: Personnel security procedure describes weaker gating than the Provisioning Workstation enforces (PS-1)
findings.description: The manifest in EVD-239 holds the signed personnel security policy in LRU-020 with a designated managing official and a dissemination record covering every provisioning role on LRU-017, so the distribution half of REQ-330 is intact. The approved revision predates the change made to national eligibility gating during the scope expansion and the at-least-annually review that would have caught it is overdue, so what LRU-017 enforces when an account is provisioned is stricter than what the published procedure tells the person provisioning it to expect. REQ-330 requires an update following any change to screening or eligibility gating, and that change happened without one. Nothing is under-protected, because the divergence runs the safe way with the machine stricter than the paper, and what is defective is that the two no longer agree. This narrative is synthetic demo content.
